nodes.rationale: A worked example connects over HTTP to the remote GitHub MCP server at `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` with a personal access token in the Authorization header and `allowedTools: ["mcp__github__list_issues"]`. A `connected` status confirms the token works; on `failed` or `needs-auth` the result must not be trusted, since Claude can fall back to built-in tools.

nodes.label: DBHub read-only database example
nodes.rationale: The DBHub example queries Postgres over stdio. Its `execute_sql` tool would run any SQL the agent emits, including writes, unless restricted — so `readonly = true` in `dbhub.toml` makes DBHub reject INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE and DDL, and `dsn = "${DATABASE_URL}"` keeps the connection string out of the file.

nodes.label: failed-status causes
nodes.rationale: Common causes of a `"failed"` server are missing environment variables (check the `env` field for stdio servers), a server that is not installed (verify the npx package and that Node.js is on PATH), an invalid database connection string, and network issues reaching a remote HTTP/SSE URL.

nodes.label: connection timeout troubleshooting
nodes.rationale: MCP connections time out after 30 seconds by default, and a server that starts slower than that fails to connect. Besides raising the limit, the doc suggests a lighter-weight server, pre-warming the server before starting the agent, and checking server logs for slow initialization.

nodes.label: MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT
nodes.rationale: `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` changes how long a running tool call may take — a distinct limit from the connection timeout governed by `MCP_TIMEOUT`.

nodes.label: 25,000-token MCP output limit
nodes.rationale: The SDK applies Claude Code's MCP output limit: a tool result larger than 25,000 tokens is written to a file and the tool result is replaced by an error message naming that file path, so the agent can read the output back in portions.

nodes.label: MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS
nodes.rationale: The `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` environment variable raises the MCP tool-output limit above its 25,000-token default.

nodes.label: anthropic/maxResultSizeChars annotation
nodes.rationale: A server can declare a higher per-tool output limit with the `anthropic/maxResultSizeChars` annotation, a server-side counterpart to the client's environment-variable limit.

nodes.label: System prompt (Agent SDK)
nodes.rationale: A system prompt is the initial instruction set that shapes how Claude behaves throughout a conversation, defining behavior, capabilities and response style. The Agent SDK offers three starting points for it: the minimal default, the `claude_code` preset, and a custom string.

nodes.label: Minimal default prompt
nodes.rationale: When `systemPrompt` (TypeScript) / `system_prompt` (Python) is unset, the SDK uses a minimal prompt covering tool calling but omitting the rest of the `claude_code` preset, including its security and safety instructions and its working-directory and environment context. This differs from `claude -p`, which uses the Claude Code system prompt by default.

nodes.label: `claude_code` preset
nodes.rationale: The `claude_code` preset is the system prompt the Claude Code CLI uses: tool usage instructions, security and safety instructions, and context about the working directory and environment. Set it as `systemPrompt: { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code" }` in TypeScript or `system_prompt={"type": "preset", "preset": "claude_code"}` in Python.

nodes.label: Custom system prompt string
nodes.rationale: Passing a custom string as `systemPrompt` replaces the default entirely: the SDK sends only what you provide. It gives complete control but loses the default tool guidance, built-in safety instructions and environment context unless you include them yourself.

nodes.label: `append` to the preset
nodes.rationale: The preset object accepts an `append` property that adds custom instructions after the preset while preserving all built-in functionality. Because nothing is removed, the doc calls it the lowest-risk customization; it is session-only and lives in code.

nodes.label: Deciding factor: resemblance to Claude Code
nodes.rationale: The deciding factor for a starting point is how closely the agent resembles Claude Code — a coding agent in a repository with a human watching streaming output and steering. The further the product is from that, the more you should write your own prompt.

nodes.label: Different surface
nodes.rationale: A different surface means the output is not read in a terminal by the person who triggered it — chat UIs, structured-output consumers, and non-coding automation each need a prompt matching how their output is rendered and reviewed. Unattended coding automation such as a CI lint-fixing job still fits the preset.

nodes.label: Different identity
nodes.rationale: A different identity means the agent should not present itself as Claude Code. A support bot, a data-analysis assistant, or any domain-specific agent needs its own name, scope and persona.

nodes.label: Different permission model
nodes.rationale: A different permission model means the agent runs autonomously without a human approving each step, or operates on a narrow set of resources. Claude Code's prompt assumes a human is in the loop with access to a full toolset.

nodes.label: Non-coding tasks
nodes.rationale: Most of Claude Code's prompt is coding guidance, so for research, content or operations agents that guidance competes with the instructions you actually need — a reason to write a custom prompt instead of using the preset.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md project context injection
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md gives persistent project context, but the SDK injects its content into the conversation and leaves the system prompt untouched, so it works with any system prompt configuration. It is persistent across sessions, shared via git, discovered without code changes, and is not loaded if `settingSources` is an empty array.

nodes.label: `settingSources` / `setting_sources`
nodes.rationale: Setting sources control which configuration levels load: `'project'` loads `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` from the working directory and `'user'` loads `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Default `query()` options enable both; if you set them explicitly you must include the sources you need. CLAUDE.md loading is controlled by setting sources, not by the `claude_code` preset.

nodes.label: Output styles
nodes.rationale: Output styles are saved markdown configurations that modify Claude's system prompt and can be reused across sessions and projects. They are markdown files with frontmatter plus prompt content, stored in `~/.claude/output-styles/` for user level or `.claude/output-styles/` for a committed project-level style.

nodes.label: `keep-coding-instructions` frontmatter
nodes.rationale: A custom output style leaves out the `claude_code` preset's software engineering instructions by default; setting `keep-coding-instructions: true` in the frontmatter keeps them and layers your instructions on top. Those instructions exist only in Claude Code's full system prompt, so the setting has no effect on the shorter system prompt pinned by `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT`.

nodes.label: Activating an output style
nodes.rationale: Output styles are activated by running `/config` in the CLI, by setting `outputStyle` in `.claude/settings.local.json`, or in the TypeScript SDK by setting `outputStyle` inside the inline `settings` object passed to `query()` — it is not a top-level `Options` field. Styles load only when `settingSources`/`setting_sources` includes `'user'` or `'project'`.

nodes.label: Python SDK has no output-style option
nodes.rationale: The Python SDK does not have an option to select an output style programmatically. For code-only deployments that cannot write to `.claude/settings.local.json`, use `append` or a custom prompt string instead.

nodes.label: Per-session dynamic prompt context
nodes.rationale: The `claude_code` preset embeds per-session context ahead of the `append` text: the working directory, whether it is a git repository, the platform, the active shell, the OS version, and auto memory paths. Any difference in that context produces a different system prompt and therefore a prompt-cache miss.

nodes.label: `excludeDynamicSections`
nodes.rationale: Setting `excludeDynamicSections: true` (TypeScript) or `"exclude_dynamic_sections": True` (Python) moves the per-session context into the first user message, leaving only the static preset and the `append` text in the system prompt so identical configurations share a cache entry across users and machines. It requires `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` v0.2.98+ or Python `claude-agent-sdk` v0.1.58+, works on the preset object form only, and is ignored for a custom prompt.

nodes.label: Tradeoff of excluding dynamic sections
nodes.rationale: The environment context still reaches Claude, but as part of the first user message rather than the system prompt. Instructions in a user message carry marginally less weight, so Claude may rely on them less strongly when reasoning about the current directory or auto memory paths — enable the option when cross-session cache reuse matters more than maximally authoritative environment context.

nodes.label: `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` CLI flag
nodes.rationale: `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` is the equivalent of `excludeDynamicSections` for non-interactive CLI mode, documented in the CLI reference.

nodes.label: Cross-session prompt-cache sharing
nodes.rationale: By default two sessions using the same preset and `append` text cannot share a prompt cache entry when they run from different working directories. Making the system prompt byte-identical across sessions is what lets a fleet of agents reuse one cache entry; CLAUDE.md content does not affect the system prompt cache because it is injected into the conversation instead.

nodes.label: `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY`
nodes.rationale: In the TypeScript SDK a custom prompt can be an array of strings with the `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY` marker between the static part and the per-request part; the SDK sends each side as its own text block with its own cache breakpoint. Passing both parts as one string means a change to the per-request part invalidates the static instructions' cache too. The form is not available in the Python SDK.

nodes.label: Boundary marker assembly rules
nodes.rationale: The SDK joins the strings on each side of the marker with a blank line and removes the marker itself so its text never reaches Claude; if the marker appears more than once the first occurrence is the split and the rest are removed; if it is omitted all strings are joined into one block, the same as passing one string.

nodes.label: Where prompt splitting applies
nodes.rationale: The SDK splits the prompt at the boundary marker only when it calls the Claude API directly or runs on Claude Platform on AWS. On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, an LLM gateway, or whenever `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1` is set, the whole prompt is sent as one block.

nodes.label: `SystemPromptFile` for large Python prompts
nodes.rationale: In Python a large custom prompt should be loaded with `system_prompt={"type": "file", "path": "..."}` rather than passed as a string, because the Python SDK passes a string prompt as one command-line argument to the CLI subprocess and a prompt exceeding the OS argument-length limit fails at process spawn before any API request (on Linux: `Argument list too long`).

nodes.label: Cache token tracking fields
nodes.rationale: Cache behaviour is observable through the `cache_creation_input_tokens` and `cache_read_input_tokens` fields on each result message, described in the Agent SDK cost-tracking docs.

nodes.label: Comparison of the four customization approaches
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md, output styles, preset-with-`append`, and a custom `systemPrompt` differ in persistence, reusability, management, and what they preserve from the preset. The first three preserve default tools, built-in safety and automatic environment context; only the custom prompt loses tools unless included, requires safety to be added, and requires environment context to be provided.

nodes.label: Responsibility taken on with a custom prompt
nodes.rationale: Choosing a custom prompt string means you get only what you write and take responsibility for replacing the tool guidance and safety instructions your agent still needs, plus supplying environment context yourself.

nodes.label: Combining approaches
nodes.rationale: The approaches compose: a persistent output style or CLAUDE.md sets long-lived behavior while `append` layers session-specific instructions on top without touching the saved configuration — for example adding OAuth and token-storage focus areas to an already-active Code Reviewer output style for one review session.

nodes.label: SDK message stream
nodes.rationale: Running a `query()` example streams messages as Claude works: a system init message, assistant messages, user messages carrying tool results, and a final result message with the session outcome.

nodes.label: Behavior surfaces outside the system prompt
nodes.rationale: Skills, hooks and permissions also shape agent behavior outside the system prompt and are documented on their own pages, alongside CLAUDE.md which is injected as conversation context rather than into the system prompt.

nodes.label: Agent SDK observability with OpenTelemetry
nodes.rationale: The Agent SDK can export traces, metrics and log events as OpenTelemetry data to any backend that accepts the OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP), hosted or self-hosted. The guide covers how telemetry is emitted, how export is configured, and how the data is tagged and filtered once it reaches the backend.

nodes.label: Production visibility questions
nodes.rationale: Running agents in production requires visibility into which tools they called, how long each model request took, how many tokens were spent, and where failures occurred. These four questions are what the telemetry export exists to answer.

nodes.label: OTLP-accepting observability backend
nodes.rationale: The export destination is any backend speaking the OpenTelemetry Protocol — a hosted observability platform or a self-hosted OpenTelemetry Collector. Confirming export works means checking the collector's own logs for incoming spans, metrics and log events after a task completes.

nodes.label: Telemetry originates in the CLI child process
nodes.rationale: The Agent SDK runs the Claude Code CLI as a child process over a local pipe, and it is the CLI — not the SDK — that carries the OpenTelemetry instrumentation: spans around each model request and tool execution, metrics for token and cost counters, and structured log events. The SDK produces no telemetry of its own; it passes configuration through and the CLI exports directly to the collector.

nodes.label: Telemetry configured by environment variables
nodes.rationale: All telemetry configuration reaches the CLI as environment variables. Because the child process inherits the application's environment by default, the variables can be set either in the process environment or per call.

nodes.label: Process-environment configuration
nodes.rationale: Setting the OpenTelemetry variables in the shell, container, or orchestrator before the application starts means every query() call picks them up automatically with no code change. This is the recommended approach for production deployments, and can be done in a Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifest, or shell profile.

nodes.label: Per-call options.env configuration
nodes.rationale: Setting the variables in ClaudeAgentOptions.env (Python) or options.env (TypeScript) lets different agents in one process use different telemetry settings. In Python env is merged on top of the inherited environment; in TypeScript env REPLACES it entirely, so the object must spread ...process.env to keep PATH, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and the rest.

nodes.label: Three independent OpenTelemetry signals
nodes.rationale: The CLI exports three independent signals — metrics, log events, and traces — each with its own enable switch and its own exporter, so only the needed ones have to be turned on.

nodes.label: Metrics signal (OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER)
nodes.rationale: The metrics signal carries counters for tokens, cost, sessions, lines of code, and tool decisions, and is enabled with OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER.

nodes.label: Log-events signal (OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER)
nodes.rationale: The log-events signal carries structured records for each prompt, API request, API error, and tool result, and is enabled with OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER.

nodes.label: Traces signal (OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER, beta)
nodes.rationale: The traces signal carries spans for each interaction, model request, tool call, and hook, and is enabled with OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER plus CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1. Tracing is in beta and span names and attributes may change between releases.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 is the beta gate required for traces; metrics and log events do not need it. With it set, each step of the agent loop becomes an inspectable span.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 master switch
nodes.rationale: Telemetry is off until CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 is set and at least one exporter is chosen. The most common configuration sends all three signals over OTLP HTTP to a collector.

nodes.label: OTLP transport configuration variables
nodes.rationale: Standard OTLP transport is configured with OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL (e.g. http/protobuf), OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (e.g. http://collector.example.com:4318) and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS (e.g. an Authorization bearer token).

nodes.label: Silent export failure by default
nodes.rationale: The CLI fails silently on export errors by default: if the endpoint is unreachable or rejects the data, the agent still runs normally and the telemetry is dropped with no error surfaced in the application.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_DIAG_STDERR=1 diagnostics
nodes.rationale: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_DIAG_STDERR=1 alongside the exporter variables surfaces exporter errors, read through the SDK's stderr callback (Python) or stderr option (TypeScript). It requires Claude Code v2.1.179 or later.

nodes.label: console exporter collides with the SDK message channel
nodes.rationale: The console exporter writes telemetry to standard output, which the SDK uses as its message channel, so console must never be set as an exporter value when running through the SDK. To inspect telemetry locally, point OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT at a local OpenTelemetry Collector instead.

nodes.label: Batched export and bounded shutdown flush
nodes.rationale: The CLI batches telemetry and exports on an interval. A clean process exit attempts a flush, but that flush is bounded by a short timeout so spans can still be dropped if the collector is slow; if the process is killed before the CLI shuts down, everything still in the batch buffer is lost.

nodes.label: Default export intervals
nodes.rationale: By default metrics export every 60 seconds while traces and log events export every 5 seconds.

nodes.label: Shortened export intervals for short-lived calls
nodes.rationale: Setting OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORT_INTERVAL and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORT_INTERVAL to 1000 shortens all three intervals so data reaches the collector while a short task is still running, narrowing both the slow-flush and the killed-process loss windows.

nodes.label: claude_code.interaction span
nodes.rationale: claude_code.interaction wraps a single turn of the agent loop, from receiving a prompt to producing a response, and is the enclosing parent for the llm_request, tool and hook spans.

nodes.label: claude_code.llm_request span
nodes.rationale: claude_code.llm_request wraps each call to the Claude API, carrying model name, latency and token counts as attributes.

nodes.label: claude_code.tool span and its children
nodes.rationale: claude_code.tool wraps each tool invocation, with child spans for the permission wait (claude_code.tool.blocked_on_user) and the execution itself (claude_code.tool.execution).

nodes.label: claude_code.hook span
nodes.rationale: claude_code.hook wraps each hook execution, and is only emitted under detailed beta tracing.

nodes.label: Detailed beta tracing pair
nodes.rationale: Detailed beta tracing is the pair ENABLE_BETA_TRACING_DETAILED=1 and BETA_TRACING_ENDPOINT — a pair that also changes where the run's logs and traces go, not merely what is recorded.

nodes.label: Subagent spans nest under the parent tool span
nodes.rationale: When an agent spawns a subagent through the Agent tool, the subagent's llm_request and tool spans nest under the parent agent's claude_code.tool span, so the full delegation chain appears as one trace.

nodes.label: session.id span attribute
nodes.rationale: Spans carry a session.id attribute by default, so several query() calls against the same session can be filtered into one timeline in the backend. Claude Code omits the attribute if OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_SESSION_ID is set to a falsy value.

nodes.label: W3C trace-context propagation into the CLI
nodes.rationale: The SDK automatically propagates W3C trace context: when query() is called while an OpenTelemetry span is active, it injects TRACEPARENT and TRACESTATE into the child process environment and the CLI makes its claude_code.interaction span a child of the caller's span, so the agent run appears inside the application's trace rather than as a disconnected root.

nodes.label: Trace context on event log records
nodes.rationale: With TRACEPARENT set, each OTLP event log record's trace_id and span_id match the calling application's trace, so events can be joined to spans in the backend. Before v2.1.212, event records emitted outside an active span carried neither field.

nodes.label: TRACEPARENT forwarded to Bash and PowerShell commands
nodes.rationale: When trace-context propagation is enabled the CLI also forwards TRACEPARENT to every Bash and PowerShell command it runs, so a command that emits its own OpenTelemetry spans has them nest under the claude_code.tool.execution span wrapping it.

nodes.label: Explicit TRACEPARENT skips auto-injection
nodes.rationale: Auto-injection is skipped when TRACEPARENT is set explicitly in options.env, allowing a specific parent context to be pinned. Interactive CLI sessions ignore inbound TRACEPARENT entirely; only Agent SDK and `claude -p` runs honor it.

nodes.label: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME override
nodes.rationale: The CLI reports service.name as claude-code by default; OTEL_SERVICE_NAME overrides it (e.g. support-triage-agent) so several agents, or the SDK running alongside other services exporting to the same collector, can be told apart in the backend.

nodes.label: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES tagging
nodes.rationale: OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES attaches arbitrary metadata (e.g. service.version=1.4.0, deployment.environment=production) as OpenTelemetry resource attributes on every span, metric and event the agent emits. Its syntax reserves commas, spaces and equals signs, so interpolated values must be percent-encoded.

nodes.label: Identity attributes describe the credential, not the end user
nodes.rationale: The CLI attaches identity attributes to every event based on the credential it uses to call Anthropic. In an application serving many end users from one deployment, those attributes identify the service's credential — not the end user on whose behalf the agent acted.

nodes.label: End-user attribution via resource attributes
nodes.rationale: To make tool calls and MCP activity attributable to an application's end users, inject end-user identity as resource attributes on each query() call — e.g. enduser.id and tenant.id from the incoming request, percent-encoded — so every span and event from that request carries the requesting user and tenant.

nodes.label: Per-user security audit trail for SIEM
nodes.rationale: With end-user identity attached, the tool_decision, tool_result, mcp_server_connection and permission_mode_changed events — exported as log records named with a claude_code. prefix — become a per-user audit trail that can be forwarded to a SIEM platform.

nodes.label: Telemetry is structural by default
nodes.rationale: By default telemetry records structure rather than content: durations, model names and tool names on every span, and token counts when the underlying API request returns usage data (so spans for failed or aborted requests may omit them). The content the agent reads and writes is not recorded unless an opt-in variable is set.

nodes.label: OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1
nodes.rationale: OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1 adds prompt text to claude_code.user_prompt events and to the claude_code.interaction span.

nodes.label: OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1
nodes.rationale: OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS=1 adds tool input arguments — file paths, shell commands, search patterns — to claude_code.tool_result events.

nodes.label: OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1
nodes.rationale: OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1 adds full tool input and output bodies as span events on claude_code.tool, truncated at 60 KB by default. It requires tracing to be enabled.

nodes.label: OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES
nodes.rationale: OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES exports full Anthropic Messages API request and response JSON as claude_code.api_request_body and claude_code.api_response_body log events: set to 1 for inline bodies truncated at 60 KB, or file:<dir> for untruncated bodies on disk with a body_ref path in the event. Bodies include the entire conversation history with extended-thinking content redacted, and enabling it implies consent to everything the three narrower variables would reveal.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH configures the 60 KB inline truncation limit applied to logged tool content and to inline raw API bodies. It requires Claude Code v2.1.214 or later.

nodes.label: Cost tracking from the message stream
nodes.rationale: Token usage and cost can be read directly from the SDK response/message stream instead of being exported to an external observability backend — the Track cost and usage guide covers this alternative.

nodes.label: Claude Code Monitoring reference
nodes.rationale: The Claude Code Monitoring page is the complete reference for every environment variable, metric name, event name and attribute the CLI emits, including the Traces (beta) exporter configuration, standard attributes, security-event audit list and redaction behavior. The Agent SDK emits the same data because it runs the same CLI.

nodes.label: Hosting the Agent SDK
nodes.rationale: The Hosting the Agent SDK guide covers deploying agents in containers where the OpenTelemetry variables can be set at the environment level.

nodes.label: Python Agent SDK reference
nodes.rationale: The page is the complete API reference for the Python Agent SDK (package claude-agent-sdk), covering its functions, classes, option and message types, hook types, built-in tool input/output schemas, error types and sandbox configuration. It notes that signature blocks and bare async for / async with fragments on the page are illustrative and must be wrapped in an async def main() run with asyncio.run().

nodes.label: Installation into a virtual environment
nodes.rationale: Install the SDK into a virtual environment: python3 -m venv .venv, source .venv/bin/activate, pip install claude-agent-sdk. On recent Debian, Ubuntu and Homebrew Python installs, running pip install against system Python fails with error: externally-managed-environment.

nodes.label: Choosing between query() and ClaudeSDKClient
nodes.rationale: query() creates a new session per interaction, handles one exchange, manages the connection automatically and does not support interrupts; ClaudeSDKClient reuses one session across multiple exchanges, is manually connected, supports interrupts and continues the chat automatically. Both support streaming input, hooks and custom tools. The doc recommends ClaudeSDKClient for interactive applications such as chat interfaces or when the next action depends on Claude's response.

nodes.label: query() function
nodes.rationale: query(prompt, options, transport) returns an AsyncIterator[Message] and creates a new session for each interaction by default; each call starts fresh with no memory of previous interactions unless continue_conversation=True or resume is passed in ClaudeAgentOptions. prompt is a str or an AsyncIterable[dict] for streaming mode.

nodes.label: tool() decorator
nodes.rationale: tool(name, description, input_schema, annotations) is a decorator that defines MCP tools with type safety and returns an SdkMcpTool instance wrapping an async handler. input_schema accepts either a simple type mapping such as {'text': str, 'count': int} (recommended) or a full JSON Schema object for complex validation.

nodes.label: ToolAnnotations behavioral hints
nodes.rationale: ToolAnnotations carries optional behavioral hints for a tool - title, readOnlyHint (default False), destructiveHint (default True), idempotentHint (default False), openWorldHint (default True) and maxResultSizeChars - and extends the MCP SDK's mcp.types.ToolAnnotations. camelCase and snake_case spellings are equivalent, snake_case and the typed maxResultSizeChars field require Python Agent SDK 0.2.140 or later, and clients should not rely on the hints for security decisions.

nodes.label: create_sdk_mcp_server()
nodes.rationale: create_sdk_mcp_server(name, version='1.0.0', tools) creates an in-process MCP server that runs inside the Python application and returns an McpSdkServerConfig that can be passed to ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers. Its tools are then addressed with names such as mcp__calc__add in allowed_tools.

nodes.label: SdkMcpTool dataclass
nodes.rationale: SdkMcpTool is the generic dataclass produced by the @tool decorator, holding name, description, input_schema (a type or JSON Schema dict), handler (an async callable returning a dict) and optional annotations.

nodes.label: list_sessions()
nodes.rationale: list_sessions(directory, limit, offset, include_worktrees=True) is a synchronous function that lists past sessions with metadata, filtered by project directory or across all projects when directory is omitted. Results are sorted by last_modified descending, offset supports pagination, and include_worktrees pulls in sessions from all worktree paths of a git repository.

nodes.label: SDKSessionInfo metadata record
nodes.rationale: SDKSessionInfo is the per-session metadata record returned by list_sessions() and get_session_info(): session_id, summary (custom title, auto-generated summary or first prompt), last_modified and created_at in epoch milliseconds, file_size (None for remote storage backends), custom_title, first_prompt, git_branch, cwd and tag.

nodes.label: get_session_messages()
nodes.rationale: get_session_messages(session_id, directory, limit, offset) synchronously retrieves the messages of a past session, searching all projects when directory is omitted, and returns a list of SessionMessage records.

nodes.label: SessionMessage record
nodes.rationale: SessionMessage carries type ('user' or 'assistant'), uuid, session_id, the raw message, parent_tool_use_id (the id of the spawning Agent tool-use block for subagent messages) and parent_agent_id (the parent subagent's agent id for nested subagents, requiring Python Agent SDK 0.2.140 or later); both parent fields are None for main-session messages and older sessions.

nodes.label: get_session_info()
nodes.rationale: get_session_info(session_id, directory) synchronously reads metadata for a single session by UUID without scanning the full project directory, returning an SDKSessionInfo or None when the session is not found.

nodes.label: rename_session()
nodes.rationale: rename_session(session_id, title, directory) renames a session by appending a custom-title entry; repeated calls are safe and the most recent title wins. It raises ValueError when session_id is not a valid UUID or the title is empty after stripping, and FileNotFoundError when the session cannot be found. The new title later appears in SDKSessionInfo.custom_title.

nodes.label: tag_session()
nodes.rationale: tag_session(session_id, tag, directory) tags a session, or clears the tag when tag is None; tags are Unicode-sanitized before storing, repeated calls are safe with the most recent tag winning, and the value is read back through SDKSessionInfo.tag. It raises ValueError on an invalid UUID or an empty sanitized tag and FileNotFoundError when the session is missing.

nodes.label: ClaudeSDKClient class
nodes.rationale: ClaudeSDKClient maintains one conversation session across multiple exchanges - the Python equivalent of how the TypeScript SDK's query() works internally. Its methods include connect, query, receive_messages, receive_response (messages up to and including a ResultMessage), interrupt, set_permission_mode, set_model, rewind_files, stop_task, get_server_info and disconnect, and it can be used as an async context manager for automatic connection management. The doc warns against using break while iterating messages because it can cause asyncio cleanup issues.

nodes.label: Runtime MCP server control on the client
nodes.rationale: ClaudeSDKClient exposes runtime MCP control: get_mcp_status() returns an McpStatusResponse for all configured servers, reconnect_mcp_server(name) retries a server that failed or disconnected, and toggle_mcp_server(name, enabled) enables or disables a server mid-session, with disabling removing its tools.

nodes.label: Interrupt buffer behavior
nodes.rationale: interrupt() sends a stop signal but does not clear the message buffer: messages already produced by the interrupted task, including its ResultMessage, remain in the stream and must be drained with receive_response() before reading a new query's response. An interrupted turn reports terminal_reason 'aborted_streaming' or 'aborted_tools'.

nodes.label: @dataclass versus TypedDict types
nodes.rationale: The SDK uses two kinds of types: @dataclass classes such as ResultMessage, AgentDefinition and TextBlock are object instances supporting attribute access (msg.result), while TypedDict classes such as ThinkingConfigEnabled, McpStdioServerConfig and SyncHookJSONOutput are plain dicts at runtime and require key access (config['budget_tokens']). The ClassName(field=value) call syntax works for both, but only dataclasses produce objects with attributes.

nodes.label: Transport abstract base class
nodes.rationale: Transport is an abstract base class for custom transport implementations that communicate with the Claude process over a custom channel such as a remote connection instead of a local subprocess. It declares connect, write, read_messages, close, is_ready and end_input. The doc warns it is a low-level internal API whose interface may change, so custom implementations must be updated to match.

nodes.label: ClaudeAgentOptions configuration dataclass
nodes.rationale: ClaudeAgentOptions is the configuration dataclass for Claude Code queries, carrying tools, prompts, MCP servers, permission behavior, session control, model choice, budgets, hooks, agents, skills, plugins, sandbox, thinking and session-store settings. Both query() and ClaudeSDKClient accept it.

nodes.label: Tool selection and gating options
nodes.rationale: tools selects the tool set (use {'type': 'preset', 'preset': 'claude_code'} for Claude Code's defaults); allowed_tools auto-approves tools without prompting but does not restrict Claude to only those tools; disallowed_tools denies tools, where a bare name such as 'Bash' removes the tool from Claude's context while a scoped rule such as 'Bash(rm *)' leaves the tool available and denies matching calls in every permission mode, including bypassPermissions.

nodes.label: Session continuation and forking options
nodes.rationale: continue_conversation resumes the most recent conversation, resume takes a session ID, session_id forces a specific UUID (not combinable with continue_conversation or resume unless fork_session is set), fork_session branches a resumed session into a new ID, resume_session_at loads the conversation only up to a given message UUID, and resume_drops_turn names the user prompt whose turn that truncation discards - with the CLI refusing the resume if the discarded range holds entries not attributable to that turn. The last two require Python Agent SDK 0.2.137 or later.

nodes.label: Turn, cost and token budget limits
nodes.rationale: max_turns caps agentic tool-use round trips, max_budget_usd stops the query when the client-side cost estimate reaches a USD value (compared against the same estimate as total_cost_usd), and task_budget sends an API-side token budget as output_config.task_budget with the task-budgets-2026-03-13 beta header.

nodes.label: Environment variables for slow or stalled API responses
nodes.rationale: The CLI subprocess reads timeout and stall-detection environment variables that are passed through ClaudeAgentOptions.env: API_TIMEOUT_MS (per-request timeout, default 600000), CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES (default 10, capped at 15, each retry getting its own timeout window), CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS (subagent stall watchdog, default 600000, applying only to run_in_background subagents) and CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG with CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS (default and minimum 300000), which aborts a request whose body stops streaming after headers arrived.

nodes.label: OutputFormat structured output configuration
nodes.rationale: output_format takes a dict of the shape {'type': 'json_schema', 'schema': {...}} where both fields are required; it configures structured output validation against the supplied JSON Schema.

nodes.label: SystemPromptPreset
nodes.rationale: SystemPromptPreset is a TypedDict with type='preset' and preset='claude_code' that uses Claude Code's own system prompt, optionally with append text. Its exclude_dynamic_sections flag moves per-session context such as the working directory, the git-repo flag and auto memory paths out of the system prompt and into the first user message, which improves prompt-cache reuse across users and machines.

nodes.label: SystemPromptFile
nodes.rationale: SystemPromptFile is a TypedDict with type='file' and path that loads a custom system prompt from disk, mapping to the CLI --system-prompt-file flag. It is the right form for a large prompt, because a string system_prompt is passed on the CLI subprocess argv and is therefore subject to an argv length limit.

nodes.label: SettingSource and setting_sources
nodes.rationale: SettingSource is Literal['user', 'project', 'local'], naming ~/.claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json. When setting_sources is omitted or None the SDK loads the same filesystem settings as the CLI (user, project and local); passing [] disables all three, and 'project' must be included to load CLAUDE.md project instructions. In Python SDK 0.1.59 and earlier an empty list was treated the same as omitting the option, so setting_sources=[] did not take effect.

nodes.label: Settings precedence order
nodes.rationale: When multiple sources are loaded, settings merge with local (.claude/settings.local.json) highest, then project (.claude/settings.json), then user (~/.claude/settings.json). Programmatic options such as agents and allowed_tools override all three filesystem sources, and managed policy settings take precedence over programmatic options.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition for programmatic subagents
nodes.rationale: AgentDefinition configures a subagent programmatically with required description and prompt plus optional tools, disallowedTools (accepting MCP server-level patterns such as mcp__server__* and mcp__*), model (an alias, 'inherit' or a full ID), skills preloaded at startup, memory source, mcpServers, initialPrompt, maxTurns, background, effort and permissionMode.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition uses camelCase field names
nodes.rationale: AgentDefinition field names use camelCase - disallowedTools, permissionMode, maxTurns - because they map directly to the wire format shared with the TypeScript SDK. This differs from ClaudeAgentOptions, which uses Python snake_case for the equivalent top-level fields such as disallowed_tools and permission_mode.

nodes.label: PermissionMode literal
nodes.rationale: PermissionMode is Literal['default', 'acceptEdits', 'plan', 'dontAsk', 'bypassPermissions', 'auto']: acceptEdits auto-accepts file edits, plan explores without editing, dontAsk denies anything not pre-approved instead of prompting, bypassPermissions skips permission checks while explicit ask rules still prompt, and auto lets a model classifier approve or deny permission prompts.

nodes.label: EffortLevel literal
nodes.rationale: EffortLevel is Literal['low', 'medium', 'high', 'xhigh', 'max'] guiding thinking depth, from minimal thinking with fastest responses to maximum effort; 'xhigh' falls back to 'high' on models that do not support it.

nodes.label: CanUseTool permission callback
nodes.rationale: CanUseTool is the async callback type Callable[[str, dict, ToolPermissionContext], Awaitable[PermissionResult]] and is the SDK replacement for the interactive permission prompt. It is invoked only when the permission evaluation flow resolves to a prompt - never for calls already approved by an allowed_tools entry, a settings allow rule, or the permission mode - and an allow rule does not pre-approve the actions no mode auto-approves.

nodes.label: ToolPermissionContext
nodes.rationale: ToolPermissionContext is the dataclass passed to a permission callback, carrying suggestions (permission updates from the CLI - Bash prompts include one with the localSettings destination, so returning it in updated_permissions writes the rule to .claude/settings.local.json and persists it), tool_use_id (always populated), agent_id (set only for subagent calls), blocked_path, decision_reason (forwarded from a PreToolUse hook's permissionDecisionReason when the hook returned 'ask'), title, display_name, description, and a reserved signal field.

nodes.label: PermissionResultAllow
nodes.rationale: PermissionResultAllow is the dataclass returned to allow a tool call, with behavior='allow', an optional updated_input dict that replaces the original tool input, and an optional updated_permissions list of PermissionUpdate objects to apply.

nodes.label: PermissionResultDeny
nodes.rationale: PermissionResultDeny is the dataclass returned to deny a tool call, with behavior='deny', a message explaining why the tool was denied, and interrupt (default False) controlling whether the current execution is interrupted.

nodes.label: PermissionUpdate
nodes.rationale: PermissionUpdate configures a programmatic permission change: type is one of addRules, replaceRules, removeRules, setMode, addDirectories or removeDirectories, with rules, behavior ('allow', 'deny' or 'ask'), mode, directories, and a destination of userSettings, projectSettings, localSettings or session.

nodes.label: PermissionRuleValue
nodes.rationale: PermissionRuleValue is the dataclass naming a single rule to add, replace or remove in a permission update: a tool_name plus optional rule_content.

nodes.label: ToolsPreset
nodes.rationale: ToolsPreset is a TypedDict with type='preset' and preset='claude_code' that selects Claude Code's default tool set for the tools option.

nodes.label: ThinkingConfig union
nodes.rationale: ThinkingConfig is a union of ThinkingConfigAdaptive (Claude decides when to think), ThinkingConfigEnabled (with an explicit budget_tokens) and ThinkingConfigDisabled, each optionally carrying display of 'summarized' or 'omitted'. On Claude Opus 4.7 and later the API default is 'omitted', so 'summarized' must be set to receive thinking content in ThinkingBlock outputs. It takes precedence over the deprecated max_thinking_tokens, and because these are TypedDicts they are plain dicts at runtime accessed with config['budget_tokens'].

nodes.label: TaskBudget
nodes.rationale: TaskBudget is a TypedDict with a single total field giving the API-side token budget for a task; it is passed as a plain dict, such as ClaudeAgentOptions(task_budget={'total': 50000}).

nodes.label: SdkBeta and the retired 1M-context beta
nodes.rationale: SdkBeta is Literal['context-1m-2025-08-07'], used with the betas field. That beta is retired as of April 30, 2026: passing the header with Claude Sonnet 4.5 or Sonnet 4 has no effect and requests exceeding the standard 200k-token context window return an error, so a 1M-token context window requires migrating to a newer model.

nodes.label: McpServerConfig transport variants
nodes.rationale: McpServerConfig is the union of McpStdioServerConfig (command with optional args and env, type optional for backwards compatibility), McpSSEServerConfig (type='sse', url, optional headers), McpHttpServerConfig (type='http', url, optional headers) and McpSdkServerConfig.

nodes.label: McpSdkServerConfig
nodes.rationale: McpSdkServerConfig is the TypedDict describing an in-process SDK MCP server created by create_sdk_mcp_server(): type='sdk', name, and the live server instance. Its serializable status form, McpSdkServerConfigStatus, keeps only type and name and omits the instance.

nodes.label: McpStatusResponse
nodes.rationale: McpStatusResponse is the return value of ClaudeSDKClient.get_mcp_status(), a TypedDict wrapping the list of server statuses under the mcpServers key.

nodes.label: McpServerStatus
nodes.rationale: McpServerStatus reports one connected MCP server with name, status ('connected', 'failed', 'needs-auth', 'pending' or 'disabled'), optional serverInfo (name and version), error, config (an McpServerStatusConfig, which adds an output-only claudeai-proxy variant for servers proxied through claude.ai), scope, and the tools the server provides with their name, description and annotations.

nodes.label: SdkPluginConfig
nodes.rationale: SdkPluginConfig is a TypedDict with type='local' (the only currently supported kind) and path, an absolute or relative path to a plugin directory; a list of them is passed as ClaudeAgentOptions.plugins.

nodes.label: Message union type
nodes.rationale: Message is the union of UserMessage, AssistantMessage, SystemMessage, ResultMessage, StreamEvent, RateLimitEvent and ConversationResetMessage - the values yielded by query() and by the client's receive_messages()/receive_response().

nodes.label: UserMessage
nodes.rationale: UserMessage carries content as text or a list of ContentBlock, uuid, parent_tool_use_id (set when the message is a tool result response), tool_use_result, and origin, which records provenance on injected turns such as task notifications and peer messages and is None when the CLI did not attribute it (requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.137 or later).

nodes.label: AssistantMessage
nodes.rationale: AssistantMessage carries a list of content blocks, the model that generated the response, parent_tool_use_id for nested responses, an optional error, per-message usage using the same keys as ResultMessage.usage, message_id (shared by multiple messages from one turn), stop_reason, session_id and uuid.

nodes.label: AssistantMessageError
nodes.rationale: AssistantMessageError is Literal['authentication_failed', 'billing_error', 'rate_limit', 'invalid_request', 'server_error', 'unknown']. The CLI can emit error types the literal does not list, such as max_output_tokens, and the SDK passes the value through unmodified, so strings outside the list should be treated like 'unknown'.

nodes.label: SystemMessage
nodes.rationale: SystemMessage is the dataclass carrying a subtype string and an arbitrary data dict of metadata; the init SystemMessage is where the session's tools list is reported.

nodes.label: ResultMessage
nodes.rationale: ResultMessage is the final message of a run, carrying subtype, duration_ms, duration_api_ms, is_error, num_turns, session_id, total_cost_usd, usage, result text, structured_output, model_usage, permission_denials, deferred_tool_use, errors, api_error_status, terminal_reason and origin. The subtype is one of 'success', 'error_during_execution', 'error_max_turns', 'error_max_budget_usd' or 'error_max_structured_output_retries', and the Python dataclass flattens all variants into one shape.

nodes.label: How a ResultMessage reports why the run ended
nodes.rationale: is_error is always True on the error_* subtypes and is also True on subtype='success' when the final model request failed; api_error_status holds the terminating API error's HTTP status and is populated only on subtype='success'; result holds the final assistant text on success (possibly empty when is_error is True); errors holds loop-level strings only on the error_* subtypes; terminal_reason says why the loop ended ('completed', 'max_turns', 'api_error', 'aborted_streaming', 'aborted_tools'), with the aborted values meaning the turn was cut short by an interrupt or a permission callback.

nodes.label: ResultMessage.usage token keys
nodes.rationale: The usage dict covers the main agent loop only and excludes subagent and other nested or auxiliary model calls, and in streaming input mode its values are per-turn. Its keys are input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens.

nodes.label: ModelUsage per-model accounting
nodes.rationale: model_usage maps model names to ModelUsage TypedDicts covering every model call made through the query pipeline - main loop, subagents and internal calls such as compaction and Workflow agents - while excluding helpers outside it such as the permission classifier and token-counting requests. Its camelCase keys include inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadInputTokens, cacheCreationInputTokens, webSearchRequests, costUSD (a client-side estimate), contextWindow, maxOutputTokens, canonicalModel and provider. In streaming input mode model_usage and total_cost_usd are cumulative across turns, so the latest result should be read rather than summed.

nodes.label: StreamEvent partial message updates
nodes.rationale: StreamEvent delivers raw Claude API stream events for partial message updates and is yielded only when include_partial_messages=True in ClaudeAgentOptions. It carries uuid, session_id and the raw event dict; its parent_tool_use_id is always None because stream events are emitted for the main session only, so subagent attribution must come from complete messages such as AssistantMessage.

nodes.label: RateLimitEvent
nodes.rationale: RateLimitEvent is emitted when rate limit status changes, for example from 'allowed' to 'allowed_warning', and carries a RateLimitInfo plus uuid and session_id. It is the signal to warn users before a hard limit or to back off when the status is 'rejected'.

nodes.label: RateLimitInfo
nodes.rationale: RateLimitInfo carries status ('allowed', 'allowed_warning' or 'rejected'), resets_at as a Unix timestamp, rate_limit_type (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_opus, seven_day_sonnet or overage), utilization as a fraction from 0.0 to 1.0, overage_status, overage_resets_at, overage_disabled_reason, and raw, the full dict from the CLI including fields not modeled.

nodes.label: ConversationResetMessage
nodes.rationale: ConversationResetMessage is emitted when the conversation is replaced without ending the connection, such as after /clear. Its new_conversation_id is an opaque identifier for the fresh conversation and is not the session_id of subsequent messages, which carry a new session_id. It requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.137 or later.

nodes.label: TaskStartedMessage
nodes.rationale: TaskStartedMessage is emitted when a background task starts - anything tracked outside the main turn: a backgrounded Bash command, a Monitor watch, a subagent spawned via the Agent tool, or a remote agent. It carries task_id, description, uuid, session_id, tool_use_id and task_type ('local_bash' for background Bash and Monitor watches, 'local_agent' or 'remote_agent').

nodes.label: TaskUsage
nodes.rationale: TaskUsage is a TypedDict of total_tokens, tool_uses and duration_ms giving the token and timing data for a background task.

nodes.label: TaskProgressMessage
nodes.rationale: TaskProgressMessage is emitted periodically for a running background task, carrying task_id, a current status description, cumulative TaskUsage, uuid, session_id, tool_use_id and last_tool_name.

nodes.label: TaskNotificationMessage
nodes.rationale: TaskNotificationMessage is emitted when a background task completes, fails or is stopped, carrying task_id, status ('completed', 'failed' or 'stopped'), output_file, summary, uuid, session_id, tool_use_id and final TaskUsage. Calling ClaudeSDKClient.stop_task() is followed by one of these with status 'stopped'.

nodes.label: ContentBlock variants
nodes.rationale: ContentBlock is the union of TextBlock (text), ThinkingBlock (thinking plus signature), ToolUseBlock (id, name, input) and ToolResultBlock (tool_use_id, optional content, optional is_error); these are the blocks that make up a message's content list.

nodes.label: ClaudeSDKError base exception
nodes.rationale: ClaudeSDKError is the base exception class for all SDK errors. When a single-shot query() ends with an error result, such as a turn-limit error, the SDK raises a ResultError after yielding the final result message; Python Agent SDK versions before 0.2.140 raised a plain Exception that was not a ClaudeSDKError subclass.

nodes.label: CLIConnectionError
nodes.rationale: CLIConnectionError is raised when the connection to Claude Code fails; it subclasses ClaudeSDKError.

nodes.label: CLINotFoundError
nodes.rationale: CLINotFoundError is raised when the Claude Code CLI is not installed or not found; it subclasses CLIConnectionError and takes an optional cli_path naming the path that was not found.

nodes.label: ProcessError
nodes.rationale: ProcessError is raised when the Claude Code process fails, carrying exit_code and stderr attributes.

nodes.label: ResultError
nodes.rationale: ResultError is raised after the final ResultMessage when the process exits because the run ended with an error result, such as a turn-limit or API error. It subclasses ProcessError and exposes subtype, errors, result, api_error_status, terminal_reason, session_id and the raw data payload. terminal_reason should be checked before subtype, because a failed final request is reported with subtype 'success' and the cause in terminal_reason, for example 'api_error'.

nodes.label: CLIJSONDecodeError
nodes.rationale: CLIJSONDecodeError is raised when JSON parsing of a CLI output line fails; it carries the offending line and the original_error exception.

nodes.label: HookEvent literal
nodes.rationale: HookEvent is Literal['PreToolUse', 'PostToolUse', 'PostToolUseFailure', 'UserPromptSubmit', 'Stop', 'SubagentStop', 'PreCompact', 'Notification', 'SubagentStart', 'PermissionRequest']. The TypeScript SDK supports additional hook events not yet available in Python.

nodes.label: HookCallback signature
nodes.rationale: HookCallback is Callable[[HookInput, str | None, HookContext], Awaitable[HookJSONOutput]]: it receives a strongly-typed hook input discriminated on hook_event_name, an optional tool_use_id for tool-related hooks, and a HookContext (a TypedDict whose only field, signal, is reserved for future abort-signal support).

nodes.label: HookMatcher
nodes.rationale: HookMatcher binds callbacks to an event: matcher is a tool name or pattern such as 'Bash' or 'Write|Edit' (None matches all tools), hooks is the list of callbacks, and timeout is in seconds - when omitted the per-event default applies, 600 seconds for most events and 30 for UserPromptSubmit.

nodes.label: HookInput union
nodes.rationale: HookInput is the union of PreToolUseHookInput, PostToolUseHookInput, PostToolUseFailureHookInput, UserPromptSubmitHookInput, StopHookInput, SubagentStopHookInput, PreCompactHookInput, NotificationHookInput, SubagentStartHookInput and PermissionRequestHookInput; the actual type is determined by the hook_event_name field.

nodes.label: BaseHookInput
nodes.rationale: BaseHookInput holds the fields present in every hook input: session_id, transcript_path (the path to the session transcript file), cwd, and an optional permission_mode.

nodes.label: PreToolUseHookInput
nodes.rationale: PreToolUseHookInput adds hook_event_name='PreToolUse', tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, and optional agent_id and agent_type that are present when the hook fires inside a subagent.

nodes.label: PostToolUseHookInput
nodes.rationale: PostToolUseHookInput adds hook_event_name='PostToolUse', tool_name, the tool_input that was used, tool_response, tool_use_id, and optional agent_id and agent_type for subagent invocations.

nodes.label: PostToolUseFailureHookInput
nodes.rationale: PostToolUseFailureHookInput fires when a tool execution fails, adding error text and an optional is_interrupt flag that is True when the failure reached Claude Code as an abort rather than as an error the tool reported. Cancelling a running tool with interrupt() does not fire this hook - the tool result carries the interruption message instead.

nodes.label: PermissionRequestHookInput
nodes.rationale: PermissionRequestHookInput fires when a permission decision is needed and lets hooks handle it programmatically, carrying tool_name, tool_input, optional permission_suggestions from the CLI, and optional agent_id and agent_type.

nodes.label: Lifecycle hook inputs
nodes.rationale: The remaining hook inputs cover session lifecycle: UserPromptSubmitHookInput (prompt), StopHookInput and SubagentStopHookInput (stop_hook_active, plus agent_id, agent_transcript_path and agent_type for subagents), PreCompactHookInput (trigger 'manual' or 'auto' and custom_instructions), NotificationHookInput (message, optional title, notification_type) and SubagentStartHookInput (agent_id, agent_type).

nodes.label: HookJSONOutput union
nodes.rationale: HookJSONOutput is the union of AsyncHookJSONOutput and SyncHookJSONOutput - the two shapes a hook callback may return.

nodes.label: SyncHookJSONOutput
nodes.rationale: SyncHookJSONOutput carries control fields continue_ (whether to proceed, default True), suppressOutput and stopReason; decision fields decision='block', systemMessage (a warning for the user) and reason (feedback for Claude); plus hookSpecificOutput. Python code writes continue_ with an underscore and the SDK converts it to continue when sending to the CLI.

nodes.label: HookSpecificOutput discriminated union
nodes.rationale: HookSpecificOutput is a discriminated union keyed on hookEventName. PreToolUse output can set permissionDecision ('allow', 'deny', 'ask' or 'defer'), permissionDecisionReason, updatedInput and additionalContext; PostToolUse can set additionalContext and updatedToolOutput (superseding the deprecated updatedMCPToolOutput, which worked only for MCP tools); PostToolUseFailure, UserPromptSubmit, Notification and SubagentStart can set additionalContext; and PermissionRequest returns a decision dict.

nodes.label: AsyncHookJSONOutput
nodes.rationale: AsyncHookJSONOutput defers hook execution: async_ set to True plus an optional asyncTimeout in milliseconds. Python code writes async_ with an underscore and the SDK converts it to async when sending to the CLI.

nodes.label: Hook usage example
nodes.rationale: The worked example registers two hooks on one options object: a PreToolUse HookMatcher scoped to Bash with a 120-second timeout that returns permissionDecision 'deny' for a command containing rm -rf /, and an unmatched HookMatcher that logs every tool use on both PreToolUse and PostToolUse using the per-event default timeout.

nodes.label: Built-in tool input/output schemas
nodes.rationale: The page documents the input and output schemas of every built-in Claude Code tool. The Python SDK does not export these as types; they describe the structure of tool inputs and outputs as they appear in messages, which is what hooks and permission handlers see.

nodes.label: Agent tool
nodes.rationale: The Agent tool (previously named Task, still accepted as an alias and still reported as Task in the init SystemMessage tools list) launches a new agent to handle complex multi-step tasks autonomously. Its input takes description, prompt, subagent_type, model, run_in_background (agents run in the background by default; set False for synchronous), name and isolation ('worktree' or 'remote'); team_name and mode are deprecated and ignored, with subagents inheriting the parent session's permission mode. Its output is discriminated on status - 'completed', 'async_launched' or 'remote_launched' - and on the completed variant usage and totalTokens come from the subagent's final API request, not the whole run.

nodes.label: AskUserQuestion tool
nodes.rationale: AskUserQuestion asks the user clarifying questions during execution: one to four questions, each with a question, a header of at most 12 characters, two to four options carrying label, description and optional preview, and a multiSelect flag. Its output returns the questions asked, an answers dict mapping question text to answer (multi-select answers comma-separated), an optional freeform response that replaces the answer list, per-question annotations holding preview and notes, and afkTimeoutMs when the dialog auto-resolved on user inactivity.

nodes.label: Bash tool
nodes.rationale: The Bash tool takes command, an optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000, with higher values clamped), a short description and run_in_background. Its output carries stdout - into which the command's stdout and stderr arrive merged as one interleaved stream - a stderr field holding notices the tool itself adds rather than the command's stderr, interrupted, isImage and backgroundTaskId.

nodes.label: Monitor tool
nodes.rationale: Monitor runs a background source and delivers each event to Claude so it can react without polling: a command script emits one event per stdout line, or a ws WebSocket source emits one event per text frame, and exactly one of the two must be provided. It takes description, timeout_ms (default 300000, max 3600000) and persistent, and returns taskId, timeoutMs (0 when persistent) and persistent. A command follows the same permission rules as Bash while a WebSocket watch prompts for approval separately, and the ws source requires Claude Code v2.1.195 or later.

nodes.label: Edit, Read and Write tools
nodes.rationale: Edit takes file_path, old_string, new_string and replace_all and returns the number of replacements; Read takes file_path with optional offset and limit and returns either text content with total_lines and lines_returned or, for images, base64 image data with mime_type and file_size; Write takes file_path and content and returns bytes_written.

nodes.label: Glob and Grep tools
nodes.rationale: Glob takes a pattern and optional path and returns matches, count and search_path. Grep takes a regular-expression pattern with optional path, glob, type, output_mode ('content', 'files_with_matches' or 'count'), the -i/-n/-B/-A/-C flags, head_limit and multiline, and returns either match objects with file, line_number, line and context arrays plus total_matches, or a files list with a count.

nodes.label: NotebookEdit tool
nodes.rationale: NotebookEdit takes notebook_path, cell_id, new_source, cell_type ('code' or 'markdown') and edit_mode ('replace', 'insert' or 'delete'), and returns the edit_type performed, the affected cell_id and the total cell count after the edit.

nodes.label: WebFetch and WebSearch tools
nodes.rationale: WebFetch takes a url and a prompt to run over the fetched content, returning bytes, HTTP code and codeText, the processed result, durationMs and the url. WebSearch takes a query with optional allowed_domains and blocked_domains and returns the query, the results and durationSeconds.

nodes.label: TodoWrite tool
nodes.rationale: TodoWrite takes a todos list of items with content, status ('pending', 'in_progress' or 'completed') and activeForm, and returns a message plus counts of total, pending, in_progress and completed items.

nodes.label: TaskCreate, TaskUpdate, TaskGet and TaskList tools
nodes.rationale: TaskCreate takes subject, description, activeForm and metadata and returns the created task id; TaskUpdate patches a task by taskId with status (including 'deleted'), subject, description, activeForm, addBlocks, addBlockedBy, owner and metadata, returning updatedFields and any statusChange; TaskGet reads one task by id, returning None when not found; TaskList returns every task with id, subject, status, owner and blockedBy.

nodes.label: Task-tracking tool model availability
nodes.rationale: On Python Agent SDK 0.2.139 and later, TodoWrite, TaskCreate, TaskGet, TaskUpdate and TaskList are not available on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5 or later versions of those families unless you opt in. On other models Claude Code provides the Task tools by default and TodoWrite only when CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=0 is set.

nodes.label: TaskOutput tool
nodes.rationale: TaskOutput (previously BashOutput, still accepted as an alias) takes task_id, block (default True) and timeout (default 30000 ms) and returns retrieval_status of 'success', 'timeout' or 'not_ready' plus the task details. It is deprecated in favour of reading the task's output file with Read, though its schema remains valid for hooks and permission handlers that encounter the tool.

nodes.label: TaskStop tool
nodes.rationale: TaskStop (previously KillShell and KillBash, both still accepted as aliases) takes a task_id - the deprecated shell_id is superseded - and returns a status message with the stopped task's id, task_type and command or description.

nodes.label: ExitPlanMode tool
nodes.rationale: ExitPlanMode takes a plan string to present to the user for approval and returns a confirmation message plus whether the user approved the plan.

nodes.label: ListMcpResources and ReadMcpResource tools
nodes.rationale: ListMcpResourcesTool takes an optional server filter and returns resources with uri, name, description, mimeType and server plus a total. ReadMcpResourceTool takes a server and a resource uri and returns the contents as entries of uri, mimeType, text and blob.

nodes.label: Continuous conversation interface example
nodes.rationale: The worked ConversationSession example keeps one connected ClaudeSDKClient across turns so Claude remembers earlier messages, exposing 'exit' to quit, 'interrupt' to call interrupt() on the current task, and 'new' to disconnect and reconnect for a fresh session with the previous context cleared.

nodes.label: Error handling example
nodes.rationale: The worked example wraps query() in handlers for CLINotFoundError, ResultError, ProcessError and CLIJSONDecodeError, catching ResultError before ProcessError because it subclasses it, and branching on terminal_reason first because a failed final request such as an API error arrives with subtype 'success'. Catching ResultError requires Python Agent SDK 0.2.140 or later.

nodes.label: SandboxSettings
nodes.rationale: SandboxSettings is a TypedDict configuring command sandboxing: enabled (default False), autoAllowBashIfSandboxed (default True), excludedCommands that always run unsandboxed without model involvement, allowUnsandboxedCommands (default True) letting the model request unsandboxed execution, network, ignoreViolations and enableWeakerNestedSandbox. The sandbox depends on platform support and, on Linux, tools such as bubblewrap and socat; by default a sandbox that cannot start falls back to running commands unsandboxed with a stderr warning, differing from the TypeScript SDK, and setting failIfUnavailable to True (undeclared on the TypedDict but forwarded to Claude Code) makes it stop with a ResultMessage of subtype 'error_during_execution' instead.

nodes.label: SandboxNetworkConfig
nodes.rationale: SandboxNetworkConfig governs network access for sandboxed Bash commands when the parent sandbox is enabled - it does not restrict the WebFetch tool, which uses permission rules instead. It carries allowedDomains, deniedDomains (taking precedence over allowedDomains), allowManagedDomainsOnly (effective only in managed settings), allowUnixSockets, allowAllUnixSockets, allowLocalBinding, allowMachLookup (macOS XPC/Mach names with a trailing wildcard), httpProxyPort and socksProxyPort. The built-in proxy enforces the allowlist on the requested hostname without terminating or inspecting TLS, so techniques such as domain fronting can potentially bypass it.

nodes.label: SandboxIgnoreViolations
nodes.rationale: SandboxIgnoreViolations is a TypedDict with file and network lists of patterns whose sandbox violations are ignored.

nodes.label: Permissions fallback for unsandboxed commands
nodes.rationale: When allowUnsandboxedCommands is enabled, the model can request execution outside the sandbox by setting dangerouslyDisableSandbox: True in the tool input; these requests fall back to the permissions system, so the can_use_tool handler is invoked and can apply custom authorization. The worked example also notes that a dummy PreToolUse hook is required to keep the stream open for can_use_tool. Commands running with dangerouslyDisableSandbox have full system access, and combining permission_mode='bypassPermissions' with unsandboxed commands lets the model execute them autonomously without approval prompts.

nodes.label: Unix socket sandbox-escape risk
nodes.rationale: Allowing Unix sockets can grant access to system services that reach outside the sandbox: allowing /var/run/docker.sock effectively grants full host system access through the Docker API, bypassing sandbox isolation, so only sockets that are genuinely needed should be allowed.

nodes.label: SDK subagent
nodes.rationale: Subagents are separate agent instances that a main agent spawns to handle focused subtasks. They exist to isolate context, run multiple analyses in parallel, and apply specialized instructions without adding to the main agent's prompt.

nodes.label: Three ways to create subagents
nodes.rationale: Subagents can be created programmatically via the `agents` parameter of `query()` options, as filesystem markdown files under `.claude/agents/`, or by relying on the built-in `general-purpose` subagent. The guide recommends the programmatic approach for SDK applications.

nodes.label: Programmatic definition (agents parameter)
nodes.rationale: Subagents are defined directly in code with the `agents` parameter of `ClaudeAgentOptions` / query options, mapping a name to an `AgentDefinition`. This is the recommended approach for SDK applications; Claude then invokes them through the Agent tool.

nodes.label: Filesystem-based definition (.claude/agents/)
nodes.rationale: Subagents can alternatively be defined as markdown files in `~/.claude/agents/` and `.claude/agents/` directories, documented under the Claude Code subagents reference.

nodes.label: Programmatic agents override same-named file agents
nodes.rationale: Programmatically defined agents take precedence over filesystem-based agents with the same name. An `agents` entry passed to `query()` therefore overrides a file-defined agent of that name, which is also a listed cause of a filesystem agent appearing not to load.

nodes.label: Built-in general-purpose subagent
nodes.rationale: When Claude calls the Agent tool without a `subagent_type`, it gets the built-in `general-purpose` subagent, which it can spawn at any time even when no agents are defined.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1
nodes.rationale: Setting `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_DISABLE_BUILTIN_AGENTS=1` removes the built-in default subagent, so an Agent tool call with no `subagent_type` fails with `subagent_type is required`.

nodes.label: Agent tool
nodes.rationale: Claude invokes subagents through the Agent tool; `Agent` must be in `allowedTools`/`allowed_tools` to auto-approve those invocations. The subagent's final message comes back as the Agent tool result.

nodes.label: Context isolation
nodes.rationale: Each subagent runs in its own conversation that starts fresh unless it is a fork; intermediate tool calls and results stay inside the subagent and only its final message returns to the parent. A research subagent can read dozens of files while the parent receives only a concise summary.

nodes.label: Parallelization
nodes.rationale: Multiple subagents can run concurrently, so independent subtasks finish in the time of the slowest one rather than the sum of all of them — for example running style-checker, security-scanner and test-coverage subagents simultaneously during a code review.

nodes.label: Specialized instructions and knowledge
nodes.rationale: Each subagent can carry a tailored system prompt with domain expertise, best practices and constraints — e.g. a database-migration subagent holding SQL rollback and data-integrity knowledge that would be noise in the main agent's instructions.

nodes.label: Tool restrictions
nodes.rationale: Subagents can be limited to specific tools, reducing the risk of unintended actions: omitting `tools` grants every tool available to subagents, while listing tools grants only those — a doc-reviewer restricted to Read and Grep can analyze but never modify files.

nodes.label: An omitted tool is absent, not denied
nodes.rationale: A tool left out of `tools` is not in the subagent's session at all: Claude simply works without it, producing no permission prompt and no error.

nodes.label: Common tool combinations
nodes.rationale: The doc tabulates four recipes: read-only analysis (Read, Grep, Glob), test execution (Bash, Read, Grep), code modification (Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob) and full access (omit the `tools` field to inherit every tool available to subagents).

nodes.label: AgentDefinition
nodes.rationale: `AgentDefinition` is the configuration object for a programmatic subagent. Only `description` and `prompt` are required; `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model`, `skills`, `memory`, `mcpServers`, `initialPrompt`, `maxTurns`, `background`, `effort` and `permissionMode` are optional.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.description
nodes.rationale: A required string giving a natural-language description of when to use this agent. Claude matches tasks to subagents from it, so clear specific descriptions are what make automatic invocation work.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.prompt
nodes.rationale: A required string holding the agent's system prompt, defining its role and behavior. It is one of the two things a non-fork subagent's context always contains.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.tools
nodes.rationale: Optional array of allowed tool names. If omitted, the agent inherits every tool available to subagents.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.disallowedTools
nodes.rationale: Optional array of tool names to remove from the agent's tool set. It also accepts MCP server-level patterns: `mcp__server` or `mcp__server__*` removes every tool from that server, and `mcp__*` removes every MCP tool from any server.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.model
nodes.rationale: Optional per-agent model override accepting an alias — `'fable'`, `'opus'`, `'sonnet'`, `'haiku'`, `'inherit'` — or a full model ID; `'inherit'` uses the main model. When omitted, Claude Code picks the model from the subagent model order.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.skills
nodes.rationale: Optional list of skill names preloaded into the agent's context at startup. Unlisted skills remain invocable through the Skill tool, and preloaded skill content is otherwise absent from a subagent's context.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.memory
nodes.rationale: Optional memory source for the agent, one of `'user'`, `'project'` or `'local'`.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.mcpServers
nodes.rationale: Optional array naming the MCP servers available to this agent, given either by name or as an inline config object.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.initialPrompt
nodes.rationale: Optional string auto-submitted as the first user turn when this agent runs as the main thread agent. It is ignored when the agent is invoked as a subagent.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.maxTurns
nodes.rationale: Optional cap on agentic turns before the agent stops. At the limit Claude Code returns the output marked as partial so Claude knows the run is unfinished, and the agent can be resumed to continue; the partial marking requires Claude Code v2.1.246 or later.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.background
nodes.rationale: Optional boolean forcing this agent to run as a non-blocking background task whenever it is invoked, regardless of what Claude requests in the Agent tool call.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.effort
nodes.rationale: Optional reasoning-effort level for this agent, one of `'low'`, `'medium'`, `'high'`, `'xhigh'`, `'max'`, or a number.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition.permissionMode
nodes.rationale: Optional `PermissionMode` governing permission handling for tool execution inside this agent.

nodes.label: camelCase field names in the Python SDK
nodes.rationale: In the Python SDK, multi-word `AgentDefinition` fields such as `disallowedTools` and `mcpServers` keep camelCase spelling to match the wire format instead of following Python's snake_case convention.

nodes.label: Subagents run in the background by default
nodes.rationale: An Agent tool call that omits the `run_in_background` input launches a background subagent; Claude sets `run_in_background: false` when it needs the result before continuing. Before Claude Code v2.1.198 this default was rolling out gradually, so an omitting call could run synchronously.

nodes.label: Subagents spawning subagents
nodes.rationale: Subagents can spawn subagents of their own, so a single prompt can grow into a tree of agents. Depth, concurrency and spend limits exist to bound how far that nesting goes.

nodes.label: What subagents inherit
nodes.rationale: A non-fork subagent's context starts fresh but is not empty: it receives its own system prompt plus the Agent tool's prompt, project CLAUDE.md loaded via `settingSources`, and tool definitions. It does not receive the parent's conversation history, tool results, or system prompt, nor preloaded skill content unless listed in `AgentDefinition.skills`.

nodes.label: The Agent tool prompt is the only parent-to-subagent channel
nodes.rationale: The only content passed from parent to subagent is the Agent tool's prompt string, so any file paths, error messages or decisions the subagent needs must be included directly in that prompt.

nodes.label: Fork the current conversation
nodes.rationale: A fork is the exception to the fresh-context rule: instead of starting empty it inherits the parent conversation. Because of that, a fork does not receive the automatically-added list of other named agents in the session.

nodes.label: SendMessage agent-name list
nodes.rationale: A subagent holding the `SendMessage` tool starts with a list of the other named agents running in the session, added by Claude Code to the subagent's first turn, so it knows which names it can address.

nodes.label: Extended thinking configuration is inherited
nodes.rationale: A subagent inherits the main session's extended thinking configuration, even though it does not inherit the parent's conversation or system prompt.

nodes.label: The parent may summarize the subagent's final message
