nodes.rationale: The parent receives the subagent's final message as the Agent tool result but may summarize it in its own response. Preserving subagent output verbatim requires an explicit instruction in the prompt or `systemPrompt` passed to the main `query()` call.

nodes.label: Subagent output scanning
nodes.rationale: In Claude Code v2.1.210 and later, the subagent's final message is scanned for instruction-shaped patterns before the parent reads it. The scan only annotates or escapes: it never removes or rewords the subagent's text.

nodes.label: Control-tag imitation neutralization
nodes.rationale: A tag only the harness emits, such as a `<system-reminder>` block, is neutralized in place: Claude Code inserts a backslash after the opening angle bracket and deletes nothing.

nodes.label: Permission-configuration mentions kept as written
nodes.rationale: References to permission configuration — `.claude/settings.json`, `bypassPermissions`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions` — are kept as written by the scan; only the `[harness: ...]` marker line is added.

nodes.label: Turn-marker escaping
nodes.rationale: A line starting with `Human:` or `Assistant:` gets a backslash before the colon so the message cannot imitate a conversation turn boundary. A turn-marker match adds no `[harness: ...]` marker line.

nodes.label: [harness: ...] marker line
nodes.rationale: For a control-tag or permission-configuration match, Claude Code prepends a `[harness: ...]` marker line naming the matched patterns, so the parent can see what the scan flagged.

nodes.label: An API error is never delivered as the subagent's result
nodes.rationale: An API error that ends a subagent early, such as a rate limit, is never delivered as its result; the foreground and background behavior is documented separately under API errors in subagents.

nodes.label: Automatic invocation
nodes.rationale: Claude decides on its own when to invoke a subagent by matching the task against each subagent's `description` — a `performance-optimizer` described as a query-tuning specialist is invoked when the prompt mentions optimizing queries.

nodes.label: Explicit invocation by name
nodes.rationale: Mentioning a subagent by name in the prompt ("Use the code-reviewer agent to check the authentication module") bypasses automatic matching and directly invokes that subagent.

nodes.label: Dynamic agent configuration
nodes.rationale: Agent definitions can be built at query time by a factory function driven by runtime conditions — the doc's example varies a security reviewer's prompt by strictness level and selects `opus` for strict reviews versus `sonnet` otherwise.

nodes.label: Detect subagent invocation
nodes.rationale: To confirm Claude delegated rather than answering directly, scan the streamed messages for `tool_use` blocks whose `name` is `"Agent"`, and treat messages carrying `parent_tool_use_id` as originating inside a subagent's execution context.

nodes.label: Agent vs Task tool naming
nodes.rationale: The tool appears as `"Agent"` in `tool_use` blocks but as `"Task"` in the `system:init` tools list, and before Claude Code v2.1.63 `tool_use` blocks also named it `"Task"`. Detection code should match both values in `block.name` to work across SDK versions.

nodes.label: parent_tool_use_id
nodes.rationale: Messages emitted from within a subagent's context carry a `parent_tool_use_id` field, which is how a consumer of the message stream tells subagent-internal messages from main-thread ones.

nodes.label: Message structure differs between Python and TypeScript
nodes.rationale: In Python, content blocks are accessed directly via `message.content`; in TypeScript, `SDKAssistantMessage` wraps the Claude API message so content is reached via `message.message.content`.

nodes.label: Resume subagents
nodes.rationale: A subagent can be resumed to continue where it left off rather than starting fresh, retaining its full conversation history including previous tool calls, results and reasoning. The procedure is: capture `session_id`, parse `agentId` from the Agent tool result, then re-query with `resume: sessionId` and the agent id named in the prompt.

nodes.label: agentId in the Agent tool result
nodes.rationale: When a subagent completes, the Agent tool result includes a text block containing `agentId: <id>`, which callers parse (e.g. with a regex over the result text) to identify the subagent they want to resume.

nodes.label: session_id and the resume option
nodes.rationale: Each `query()` call starts a new session by default, so the `session_id` captured from the first query's messages must be passed back as `resume` in the second query's options to reach the subagent's transcript. When using a custom agent, the same agent definition must be passed in `agents` for both queries.

nodes.label: Explore and Plan agents are one-shot
nodes.rationale: The built-in `Explore` and `Plan` agents are one-shot and return no `agentId`, so a custom agent or `general-purpose` must be used when resumption is required.

nodes.label: Subagent transcripts persist separately
nodes.rationale: Subagent transcripts are stored in separate files and persist independently of the main conversation; compaction behavior and the `cleanupPeriodDays` cleanup period are documented in the Claude Code subagents reference.

nodes.label: Cap subagent depth, concurrency, and spend
nodes.rationale: Claude decides on its own when and how many subagents to spawn, each subagent's API requests count toward the query's `total_cost_usd`, and subagents can nest — so growth is bounded three ways: spawn depth, concurrent count, and total spend.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH
nodes.rationale: The depth limit environment variable defaults to `3` layers of subagents below the main agent; `1` stops your subagents from spawning any of their own. At the limit a bottom-layer subagent simply cannot spawn and does its delegated work itself.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS
nodes.rationale: The concurrency limit environment variable defaults to `20` subagents at once, counting every subagent Claude spawns with the Agent tool. At the limit Claude Code refuses to spawn another and returns `Concurrent subagent limit reached` until the running count drops; sessions with ultracode active are never refused.

nodes.label: maxBudgetUsd / max_budget_usd
nodes.rationale: The spend cap is a query option (`maxBudgetUsd` in TypeScript, `max_budget_usd` in Python), unlimited by default and compared against `total_cost_usd` so subagent requests count. At the cap Claude Code refuses to spawn more subagents with `Budget limit reached`, stops still-running background subagents, and ends the query with the `error_max_budget_usd` result subtype.

nodes.label: env option differs between the two SDKs
nodes.rationale: The TypeScript SDK replaces the subprocess environment with the `env` option, so `process.env` must be spread into it to keep variables like `PATH`, while the Python SDK merges `env` into the inherited environment.

nodes.label: What you observe at each limit
nodes.rationale: Under the spend cap you see `success` and the estimated cost; at the spend cap you see `error_max_budget_usd` with a cost at or above the cap and then your error handler runs; at the concurrency limit a `tool_result` block carrying `Concurrent subagent limit reached` appears in the message stream and Claude receives the same block as the Agent tool result.

nodes.label: SDK version floor for the limits
nodes.rationale: The depth, concurrency and spend limits as described require TypeScript SDK v0.3.219 or Python SDK v0.2.127 and later — the releases bundling Claude Code v2.1.219 or later. On earlier releases some limits are missing or default differently, so upgrade before relying on them to bound a run.

nodes.label: Running Opus 5 with subagents
nodes.rationale: Claude Opus 5 delegates to subagents more readily than earlier models, so the depth, concurrency and spend limits matter most on Opus 5 queries. Prompt-level delegation instructions only steer Claude, so the limits must be set as well — Claude Code enforces them however Claude decides to delegate.

nodes.label: claude_code preset adds an Opus 5 delegation line
nodes.rationale: With the `claude_code` system-prompt preset and an Opus 5 model, Claude Code adds a line telling Claude not to call the Agent tool unless asked, while the tool stays available. With a custom prompt or no `systemPrompt` Claude Code does not build its system prompt, so that line is absent and the delegation instruction must be added by hand.

nodes.label: Workflow tool for large-scale orchestration
nodes.rationale: Subagents suit a few delegated tasks per turn; runs coordinating dozens to hundreds of agents should use the `Workflow` tool, which moves orchestration into a script the runtime executes outside the conversation context. It is available in the TypeScript Agent SDK v0.3.149 and later, and `Workflow` must be in `allowedTools` to auto-approve workflow runs.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting: Claude not delegating
nodes.rationale: When Claude completes tasks directly instead of delegating, the two remedies are explicit prompting (name the subagent in the prompt) and writing a clearer `description` that says exactly when the subagent should be used.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting: filesystem agents not loading
nodes.rationale: Claude Code watches `~/.claude/agents/` and `.claude/agents/` and picks up new or edited files within seconds. Listed causes for a definition never appearing: a newly created agents directory, invalid frontmatter or a duplicate `name`, `--disable-slash-commands`, a file under an added (`--add-dir`) directory, or a programmatic agent with the same name.

nodes.label: The watcher covers only pre-existing directories
nodes.rationale: The agent-file watcher covers only directories that existed when the session started, so the first file in a newly created `agents` directory needs a session restart. The doc calls this the most common cause of a filesystem agent not loading.

nodes.label: @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk package
nodes.rationale: The TypeScript Agent SDK is installed as `npm install @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` and is the complete API surface for driving Claude Code programmatically: functions, option types, message types, hook types, tool input/output schemas, permission types and sandbox configuration.

nodes.label: Bundled native Claude Code binary
nodes.rationale: The SDK ships a native Claude Code binary for the host platform as an optional npm dependency such as `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64`, so most installs need no separate Claude Code install. The SDK version tracks the bundled Claude Code version — SDK v0.3.191 bundles Claude Code v2.1.191 — so a feature needing a given Claude Code version needs the SDK release with the same patch number or later.

nodes.label: Native CLI binary not found fallback
nodes.rationale: If a package manager skips optional dependencies the SDK throws `Native CLI binary for <platform>-<arch> not found`; the documented remedy is to set `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable` to a separately installed `claude` binary. Package managers that ignore npm's `libc` field, such as Yarn 1.x, install both the glibc and musl Linux packages, roughly doubling install size; from Agent SDK v0.2.141 the SDK still launches the correct variant.

nodes.label: Compile to a single executable with extractFromBunfs
nodes.rationale: Compiling an app with `bun build --compile` breaks the SDK's runtime resolution of the bundled CLI, because `require.resolve` does not work inside the compiled executable's `$bunfs` virtual filesystem. The fix is to embed the platform binary as a file asset, call `extractFromBunfs()` (requires SDK v0.3.144+) to copy it to a real per-user temp path, and pass that path to `pathToClaudeCodeExecutable`; outside a compiled executable the helper returns its input unchanged.

nodes.label: query() function
nodes.rationale: `query({prompt, options})` is the primary entry point: it takes a string prompt or an `AsyncIterable<SDKUserMessage>` for streaming mode plus an optional `Options` object, and returns a `Query` object that extends `AsyncGenerator<SDKMessage, void>`, streaming messages as they arrive.

nodes.label: startup() pre-warming function
nodes.rationale: `startup({options, initializeTimeoutMs})` pre-warms the CLI subprocess by spawning it and completing the initialize handshake before a prompt exists, returning a `Promise<WarmQuery>`. `initializeTimeoutMs` defaults to 60000 and the promise rejects on timeout; calling it at application boot moves subprocess spawn and initialization out of the critical path.

nodes.label: WarmQuery handle
nodes.rationale: `WarmQuery` is the handle `startup()` returns: `query(prompt)` sends a prompt to the already-ready subprocess and returns a `Query`, and can only be called once per handle; `close()` discards the warm subprocess without sending a prompt. It implements `AsyncDisposable`, so `await using` cleans it up automatically.

nodes.label: tool() type-safe MCP tool definition
nodes.rationale: `tool(name, description, inputSchema, handler, extras)` creates a type-safe MCP tool definition for SDK MCP servers. The input schema is a Zod raw shape (Zod 3 and Zod 4 both supported), the handler returns a `CallToolResult`, and `extras` carries `annotations`, a one-line `searchHint` shown in the deferred-tool list when tool search is active, and `alwaysLoad: true` to keep the tool's full schema in the initial prompt instead of deferring it.

nodes.label: ToolAnnotations behavioral hints
nodes.rationale: `ToolAnnotations`, re-exported from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js`, carries optional MCP behavioral hints — `title`, `readOnlyHint` (default false), `destructiveHint` (default true), `idempotentHint` (default false) and `openWorldHint` (default true). The doc states explicitly that clients should not rely on them for security decisions.

nodes.label: createSdkMcpServer() in-process MCP server
nodes.rationale: `createSdkMcpServer({name, version, instructions, tools, alwaysLoad, timeout})` creates an MCP server instance that runs in the same process as the application. `instructions` is returned from `initialize` and surfaced to the model as an MCP instructions block; `alwaysLoad` keeps every tool of the server out of tool-search deferral; `timeout` (whole milliseconds, minimum 1000, SDK v0.3.248+) replaces `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` for that server.

nodes.label: listSessions() session discovery
nodes.rationale: `listSessions(options)` discovers past sessions with light metadata, filtered by `dir` (omit to search all projects), capped by `limit`, and including sibling git worktree paths by default via `includeWorktrees`. Results are sorted by `lastModified` descending, so the first item is the newest.

nodes.label: SDKSessionInfo metadata record
nodes.rationale: `SDKSessionInfo` is the per-session metadata record: `sessionId`, a `summary` display title (custom title, auto-generated summary, or first prompt), `lastModified` and `createdAt` epoch milliseconds, `fileSize` (populated only for local JSONL storage), `customTitle`, `firstPrompt`, `gitBranch`, `cwd` and `tag`.

nodes.label: getSessionMessages() and SessionMessage
nodes.rationale: `getSessionMessages(sessionId, options)` reads user and assistant messages from a past session transcript with `dir`, `limit` and `offset`. Each `SessionMessage` carries `type`, `uuid`, `session_id`, the raw `message` payload, `parent_tool_use_id` naming the spawning Agent tool call for subagent messages, and `parent_agent_id` naming the spawning subagent for nested subagents (Claude Code v2.1.202+).

nodes.label: getSessionInfo() single-session lookup
nodes.rationale: `getSessionInfo(sessionId, options)` reads metadata for one session by ID without scanning the full project directory, returning an `SDKSessionInfo` or `undefined` when the session is not found.

nodes.label: renameSession() and tagSession()
nodes.rationale: `renameSession(sessionId, title, options)` renames a session by appending a custom-title entry, and `tagSession(sessionId, tag, options)` tags one, with `null` clearing the tag. Both are safe to call repeatedly: the most recent title or tag wins. Titles must be non-empty after trimming whitespace.

nodes.label: resolveSettings() offline settings snapshot
nodes.rationale: `resolveSettings(options)` (alpha) resolves the effective Claude Code settings for a directory using the same merge engine as the CLI without spawning the CLI, so you can inspect what configuration a `query()` call would see. The snapshot deliberately differs from a live session: it reads MDM sources but never executes a `policyHelper` subprocess, it fetches no server-managed settings unless you pass them, and it returns `permissions.defaultMode` as-is even where a live session would ignore `auto` from project and local tiers.

nodes.label: ResolvedSettings return shape
nodes.rationale: `ResolvedSettings` describes the merged configuration and where each key came from: `effective` is the merged `Settings` after applying every enabled source in precedence order, `provenance` maps each top-level key to the source that supplied it, and `sources` lists per-source raw settings ordered from lowest to highest precedence.

nodes.label: Options configuration object
nodes.rationale: `Options` is the configuration object for `query()`, spanning execution control (`abortController`, `cwd`, `env`, `executable`, `maxTurns`, `maxBudgetUsd`), model and reasoning (`model`, `fallbackModel`, `effort`, `thinking`), context and prompt shaping (`systemPrompt`, `settingSources`, `settings`, `additionalDirectories`), extension points (`agents`, `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `plugins`, `skills`, `toolAliases`, `toolConfig`), permissions (`allowedTools`, `disallowedTools`, `permissionMode`, `canUseTool`, `allowDangerouslySkipPermissions`), session lifecycle (`resume`, `continue`, `forkSession`, `sessionId`, `persistSession`, `sessionStore`) and observability (`includePartialMessages`, `includeHookEvents`, `stderr`, `debug`).

nodes.label: env option replaces rather than merges
nodes.rationale: Setting the `env` option replaces the subprocess environment instead of merging with `process.env`, so a caller must pass `{ ...process.env, YOUR_VAR: 'value' }` to keep inherited variables such as `PATH`. `CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_CLIENT_APP` identifies the calling app in the User-Agent header.

nodes.label: API timeout and stall-watchdog environment variables
nodes.rationale: The CLI subprocess reads timeout and stall-detection env vars passed through the `env` option: `API_TIMEOUT_MS` (per-request timeout, default 600000, applies to the main loop and all subagents), `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_RETRIES` (default 10, capped at 15, each retry getting its own timeout window), `CLAUDE_ASYNC_AGENT_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 600000, a watchdog for `run_in_background` subagents that aborts and fails the task on stall), and `CLAUDE_ENABLE_STREAM_WATCHDOG` with `CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` (default and minimum 300000) which aborts a request whose body stops streaming after headers arrive.

nodes.label: allowedTools and disallowedTools semantics
nodes.rationale: `allowedTools` auto-approves tools without prompting but does NOT restrict Claude to only those tools — unlisted tools fall through to `permissionMode` and `canUseTool`. `disallowedTools` is the blocking mechanism, and its two forms differ: a bare name such as `"Bash"` removes the tool from Claude's context, while a scoped rule such as `"Bash(rm *)"` leaves the tool available and denies matching calls in every permission mode, including `bypassPermissions`.

nodes.label: systemPrompt configuration and caching
nodes.rationale: `systemPrompt` accepts a custom string, an array of strings with the exported `SYSTEM_PROMPT_DYNAMIC_BOUNDARY` constant separating static from per-request parts to cache the static half, or the preset object `{ type: 'preset', preset: 'claude_code' }`. The preset form takes `append` to extend it and `excludeDynamicSections: true` to move per-session context into the first user message for better prompt-cache reuse across machines. `outputStyle` is deliberately NOT an Options field: it is set in the inline `settings` object or a settings file.

nodes.label: Query object and its control methods
nodes.rationale: The `Query` object extends `AsyncGenerator<SDKMessage, void>` with control methods: `interrupt()`, `rewindFiles()`, `setPermissionMode()`, `setModel()`, `applyFlagSettings()`, `initializationResult()`, `reinitialize()`, `supportedCommands()`, `supportedModels()`, `supportedAgents()`, `mcpServerStatus()`, `getContextUsage()`, `readFile()`, `reloadSkills()`, `accountInfo()`, `reconnectMcpServer()`, `toggleMcpServer()`, `setMcpServers()`, `streamInput()`, `stopTask()` and `close()`. Several — `interrupt`, `setPermissionMode`, `setModel`, `applyFlagSettings` — are available only in streaming input mode.

nodes.label: reinitialize() and permission-request redelivery
nodes.rationale: `reinitialize()` re-sends the `initialize` control request to the running CLI and returns a fresh result rather than the cached first-connect one. Its purpose is recovery after a transport gap: pending permission requests reach the `canUseTool` callback again, so the callback must be idempotent per request ID because a request whose response was lost is dispatched a second time. Requires Claude Code v2.1.195 or later.

nodes.label: applyFlagSettings() runtime settings changes
nodes.rationale: `applyFlagSettings()` merges settings into a running session's flag-settings layer without restarting the query — the same layer `query()`'s inline `settings` option populates. Only some keys take effect mid-session: `effortLevel`, `ultracode`, `permissions`, `hooks`, `skillOverrides`, `fastMode` and `agent` apply on the next turn; `model` applies during the current turn from the next model call onward (v2.1.212+); system prompt options have no mid-session effect at all even though the call succeeds. Successive calls shallow-merge top-level keys, `null` clears a key back to lower-precedence sources, and `undefined` is dropped by JSON serialization. TypeScript-only — the Python SDK has no equivalent.

nodes.label: readFile() session filesystem read
nodes.rationale: `readFile(path, options)` reads a file from the session's filesystem, resolving the path against `cwd` and applying the same read-permission rules as the Read tool. `maxBytes` changes the read cap (default 1 MB, ceiling 10 MB) and `encoding: 'base64'` handles binary files. It resolves with an `SDKControlReadFileResponse` or `null` on permission denial, a missing file, or a transport error. Requires TypeScript SDK v0.2.121 or later.

nodes.label: SDKControlInitializeResponse
nodes.rationale: `SDKControlInitializeResponse` is what `initializationResult()` returns: `commands`, `agents`, `output_style`, `available_output_styles`, `models`, `account`, `fast_mode_state`, `fast_mode_disabled_reason` and `hooks_applied`. `hooks_applied` (SDK v0.3.238+) is `true` when Claude Code registered the request's hooks — a session's first initialize, or a repeated one over the CLI's stdin, which replaces earlier hooks — and `false` for a repeated initialize sent to a remote session, so a second client cannot replace the first client's hooks. The control-response wrapper may also carry `pending_permission_requests`, an array of complete `control_request` messages awaiting a reply that the SDK dispatches to `canUseTool`.

nodes.label: SDKControlInterruptResponse interrupt receipt
nodes.rationale: The interrupt receipt lists which queued user messages survive an interrupt. `still_queued` names the UUIDs Claude Code will still process unless cancelled, so resending one of them delivers it to Claude twice; the list covers only messages enqueued with a UUID and only main-thread messages, and can include UUIDs the client never sent such as scheduled-task triggers. A direct control-protocol client can set `cancel_queued: true` (capability `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1`, Claude Code v2.1.219+), which moves those messages to `cancelled` and runs none of them. The receipt is a snapshot taken when the interrupt is processed and arrives before the interrupted turn's result, which is why it must be read instead of inspecting the queue afterward.

nodes.label: SDKControlGetContextUsageResponse
nodes.rationale: The return type of `getContextUsage()` is the same payload Claude Code renders for `/context`, so it carries display fields (`color`, `gridRows`) alongside token counts. Attribution is read from the collection fields: `categories` for per-category totals, `mcpTools` and `agents` for individual MCP tools and subagents, `memoryFiles` for each loaded memory file, and `skills.skillFrontmatter` for each included skill. `totalTokens` is measured against `maxTokens`, the model's context window or the lower auto-compaction window; the optional `deferredBuiltinTools`, `systemTools` and `systemPromptSections` diagnostics are left unset in practice.

nodes.label: SDKControlReadFileResponse
nodes.rationale: The return type of `readFile()` carries `contents` (file text, or base64 data when `encoding: 'base64'` was requested), the resolved `absPath`, an optional `encoding` field set to `'base64'` in that case, and `truncated` when the file exceeded the `maxBytes` cap and was cut at that limit.

nodes.label: SDKControlReloadSkillsResponse
nodes.rationale: The return type of `reloadSkills()` carries a `skills` array listing the skills available after the reload, in the same `SlashCommand` shape `supportedCommands()` returns. `reloadSkills()` itself makes skills added or edited mid-session available to the running session and requires Agent SDK v0.3.163 or later.

nodes.label: AgentDefinition programmatic subagent
nodes.rationale: `AgentDefinition` configures a subagent programmatically: required `description` and `prompt`, plus optional `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `model`, `mcpServers`, `skills`, `initialPrompt`, `maxTurns`, `background`, `memory`, `effort`, `permissionMode` and the experimental `criticalSystemReminder_EXPERIMENTAL`. Omitting `tools` inherits every tool available to subagents; `disallowedTools` also accepts MCP server-level patterns (`mcp__server`, `mcp__server__*`, `mcp__*`); `model` accepts an alias such as `'fable'`, `'opus'`, `'sonnet'`, `'haiku'`, `'inherit'`, or a full model ID.

nodes.label: AgentMcpServerSpec
nodes.rationale: `AgentMcpServerSpec` names the MCP servers available to a subagent: either a string referencing a server from the parent's `mcpServers` config, or an inline record mapping server names to process-transport configs (`McpStdioServerConfig | McpSSEServerConfig | McpHttpServerConfig | McpSdkServerConfig`).

nodes.label: SettingSource filesystem tiers
nodes.rationale: `SettingSource` is `"user" | "project" | "local"`, mapping to `~/.claude/settings.json`, `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json`. When `settingSources` is omitted, `query()` loads the same filesystem settings as the CLI; passing `[]` disables user, project and local settings entirely. Loading CLAUDE.md project instructions requires including `"project"`.

nodes.label: Settings precedence order
nodes.rationale: Loaded sources merge highest-to-lowest as local, then project, then user settings. Programmatic options such as `agents`, `allowedTools` and `settings` override all three filesystem tiers, and managed policy settings take precedence over programmatic options. Endpoint-managed policy loads regardless of `settingSources`.

nodes.label: PermissionMode values
nodes.rationale: `PermissionMode` is one of `default` (standard behavior), `acceptEdits` (auto-accept file edits), `bypassPermissions` (bypass checks, though explicit ask rules still prompt), `plan` (explore without editing), `dontAsk` (never prompt, deny anything not pre-approved) and `auto` (a model classifier approves or denies permission prompts).

nodes.label: CanUseTool callback
nodes.rationale: `CanUseTool` is the SDK's replacement for the interactive permission prompt and is invoked ONLY when the permission evaluation flow resolves to a prompt — never for calls already approved by `allowedTools`, a settings allow rule, or a permission mode such as `acceptEdits` or `bypassPermissions`. To gate every tool call a `PreToolUse` hook is required instead. Its options carry `signal`, `suggestions`, `blockedPath`, `decisionReason`, `toolUseID`, `agentID` and `requestId`. Returning `null` is legal only when the application already sent the `control_response` itself echoing `requestId`; in any other case `null` leaves the tool call blocked indefinitely because permission prompts never time out.

nodes.label: PermissionResult
nodes.rationale: `PermissionResult` is the discriminated answer a permission check returns: an `allow` arm carrying optional `updatedInput`, `updatedPermissions` and `toolUseID`, or a `deny` arm carrying a required `message` plus optional `interrupt` and `toolUseID`.

nodes.label: ToolConfig built-in tool behavior
nodes.rationale: `ToolConfig` configures built-in tool behavior. Its only member is `askUserQuestion.previewFormat` (`'markdown' | 'html'`), which opts into the `preview` field on `AskUserQuestion` options and sets its content format; when unset, Claude emits no previews.

nodes.label: McpServerConfig transports
nodes.rationale: `McpServerConfig` is the union of MCP server transports: `McpStdioServerConfig` (`command`, `args`, `env`), `McpSSEServerConfig` (`type: "sse"`, `url`, `headers`), `McpHttpServerConfig` (`type: "http"`, `url`, `headers`), `McpSdkServerConfigWithInstance` (`type: "sdk"`, `name`, `timeout`, in-process `instance`) and, for status reporting, `McpClaudeAIProxyServerConfig` (`type: "claudeai-proxy"`, `url`, `id`).

nodes.label: strictMcpConfig isolation
nodes.rationale: `strictMcpConfig` makes the session use only the servers passed in `mcpServers`, ignoring project `.mcp.json`, user settings, plugin-provided MCP servers and claude.ai connectors.

nodes.label: SdkPluginConfig local plugin loading
nodes.rationale: `SdkPluginConfig` loads a plugin from a local path: `type` must be `'local'`, `path` is an absolute or relative plugin directory, and `skipMcpDiscovery: true` loads the plugin's skills, hooks, agents and commands while ignoring its `.mcp.json` and manifest `mcpServers` — set it when the application owns the plugin's MCP connections.

nodes.label: SDKMessage union
nodes.rationale: `SDKMessage` is the union of every message a query streams, spanning assistant/user/result/system messages, partial stream events, compaction boundaries, hook lifecycle events, task lifecycle events, tool progress, auth status, rate-limit events, permission denials, prompt suggestions, informational banners and conversation resets.

nodes.label: SDKAssistantMessage
nodes.rationale: `SDKAssistantMessage` carries a `BetaMessage` from the Anthropic SDK plus `parent_tool_use_id`, an optional `error` from a closed set (`authentication_failed`, `rate_limit`, `overloaded` for a 529 versus `rate_limit` for a 429, `model_not_found`, `max_output_tokens`, and others), `aborted: true` when an interrupt truncated the message mid-stream (SDK v0.3.214+), a display-only `timestamp` from the producing machine's clock that must not be used for ordering, and `context_usage` when the message delivers a `/context` result.

nodes.label: SDKUserMessage
nodes.rationale: `SDKUserMessage` is user input, carrying `message`, `parent_tool_use_id`, optional `uuid`/`session_id`, `isSynthetic`, `shouldQuery`, `tool_use_result` and `origin`. Setting `shouldQuery: false` appends the message to the transcript without triggering an assistant turn, holding it to merge into the next turn-triggering message — the way to inject out-of-band context without spending a model call. `tool_use_result` is the tool's structured output object rather than the text sent to the model, typed `unknown` because its shape depends on the tool.

nodes.label: SDKUserMessageReplay
nodes.rationale: `SDKUserMessageReplay` is a user message with a required `uuid` and `isReplay: true`. A user turn injected from outside the session — one whose `origin` kind is `peer` or `channel` — reaches the stream as a replay whether it arrived during an active turn or started a new one while idle. Before v2.1.207 an injected turn delivered while idle produced no stream message at all and only appeared on re-reading the transcript.

nodes.label: SDKResultMessage
nodes.rationale: `SDKResultMessage` is the final message of a turn, discriminated on `subtype`: a `success` arm, and an error arm covering `error_max_turns`, `error_during_execution`, `error_max_budget_usd` and `error_max_structured_output_retries`. It carries timing (`duration_ms`, `duration_api_ms`, `ttft_ms`, `ttft_stream_ms`, `request_sent_wall_ms`), accounting (`usage`, `modelUsage`, `total_cost_usd`), `permission_denials`, `stop_reason`, `terminal_reason`, fast-mode state, `structured_output`, `deferred_tool_use` and `origin`. `usage` covers the main agent loop only, so `modelUsage` is the field to use for token and cost accounting across subagents and internal calls.

nodes.label: terminal_reason loop-exit codes
nodes.rationale: `terminal_reason` on a result names why the loop ended, from a closed set: `completed`, `max_turns`, `tool_deferred`, `aborted_streaming`, `aborted_tools`, `hook_stopped`, `stop_hook_prevented`, `background_requested`, `blocking_limit`, `rapid_refill_breaker`, `prompt_too_long`, `image_error`, `model_error`, `api_error`, `malformed_tool_use_exhausted`, `budget_exhausted`, `structured_output_retry_exhausted`, `tool_deferred_unavailable` and `turn_setup_failed`.

nodes.label: fast_mode_disabled_reason codes
nodes.rationale: When fast mode is unavailable, `fast_mode_disabled_reason` names the check that blocked it: `free`, `preference`, `extra_usage_disabled`, `network_error`, `unknown`, `not_first_party`, `disabled_by_env`, `model_not_allowed`, `sdk_opt_in_required` and `pending`. The doc's guidance is to render the reason code rather than re-derive availability. During the cooldown after a fast-mode rate limit, `fast_mode_state` is `"cooldown"` with no reason code. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.

nodes.label: user_message_uuid echo contract
nodes.rationale: Claude Code echoes `user_message_uuid` only when the caller set `uuid` on the triggering `SDKUserMessage` — a string prompt passed to `query()` carries none. It appears on the success result with `is_error` false (SDK v0.3.216+), on an error result answering a sent message (v0.3.246+), and on exactly one frame of the turn's first reply (v0.3.246+), so a reply can be bound before the result arrives. It is omitted on later frames of the same turn, subagent frames, synthetic turns and results with no single triggering message.

nodes.label: queued_turn_count
nodes.rationale: `queued_turn_count` (SDK v0.3.242+) counts the messages sent with `origin: { kind: "human" }` still waiting in the command queue when the result was produced. A `0` does not mean no turn follows, because messages sent without that origin and task notifications are not counted; an absent field marks the final result Claude Code emits after a crash or fatal startup error, which may also carry zeroed totals.

nodes.label: SDKSystemMessage init message
nodes.rationale: The `system`/`init` message reports the session's starting state: `agents`, `apiKeySource`, `betas`, `claude_code_version`, `cwd`, `tools`, `mcp_servers`, `model`, `permissionMode`, `slash_commands`, `terminal_slash_commands`, `output_style`, `skills`, `plugins`, fast-mode fields, `effort` and `capabilities`. `terminal_slash_commands` (SDK v0.3.229+) names entries whose interface is bound to the local terminal so a remote or mobile client can hide them; `effort` is set only on the init message sent to Remote Control clients.

nodes.label: capabilities array for feature detection
nodes.rationale: The `capabilities` array on the init message names the protocol behaviors the running CLI implements, so a client can feature-detect instead of comparing `claude_code_version` strings. It is an open set — unrecognized values must be ignored and the specific capability relied on must be checked. Documented members are `interrupt_receipt_v1` and `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1`. Requires Claude Code v2.1.205 or later and is absent on earlier CLIs.

nodes.label: SDKPartialAssistantMessage stream events
nodes.rationale: `SDKPartialAssistantMessage` (`type: "stream_event"`) is emitted only when `includePartialMessages` is true and wraps a `BetaRawMessageStreamEvent`. Its `parent_tool_use_id` is always `null` because stream events are emitted for the main session only; subagent attribution must come from complete messages or from enabling `forwardSubagentText`.

nodes.label: SDKCompactBoundaryMessage
nodes.rationale: `SDKCompactBoundaryMessage` marks a conversation compaction boundary, carrying `compact_metadata` with the `trigger` (`"manual"` or `"auto"`) and `pre_tokens`, the token count before compaction.

nodes.label: SDKInformationalMessage
nodes.rationale: `SDKInformationalMessage` is a generic text banner from the loop carrying non-error status lines, hook feedback such as a `UserPromptSubmit` block reason, and command output, rendered as plaintext at a `level` of `info`, `notice`, `suggestion` or `warning`. On Claude Code v2.1.227+ a hook's `systemMessage` can arrive as this message with each line prefixed by the hook's name.

nodes.label: SDKWorkerShuttingDownMessage
nodes.rationale: Emitted on graceful worker teardown so remote clients can show why the worker exited instead of waiting for a heartbeat timeout, carrying a short snake_case `reason` such as `"host_exit"` or `"remote_control_disabled"`. It must be acted on only when streaming live: a resumed session replays past instances of this message.

nodes.label: SDKPluginInstallMessage
nodes.rationale: Plugin installation progress events, emitted when `CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL` is set so an application can track marketplace plugin installation before the first turn. `started` and `completed` bracket the overall install, while `installed` and `failed` report individual marketplaces and include `name`.

nodes.label: SDKPermissionDeniedMessage
nodes.rationale: A stream event emitted when the permission system denies a tool call without an interactive prompt, so a UI can render the denial as it happens. What it reports depends on configuration: with a `canUseTool` callback it reports only the denials Claude Code decides on its own; with neither callback nor prompt tool it also reports every call that would have prompted (v2.1.223+); with an MCP prompt tool set by `permissionPromptToolName` it is not emitted at all. In every configuration it skips denials decided on the `PreToolUse` hook path, and it is best-effort.

nodes.label: SDKPermissionDenial authoritative record
nodes.rationale: `SDKPermissionDenial` (`tool_name`, `tool_use_id`, `tool_input`) is the entry shape of the result message's `permission_denials` array, which the doc names the authoritative record of denied tool uses — the streamed denial event is best-effort and can be missing.

nodes.label: SDKContextUsage
nodes.rationale: `SDKContextUsage` (SDK v0.3.232+) is the structured form of the `/context` report attached to the assistant message that delivers a `/context` result. Unlike the control-response form it carries only the data needed to render the breakdown, without display fields. `total_tokens` is not clamped to the window so it can exceed `raw_max_tokens`, `percentage` can exceed 100, and `over_limit.kind` distinguishes a `hard_limit` (the model's own limit) from a `compaction_window`. The type evolves additively: read known fields and ignore unrecognized ones.

nodes.label: SDKContextUsageCategory
nodes.rationale: One row of the `/context` usage-by-category breakdown, carrying a display `name`, a `tokens` count that may be zero, and a `kind` that must be used for classification instead of the name: `used` (content occupying the window), `free` (remaining window), `buffer` (the compaction reserve) and `deferred` (tool schemas held out of the window and excluded from the usage calculation).

nodes.label: SDKMessageOrigin provenance
nodes.rationale: `SDKMessageOrigin` is the provenance of a user-role message, appearing as `origin` on `SDKUserMessage` and forwarded onto the corresponding result. Kinds are `human`, `channel`, `peer`, `task-notification`, `coordinator`, `auto-continuation` and `unclassified`. An application forwarding what a user typed must set `{ kind: "human" }` explicitly: Claude Code treats a user message with no origin as unattributed and checks requiring a human-typed prompt, such as the `ultracode` workflow keyword, reject it. Before v2.1.210 an absent origin was treated as human input.

nodes.label: Task-notification subkinds
nodes.rationale: `subkind` is set on a task notification's origin only when Anthropic servers verified where the notification came from (Claude Code v2.1.213+). `scheduled-trigger` marks a routine's stored prompt delivered because a schedule, API trigger, GitHub trigger or Run now fired, and is framed to the model as the session's assigned task; `peer-send-message` marks a server-verified message from another of the user's sessions (v2.1.224+). Everything else — locally-fired scheduled tasks, PR activity, finished background tasks — has no subkind, and cross-session `SendMessage` traffic is not a task notification at all but a `peer` origin.

nodes.label: Peer origin fields and trust model
nodes.rationale: A `peer` origin identifies the sending agent — an in-process teammate or a cross-session peer (Claude Code v2.1.224+ on macOS and Linux). The trust model is explicit: `from` and `fromSession` are sender-asserted and forgeable by any same-user process, so `verifiedPeerPid` — the connecting process ID verified by the kernel from the socket itself, never from the payload — is what identifies the sender. Its absence means unverified; for relayed traffic it names the relay rather than the author; and because process IDs are recyclable it is provenance, not an authentication token. `name` is normalized (control/format/surrogate/separator code points stripped, trimmed, capped at 64 code points) and `body` is byte-exact with what the model sees.

nodes.label: HookEvent catalogue
nodes.rationale: `HookEvent` enumerates every hook point: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PostToolBatch`, `Notification`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `UserPromptExpansion`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `PreModelSwitch`, `PostModelSwitch`, `PermissionRequest`, `PermissionDenied`, `Setup`, `TeammateIdle`, `TaskCreated`, `TaskCompleted`, `Elicitation`, `ElicitationResult`, `ConfigChange`, `DirectoryAdded`, `WorktreeCreate`, `WorktreeRemove`, `InstructionsLoaded`, `CwdChanged`, `FileChanged` and `MessageDisplay`.

nodes.label: HookCallback and HookCallbackMatcher
nodes.rationale: `HookCallback` is `(input: HookInput, toolUseID: string | undefined, options: { signal: AbortSignal }) => Promise<HookJSONOutput>`. `HookCallbackMatcher` groups callbacks under an optional `matcher` string with a `timeout` in seconds applied to all hooks in that matcher, and the `hooks` option of `Options` is a partial record from `HookEvent` to arrays of these matchers.

nodes.label: BaseHookInput common fields
nodes.rationale: Every hook input extends `BaseHookInput`, which carries `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `prompt_id`, `permission_mode`, `effort`, `agent_id` and `agent_type`. `prompt_id` is a UUID identifying the user prompt being processed, matching the `prompt.id` attribute on OpenTelemetry events, and is absent until the first user input. Requires Claude Code v2.1.196 or later.

nodes.label: HookInput union
nodes.rationale: `HookInput` is the union of every per-event hook input type, each discriminated by its `hook_event_name` literal and each extending `BaseHookInput`.

nodes.label: PreToolUseHookInput
nodes.rationale: `PreToolUseHookInput` carries `tool_name`, `tool_input` and `tool_use_id` before a tool runs. It is the hook point that can gate EVERY tool call, unlike `canUseTool`, which fires only when the permission flow resolves to a prompt.

nodes.label: PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure and PostToolBatch inputs
nodes.rationale: `PostToolUseHookInput` adds `tool_response` and `duration_ms` after a successful call; `PostToolUseFailureHookInput` carries `error`, `is_interrupt` and `duration_ms`; `PostToolBatchHookInput` fires once after every tool call in a batch has resolved, before the next model request, carrying a `tool_calls` array whose `tool_response` holds the serialized `tool_result` content the model sees rather than the structured output object.

nodes.label: PreModelSwitch and PostModelSwitch inputs
nodes.rationale: `PreModelSwitchHookInput` fires before a requested model switch takes effect and carries `from_model`, `to_model`, `requested_model`, a `source` of `command`/`picker`/`sdk`, and the cost estimate for re-sending the conversation: `context_tokens`, `prompt_cache_warm`, `cache_ttl`, `estimated_cache_write_usd` and `pricing`. `PostModelSwitchHookInput` fires after the change with the same fields plus the `auto` and `resume` source values.

nodes.label: Session and subagent lifecycle hook inputs
nodes.rationale: `SessionStartHookInput` carries a `source` of `startup`/`resume`/`clear`/`compact`/`fork`; `SessionEndHookInput` carries an exit `reason`; `StopHookInput` and `SubagentStopHookInput` carry `stop_hook_active`, the last assistant message, and summaries of live `background_tasks` and `session_crons`; `SubagentStartHookInput` carries `agent_id` and `agent_type`; `PreCompactHookInput` and `PostCompactHookInput` carry the compaction `trigger` plus custom instructions or the resulting summary.

nodes.label: Environment and configuration hook inputs
nodes.rationale: A family of hook inputs reports environment change: `ConfigChangeHookInput` (which settings source or skills directory changed), `InstructionsLoadedHookInput` (`file_path`, `memory_type`, and a `load_reason` of `session_start`/`nested_traversal`/`path_glob_match`/`include`/`compact`), `DirectoryAddedHookInput` (`/add-dir` versus the SDK's `register_repo_root` control request), `WorktreeCreate`/`WorktreeRemove`, `CwdChangedHookInput`, `FileChangedHookInput` (`change`/`add`/`unlink`) and `MessageDisplayHookInput`.

nodes.label: HookJSONOutput and the async form
nodes.rationale: `HookJSONOutput` is `AsyncHookJSONOutput | SyncHookJSONOutput`. The async form is just `{ async: true, asyncTimeout? }`, releasing the loop while the hook continues in the background.

nodes.label: SyncHookJSONOutput and hookSpecificOutput
nodes.rationale: `SyncHookJSONOutput` carries generic controls (`continue`, `suppressOutput`, `stopReason`, `decision`, `systemMessage`, `reason`, `terminalSequence`) plus a `hookSpecificOutput` discriminated on `hookEventName`. `PreToolUse` may return `permissionDecision` of `allow`/`deny`/`ask`/`defer` with `updatedInput` and `additionalContext`; `SessionStart` may return `initialUserMessage`, `sessionTitle`, `watchPaths` and `reloadSkills`; `PostToolUse` may return `updatedToolOutput` and a `classifierContext` note for the auto-mode permission classifier capped at 2000 characters and explicitly not to be filled with untrusted tool output; `PreModelSwitch` uses the same allow/deny/ask contract, where every surface other than interactive `/model` treats `ask` as a refusal.

nodes.label: ToolInputSchemas union
nodes.rationale: `ToolInputSchemas` is the exported union of input types for every built-in Claude Code tool — Agent, Artifact, AskUserQuestion, Bash, the Cron trio, plan-mode and worktree tools, file tools, Glob, Grep, MCP resource tools, Monitor, NotebookEdit, Projects, PushNotification, REPL, ReportFindings, ScheduleWakeup, RemoteTrigger, the Task tools, TodoWrite, WebFetch, WebSearch and Workflow — enabling type-safe tool interactions.

nodes.label: ToolOutputSchemas union
nodes.rationale: `ToolOutputSchemas` is the exported union of output types for every built-in tool, representing the actual response data each returns. It mirrors the input union member for member and is what `tool_use_result` on a user message resolves to for built-in tools.

nodes.label: Agent tool (formerly Task)
nodes.rationale: The `Agent` tool launches a subagent for complex multi-step work. The previous name `Task` is still accepted as an alias and the init message's `tools` array still lists it as `Task` for backward compatibility. Its input carries `description`, `prompt`, `subagent_type`, `model`, `run_in_background`, `name` and `isolation` (`worktree` or `remote`); `mode` and `team_name` are deprecated and ignored, because subagents inherit the parent session's permission mode with an `AgentDefinition.permissionMode` override, except under a parent using `bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits` or `auto`.

nodes.label: AgentOutput result shapes
nodes.rationale: `AgentOutput` is discriminated on `status`: `completed` carries the subagent's `content`, `agentId`, `resolvedModel`, `modelsUsed`, tool and duration totals, `usage`, `toolStats` and any kept `worktreePath`/`worktreeBranch`; `async_launched` carries the background task's `agentId` and `outputFile`; `remote_launched` carries a `taskId` and `sessionUrl` for a dispatched cloud session. `usage` and `totalTokens` are filled from the subagent's FINAL API request, not the whole run — a caveat that makes them unsuitable for whole-run accounting.

nodes.label: Bash tool input and output
nodes.rationale: `BashInput` carries `command`, a `timeout` in milliseconds clamped to a 600000 maximum, `description`, `run_in_background` and `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`; the working directory persists between commands while shell state such as exported environment variables does not. `BashOutput`'s `stdout` merges the command's stdout AND stderr into one interleaved stream while its `stderr` carries only notices the tool itself adds, and it also reports `timedOutAfterMs`, `backgroundCwdHint`, `backgroundEndsWithFinalResponse` and a structured `gitOperation` summary of commits, pushes, branch merges and PR actions.

nodes.label: Monitor tool
nodes.rationale: `Monitor` runs a background source and delivers each event to Claude so it can react without polling: `command` runs a script emitting one event per stdout line, or `ws` opens a WebSocket emitting one event per text frame (Claude Code v2.1.195+), and exactly one of the two must be given. `persistent: true` is for session-length watches such as log tails. A command monitor follows the same permission rules as Bash while a WebSocket watch prompts separately, and the output's `taskId` is what `TaskStop` cancels.

nodes.label: Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep tools
nodes.rationale: The file toolset covers `Read` (`file_path`, `offset`, `limit`, `pages` for PDF ranges), `Write`, `Edit` (exact string replacement with `replace_all`), `Glob` (pattern matching sorted by modification time) and `Grep` (a ripgrep-backed search with `output_mode`, context flags, `head_limit`, `offset` and `multiline`). `FileReadOutput` is discriminated on `type` — `text`, `image`, `notebook`, `pdf`, `parts` and `file_unchanged` — and `Edit`/`Write` return a `structuredPatch` plus an optional `gitDiff`.

nodes.label: Grep and Glob pre-pagination totals
nodes.rationale: `GlobOutput.totalMatches` (Claude Code v2.1.191+) reports matches before truncation and is a lower bound when `countIsComplete` is false. `GrepOutput.totalFiles` (v2.1.208+) and `totalLines` (v2.1.210+) report totals before `head_limit`/`offset` pagination, and in `count` mode `numFiles`/`numMatches` are totals over the full result set — before v2.1.208 a truncating limit also truncated those totals.

nodes.label: TodoWrite and the Task tools
nodes.rationale: `TodoWrite` manages a structured task list, while `TaskCreate`, `TaskUpdate`, `TaskGet` and `TaskList` manage individual tasks with IDs, statuses, owners and `blocks`/`blockedBy` dependency edges. On TypeScript Agent SDK 0.3.233+ none of these five tools is available on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5 or later versions of those families without an explicit opt-in; on other models the Task tools are provided by default and `TodoWrite` only when `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=0`.

nodes.label: Workflow tool
nodes.rationale: `Workflow` runs a dynamic workflow: a script orchestrating many subagents in the background and returning one consolidated result (Agent SDK v0.3.149+). At least one of `script`, `name` or `scriptPath` is required, `scriptPath` takes precedence, `args` is exposed to the script as the global `args` and must be passed as real JSON rather than a JSON-encoded string, and `resumeFromRunId` resumes a prior run in the same session. The output returns immediately with `status`, `taskId`, `runId`, `transcriptDir` and `scriptPath` — and `error` must be checked first, because a script that fails its syntax check returns `async_launched` with `error` set and never runs.

nodes.label: Worktree and plan-mode tools
nodes.rationale: `EnterWorktree` creates or switches into a temporary git worktree (`name` and `path` are mutually exclusive, and the target must be a registered worktree of the repository or, from within a worktree session, under `.claude/worktrees/`), and `ExitWorktree` returns to the original directory with a `keep` or `remove` action where `discard_changes: true` is required to remove a worktree holding uncommitted files or unmerged commits. `EnterPlanMode` and `ExitPlanMode` bracket plan mode; `ExitPlanMode`'s `allowedPrompts` is deprecated and ignored but still accepted so existing callers and transcripts validate.

nodes.label: CronCreate, CronDelete, CronList and ScheduleWakeup
nodes.rationale: `CronCreate` schedules a prompt on a 5-field cron in local time; jobs are session-scoped by default and `durable: true` requests persistence to `.claude/scheduled_tasks.json`, but durable scheduling is not available in every session — Claude Code accepts the flag and creates a session-only job, so the output's `durable` field is what says whether it persisted. `ScheduleWakeup` backs the self-paced `/loop`, clamping `delaySeconds` to between 60 and 3600, and `stop: true` (v2.1.202+) cancels the pending wakeup, reporting how many it cancelled in `cancelledWakeups` (v2.1.206+).

nodes.label: RemoteTrigger tool for Routines
nodes.rationale: `RemoteTrigger` manages Routines, the cloud-hosted scheduled and triggered Claude Code runs, and backs the `/schedule` command. Actions are `list`, `get`, `create`, `update`, `run`, `create_webhook_trigger` (v2.1.225+, attaching an event source such as a GitHub event), `list_runs` and `get_run_log` (both v2.1.227+). The tool is present only for a claude.ai account on a plan with Routines enabled and is absent when organization policy disables Claude Code on the web or, from v2.1.227, when an Owner turned routines off.

nodes.label: Artifact tool
nodes.rationale: `Artifact` publishes a local `.html` or `.md` file as a hosted page or lists the user's published artifacts. `url` targets an existing artifact to update in place instead of minting a new one, and `force` is a last-resort overwrite discarding a newer version another session published — the documented recovery on a conflict is to merge onto the returned newer content and publish again. `capabilities` and `contract` (both Agent SDK v0.3.235+) declare the page's runtime capabilities and runtime version. The types are exported but the tool is off by default in Agent SDK sessions, and API-key-authenticated sessions cannot publish at all.

nodes.label: Projects tool
nodes.rationale: `Projects` reads and writes the claude.ai Project attached to the session, dispatching on `method`: `project_info` returns metadata and the doc list, `project_read` reads one doc, `project_search` queries the knowledge base (returning RAG `hits` with `rag: true` when the index is available and falling back to a `docs` path list otherwise), `project_write` creates or replaces a doc from exactly one of `content` or `local_path`, and `project_delete` removes one.

nodes.label: ReportFindings tool
nodes.rationale: `ReportFindings` reports code-review findings as a structured list so Claude Code renders them instead of printing text (Claude Code v2.1.196+). Findings are ordered most-severe first with at most 32 per call and an empty array when none survived; each carries `file`, optional 1-indexed `line`, `summary`, `failure_scenario`, an optional 60-character `short_summary` (v2.1.212+), a kebab-case `category` (v2.1.199+), a `verdict` set only when a verify pass ran, and an `outcome` set only when re-reporting after applying fixes.

nodes.label: REPL tool
nodes.rationale: `REPL` executes JavaScript in a persistent REPL where state persists across calls and top-level await is supported, with a `timeout` defaulting to 30000 ms and capped at 600000. The types are exported but the tool is off in SDK sessions unless `CLAUDE_CODE_REPL=1` is set in the `env` option, and it also requires the Bun-based `claude` executable the native installer provides.

nodes.label: McpInput and McpOutput for dynamic MCP tools
nodes.rationale: MCP tools appear under dynamic names of the form `mcp__<server>__<tool>`. `McpInput` is an open object because each server defines its own parameters, and `McpOutput` is a string or an array of content blocks; the trailing bare-object branch of the exported type is a schema-generation artifact, since a server's structured output is serialized to a JSON string before return, and at runtime the value may also be `undefined` even though the type does not model that.

nodes.label: AskUserQuestion tool
nodes.rationale: `AskUserQuestion` asks the user clarifying questions during execution, taking an array of `questions` each with a `header`, labelled `options` carrying descriptions and optional `preview`, and a `multiSelect` flag. Its output returns the questions plus `answers`, and a `response` field set when the user typed a freeform reply instead — in which case Claude receives "The user responded: …" rather than the per-question answer list.

nodes.label: PermissionUpdate operations
nodes.rationale: `PermissionUpdate` is the operation union for changing permissions at runtime: `addRules`, `replaceRules` and `removeRules` (each carrying `rules` of `PermissionRuleValue`, a `behavior` of `allow`/`deny`/`ask`, and a destination), `setMode`, `addDirectories` and `removeDirectories`. A `PermissionRuleValue` is a `toolName` plus optional `ruleContent`.

nodes.label: PermissionUpdateDestination tiers
nodes.rationale: `PermissionUpdateDestination` selects where a permission change is written: `userSettings`, `projectSettings`, `localSettings`, `session` (current session only) or `cliArg`. Bash permission prompts include a suggestion with the `localSettings` destination, so returning it in `updatedPermissions` writes the rule to `.claude/settings.local.json` and persists it across sessions.

nodes.label: ApiKeySource
nodes.rationale: `ApiKeySource`, reported as `apiKeySource` on the init message, says where the session's API key came from. Claude Code reports only four values — `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `apiKeyHelper`, `/login managed key`, and `none` for a session authenticating another way such as a claude.ai login, bearer token or cloud provider. The type retains `user`, `project`, `org`, `temporary` and `oauth` so older code still compiles, but Claude Code never reports them.

nodes.label: SdkBeta and the retired 1M-context beta
nodes.rationale: `SdkBeta` currently holds only `context-1m-2025-08-07`, which is RETIRED as of April 30, 2026: passing it with Claude Sonnet 4.5 or Sonnet 4 has no effect and requests exceeding the 200k window error. A 1M-token window now requires migrating to Claude Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7 or Opus 4.8, which include it at standard pricing with no beta header.

nodes.label: SlashCommand
nodes.rationale: `SlashCommand` describes an available slash command with `name`, `description`, `argumentHint` and optional `aliases`. It is also the shape `reloadSkills()` returns for the reloaded skill list.

nodes.label: ModelInfo
nodes.rationale: `ModelInfo` describes an available model: `value` (the identifier to pass in API calls), `resolvedModel` (the canonical wire model ID an alias entry resolves to, Claude Code v2.1.197+, so a host can match a stored explicit ID against the alias covering it), `displayName`, `description`, and capability flags `supportsEffort`, `supportedEffortLevels`, `supportsAdaptiveThinking`, `supportsFastMode` and `supportsAutoMode`.

nodes.label: AgentInfo
nodes.rationale: `AgentInfo` describes an invocable subagent with `name` (an agent type identifier such as `"Explore"` or `"general-purpose"`), `description`, and `model` — an alias, a model ID, or `'inherit'` for the parent's model; when undefined, Claude Code picks the model by the documented subagent model order.

nodes.label: McpServerStatus
nodes.rationale: `McpServerStatus` reports a connected MCP server's `name`, a `status` of `connected`/`failed`/`needs-auth`/`pending`/`disabled`, `serverInfo`, `error`, its `config` as an `McpServerStatusConfig` union of every transport type, `scope`, and its `tools` with names, descriptions and read-only/destructive/open-world annotations.

nodes.label: ModelUsage per-model accounting
nodes.rationale: `ModelUsage` is the per-model usage record in result messages: token counts, `webSearchRequests`, an estimated `costUSD`, `contextWindow`, `maxOutputTokens`, plus `canonicalModel` and `provider` (Claude Code v2.1.218+) and `costBasis` (v2.1.246+). `canonicalModel` is the ID the pricing lookup uses and can differ from the raw key when that key is a provider-specific ID or alias; `provider` names the backend (`firstParty`, `bedrock`, `vertex`, `foundry`, `anthropicAws`, `mantle`, `gateway`); `costBasis` is `list`, `managed` or `unknown`.

nodes.label: Usage and NonNullableUsage
nodes.rationale: `Usage` is the `BetaUsage` type from `@anthropic-ai/sdk`: input/output tokens, cache creation and read tokens with 5m and 1h ephemeral breakdowns, `server_tool_use`, `service_tier`, `speed`, `inference_geo` and `iterations`. `NonNullableUsage` is a mapped type making every field non-nullable, and is what result messages carry.

nodes.label: ThinkingConfig
nodes.rationale: `ThinkingConfig` controls reasoning and takes precedence over the deprecated `maxThinkingTokens`: `{ type: 'adaptive' }` lets the model decide when and how much to reason (Opus 4.6+), `{ type: 'enabled', budgetTokens }` sets a fixed budget, `{ type: 'disabled' }` turns extended thinking off. The optional `display` field is `"summarized"` or `"omitted"`; on Claude Opus 4.7 and later the API default is `"omitted"`, and Claude Code does not send `display` to Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud's Agent Platform, so those providers return empty thinking blocks even when `"summarized"` is set.

nodes.label: CallToolResult
nodes.rationale: `CallToolResult`, from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk/types.js`, is what an SDK MCP tool handler returns: a `content` array of `text`/`image`/`audio`/`resource`/`resource_link` blocks, an optional `structuredContent` JSON object that can be returned alongside `content`, and `isError`.

nodes.label: spawnClaudeCodeProcess, SpawnedProcess and SpawnOptions
nodes.rationale: The `spawnClaudeCodeProcess` option supplies a custom spawn function so Claude Code can run in VMs, containers or remote environments. `SpawnedProcess` is the interface the function must return — `ChildProcess` already satisfies it — and `SpawnOptions` carries `command`, `args`, `cwd`, `env` and a `signal`. That signal does NOT fire the instant `Options.abortController` aborts: the SDK first closes stdin and waits about two seconds for a clean CLI shutdown, so reacting immediately requires listening on the caller's own abort signal.

nodes.label: McpSetServersResult and setMcpServers rules
nodes.rationale: `setMcpServers()` resolves with `added`, `removed` and per-server `errors`. Its rules: servers the call does not name keep running if plugin-provided (Agent SDK v0.3.210+); a named server is replaced only when its config differs from the one passed, except for built-in servers the CLI started at startup, which are dropped from the call and reported in `errors`. The promise resolves after newly added stdio, HTTP and SSE servers connect or fail, so their tools are available on the next turn.

nodes.label: RewindFilesResult and link safety
nodes.rationale: `rewindFiles(userMessageId, options)` restores files to their state at a given user message and requires `enableFileCheckpointing: true`; `{ dryRun: true }` previews. The result carries `canRewind`, `error`, `filesChanged`, `insertions`, `deletions` and `skippedLinks` — the count of tracked paths the rewind refused to restore or delete for link safety (a symlink, hard link or other non-regular file, a parent directory that no longer resolves to where it pointed at checkpoint time, or an unsafely-readable backup). Requires Claude Code v2.1.216+, and a dry-run never sets it.

nodes.label: Task lifecycle stream messages
nodes.rationale: `SDKTaskStartedMessage`, `SDKTaskProgressMessage` and `SDKTaskUpdatedMessage` track background tasks. `task_type` is `local_bash`, `local_agent` or `remote_agent`; `ambient: true` (SDK v0.3.247+) marks tasks Claude Code starts for its own operation, which should be excluded from activity indicators; `is_backgrounded` and `spawn_depth` (v0.3.238+) describe how the task started, with a main-thread subagent at depth 1 and a resumed subagent always reporting `is_backgrounded: true`. `task_updated` carries a `patch` to merge into a local task map keyed by `task_id`.

nodes.label: SDKTaskNotificationMessage
nodes.rationale: Emitted when a background task completes, fails or is stopped, carrying `task_id`, `status`, `output_file`, `summary` and usage totals. Claude Code prepends a notice to every task notification it sends the model — except deliveries stamped with the `scheduled-trigger` subkind, which get assigned-task framing — stating that no human input has occurred, so the model does not treat the notification as a user instruction or approval. Detection must be done by checking `origin.kind === "task-notification"`, never by matching the notice text.

nodes.label: SDKBackgroundTasksChangedMessage
nodes.rationale: Emitted whenever the set of live background tasks changes, carrying the FULL live set in `tasks`. The documented discipline is to replace any cached set with each payload rather than pairing `task_started` and `task_notification` events, so the next membership change corrects any missed event; ordering relative to per-task events is unspecified. Nothing is emitted at startup, and a repeated `initialize` on a running session is followed by a snapshot even when empty (Agent SDK v0.3.239+). Requires Claude Code v2.1.203 or later.

nodes.label: SDKToolProgressMessage and subagent retries
nodes.rationale: A `tool_progress` message is emitted every 30 seconds with `heartbeat: true` while a main-conversation tool call runs, so a long call can be distinguished from a stalled session; heartbeats are not emitted for the Agent tool or for calls inside a subagent. `subagent_retry` reports an API-error backoff, and the doc is explicit about rendering it: track the indicator by `parent_tool_use_id` (unique per subagent) rather than `tool_use_id` (shared by parallel subagents), clear it when a later message lacks the field or the result arrives rather than deriving it from counters that `attempt` can exceed, and treat `error_category` as a closed token set rather than display text.

nodes.label: Hook lifecycle stream messages
nodes.rationale: `SDKHookStartedMessage`, `SDKHookProgressMessage` and `SDKHookResponseMessage` report hook execution with `hook_id`, `hook_name`, `hook_event`, stdout/stderr, `exit_code` and an `outcome` of `success`/`error`/`cancelled`. They are delivered to the stream immediately, including while a `SessionStart` or `Setup` hook is still running during startup; Claude Code v2.1.169 through v2.1.203 batched them until the hook completed, and v2.1.204 restored live delivery.

nodes.label: includeHookEvents option and its exceptions
nodes.rationale: `includeHookEvents` adds hook lifecycle events to the message stream, but the contract has exceptions: `SessionStart` and `Setup` lifecycle events are always included and need no opt-in, and some events — `Notification`, `SessionEnd`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact` — never produce an `SDKHookStartedMessage` even with the option, emitting only a progress message while a command hook produces output for more than a second and a response message only when a background hook finishes.

nodes.label: SDKRateLimitEvent
nodes.rationale: `SDKRateLimitEvent` reports a rate limit with a `status` of `allowed`/`allowed_warning`/`rejected`, `resetsAt` and `utilization`. When `errorCode` is `"credits_required"` the rejection is a claude.ai subscription whose included usage is exhausted and the session cannot continue until credits are bought; `canUserPurchaseCredits` and `hasChargeableSavedPaymentMethod` say whether the user can. All three fields are absent on other rate-limit events. Requires Claude Code v2.1.181 or later.

nodes.label: SDKCommandsChangedMessage
nodes.rationale: Emitted when the set of available commands changes mid-session, such as when skills are discovered as the agent enters a subdirectory. `commands` is the full updated list and must replace any cached one. From Agent SDK v0.3.216, `supportedCommands()` tracks these pushes and returns the same updated list; earlier SDK versions return only the initialization snapshot and never reflect mid-session changes.

nodes.label: SDKConversationResetMessage
nodes.rationale: Emitted when a session's conversation is replaced without ending the session — in a `query()` call, only `/clear` and its aliases produce it. The handling contract is to mount an empty transcript under `new_conversation_id` and discard any cached session title. The type is declared in the published typings only from Claude Code v2.1.203; before that `SDKMessage` referenced it without declaring it, so narrowing on it failed to typecheck with `skipLibCheck` disabled.

nodes.label: AbortError and untyped failures
nodes.rationale: `AbortError extends Error` is the ONLY error class in the SDK's typed API. Other failures — the Claude Code process exiting or failing to launch — reject the message iteration with errors carrying no SDK class to match on, so they must be keyed by message text using the troubleshooting page.

nodes.label: SandboxSettings
nodes.rationale: `SandboxSettings` configures command sandboxing programmatically: `enabled`, `failIfUnavailable` (default true — set false to fall back to unsandboxed execution with a stderr warning), `autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` (default true), `excludedCommands` that always bypass the sandbox with no model involvement, `allowUnsandboxedCommands` (default true), `network`, `filesystem`, `ignoreViolations`, `enableWeakerNestedSandbox` and a custom `ripgrep` binary. When `enabled` is true and the sandbox cannot start, `query()` reports a result with `subtype: "error_during_execution"` and, for a single-message call, throws after yielding it.

nodes.label: SandboxNetworkConfig
nodes.rationale: `SandboxNetworkConfig` governs sandboxed Bash network access — explicitly NOT the WebFetch tool, which uses permission rules instead. It carries `allowedDomains`, `deniedDomains` (taking precedence over allows), `strictAllowlist` (deny rather than prompt for hosts outside the allowlist; honored only from user, managed or CLI `--settings` sources, never project settings; Claude Code v2.1.219+), `allowManagedDomainsOnly` (managed-settings only, with no effect via SDK options), `allowLocalBinding`, `allowUnixSockets`, `allowAllUnixSockets` and proxy ports. The built-in proxy enforces `allowedDomains` on the requested hostname and does not terminate or inspect TLS, so domain fronting can potentially bypass it.

nodes.label: SandboxFilesystemConfig
nodes.rationale: `SandboxFilesystemConfig` restricts sandboxed filesystem access with `allowWrite`, `denyWrite` and `denyRead` path-pattern arrays, all defaulting to empty.

nodes.label: Permissions fallback for unsandboxed commands
nodes.rationale: When `allowUnsandboxedCommands` is enabled the model can request execution outside the sandbox by setting `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` in tool input; such requests fall back to the permissions system, invoking the `canUseTool` handler so the application can authorize them. The documented hazard is the combination with `permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions'`, which lets the model autonomously run unsandboxed commands without approval prompts and effectively escape sandbox isolation silently.

nodes.label: Unix socket sandbox-escape warning
nodes.rationale: Allowing a Unix socket through `allowUnixSockets` can grant access to system services that reach outside the sandbox: the doc's worked example is `/var/run/docker.sock`, which effectively grants full host system access through the Docker API and bypasses sandbox isolation entirely. Only strictly necessary sockets should be allowed.

nodes.label: Agent teams
nodes.rationale: Agent teams coordinate multiple Claude Code instances working together: one session acts as team lead, coordinating work, assigning tasks and synthesizing results, while teammates work independently in their own context windows and communicate directly with each other. They are experimental, disabled by default, and are most effective for research/review, new modules, competing-hypothesis debugging, and cross-layer coordination.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS
nodes.rationale: Agent teams are enabled only by setting the environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS to 1, in the shell or in settings.json's env block. Without it no team is set up at session start, no team directories are written, and Claude does not spawn or propose teammates.

nodes.label: Team lead
nodes.rationale: The team lead is the main Claude Code session that spawns teammates, creates and assigns tasks, and coordinates and synthesizes their work. Its entry in the team config always carries the agent type 'team-lead'.

nodes.label: Teammate
nodes.rationale: A teammate is a separate, full Claude Code instance that works on assigned tasks in its own context window. The lead assigns every teammate a name at spawn time, and any teammate can message any other by that name.

nodes.label: Shared task list
nodes.rationale: The shared task list coordinates work across the team: the lead creates tasks and teammates work through them, with three states — pending, in progress, completed. The lead can assign tasks explicitly, or a teammate can self-claim the next unassigned, unblocked task after finishing one.

nodes.label: Mailbox
nodes.rationale: The mailbox is the messaging system between agents: each agent's mailbox is a JSON file at ~/.claude/teams/{team-name}/inboxes/{agent-name}.json. Messages are delivered automatically to recipients, so the lead never has to poll for updates.

nodes.label: Subagents (the lighter alternative)
nodes.rationale: Subagents work within a single session: they get their own context window but return a result to the caller, the main agent manages all work, and token cost is lower because results are summarized back into the main context. Use subagents for focused tasks where only the result matters, and agent teams when workers must discuss, challenge each other, and coordinate on their own.

nodes.label: Cross-session messaging
nodes.rationale: Cross-session messaging lets Claude pass findings between separate sessions the user runs themselves, without forming a team. The docs advise checking whether this lighter option does the job before setting up an agent team.

nodes.label: Agent team token cost
nodes.rationale: Agent teams use significantly more tokens than a single session because each teammate is a separate Claude instance with its own context window, so usage scales with the number of active teammates. The extra tokens are usually worthwhile for research, review and new feature work, and wasteful for routine tasks.

nodes.label: Teammate display mode
nodes.rationale: Agent teams support two display modes — in-process and split panes — and the mode changes real behavior, not just presentation: which tools a subagent definition contributes, whether its body replaces or appends to the system prompt, and whether its mcpServers apply all depend on the teammate's display mode.

nodes.label: In-process display mode
nodes.rationale: In-process is the default mode (since v2.1.179; the default was previously 'auto'): all teammates run inside the main terminal and are selected with arrow keys in the agent panel, then opened with Enter. It works in any terminal with no extra setup.

nodes.label: Split-pane display mode
nodes.rationale: In split-pane mode each teammate gets its own pane, so all output is visible at once and a user can click into a pane to interact directly. It is not supported in VS Code's integrated terminal, Windows Terminal, or Ghostty.

nodes.label: teammateMode setting and --teammate-mode flag
nodes.rationale: The display mode is chosen with teammateMode in ~/.claude/settings.json, or per session with the experimental --teammate-mode flag (which does not appear in claude --help). Values are 'in-process' (default), 'auto' (split panes when already in tmux or in iTerm2 with it2, otherwise in-process), 'tmux' (split panes, auto-detecting tmux vs iTerm2), and, since v2.1.186, 'iterm2' for explicit iTerm2 native panes.

nodes.label: tmux or iTerm2 it2 requirement
nodes.rationale: Split-pane mode requires either tmux or iTerm2 with the it2 CLI installed and the iTerm2 Python API enabled. The 'iterm2' mode shows an error with the install command when it2 is missing, and tmux works best on macOS with tmux -CC in iTerm2 as the suggested entrypoint.

nodes.label: Orphaned tmux sessions
nodes.rationale: A tmux session can persist after the Claude Code session ends when cleanup did not complete; the remedy is to list sessions with `tmux ls` and end the team's with `tmux kill-session -t <session-name>`.

nodes.label: Teammate model selection order
nodes.rationale: Claude Code picks a teammate's model from the first rule that applies: the model named in the spawn prompt; then a subagent definition's model (where 'inherit' means the lead's model); then CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL when set to anything but 'inherit'; then the lead's current model. Before v2.1.251 CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL came first, and teammateDefaultModel was removed in v2.1.234 and is ignored.

nodes.label: availableModels allowlist substitution
nodes.rationale: The selected teammate model is checked against the organization's availableModels allowlist. A blocked family alias such as 'opus' runs on the newest permitted version of that family on the Anthropic API and Claude Platform on AWS; any other blocked value — including a family alias on providers where substitution does not operate — falls back to the lead's model, trying CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL first if it is set.

nodes.label: Effort level inheritance
