nodes.rationale: Claude can load a typeface from Google Fonts, the one external font source an artifact page may load from; any other typeface is inlined as a @font-face data URI, and every typeface gets a fallback stack so the page still renders if a font does not load. Blocking fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com is optional and only degrades artifacts to fallback typefaces.

nodes.label: /design canvas
nodes.rationale: Running /design with a brief mocks up a UI, screen flow, landing page or poster: Claude drafts artboards on one canvas and publishes the canvas as an artifact running a research preview of Claude Design's editor. Where saving is enabled you edit an element and save to publish a new version; otherwise you view and export as PNG or PDF. Requires artifacts to be available and Claude Code v2.1.234 or later.

nodes.label: HTML document shell served under a strict CSP
nodes.rationale: Claude Code wraps the published file in an HTML document shell and serves it under a strict Content Security Policy, which is what shapes everything the page can do.

nodes.label: Page constraints
nodes.rationale: Each artifact is one self-contained page, and the documented constraint set covers external requests, the absence of a backend, single-page-ness, permitted source file types, and rendered size.

nodes.label: External-request allowlist: four CDNs plus Google Fonts
nodes.rationale: The page may load typefaces from Google Fonts and scripts from four public CDN hosts — cdnjs.cloudflare.com, cdn.tailwindcss.com, code.jquery.com, and selected jsDelivr paths such as /npm/. The CSP blocks every external image and all other external scripts, stylesheets and fonts, and confines fetch, XHR and WebSocket to the page's own origin and the Google Fonts hosts, so Claude inlines other CSS/JS and embeds images as data URIs. A blocked library, unlike a blocked font, has no fallback.

nodes.label: Constraint: no backend
nodes.rationale: An artifact is a static page: it cannot store data submitted through a form or authenticate viewers itself, and its only way to fetch data at view time is calling MCP connectors rather than an API of its own.

nodes.label: Constraint: single page, no relative links
nodes.rationale: Relative links do not resolve because nothing is deployed alongside the page, so multi-section content uses in-page anchors rather than separate files.

nodes.label: Constraint: .html, .htm or .md source files
nodes.rationale: The published file must be .html, .htm, or .md; Markdown files render as styled HTML.

nodes.label: Constraint: 16 MiB rendered size
nodes.rationale: The rendered page must be 16 MiB or smaller; large embedded images are the usual cause when a publish fails for size.

nodes.label: Artifacts cost output tokens
nodes.rationale: Generating an artifact uses output tokens like any other response, and a styled page costs more than the same content as terminal text — inline CSS, interactive JavaScript, and especially data-URI images being the main contributors. Reduce cost by preferring SVG or HTML/CSS diagrams over raster images, omitting unneeded interactivity, and summarizing large datasets rather than inlining them.

nodes.label: Availability requirements
nodes.rationale: Artifacts require every listed condition — plan, authentication, model provider, organization policy, and surface — to be met at once. When one is not met, Claude writes a local HTML file or says it cannot publish.

nodes.label: Requirement: Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan
nodes.rationale: Artifacts need a Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan. On Pro and Max they are private until shared with no admin management; on Team plans they are on by default; on Enterprise plans an Owner must enable them in claude.ai admin settings.

nodes.label: Requirement: a claude.ai-backed session
nodes.rationale: The session must be backed by a claude.ai account via /login in the CLI or desktop app; Claude Tag sessions are signed in through the agent's identity. Sessions using an API key, an LLM gateway token, or a cloud-provider credential cannot publish.

nodes.label: Requirement: the Anthropic API as model provider
nodes.rationale: Artifacts are available only on the Anthropic API, not on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry.

nodes.label: Requirement: no CMEK, HIPAA or Zero Data Retention
nodes.rationale: Artifacts are unavailable when customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), HIPAA, or Zero Data Retention are enabled for the organization.

nodes.label: Requirement: a supported surface and version
nodes.rationale: The surface must be Claude Code CLI 2.1.183 or later, or the Claude desktop app 1.13576.0 or later; Claude Tag sessions can publish when both Claude Tag and artifacts are enabled for the organization. Artifacts are off by default in the Agent SDK, GitHub Action and MCP-server contexts, and when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC is set.

nodes.label: Disabling artifacts for your own sessions
nodes.rationale: Artifacts can be turned off for your own sessions regardless of the organization's setting via the /config Artifacts row (which writes "enableArtifact": false to user settings), setting "enableArtifact": false in a settings file (the deprecated "disableArtifact": true also works), setting CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT=1, or adding Artifact to permissions.deny.

nodes.label: A disable cannot be re-enabled by a higher-precedence file
nodes.rationale: Once artifacts are turned off in a --settings file, with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ARTIFACT, or by an administrator in managed settings, no settings file turns them back on. Before v2.1.242 a file higher in the precedence stack could re-enable them over a lower file's "enableArtifact": false.

nodes.label: Project-scoped disable in .claude/settings.json
nodes.rationale: Setting "enableArtifact": false in a project's .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json turns artifacts off for sessions in that project; an "enableArtifact": true in either file does not turn them back on. Honoring the key in project and local settings requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

nodes.label: Organization management of artifacts
nodes.rationale: Owners on Team and Enterprise plans control artifacts from claude.ai admin settings, with an Artifacts toggle under Settings > Claude Code > Capabilities and, on Enterprise with role-based access control, a per-role Artifacts permission under Settings > Roles. Artifact content is stored on Anthropic-operated infrastructure and is visible only to authenticated members of the publishing organization unless shared publicly.

nodes.label: Enable artifact connectors toggle
nodes.rationale: Connector calls from artifacts have their own toggle, separate from the Artifacts toggle: Settings > Capabilities > Enable artifact connectors. It sits under Capabilities rather than Claude Code because the same toggle also governs connector calls from artifacts created in claude.ai conversations.

nodes.label: External sharing control
nodes.rationale: Public sharing is off by default on Team and Enterprise plans; an Owner enables it with External sharing under the Artifacts toggle in Settings > Claude Code > Capabilities. Turning it back off blocks access through existing public links without changing each artifact's audience, and access resumes if it is re-enabled.

nodes.label: Artifact retention policy
nodes.rationale: Settings > Data & privacy controls sets how long artifacts are kept before automatic deletion, with separate retention periods for artifacts still private to their author and artifacts that have been shared.

nodes.label: claude_artifact_* audit log events
nodes.rationale: Publishing, sharing and deleting an artifact each appear in the organization's audit log under the claude_artifact_* event types — the same family used for artifacts created in claude.ai conversations.

nodes.label: Sandboxed *.claudeusercontent.com viewer origin
nodes.rationale: The claude.ai viewer loads each artifact from a sandboxed *.claudeusercontent.com origin, so an organization that restricts outbound network access must allowlist that domain alongside claude.ai. Blocked font and CDN hosts should be rejected fast rather than dropped silently, so requests fail immediately instead of delaying first render or hanging.

nodes.label: Compliance API artifact endpoints
nodes.rationale: The Compliance API exposes GET /v1/compliance/code/artifacts to list an organization's artifacts, GET /v1/compliance/code/artifacts/{artifact_id}/versions/{version_id} to retrieve a specific version's content, and DELETE /v1/compliance/code/artifacts/{artifact_id} to delete an artifact.

nodes.label: First-launch browser login
nodes.rationale: Running `claude` after installation opens a browser window for login on first launch; pressing `c` copies the login URL when the browser does not open. If `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set, Claude Code skips the login prompt and asks you to approve the key instead. On success the terminal shows `Login successful`.

nodes.label: Paste-the-login-code fallback
nodes.rationale: When the browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back, paste it at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt. This happens when the browser cannot reach Claude Code's local callback server, which is common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers.

nodes.label: /logout
nodes.rationale: `/logout` logs you out and re-authenticates; it also resets the first-launch setup state so the next `claude` run walks through login and setup again. After a keyless Console sign-in, `/logout` removes and revokes the credential that sign-in wrote.

nodes.label: Subscription OAuth credential from /login
nodes.rationale: Subscription OAuth credentials obtained through `/login` are the default credential for Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users, and rank last (7th) in Claude Code's authentication precedence order.

nodes.label: Team authentication options
nodes.rationale: Teams and organizations can configure Claude Code access through Claude for Teams or Enterprise (recommended for most teams), the Claude Console, a self-hosted Claude apps gateway, Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry.

nodes.label: Claude for Teams or Enterprise
nodes.rationale: Claude for Teams is a self-service plan with collaboration features, admin tools, and billing management for smaller teams; Claude for Enterprise adds SSO, domain capture, role-based permissions, a compliance API, and managed policy settings for organization-wide Claude Code configuration. Members install Claude Code and log in with their Claude.ai accounts.

nodes.label: Claude Console authentication
nodes.rationale: Organizations that prefer API-based billing set up access through the Claude Console: create or reuse a Console account, add users by bulk invite or SSO, assign roles, and have each user accept the invite, check system requirements, install Claude Code, and log in with Console credentials.

nodes.label: Console roles: Claude Code vs Developer
nodes.rationale: When inviting Console users an admin assigns either the Claude Code role, whose users can only create Claude Code API keys, or the Developer role, whose users can create any kind of API key.

nodes.label: Console sign-in without an API key
nodes.rationale: From Claude Code v2.1.242, choosing the Anthropic Console account at `/login` offers two routes: 'Sign in with your Console account' (recommended) keeps the OAuth token as an Anthropic profile and creates no API key, while 'Create an API key' (legacy) mints and stores a Console API key. The keyless route also signs you out of any claude.ai login stored on the machine.

nodes.label: Cases where an API key is created without asking
nodes.rationale: Claude Code does not offer the keyless choice and creates an API key without asking when the session runs against a cloud provider or Claude Platform on AWS, when any settings file sets `forceLoginOrgUUID` or sets `forceLoginMethod` to `"claudeai"` or `"console"`, or when a managed settings source exists but cannot be read and no other managed source supplies a policy.

nodes.label: Anthropic profile credential
nodes.rationale: A profile is a named credential configuration file in the Anthropic configuration directory (`~/.config/anthropic` on macOS and Linux, `%APPDATA%\Anthropic` on Windows). Its auth mode is `oidc_federation` for Workload Identity Federation or `user_oauth` when `ant auth login` or a keyless Console sign-in wrote it; Claude Code refreshes the profile's login automatically.

nodes.label: Anthropic profile login expired
nodes.rationale: When a `user_oauth` profile's login has expired and Claude Code cannot renew it, requests fail with the error 'Anthropic profile login expired' until you sign in again.

nodes.label: Named profile via ANTHROPIC_PROFILE
nodes.rationale: The first profile source Claude Code checks is the profile named by `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE`; it ranks above a `/login` credential whichever auth mode the profile has. Unsetting `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE` stops Claude Code selecting it.

nodes.label: Workload Identity Federation variables
nodes.rationale: The second profile source is the pair `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID` and `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID` set together; it ranks above a `/login` credential. Claude Code also reads the other WIF variables, such as `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`, when exchanging the identity token.

nodes.label: Active profile source
nodes.rationale: The third profile source is the `active_config` file in the configuration directory, or a profile named `default`. It ranks above `/login` when its auth mode is `oidc_federation` but below a working `/login` credential when its mode is `user_oauth` — a rule that keeps a leftover `ant auth login` profile from moving requests off the signed-in account.

nodes.label: Cloud provider authentication
nodes.rationale: Organizations on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry set the required environment variables before running `claude`, or pick '3rd-party platform' at the login prompt to launch an interactive setup wizard for Bedrock and Vertex AI; no browser login is needed. These credentials rank first in the precedence order when `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` is set.

nodes.label: Claude apps gateway session
nodes.rationale: A self-hosted Claude apps gateway signs developers in with corporate SSO through `/login` and routes inference to the configured cloud provider; the gateway-issued token is the session's only credential. A signed-in gateway session sits outside the precedence list as a provider selection and outranks Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry.

nodes.label: forceLoginMethod
nodes.rationale: `forceLoginMethod`, set in managed settings, directs which login method developers use — `"claudeai"`, `"console"`, or `"gateway"`. On the terminal's interactive login screen Claude Code only pre-selects a `claudeai` or `console` method without enforcing it, so a developer can still complete a Console login there.

nodes.label: forceLoginOrgUUID
nodes.rationale: `forceLoginOrgUUID` requires that developers' claude.ai logins belong to a specific Anthropic organization: Claude Code errors and exits at startup when the claude.ai credential in use belongs to an unlisted organization. For Console logins it only pre-selects the organization on the sign-in page and never checks which organization the resulting Console credential belongs to.

nodes.label: Login paths and key enforcement
nodes.rationale: Developers log in from the terminal `/login` flow, the VS Code extension, the Agent SDK, `claude setup-token`, `/install-github-app`, and gateway sign-in. From v2.1.212 every path applies `forceLoginMethod` (before that, only terminal logins applied either key), but only terminal, VS Code, and Agent SDK logins verify `forceLoginOrgUUID`; `claude setup-token` and `/install-github-app` can mint a token in a different organization, and gateway sign-in does not authenticate against an Anthropic organization at all.

nodes.label: Deploying the login keys in both managed sources
nodes.rationale: Deploy the login keys through device management tooling: server-managed settings reach only already-authenticated accounts and cannot redirect a first login. Managed-settings sources do not merge — cached server-managed settings replace the device-managed file except for the `env` block (per-key merge in v2.1.223+) and the cross-source lock keys — and `forceLoginMethod`/`forceLoginOrgUUID` are neither, so set them in both places.

nodes.label: Startup block for environment credentials
nodes.rationale: The login keys also decide whether a session with no login credential can start: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, and `apiKeyHelper` sessions are blocked at startup because organization membership cannot be verified for an environment credential. Cloud provider sessions and Anthropic profile/federation credentials are not blocked.

nodes.label: Credential storage locations
nodes.rationale: macOS stores credentials in the encrypted Keychain, falling back to `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with mode `0600` when the Keychain rejects the write (for example locked in an SSH session), and a Console login that creates an API key fails until the Keychain is writable. Linux uses `~/.claude/.credentials.json` at mode `0600`; Windows uses `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json` under the user profile's access controls.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocation
nodes.rationale: Setting `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` keeps `.credentials.json` under that directory instead, including the file the macOS fallback writes, and keys the macOS Keychain entry to that directory, so a session with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` reads a different entry.

nodes.label: Supported authentication types
nodes.rationale: Claude Code supports Claude.ai credentials, Claude API credentials, Microsoft Foundry Auth, Bedrock Auth, Vertex Auth, Anthropic profile and Workload Identity Federation credentials, and Claude apps gateway session tokens.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL for a custom endpoint
nodes.rationale: Claude Code manages `.credentials.json` itself through `/login` and `/logout`; to route requests through a custom API endpoint, set the `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` environment variable instead of editing that file.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper custom credential script
nodes.rationale: The `apiKeyHelper` setting runs a shell script that returns an API key; its output ranks fourth in the authentication precedence order and is the recommended path for dynamic or rotating credentials such as short-lived tokens fetched from a vault.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper refresh interval
nodes.rationale: Claude Code re-runs `apiKeyHelper` after five minutes by default; the `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS` environment variable sets a custom refresh interval.

nodes.label: Slow helper notice
nodes.rationale: If `apiKeyHelper` takes longer than 10 seconds to return a key, Claude Code shows a warning notice in the prompt bar with the elapsed time, signalling that the credential script should be optimized.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper failure behavior
nodes.rationale: When the helper script errors, times out, or prints nothing, requests fail with 'Your apiKeyHelper script is failing' within three attempts. Before v2.1.208 those failures surfaced as a generic 401 after about ten silent retries.

nodes.label: Surfaces that read env credentials
nodes.rationale: `apiKeyHelper`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` apply to the CLI and the surfaces wrapping it — the VS Code extension, the Agent SDK, and GitHub Actions. Claude Desktop and cloud sessions neither call the helper nor read those variables; they use OAuth, except desktop sessions on a third-party inference configuration.

nodes.label: Expiring-login startup warning
nodes.rationale: Within three days of a `/login` credential expiring, Claude Code shows 'Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew' at startup (v2.1.203+; before v2.1.217 the warning appeared five days out). It is informational, never blocks a request, and only appears when a claude.ai or Claude Console login is the active credential.

nodes.label: Login expired error
nodes.rationale: Once the stored login expires and cannot be refreshed, every model request fails with 'Login expired · Please run /login' until you sign in again. Before v2.1.206 Claude Code reported an expired login on model requests as a model error instead.

nodes.label: Unattended sessions stall on expiry
nodes.rationale: Renewing early matters most for unattended work: a background session in agent view or a Remote Control session that outlives its login stops making progress once the credential expires and cannot recover until you sign in again.

nodes.label: /status credential rows
nodes.rationale: `/status` reports which credential is active: a `Login method` row for a subscription account, an `API key` row when an API key is in use, a `Profile` row naming the chosen profile source in place of `Login method`, and a `Login` row reading 'Expired — log in again' with the saved organization and email (v2.1.210+).

nodes.label: Authentication precedence order
nodes.rationale: With multiple credentials present Claude Code chooses in this order: cloud provider credentials, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `apiKeyHelper` output, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, Anthropic profile and federation credentials, then subscription OAuth credentials from `/login`.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: The `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable ranks second in precedence and is sent as the `Authorization: Bearer` header — the credential to use when routing through an LLM gateway or proxy that authenticates with bearer tokens rather than Anthropic API keys.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
nodes.rationale: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` ranks third in precedence and is sent as the `X-Api-Key` header for direct Anthropic API access. In interactive mode you approve or decline it once and the choice is remembered (changeable via the 'Use custom API key' toggle in `/config`); in non-interactive `-p` mode the key is always used when present.

nodes.label: API key overriding an active subscription
nodes.rationale: With an active Claude subscription and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` also set, the API key takes precedence once approved, which can cause authentication failures if the key belongs to a disabled or expired organization; `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` falls back to the subscription.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` holds a long-lived OAuth token for CI pipelines and scripts without browser login and ranks fifth in precedence. Running `/login` while it is set switches only the current session; every new session reads the variable again until it is removed from the shell profile or a settings file's `env` block.

nodes.label: claude setup-token
nodes.rationale: `claude setup-token` generates a one-year OAuth token through the same browser authorization flow as `/login`, prints it to the terminal, and saves it nowhere — you copy it into `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. It authenticates with a Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise subscription and can only make model requests.

nodes.label: Bare mode credential limits
nodes.rationale: In bare mode Claude Code reads neither profiles and federation variables (so `/status` shows no `Profile` row) nor `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`; a script passing `--bare` must authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper` instead.

nodes.label: Features requiring a claude.ai login
nodes.rationale: Some features need the claude.ai login itself — claude.ai connectors, `/schedule` routines, and Remote Control sessions. They are unavailable while a profile or federation source is selected, and a `setup-token` credential cannot reach them either, though locally configured MCP servers still work.

nodes.label: Claude Code on the Web credentials
nodes.rationale: Claude Code on the Web always uses your subscription credentials: setting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in the sandbox environment does not override them.

nodes.label: Claude Code changelog page
nodes.rationale: Release notes for Claude Code, including new features, improvements, and bug fixes by version. The page is generated from CHANGELOG.md on GitHub (anthropics/claude-code); `claude --version` reports the installed version. Entries run from 0.2.21 (April 2, 2025) to 2.1.257 (September 1, 2026).

nodes.label: Versioned Update entry
nodes.rationale: Each release is one `<Update label="<version>" description="<date>">` block whose bullets are prefixed by verb class — Added, Fixed, Improved, Changed, Removed, Deprecated — plus platform-scoped prefixes such as `[VSCode]`, `[SDK]`, `[IDE]`, `Windows:`, and `Bedrock:`. Some releases carry only 'Bug fixes and reliability improvements'.

nodes.label: Model release cadence
nodes.rationale: New Claude models ship as a Claude Code release that both adds the model and makes it the default for its family, requiring users to update the CLI for access. The changelog shows the sequence Sonnet 4/Opus 4 (1.0.0), Opus 4.1, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Opus 5, Fable 5.1.

nodes.label: Claude Fable 5.1
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.257 (September 1, 2026) as `claude-fable-5-1` and the new default Fable model: 1M context, $10/$50 per Mtok with $0.25/Mtok cache reads. The `fable` and `best` aliases in Claude apps gateway sessions keep resolving to Fable 5 because gateways not yet configured for 5.1 reject it; users pick 5.1 explicitly in `/model`.

nodes.label: Claude Opus 5
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.219 (July 24, 2026) as `claude-opus-5`, the default Opus model, with 1M context and fast mode at $10/$50 per Mtok. In 2.1.251 Opus 5 became the default model for seat-based Enterprise subscriptions, matching other premium plans.

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet 5
nodes.rationale: Introduced in 2.1.197 (June 30, 2026) as the default model in Claude Code, with a native 1M-token context window and promotional $2/$10 per Mtok pricing through August 31; 2.1.243 made $2/$10 its standard list price. 2.1.247 changed its default auto-compact window to the full 1M context, so sessions auto-compact near 967K tokens.

nodes.label: Claude Fable 5
nodes.rationale: Introduced in 2.1.170 (June 9, 2026) as a Mythos-class model made safe for general use, described as exceeding the capabilities of any previously generally-available model. Fable access is gated on usage credits, consented through `/model fable`, and Fable is offered as an advisor model in `/advisor`. Fable 5 model IDs include 1M context by default, so a `[1m]` suffix is stripped automatically (2.1.173).

nodes.label: Claude Opus 4.8
nodes.rationale: Shipped in 2.1.154 (May 28, 2026) defaulting to high effort with `/effort xhigh` for the hardest tasks, and fast mode at 2x the standard rate for 2.5x the speed. 2.1.207 made Opus 4.8 the default on Bedrock, Vertex, and Claude Platform on AWS.

nodes.label: Claude Opus 4.6
nodes.rationale: Released in 2.1.32 (February 5, 2026). 2.1.75 gave it a 1M context window by default for Max, Team, and Enterprise plans (previously requiring extra usage); 2.1.36 brought fast mode to it; 2.1.68 set its default effort to medium for Max and Team subscribers, and 2.1.117 raised the Pro/Max default effort on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 to high.

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet 4.6
nodes.rationale: Support added in 2.1.45 (February 17, 2026). Sonnet 4.5 with 1M context was removed from the Max plan in favour of Sonnet 4.6 (2.1.49), and 2.1.69 automatically migrated Sonnet 4.5 users on Pro/Max/Team Premium to Sonnet 4.6.

nodes.label: Claude Haiku 4.5 and the Explore agent
nodes.rationale: Haiku 4.5 was added to the model selector in 2.0.17 (October 15, 2025), automatically using Sonnet in plan mode and Haiku for execution, and powering the new Explore subagent for context-efficient codebase search. 2.1.198 later changed the built-in Explore agent to inherit the main session's model (capped at Opus) rather than running on Haiku.

nodes.label: 1M-token context window
nodes.rationale: A 1M context window became a per-model native capability rather than an add-on: Opus 4.6 got it by default for Max/Team/Enterprise (2.1.75), Opus 4.7 natively (2.1.117 fixed Claude Code computing against 200K instead), Sonnet 5 and Fable 5 natively, and model IDs carry a `[1m]` suffix that is normalized away where the window is native (2.1.173).

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.50 to disable 1M context support. 2.1.223 broadened it to hold EVERY Claude model with a native 1M window to 200K via auto-compaction rather than a fixed list, and added a startup warning when auto-compaction is not holding the session to 200K. The same release made auto-compact keep unrecognized model IDs inside an assumed window, with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_UNKNOWN_MODEL_WINDOW_ENFORCEMENT=1` to restore the old behaviour.

nodes.label: Reasoning effort levels
nodes.rationale: `/effort` (added 2.1.76) sets the model's reasoning effort; 2.1.72 simplified levels to low/medium/high, 2.1.111 added `xhigh` for Opus 4.7 between high and max plus an interactive slider, and 2.1.94 changed the default from medium to high for API-key, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, Team and Enterprise users. 2.1.251 made `/effort` save a default per model; 2.1.257 added `s` for session-only change and made `--effort` lift a new model's default-effort hold for that session only. Effort is exposed to hooks (`$CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `effort.level`), skills (`${CLAUDE_EFFORT}`), the status line, and OTel.

nodes.label: Fast mode
nodes.rationale: `/fast` trades price for speed on Opus-family models. It reached Opus 4.6 in 2.1.36, defaulted to Opus 4.7 in 2.1.142, became far cheaper on Opus 4.8 in 2.1.154 (2x rate for 2.5x speed), and 2.1.219 removed Opus 4.7 from fast mode so `/fast` applies to Opus 5 and Opus 4.8. `CLAUDE_CODE_OPUS_4_6_FAST_MODE_OVERRIDE` was deprecated then made a no-op in 2.1.160.

nodes.label: Model selection settings and env vars
nodes.rationale: Model resolution is layered: `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL` alias pins (1.0.88) with `_NAME`/`_DESCRIPTION`/`_SUPPORTS` display and capability overrides (2.1.84), `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL` for the model new sessions start on while `/model` still overrides and persists (2.1.236), `modelOverrides` to map picker entries to provider IDs such as Bedrock ARNs (2.1.73), `modelPicker` to curate the list (2.1.243), `fallbackModel` for up to three ordered fallbacks (2.1.166), and `availableModels`/`enforceAvailableModels` org allowlists (2.1.175, 2.1.187).

nodes.label: /model default-vs-session scope reversal
nodes.rationale: The meaning of a `/model` pick flipped twice. In 2.1.144 `/model` changed the CURRENT SESSION only, with `d` in the picker to set a default for new sessions. In 2.1.153 it changed again to SAVE the selection as the default (matching the IDE), with `s` for session-only — and the `modelPicker:setAsDefault` keybinding was renamed `modelPicker:thisSessionOnly`.

nodes.label: Permission system
nodes.rationale: Tool use is gated by permission rules (allow/ask/deny) held in settings files across user, project, local and managed scopes, surfaced by `/permissions` (renamed from `/allowed-tools` in 1.0.7) and by per-call approval dialogs. The changelog's largest recurring category is closing bypasses in this system and reducing false prompts.

nodes.label: Permission modes
nodes.rationale: Sessions run in one of several modes cycled with Shift+Tab: manual (renamed from 'default' across CLI, `--help`, VS Code and JetBrains in 2.1.200, with `--permission-mode manual` and `"defaultMode": "manual"` accepted alongside `default`), acceptEdits, plan, auto, and bypassPermissions. 2.1.257 made `defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in project `.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json` be IGNORED, like `"auto"` — it must be set in user or managed settings or passed as `--permission-mode`.

nodes.label: Auto mode
nodes.rationale: A permission mode in which an LLM safety classifier adjudicates tool calls instead of a static analyzer. It progressively lost its gates: `--enable-auto-mode` dropped in 2.1.111, opt-in consent removed in 2.1.152, `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_AUTO_MODE` no longer needed on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry in 2.1.207, and `disableAutoMode` became the way to turn it off. Rules live under `settings.autoMode` (`allow`, `soft_deny`, `hard_deny`, `environment`, `classifyAllShell`, `$defaults`) and are editable from a `/permissions` Auto mode tab (2.1.246).

nodes.label: Auto mode safety classifier
nodes.rationale: The model-backed check that grants or denies each auto-mode tool call. 2.1.210 pinned it to Sonnet 5 by default for external sessions, validated on the session's first request. It progressively absorbed decisions from static analysis — subagent spawns (2.1.178), `SendMessage` sends (2.1.222), dangerous-rm / background-`&` / suspicious-Windows-path checks (2.1.218), plan-mode Bash the analyzer cannot prove read-only (2.1.218), and Monitor commands (2.1.236) — and denials surface in `/permissions` Recent with `r` to retry.

nodes.label: Containment Escape rule
nodes.rationale: Added to auto mode in 2.1.257: cloud metadata-credential fetches, egress evasion, and cross-tenant reach are no longer auto-approved unless the environment marks them expected. It sits alongside earlier auto-mode safety rules blocking destructive git commands, `terraform`/`pulumi`/`cdk destroy`, session-transcript tampering, and bulk repository exfiltration.

nodes.label: Permission rule syntax
nodes.rationale: Rules are written `Tool(argument)` and gained: `*` wildcards at any position in Bash rules such as `Bash(npm *)`, `Bash(* install)`, `Bash(git * main)` (2.1.0); `mcp__server__*` MCP wildcards (2.0.70); `Task(AgentName)`/`Agent(x,y)` agent restrictions; `Tool(param:value)` input-parameter matching such as `Agent(model:opus)` (2.1.178); and glob tool-name position where `"*"` denies all tools (2.1.166). 2.1.214 narrowed single-segment `dir/**` allow rules to `<cwd>/dir` only, while deny/ask rules keep any-depth matching.

nodes.label: Bash permission-check hardening
nodes.rationale: A continuous stream of fixes where the shell parser and the permission analyzer disagreed: prefix-matching bypasses, shell line continuations, heredoc delimiter smuggling, `env`/`sudo`/`watch`/`setsid` exec wrappers, `find -exec`/`-delete`, `< file` input redirects, `/dev/tcp` redirects, zsh `[[ ]]` regex conditionals and variable subscripts, arithmetic assignments to integer variables, dangling `&&`/`||`, and commands over 10,000 characters (which now always prompt). The stated design rule is to fail closed and prompt whenever the analyzer cannot prove a command's shape.

nodes.label: PowerShell tool
nodes.rationale: Introduced as an opt-in Windows preview in 2.1.84, controlled by `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL` (also enabling it on Linux/macOS with `pwsh` on PATH), enabled by default on Windows for Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry users in 2.1.143, and made the primary Windows shell when enabled (2.1.126). It passes `-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` unless `CLAUDE_CODE_POWERSHELL_RESPECT_EXECUTION_POLICY=1`, and carries its own permission-bypass hardening (built-in `cd` forms, `$PSDefaultParameterValues` writes, trailing `&` background jobs, quote+whitespace argument splitting).

nodes.label: Bash sandbox
nodes.rationale: A sandbox mode for the Bash tool on Linux and macOS was released in 2.0.24 and grew a large `sandbox.*` settings surface: `filesystem.allowWrite`/`denyRead`/`allowRead`/`disabled`, `network.allowedDomains`/`deniedDomains`/`strictAllowlist`/`allowMachLookup`/`enableWeakerNetworkIsolation`, `credentials`, `excludedCommands`, `allowUnsandboxedCommands`, `failIfUnavailable`, and managed `bwrapPath`/`socatPath`/`ripgrep` binary overrides. A silent disable when dependencies are missing was made a visible startup warning in 2.1.78.

nodes.label: Sandbox credential masking
nodes.rationale: Sandboxed commands can be shown sentinel credentials while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on egress: `mode: "mask"` for credential files on Linux/WSL (2.1.221, falling back to `deny` on macOS), plus `extract`/`onExtractNoMatch` for structured env values, `decode: "jwt"` with `maskClaims`, and `awsPairs`/`sigv4` for AWS SigV4 re-signing (2.1.224). These require `network.tlsTerminate` and are honored only from user, managed, or `--settings` sources.

nodes.label: --restricted mode
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.248 as `--restricted` / `CLAUDE_CODE_RESTRICTED=1`: removes the built-in tools that run commands or code plus `WebFetch` (unless named in `--tools`), keeps file tools inside the working directory, refuses `bypassPermissions`, and ignores user, project and local settings files.

nodes.label: Reduced-footprint launch modes
nodes.rationale: Several flags strip customization for speed or troubleshooting: `--bare` for scripted `-p` calls (2.1.81) skips hooks, LSP, plugin sync and skill walks and requires an API key rather than OAuth; `--safe-mode` / `CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE` (2.1.169) disables CLAUDE.md, plugins, skills, hooks and MCP for troubleshooting; `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE` (2.1.50) strips skills, session memory, custom agents, MCP tools, attachments, hooks and CLAUDE.md; and `disableBundledSkills` / `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BUNDLED_SKILLS` hides bundled skills and built-in slash commands from the model.

nodes.label: Symlink and path-traversal hardening
nodes.rationale: A recurring security class: file tools following a symlink swapped inside the working directory after the permission check (2.1.251), Grep/Glob not applying `Read(...)` denies through symlinked search paths, writes through a symlinked parent escaping the working directory in acceptEdits, workflow and scheduled-task writes following a `.claude` symlink, plugin components declared at symlinked paths reading outside the plugin (2.1.257), Windows NT-namespace `\??\` paths bypassing UNC validation (an NTLM credential-leak vector), and Cygwin-style symlinks on Windows Git Bash.

nodes.label: Hooks system
nodes.rationale: Hooks were released in 1.0.38 (June 30, 2025) and became the main programmable extension point. The event catalogue grew steadily: PreToolUse/PostToolUse, Stop/SubagentStop (split in 1.0.41), UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, SessionEnd, PreCompact, PostCompact, SubagentStart, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, Notification, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, FileChanged, InstructionsLoaded, DirectoryAdded, StopFailure, MessageDisplay, Elicitation/ElicitationResult, PostToolUseFailure, and PreModelSwitch/PostModelSwitch (2.1.251).

nodes.label: Hook invocation types
nodes.rationale: Beyond shell commands, hooks can be `type: "http"` posting and receiving JSON (2.1.63), prompt-type and agent-type hooks evaluated by a model, and `type: "mcp_tool"` invoking an MCP tool directly (2.1.118). An `args: string[]` exec form spawns without a shell so path placeholders need no quoting (2.1.139), and `once: true` plus per-command `timeout` control execution. Prompt- and agent-type hooks are rejected for `SessionStart`/`Setup`/`SubagentStart`, which require command-type hooks.

nodes.label: Hook output and blocking contract
nodes.rationale: Hooks communicate through exit code 2 plus schema-validated stdout JSON: `permissionDecision` allow/deny/ask plus `"defer"` for headless pause-and-resume (2.1.89), `updatedInput` middleware, `additionalContext`, `continue: false` with `stopReason`, `continueOnBlock` for PostToolUse, `hookSpecificOutput.sessionTitle`, `reloadSkills: true`, `updatedToolOutput`, `terminalSequence`, and `worktreePath`. Hardening made a `permissions.deny` rule always outrank a hook's `allow` or `ask`, and hook output over 50K characters is written to disk with a preview instead of injected into context.

nodes.label: Hook `if` conditions
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.85, a hook may carry an `if` field using permission-rule syntax (for example `Bash(git *)` or `Edit(src/**)`) so it only runs on matching tool calls, cutting process-spawn overhead. Repeated fixes taught it to match compound commands, env-var prefixes, `$()`/backtick substitution, and documented file-path patterns; 2.1.214 narrowed single-segment `dir/**` `if` conditions to `<cwd>/dir`, requiring `**/dir/**` for any-depth matching.

nodes.label: Claude Skills
nodes.rationale: Skills landed in 2.0.20 and were merged with slash commands in 2.1.3 as a single mental model. A skill is a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter supporting `name`, `description`, `allowed-tools`, `disallowed-tools`, `paths:` globs, `model`, `effort`, `agent`, `context: fork`, `background`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, and `argument-hint`; frontmatter keys accept kebab-, snake- and camelCase and boolean-ish `yes/no/on/off/1/0`. Skills hot-reload from `~/.claude/skills` and `.claude/skills` (2.1.0), load from nested `.claude/skills` directories with `<dir>:<name>` disambiguation (2.1.178), and expose `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`, `${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}` and `${CLAUDE_EFFORT}`.

nodes.label: Skill listing budget and truncation
nodes.rationale: The system prompt's skill listing is size-capped, and the cap moved repeatedly: descriptions capped at 250 characters in 2.1.86, raised to 1,536 in 2.1.105 with a startup warning when truncated, and scaled to 2% of the model's context window in 2.1.32. `skillOverrides` controls per-skill visibility (`off`, `user-invocable-only`, `name-only`), and truncation is reported through `/doctor` rather than a startup notification.

nodes.label: Bundled skills
nodes.rationale: Claude Code ships first-party skills including `/claude-api` (2.1.69, with `upgrade`, `cost-optimize` and `prompt-audit` subcommands and Admin API coverage), `/dataviz` (2.1.198), `/less-permission-prompts` (2.1.111), `/team-onboarding`, `/powerup`, and a `workflow-authoring` reference. Their context cost is actively managed: the `claude-api` skill dropped from ~200k+ to ~25k tokens by loading references on demand (2.1.234), and the Workflow tool's description shrank from 5.7k to about 1k tokens (2.1.248).

nodes.label: Plugin system
nodes.rationale: Released in 2.0.12 (October 9, 2025) to extend Claude Code with custom commands, agents, hooks, and MCP servers from marketplaces, via `/plugin install`, `/plugin enable/disable`, `/plugin marketplace`, and `claude plugin validate`. Plugins later gained skills, LSP servers, themes, monitors, output styles, `bin/` executables, `settings.json` defaults, `userConfig` options with keychain-backed `sensitive: true` values, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` variables, `defaultEnabled: false`, dependency resolution with version pinning, and `claude plugin init/tag/prune/details`.

nodes.label: Plugin marketplace sources
nodes.rationale: Marketplaces resolve plugins from a growing set of source types: `github`/`git` (with `#branch`/`@ref` fragments, SHA pinning, `skipLfs`, and bare gitlab.com URLs including nested subgroups), `git-subdir` for a subdirectory of a repo, `npm` with custom registries and version pinning, `archive` for a zip over HTTPS with optional SHA-256 pinning (2.1.224), `command` where a local program prints the plugin directory and is re-resolved each session (2.1.229), `settings` for inline entries in settings.json, and local directory/zip paths via `--plugin-dir` or `--plugin-url`. A `headersHelper` can mint short-lived HTTP headers for catalog and archive fetches (2.1.238).

nodes.label: Managed plugin and marketplace policy
nodes.rationale: Administrators constrain plugins through `extraKnownMarketplaces` (aliased `additionalMarketplaces`), `strictKnownMarketplaces` (aliased `allowedMarketplaces`) with `hostPattern`/`pathPattern` regexes and `"owner/*"` wildcards, `blockedMarketplaces`, `pluginSuggestionMarketplaces`, `pluginTrustMessage`, and `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`. Enforcement was extended across install, update, refresh and autoupdate, and blocked plugins are hidden from marketplace views rather than merely failing to install.

nodes.label: Subagents
nodes.rationale: Custom subagents arrived in 1.0.60 (`/agents`, later removed as a wizard in 2.1.198 in favour of editing `.claude/agents/` or asking Claude). Agent markdown frontmatter accumulated `model`, `tools`, `disallowedTools`, `permissionMode`, `memory`, `skills`, `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `isolation: worktree`, `background: true`, `effort`, `maxTurns`, `initialPrompt`, and `experimental.cacheTtl`; agent names may not contain `:`, which is reserved for plugin namespacing.

nodes.label: Background-by-default subagents
nodes.rationale: 2.1.198 (July 1, 2026) made subagents run in the background by default so Claude keeps working while they run and is notified when they finish, ending a gradual rollout. 2.1.232 extended this: subagent forking is on by default, a `subagent_type: "fork"` subagent inherits the full conversation and prompt cache, and non-teammate agent spawns in interactive sessions run in the background by default.

nodes.label: Subagent nesting depth and spawn caps
nodes.rationale: Nesting oscillated: 2.1.172 allowed subagents to spawn subagents up to 5 levels, 2.1.217 turned nesting off by default behind `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`, and 2.1.219 set the default depth to 3. Runaway fan-out is bounded by `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS` (default 20, 2.1.217) and a per-session `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENTS_PER_SESSION` (default 200, 2.1.212) — while 2.1.224 removed the older hard 200-agent-per-session spawn cap. `--max-budget-usd` also halts and denies background spawns once reached.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL precedence change
nodes.rationale: 2.1.251 changed `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` to set the DEFAULT subagent model rather than override everything: an agent definition's `model:` and an explicit per-spawn model now take precedence over it. 2.1.257 then added `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE` to restore the old behaviour of applying the env var (or the main model) to every subagent, ignoring per-spawn and agent-definition overrides.

nodes.label: Agent view (`claude agents`)
nodes.rationale: Added as a Research Preview in 2.1.139: a single list of every Claude Code session — running, blocked on you, or done — opened with `claude agents` or by pressing `←`. It gained `--json` scripting output with `id`, `state`, `waitingFor` and `--all`, dispatch flags (`--add-dir`, `--settings`, `--mcp-config`, `--plugin-dir`, `--permission-mode`, `--model`, `--effort`, `--agent`, `--cwd`, `--dangerously-skip-permissions`), Needs input / Working / Completed grouping, PR links, pinning with Ctrl+T, and `! <command>` to run a shell command as an attachable background session.

nodes.label: Background sessions and daemon
nodes.rationale: Background agents landed in 2.0.60 and grew into a full daemon-backed session tier: `claude --bg`, `/background`, `←` to detach, plus `attach`, `logs`, `stop`, `respawn` and `rm` subcommands (listed in `claude --help` from 2.1.251). Sessions survive retire→wake carrying their flags, upgrade to a new binary in the background, are shed under memory pressure, and by 2.1.221 commit and push to preserve work, opening a draft PR only when the task calls for one and always reporting where the work lives.

nodes.label: Agent teams
nodes.rationale: A token-intensive research preview behind `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`, added in 2.1.32, where teammates run in tmux/iTerm2 panes or in-process. 2.1.178 removed the `TeamCreate`/`TeamDelete` tools: every session now has one implicit team and teammates are spawned directly with the Agent tool's `name` parameter, with `team_name` accepted but ignored. Teammates inherit the leader's model and effort unless the spawn names one, and `teammateMode: "iterm2"` selects the pane backend.

nodes.label: Cross-session messaging
nodes.rationale: `SendMessage` plus `ListAgents` let Claude Code sessions message each other, added for macOS and Linux in 2.1.224 and for Windows in 2.1.239, with `@`-mention addressing by session name (2.1.232) and `notify_when_idle` one-shot idle notices (2.1.236). It is governed by `crossSessionInbound` (accept/hold/refuse) and `dialogExpiry`, uses a hardened per-user socket directory, and 2.1.166 established that relayed messages carry NO user authority — receivers refuse relayed permission requests and auto mode blocks them.

nodes.label: Remote Control
nodes.rationale: Bridges a local terminal, Desktop or IDE session to claude.ai/code so it can be continued from a browser or phone, driven by `/remote-control`, `claude remote-control` (with `--continue`, `--spawn`, `--name`) and `remoteControlAtStartup`. It is disabled when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a non-Anthropic host or under Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry, cannot be enabled by repo-local settings (2.1.222), and 2.1.257 fixed dismissing its consent prompt being counted as consent.

nodes.label: Dynamic workflows
nodes.rationale: Introduced in 2.1.154: ask Claude to create a workflow and it orchestrates tens to hundreds of background agents, viewed with `/workflows`. The trigger keyword was renamed from `workflow` to `ultracode` in 2.1.160 (highlighted in violet, with a `/config` toggle), and 2.1.219 added an advisory `workflowSizeGuideline` defaulting to medium (aim for fewer than 15 agents). Workflow scripts run in a sandbox — dynamic `import()` escape was closed in 2.1.223 — and `agent({schema})` subagents abort after 5 schema-validation failures.

nodes.label: /goal completion conditions
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.139: set a completion condition and Claude keeps working across turns until it is met, in interactive, `-p` and Remote Control, with a live elapsed/turns/tokens overlay. Later releases bounded it — check-ins on long-running background work start after 30 minutes then back off to 1h and 2h (`CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES=0` opts out), at most three check-ins per goal until the user's next message (2.1.246), and the goal clears itself with a notice when a turn dies on an unrecoverable error (2.1.234).

nodes.label: /loop and scheduled tasks
nodes.rationale: `/loop` (2.1.71) runs a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval, alongside in-session cron scheduling tools (`CronCreate`/`CronList`) disableable with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON`. `/proactive` became its alias in 2.1.105, self-paced dynamic mode and the no-prompt autonomous default became always available in 2.1.248, and `/usage` gained a Loops breakdown (per-loop run count, tokens, tokens per run, last run) in 2.1.243. Scheduled-task and webhook deliveries classify as task notifications, so they cannot approve a pending action or set the session title.

nodes.label: Git worktree isolation
nodes.rationale: `--worktree`/`-w` (2.1.49) starts a session in an isolated git worktree; subagents and workflow agents take `isolation: "worktree"`; `EnterWorktree`/`ExitWorktree` tools move a live session in and out. Settings include `worktree.baseRef` (`fresh` vs `head`, default `fresh` branching from `origin/<default>`), `worktree.sparsePaths` for monorepos, `worktree.bgIsolation: "none"`, and `.worktreeinclude`. 2.1.222 extended isolation to file edits and Bash in every session type after subagents were found redirecting git into the shared checkout via `git -C`, `--git-dir`, or `GIT_DIR`.

nodes.label: /fork, /branch and /subtask
nodes.rationale: Conversation forking changed names and shape twice: 2.1.77 renamed `/fork` to `/branch` (keeping `/fork` as an alias), then 2.1.212 reintroduced `/fork` as 'copy this conversation into a NEW BACKGROUND SESSION with its own agent-view row' while the in-session subagent it used to launch became `/subtask`. 2.1.221 gave a forked session its own worktree instead of sharing the original checkout, and 2.1.257 made `/fork` keep the original prompt cache by delivering the worktree briefing as a message rather than a system-prompt change.

nodes.label: MCP transports and server config
nodes.rationale: MCP support grew from stdio to SSE (0.2.54) and streamable HTTP (1.0.27) plus WebSocket, configured in `.mcp.json` (project scope, 0.2.50), `--mcp-config` (multiple files), settings scopes renamed local/user (0.2.49), and `claude mcp add/add-json/add-from-claude-desktop/login/logout/remove/serve`. Servers receive `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` and `CLAUDECODE=1`; `headersHelper` mints dynamic headers; `alwaysLoad`, per-server `timeout`/`request_timeout_ms`, `MCP_TIMEOUT`, `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, and `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` tune behaviour. Tool descriptions and server instructions are capped at 2KB (2.1.84).

nodes.label: MCP OAuth
nodes.rationale: Remote MCP servers gained OAuth in 1.0.27 with Authorization Server discovery (1.0.35), pre-configured `--client-id`/`--client-secret` for servers without Dynamic Client Registration (2.1.30), RFC 9728 Protected Resource Metadata discovery (2.1.85), Client ID Metadata Documents / SEP-991 (2.1.81), step-up authorization on `403 insufficient_scope`, an `oauth.authServerMetadataUrl` override, and manual URL paste fallback. A long tail of fixes addressed refresh-token races across concurrent sessions, keychain contention, and `127.0.0.1`-vs-`localhost` redirect URIs.

nodes.label: MCP tool search and deferral
nodes.rationale: When MCP tool descriptions exceed a share of the context window their schemas are deferred and discovered on demand via a search tool instead of loaded upfront. 2.1.7 enabled auto mode for all users at a 10%-of-context threshold, disableable by adding `MCPSearch` to `disallowedTools`; `auto:N` (2.1.9) sets the threshold as a context-window percentage; `alwaysLoad` on a server opts its tools out of deferral. Tool search is disabled by default on Vertex AI (opt in with `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`) and is detected as unsupported behind third-party gateways.

nodes.label: Enterprise MCP allow/deny policy
nodes.rationale: Administrators gate MCP through managed `allowedMcpServers`/`deniedMcpServers` (2.0.22), a deployed `managed-mcp.json`, `allowAllClaudeAiMcps` (2.1.149), and `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`. Enforcement was repeatedly extended to reconnects, IDE-typed configs, `--mcp-config`, subagent frontmatter servers, and the first session after install, and `${VAR}` references in policy entries resolve from the startup environment and managed-settings env rather than settings-file env.

nodes.label: MCP elicitation
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.76: MCP servers can request structured input mid-task through an interactive dialog (form fields or a browser URL), with new `Elicitation` and `ElicitationResult` hooks to intercept and override responses before they are returned to the server.

nodes.label: claude.ai MCP connectors
nodes.rationale: Support for using claude.ai MCP connectors inside Claude Code was added in 2.1.46, opt-out via `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false`. Connectors deduplicate against identically-configured local servers (local config wins), show a `managed` marker when their auth is organization-managed, collapse behind a 'Show unused connectors' row in `/mcp`, and are disabled — along with Remote Control, `/schedule` and notification preferences — when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `apiKeyHelper` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is set.

nodes.label: Managed and server-managed settings
nodes.rationale: Enterprise managed settings arrived in 2.0.68 and expanded to macOS plist and Windows Registry sources (2.1.51), a `managed-settings.d/` drop-in directory merging alphabetically (2.1.83), WSL inheritance of Windows settings, `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` fail-closed startup, `requiredMinimumVersion`/`requiredMaximumVersion`, `parentSettingsBehavior`, `managedSourcesBehavior`, and a `Skipped sources` line in `/status`. The Windows path moved from `C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode` to `C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode`, with the old fallback removed in 2.1.75.

nodes.label: Managed-settings security approval prompt
nodes.rationale: Server-delivered settings that could weaken security require explicit user approval before applying, and the dialog lists only what changed since last approval. 2.1.251 extended approval to settings that terminate sandbox TLS, route sandbox traffic through a proxy, inject credentials or weaken sandbox isolation, and to `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` from managed or project settings that set a credential, org/tenant, routing or API-behavior header. Benign feature, cost, timeout, MCP-startup-mode and routine OpenTelemetry toggles were exempted so the prompt stays meaningful.

nodes.label: Narrowing what project settings may do
nodes.rationale: A repeated direction of travel is stripping powers from repo-resident settings, since a checked-in file is attacker-controlled: `autoMode` no longer read from `.claude/settings.local.json` (2.1.207), `pluginConfigs` no longer read from project settings (2.1.207), `sandbox.ripgrep` honored only from user/managed/`--settings` (2.1.232), Remote Control auto-start not enableable by repo-local settings (2.1.222), project settings unable to enable detailed beta tracing or raw API body logging (2.1.251), project `env` unable to set `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`/`CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR`/`TMPDIR` (2.1.251), and `defaultMode: bypassPermissions` ignored in project settings (2.1.257).

nodes.label: Workspace trust
nodes.rationale: A per-directory trust dialog gates features that execute repo-controlled content. Fixes made it stricter over time: nested git repositories no longer inherit trust from a parent (2.1.232), `statusLine` and `fileSuggestion` hook commands require trust acceptance (2.1.51), agent-frontmatter hooks require the agent file's own folder to be trusted (2.1.218), project `.mcp.json` `headersHelper` and inline agent-file MCP servers require the folder's trust dialog (2.1.238), and `claude mcp list`/`get` no longer spawn `.mcp.json` servers self-approved by a committed `.claude/settings.json` (2.1.196).

nodes.label: Third-party model providers
nodes.rationale: Claude Code runs against Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Foundry (2.0.45), Bedrock powered by Mantle (`CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE=1`, 2.1.94), Claude Platform on AWS, and Anthropic-compatible gateways via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. A recurring theme is closing the feature gap: auto mode, `/radio`, `/code-review`, `/loop`, cross-session messaging, session recap, the fullscreen offer, streaming tool execution and immediate `/model`//`fast`//`effort` all reached these providers in later releases, and interactive Bedrock (2.1.92) and Vertex (2.1.98) setup wizards were added to the login screen.

nodes.label: Claude apps gateway
nodes.rationale: An organization-operated gateway that fronts Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS upstreams, with sign-in through `/login`, spend limits surfaced in `/usage` and a `rate_limits.spend_limit` status-line field (2.1.251), a `desktop:` settings overlay validated against Desktop's schema, `forward_user_identity` per-user spend attribution, model discovery behind `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1`, and pinned-TLS verification for sign-in and token refresh (2.1.257).

nodes.label: Self-hosted environments
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.224: `claude self-hosted-runner` turns your own machines or containers into a place Claude Code web, mobile, and desktop sessions can run, on Team and Enterprise plans. It gained `--base-dir` (required on Windows), `--client-label`/`SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER_CLIENT_LABEL`, `--defer-shutdown-max-min` for graceful SIGTERM draining, `--proxy-authorization-command`/`--proxy-authorization-file` for egress proxies, `--configure-git` push negotiation, and server-supplied hook support.

nodes.label: Cloud sessions and Claude Code on the web
nodes.rationale: Sessions can run in Anthropic-hosted containers reached from the web, desktop and mobile apps, set up with `/web-setup` and continued locally with `claude --teleport <session id>`. They carry a network proxy that applies the environment's allowed domains, seed from the local repo's uncommitted changes (with credential-file and swap/temp copies excluded, 2.1.248), and recover across container restarts by re-running the interrupted turn.

nodes.label: /code-review and /ultrareview
nodes.rationale: `/simplify` was renamed `/code-review` in 2.1.147 and now reports correctness bugs at a chosen effort level with `--comment` to post inline GitHub PR comments (GitLab MR notes via `glab mr note` from 2.1.257) and `--fix` to apply findings; `/simplify` reverted to a cleanup-only review in 2.1.154 and `/review` became an alias of `/code-review` in 2.1.223. `/ultrareview` (2.1.111) runs a deep multi-agent review in a cloud session, also available as the non-interactive `claude ultrareview [target]` subcommand for CI. 2.1.215 stopped Claude from running `/verify` and `/code-review` on its own.

nodes.label: Prompt caching controls
nodes.rationale: Prompt-cache health is treated as a first-class cost lever: `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H` and `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` env vars (2.1.108), `promptCacheTtl` and `subagentPromptCacheTtl` settings plus per-agent `experimental.cacheTtl` frontmatter, a `/cost` prompt-cache line and `prompt_cache` status-line object (2.1.251), and a `/model`//`effort` warning before a change that would re-read history uncached. Dozens of fixes target silent cache busts from rotating tokens, changing tool schemas, re-injected CLAUDE.md, workflow fan-out prefixes, and mid-conversation system blocks behind gateways.

nodes.label: Context management and compaction
nodes.rationale: Automatic conversation compaction shipped in 0.2.47 and is inspected with `/context` (1.0.86) and forced with `/compact`. Guards accumulated: a circuit breaker after 3 failed auto-compactions (2.1.76), a thrash-loop detector when context refills immediately after compacting three times (2.1.89), `DISABLE_COMPACT` and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS`, PreCompact hooks able to block compaction, PostCompact hooks, and 'Summarize from here' / 'Summarize up to here' partial summarization. Tool results over 50K characters are persisted to disk rather than kept inline (2.1.51).

nodes.label: Memory and CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md gained `@path/to/file.md` imports (0.2.107) and `.claude/rules/*.md` with `paths:` frontmatter (2.0.64); the `#` quick-memory shortcut was removed in 2.0.70. Claude began automatically saving and recalling memories in 2.1.32/2.1.59, managed with `/memory`, stored under an `autoMemoryDirectory`, indexed by a `MEMORY.md` capped at 200 lines and 25KB, carrying ISO `modified` timestamps, and shared across git worktrees of one repository. `claudeMdExcludes`, `CLAUDE_MEMORY_STORES`, and a context-window-scaled 'CLAUDE.md is too long' warning bound its footprint; HTML comments in CLAUDE.md are hidden from auto-injection (2.1.72).

nodes.label: Native binary distribution
nodes.rationale: 2.1.113 changed the CLI to spawn a native Claude Code binary via a per-platform optional dependency instead of bundled JavaScript, after 2.1.15 deprecated npm installs. Native builds replace the `Glob` and `Grep` tools with embedded `bfs` and `ugrep` reachable through the Bash tool (2.1.117), and size and memory were cut repeatedly — zstd compression taking Linux x64 downloads from ~340 MB to ~75 MB, on-demand code loading saving 40–70 MB per session, and dropping six rarely used syntax-highlighting languages saving 2.5 MB (2.1.251).

nodes.label: Fullscreen renderer
nodes.rationale: Flicker-free alt-screen rendering with virtualized scrollback began as `CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1` (2.1.89), became `/tui fullscreen` plus a `tui` setting (2.1.110), gained mouse selection, click, wheel scroll and auto-copy-on-select, and was offered on first launch (with the offer capped at three launches and extended to Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry in 2.1.239). `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ALTERNATE_SCREEN=1`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS`, `autoScrollEnabled` and `wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled` opt out of parts of it; a failed start now falls back to the classic renderer instead of exiting.

nodes.label: Screen-reader mode
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.208 as opt-in plain-text rendering via `claude --ax-screen-reader`, `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER=1`, or `"axScreenReader": true`. It gained deletion announcements for word and line kills, permission-mode change announcements, numbered-list rendering of the `/effort` selector, native-cursor tracking so magnifiers follow focus, and per-turn heading navigation plus live announcements in the VS Code extension (2.1.236).

nodes.label: Customizable keybindings
nodes.rationale: 2.1.18 added `~/.claude/keybindings.json` with per-context bindings and chord sequences, configured through `/keybindings`. Bindable actions grew to include `chat:newline`, `chat:submit`, `chat:killAgents`, `chat:fastMode`, `selection:copy`, `selection:clear`, `voice:pushToTalk`, `modelPicker:thisSessionOnly`, and an `Agents` context (2.1.257). A `keybindingFlavor: "readline"` setting (2.1.238) makes word keys behave as in Bash; an unknown action name is now skipped so the default binding survives rather than deadening the key.

nodes.label: Status line
nodes.rationale: `/statusline` (1.0.71) runs a user command whose stdin JSON grew to carry session cost, `exceeds_200k_tokens`, `context_window` with `used_percentage`/`remaining_percentage`, `current_usage`, `rate_limits` (5-hour and 7-day windows with `used_percentage` and `resets_at`), `effort.level`, `thinking.enabled`, `workspace.git_worktree`, `added_dirs`, GitHub repo and PR information, a `prompt_cache` object, and `rate_limits.spend_limit`. `refreshInterval` re-runs it every N seconds, and `COLUMNS`/`LINES` are exported so scripts can size output.

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry instrumentation
nodes.rationale: OTel metrics, logs and traces expose usage, cost, tool decisions and agent structure, with events such as `claude_code.assistant_response`, `skill_activated`, `at_mention`, `tool_result`, `tool_decision`, `pull_request.count` and `active_time.total`, and attributes including `agent_id`/`parent_agent_id`, `workflow.run_id`/`workflow.name`, `message.uuid`, `client_request_id`, `tool_source`, `effort`, `speed` and `app.entrypoint`. Content logging is opt-in through `OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS`, `OTEL_LOG_ASSISTANT_RESPONSES`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS`, `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT` and `OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES`, with a 60 KB content cap tunable by `CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_CONTENT_MAX_LENGTH`.

nodes.label: /usage, /cost and usage credits
nodes.rationale: 2.1.118 merged `/cost` and `/stats` into `/usage`, which reports plan limits and a per-category breakdown of what drives them — skills, subagents, plugins, per-MCP-server cost, large session files, and a Loops breakdown. 'Extra usage' was renamed 'usage credits' with `/extra-usage` becoming `/usage-credits` (2.1.144), a `modelPricing` managed setting lets an organization use contracted rates instead of list price for `/cost`, the status line and telemetry (2.1.243), and `--max-budget-usd` caps spend including background subagents.

nodes.label: Read-before-edit rule relaxations
nodes.rationale: Edit historically required a prior Read of the same file. That was progressively relaxed: `sed -n`/`cat` views satisfy it (2.1.89), `head`/`tail` views satisfy it (2.1.144), single-file `grep`/`egrep`/`fgrep` satisfy it (2.1.160), and 2.1.228 changed the Write tool so newer models can overwrite an unread existing file, matching Edit's rules, while older models still require the read first.

nodes.label: Todo/task tools removed on newer models
nodes.rationale: 2.1.233 made `TaskCreate`/`TaskGet`/`TaskUpdate`/`TaskList` and `TodoWrite` unavailable on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5 and newer models, restorable with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1`. This reversed the 2.1.16 direction, which had introduced a new task-management system with dependency tracking (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TASKS=false` kept the old one), itself replacing the Todo list added in 0.2.93.

nodes.label: LSP tool
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.0.74 for code intelligence — go-to-definition, find references, hover documentation — with servers supplied by plugins, a `startupTimeout` setting, `clientInfo` identification to language servers, and a `workspaceSymbol` operation taking a `query`. It is only enabled when LSP servers are configured, restarts a crashed server on the next request, and its `findReferences` no longer returns results from gitignored directories.

nodes.label: Monitor tool
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.98 for streaming events from background scripts, with plugins able to declare background `monitors` that auto-arm at session start or on skill invoke (2.1.105). 2.1.236 made auto mode set aside `Monitor` allow rules so Monitor commands are reviewed like Bash commands, and 2.1.257 made `claude -p` wait for an armed Monitor to fire or time out rather than exiting about five seconds after its final result.

nodes.label: EndConversation tool
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.214: Claude can end sessions with highly abusive users or jailbreak attempts, matching behaviour present on claude.ai since 2025, and the entry links Anthropic's research post on ending a subset of conversations.

nodes.label: SendFeedback tool
nodes.rationale: Added in 2.1.247: when something goes wrong in a session, Claude can draft a feedback report for the user to review and send from `/feedback`, turned off with the `feedbackDrafts` setting.

nodes.label: Claude in Chrome
nodes.rationale: A Chrome-extension browser-control integration added in beta in 2.0.72 and made generally available in 2.1.198, with `/chrome` browser selection, per-session tab-group isolation closed on `/clear` and exit, and 2.1.251 routing all browser actions through Claude Code's own permission checks — including in telemetry-disabled sessions, which previously used the extension's own prompts.

nodes.label: Output styles
nodes.rationale: Released in 1.0.81 with built-in Explanatory and Learning styles, deprecated in 2.0.30 in favour of system-prompt flags, then un-deprecated in 2.0.32 after community feedback. `/output-style` was deprecated again in 2.1.73 in favour of `/config`, with the style fixed at session start for better prompt caching; plugins can ship styles, `keep-coding-instructions` frontmatter preserves coding guidance, and a built-in 'Concise' style was added in 2.1.237.

nodes.label: Claude Agent SDK
nodes.rationale: TypeScript and Python SDKs shipped in 1.0.23; 2.0.0 renamed the Claude Code SDK to the Claude Agent SDK and 2.0.25 removed the legacy entrypoint in favour of `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`. The SDK surface grew `canUseTool`, custom tool callbacks, hook timeouts, `SDKRateLimitInfo`/`SDKRateLimitEvent`, `SDKUserMessageReplay`, `--include-partial-messages`, `--forward-subagent-text`, `--json-schema` structured output, `setMcpServers()`, `register_repo_root`, and model-capability fields `supportsEffort`/`supportedEffortLevels`/`supportsAdaptiveThinking`.

nodes.label: Headless mode and stream-json
nodes.rationale: Print mode (`-p`) gained `--output-format=stream-json` streaming in 0.2.66 and nested message objects in `--print` JSON in 0.2.117 (a breaking change for forwards compatibility). The init event carries `mcp_server_errors` and `plugin_errors`; `--input-format stream-json` accepts client-injected messages; SIGTERM aborts the turn, kills the process tree and exits 143; and `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections` improves cross-user prompt caching.

nodes.label: Credential isolation across providers
nodes.rationale: A recurring defect class is a credential intended for one host being sent to another: telemetry requests to Anthropic carrying a third-party gateway's API key (2.1.246, fixed so a credential is only sent to its own host), a custom gateway receiving the user's Anthropic OAuth credential (2.1.153), a leftover Anthropic key or auth token sent alongside a Foundry subscription key (2.1.257), stray host `Authorization` or profile headers reaching Foundry/Vertex/Bedrock, and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1` (2.1.83) stripping Anthropic and cloud-provider credentials from Bash, hook and MCP subprocess environments.

nodes.label: Session transcripts, resume and retention
nodes.rationale: Sessions persist as JSONL transcripts resumable with `--continue`/`--resume` (0.2.93), `/resume`, named sessions via `/rename` (2.0.64), `--from-pr`, and `--teleport`. Retention is governed by `cleanupPeriodDays`, which was extended to cover `~/.claude/tasks/`, `shell-snapshots/` and `backups/` (2.1.117), rejected at `0` because that silently disabled persistence (2.1.89), and given a `desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays` exemption cap after desktop-written sessions were found disappearing at 30 days (2.1.248).

nodes.label: Long-session memory and performance program
nodes.rationale: A sustained, release-after-release campaign against unbounded growth in long sessions: MCP stdio stderr capped, SSE frames capped at 16 MB, LSP documents held in a 50-doc LRU, the file-edit read cache bounded to 16 MB, transcripts pruned of superseded file-history backups (up to 79x smaller in edit-heavy sessions), subagent tool results released once out of the display window, Yoga WASM linear memory reset, and message normalization made linear rather than quadratic. Many entries pair a leak fix with a measured saving (for example ~426KB, ~16MB, ~400MB, 3x, 68%).

nodes.label: Deprecations and removals
nodes.rationale: Things removed outright include the `/agents` wizard, `/tag`, `/vim`, `/ultraplan` and ultraplan itself, the `TeamCreate`/`TeamDelete` tools, the Task tool's `mode` and `resume` parameters, `AgentOutputTool`/`BashOutputTool` (folded into `TaskOutputTool`, itself later deprecated in favour of `Read` on the output file), the legacy SDK entrypoint, `claude config` commands, the `#` memory shortcut, `.claude.json` `allowedTools`/`ignorePatterns`/`env`/`todoFeatureEnabled`, `DEBUG=true` (replaced by `ANTHROPIC_LOG=debug`), `CLAUDE_CODE_OPUS_4_6_FAST_MODE_OVERRIDE`, the Windows `C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode` managed-settings path, and the 200-subagent-per-session cap.

nodes.label: gateway.yaml config file
nodes.rationale: A Claude apps gateway deployment is configured by one YAML file, conventionally gateway.yaml, which defines where the gateway listens, how developers sign in, where inference goes, and which policies and telemetry apply. The gateway reads it once at startup via `claude gateway --config /path/to/gateway.yaml`.

nodes.label: Boot-time schema validation
nodes.rationale: Every option is validated against a schema at boot, so a malformed config fails at start with a field-level error rather than at first use. Unknown keys fail boot, so a typo surfaces as a named error rather than a silently ignored setting.

nodes.label: Secret expansion (${VAR} and ${file:/path})
nodes.rationale: Secrets such as client_secret, jwt_secret and postgres_url are referenced rather than written inline: ${VAR} resolves an environment variable (boot fails if undefined) and ${file:/path} resolves the trimmed contents of an absolute path. The file form must be the field's entire value and is not expanded inside a longer string, so a database password belongs in store.password rather than embedded in postgres_url.

nodes.label: listen section
nodes.rationale: A required section controlling where the gateway serves: host (default 0.0.0.0), port (default 8080), the externally visible public_url, optional TLS termination via tls.cert / tls.key, and trusted_proxies.

nodes.label: listen.public_url
nodes.rationale: The externally visible https:// origin used to build the IdP redirect_uri and discovery metadata. Required whenever host is not a loopback address, because the gateway never derives its own origin from client-spoofable X-Forwarded-* headers; boot fails without it. It is also required to enable telemetry, since the gateway builds the OTLP endpoint it pushes to clients from this URL.

nodes.label: listen.trusted_proxies
nodes.rationale: CIDRs or IPs of load balancers in front of the gateway. When set, the gateway trusts X-Forwarded-For only from these peers and records the real client IP for per-IP rate limiting and audit — equivalent to nginx set_real_ip_from. It governs client-IP resolution only, not origin derivation.

nodes.label: oidc section
nodes.rationale: A required section connecting the gateway to the organization's identity provider and deciding who can sign in: issuer (must serve /.well-known/openid-configuration), client_id/client_secret, claim mapping, and restriction by allowed_email_domains or allowed_groups. An id_token whose email_verified claim is explicitly false is always rejected.

nodes.label: oidc.allowed_groups matching semantics
nodes.rationale: Restricts sign-in to members of the listed IdP groups; a user in an allowed email domain but in none of these groups is rejected. Matching is an exact, case-sensitive string comparison and the gateway does not expand nested groups, so a sub-group must be listed explicitly or the IdP must emit flattened membership.

nodes.label: oidc.groups_claim
nodes.rationale: Names which id_token claim carries group membership, defaulting to `groups`. Microsoft Entra emits app roles under `roles`. The field accepts a flat key or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer such as /resource_access/gateway/roles for nested claims.

nodes.label: oidc.google_groups Directory API lookup
nodes.rationale: Because Google's id_token carries no groups claim, the gateway can look up the signed-in user's groups through the Google Workspace Admin SDK Directory API using a delegated service account and an impersonated admin_email. Each user's group email addresses become their groups claim, so allowed_groups and managed policy matchers match on group emails.

nodes.label: oidc.email_claim
nodes.rationale: Names which id_token claim carries the user's email, default `email`. Some IdPs such as ADFS and Entra B2C emit upn or preferred_username instead; the field accepts a flat key, a JSON Pointer, or a list of fallback keys where the first present key is used.

nodes.label: oidc.scopes and offline_access
nodes.rationale: scopes fully overrides the OIDC scopes the gateway requests, defaulting to [openid, profile, email, offline_access], and must include openid. Dropping offline_access disables refresh tokens, so developers re-run the browser login every session.ttl_hours.

nodes.label: oidc.use_pkce
nodes.rationale: Sends a PKCE (S256) challenge on the authorization request, default true, and should be set false only if the IdP rejects PKCE for this confidential client. PKCE is one of the gateway-managed protocol params that extra_auth_params cannot override.

nodes.label: oidc.use_proxy — IdP requests through a forward proxy
nodes.rationale: Inference upstreams honor HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY on every version, but the gateway's own discovery, JWKS, token and userinfo requests go direct unless oidc.use_proxy: true (v2.1.227 or later). With use_proxy: true the pod resolves each IdP hostname itself and asks the proxy to CONNECT to the resolved IP, so the proxy must accept CONNECT to the IP of every host the discovery document names.

nodes.label: SSRF guard and CLAUDE_GATEWAY_ALLOW_LOOPBACK
