To change the window instead, set CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW or run /autocompact where the variable is not set.

nodes.label: Subagents in cloud sessions
nodes.rationale: Subagents work the same way as locally: Claude spawns them with the Agent tool to offload research or parallel work into a separate context window, and subagents defined in the repo's .claude/agents/ are picked up automatically.

nodes.label: Agent teams are opt-in
nodes.rationale: Agent teams are off by default in cloud sessions and are enabled by adding CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1 to the environment variables.

nodes.label: Permission modes in cloud sessions
nodes.rationale: A cloud session's permission mode is chosen from the mode dropdown both at task creation and while the session runs. Reopening a session whose environment expired, or messaging one a self-hosted runner released while idle, resumes it in the permission mode it was in.

nodes.label: Review changes and inline comments
nodes.rationale: Each session shows a diff indicator with lines added and removed (for example +42 -18); selecting it opens the diff view where inline comments can be left on specific lines and sent to Claude with the next message.

nodes.label: Diffs computed from raw git blobs
nodes.rationale: Claude Code computes session diffs, including the per-file diffs shown as it edits, from raw git blob content, so diff drivers and textconv filters configured in the repository do not apply.

nodes.label: Share sessions
nodes.rationale: Sharing works by toggling a session's visibility and then sharing the session link as-is. Recipients see the latest state when they open the link, but their view does not update in real time.

nodes.label: Enterprise/Team sharing visibility
nodes.rationale: Enterprise and Team accounts choose between Private and Team visibility, where Team makes the session visible to other members of the claude.ai organization. Repository access verification is enabled by default, and the sharer's display name is visible to recipients. Claude in Slack sessions are automatically shared with Team visibility.

nodes.label: Max/Pro sharing visibility
nodes.rationale: Max and Pro accounts choose between Private and Public visibility, where Public makes the session visible to any user logged into claude.ai. Repository access verification is NOT enabled by default, so sessions should be checked for code and credentials from private repositories before sharing; Settings > Claude Code > Sharing settings can require repository access or hide the sharer's name.

nodes.label: Archive sessions
nodes.rationale: Archiving hides a session from the default session list while leaving it viewable under an archived filter; a session is archived by hovering it in the sidebar and selecting the archive icon.

nodes.label: Delete sessions
nodes.rationale: Deleting a session permanently removes the session and its data and cannot be undone. It is done from the sidebar under the archived filter or from the session menu dropdown, with a confirmation prompt.

nodes.label: Auto-fix pull requests
nodes.rationale: Auto-fix lets Claude watch a pull request and respond automatically to CI failures and review comments: it subscribes to GitHub activity on the PR, investigates each event, and pushes a fix if one is clear. It is a per-PR toggle and requires the Claude GitHub App installed on the repository.

nodes.label: Ways to turn on auto-fix
nodes.rationale: Auto-fix can be enabled from the CI status bar of a web-created PR, from the terminal with /autofix-pr on the PR's branch (Claude Code detects the PR with gh, spawns a web session, and enables auto-fix in one step), from the mobile app by asking Claude, or by pasting any PR URL into a session.

nodes.label: How Claude responds to PR activity
nodes.rationale: For each PR event Claude triages: clear fixes that do not conflict with earlier instructions are made, pushed and explained; ambiguous or architecturally significant reviewer comments are escalated to the user before acting; duplicate or no-action events are noted in the session and skipped.

nodes.label: No webhook for base-branch merge conflicts
nodes.rationale: GitHub emits no webhook when the base branch advances and creates a merge conflict, so auto-fix cannot react to conflicts on its own; the user must open the session and ask Claude to rebase.

nodes.label: Replies posted under the user's GitHub account
nodes.rationale: Claude may reply to review comment threads on GitHub while resolving them. Replies are posted using the user's GitHub account so they appear under that username, but each is labeled as coming from Claude Code.

nodes.label: Comment-triggered automation risk
nodes.rationale: Repositories using comment-triggered automation such as Atlantis, Terraform Cloud, or custom GitHub Actions on issue_comment events can be driven by Claude's replies on the user's behalf. The docs advise reviewing repository automation and disabling auto-fix where a PR comment can deploy infrastructure or run privileged operations.

nodes.label: Security and isolation model
nodes.rationale: Each cloud session is separated from the user's machine and from other sessions through several layers: isolated VMs, network access controls, credential protection, API-credential handling outside the sandbox, and analysis performed inside the session's isolated environment before PRs are created.

nodes.label: Isolated virtual machines
nodes.rationale: Each session runs in an isolated, Anthropic-managed VM; sessions routed to a self-hosted environment run on the organization's own infrastructure, where isolation becomes the deployment's responsibility.

nodes.label: Network access controls
nodes.rationale: In Anthropic-hosted environments network access is limited by default and can be disabled; in a self-hosted environment egress is restricted at the organization's own network boundary. Even with network access disabled, Claude Code can still reach the Anthropic API, which may allow data to exit the VM.

nodes.label: Git credentials held outside the sandbox
nodes.rationale: In Anthropic-hosted environments git credentials and signing keys stay outside the sandbox and a proxy authenticates on the session's behalf with scoped credentials; a self-hosted deployment supplies its own git credentials.

nodes.label: API credentials attached after leaving the session
nodes.rationale: Keys added to an Anthropic-hosted cloud environment stay outside the sandbox and are attached to matching requests after they leave the session; a self-hosted environment does not have API credentials.

nodes.label: Session creation failed
nodes.rationale: 'Session creation failed' or a stall at provisioning means Claude Code could not allocate a VM. Remedies: check status.claude.com, retry after a minute since capacity is provisioned on demand, and confirm the connecting GitHub account can reach the repository (App installation is not required).

nodes.label: Unable to get organization UUID
nodes.rationale: With API-key authentication or stale stored account details, `claude --cloud` and `claude --teleport` fail with 'Unable to get organization UUID' (or 'Error loading Claude Code sessions' in the picker). The fix is running /login to sign in with the claude.ai account and retrying.

nodes.label: Remote Control session expired or access denied
nodes.rationale: Because --teleport connects through the same Remote Control infrastructure, authentication and expiry errors surface with Remote Control wording ('Remote Control session expired', 'Access denied'); the connection token is short-lived and account-scoped. Fixes: /login to refresh credentials, confirm the same account owns the session, and note that 'Remote Control may not be available for this organization' means an Owner has not enabled cloud sessions.

nodes.label: Environment expired
nodes.rationale: Cloud sessions stop after a period of inactivity and the VM is reclaimed, marking the session expired in the list. Reopening it from claude.ai/code provisions a fresh VM with conversation history restored, but background work still running at reclaim time — subagents and shell commands — is not restored.

nodes.label: Shared rate limits, no separate compute charge
nodes.rationale: Claude Code on the web shares rate limits with all other Claude and Claude Code usage in the account, and running multiple tasks in parallel consumes rate limits proportionately. There is no separate compute charge for the cloud VM.

nodes.label: GitHub-only cloning and PR creation
nodes.rationale: Repository cloning and pull request creation require GitHub; self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server is supported for Team and Enterprise plans. GitLab, Bitbucket and other non-GitHub repositories can be sent as a local bundle, but such sessions cannot push results back to the remote.

nodes.label: Organization IP allowlist breaks hosted sessions
nodes.rationale: Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions call the Anthropic API from Anthropic-managed infrastructure, so every such session fails with an authentication error when the organization has IP allowlisting enabled — as do Code Review and routines on hosted environments. Support can exempt Anthropic-hosted services from the allowlist.

nodes.label: The .claude directory explorer
nodes.rationale: This page documents where Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, settings.json, hooks, skills, commands, subagents, workflows, rules and auto memory, split across the project's .claude directory and ~/.claude in the home directory. It presents an interactive file-tree explorer showing, for each file, what it does, when it loads, and an example.

nodes.label: Project scope configuration
nodes.rationale: Project-scoped configuration is everything Claude Code reads that is specific to one repository: CLAUDE.md, .mcp.json and .worktreeinclude at the project root, plus the .claude/ directory. Most of it is meant to be committed so the team shares it; a few files such as settings.local.json are gitignored when Claude Code saves settings to them.

nodes.label: Global (~) scope configuration
nodes.rationale: The home directory holds ~/.claude.json (app state) and ~/.claude/, the personal counterpart to a project's .claude/ directory. Files there apply to every project the user works in and are never committed to any repository.

nodes.label: Project CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md holds project-specific instructions — conventions, common commands, architectural context — and is loaded into context at the start of every session. It is committed, editable in-session with /memory, and also works at .claude/CLAUDE.md if you prefer to keep the project root clean.

nodes.label: The 200-line CLAUDE.md guideline
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md should target under 200 lines: longer files still load in full but may reduce adherence. Because it loads into every session, anything that only matters for specific tasks should move to a skill or a path-scoped rule, and when CLAUDE.md approaches 200 lines it should be split into rules.

nodes.label: .mcp.json (team-shared MCP servers)
nodes.rationale: .mcp.json configures the project-scoped Model Context Protocol servers a whole team uses, giving Claude access to databases, APIs and browsers. It lives at the project root rather than inside .claude/; servers connect when the session begins and their tool schemas are deferred by default, loading on demand via tool search.

nodes.label: Environment-variable references for MCP secrets
nodes.rationale: Secrets in .mcp.json are written as environment-variable references such as ${NOTION_TOKEN}, which Claude Code resolves from the shell environment when it starts the server, so the token never lands in the committed file.

nodes.label: .worktreeinclude
nodes.rationale: .worktreeinclude lists gitignored files (in .gitignore pattern syntax) to copy from the main repository into each new worktree, because worktrees are fresh checkouts where untracked files like .env are missing. Only files that both match a pattern and are gitignored are copied, so tracked files are never duplicated. It is read when Claude creates a worktree via --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool, or subagent isolation: worktree, and also applies to parallel desktop-app sessions.

nodes.label: WorktreeCreate hook bypasses .worktreeinclude
nodes.rationale: .worktreeinclude is git-only: if a WorktreeCreate hook is configured for a different version-control system, the file is not read at all and the hook script must copy the files itself.

nodes.label: Project .claude/ directory
nodes.rationale: The project .claude/ folder holds project-level configuration, rules and extensions: settings.json, settings.local.json, rules/, skills/, commands/, output-styles/, agents/, workflows/ and agent-memory/. If you use git, most files here should be committed so the team shares them.

nodes.label: settings.json
nodes.rationale: settings.json carries configuration Claude Code applies directly: permissions, hooks, statusLine, model, env and outputStyle. Unlike CLAUDE.md, which Claude reads as guidance, these settings are enforced whether Claude follows them or not.

nodes.label: Hooks and permissions as enforcement
nodes.rationale: Permissions allow, deny or prompt before Claude uses specific tools or commands, and hooks run user scripts on events such as before a tool call or after a file edit. They are the mechanism for guaranteed behavior, as opposed to instruction files Claude merely reads. Bash permission patterns support wildcards, e.g. Bash(npm test *) matches any command starting with npm test.

nodes.label: settings.local.json
nodes.rationale: settings.local.json holds personal settings for one project in the same JSON schema as settings.json, taking precedence over the team defaults and being the highest of the user-editable settings files. When Claude Code saves a setting to it in a repository that does not already ignore it, it adds **/.claude/settings.local.json to the user's global git excludes file.

nodes.label: Settings precedence order
nodes.rationale: Settings files are merged key by key in a precedence order: global ~/.claude/settings.json provides defaults, project settings.json overrides matching keys, settings.local.json overrides that, and CLI flags plus managed settings override everything.

nodes.label: Array settings combine, scalar settings resolve
nodes.rationale: Merging differs by value shape: array settings such as permissions.allow combine across all scopes, while scalar settings such as model take the most specific value.

nodes.label: rules/ directory
nodes.rationale: rules/ splits project instructions into topic files that can load conditionally. Like CLAUDE.md, rules are guidance Claude reads rather than configuration Claude Code enforces. Subdirectories work: .claude/rules/frontend/react.md is discovered automatically.

nodes.label: paths: frontmatter scoping for rules
nodes.rationale: A rule without paths: frontmatter loads at session start like CLAUDE.md; a rule with paths: globs loads only when Claude reads a matching file. Examples include testing.md scoped to **/*.test.ts and api-design.md scoped to src/api/**/*.ts.

nodes.label: skills/ directory
nodes.rationale: Each skill is a folder containing SKILL.md plus any supporting files, invoked with /skill-name or auto-invoked when Claude matches the task to the skill. The description frontmatter is what determines when Claude auto-invokes it.

nodes.label: Skill invocation-control frontmatter
nodes.rationale: By default both the user and Claude can invoke a skill. Frontmatter narrows that: disable-model-invocation: true makes a skill user-only (for workflows like /deploy), while user-invocable: false hides it from the / menu but still lets Claude invoke it.

nodes.label: Bundled supporting files in a skill
nodes.rationale: Skills can bundle reference docs, templates and scripts beside SKILL.md. The skill directory path is prepended to SKILL.md, so Claude can read a bundled file such as checklist.md by name on demand; scripts referenced from bash injection commands use the ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} placeholder.

nodes.label: $ARGUMENTS and !`...` bash injection
nodes.rationale: Skills and commands accept arguments: $ARGUMENTS substitutes whatever was typed after the name (with $0, $1 and so on for positional access), and a !`...` line runs a shell command and injects its output into the prompt before Claude sees it — for example !`git diff $ARGUMENTS` or !`gh issue view $ARGUMENTS`.

nodes.label: commands/ directory
nodes.rationale: commands/ holds single-file prompts invoked with /name: commands/deploy.md creates /deploy exactly as skills/deploy/SKILL.md does, and both can be auto-invoked by Claude. Commands and skills are now the same mechanism; commands remain supported but new workflows should be skills, and if a skill and command share a name the skill takes precedence.

nodes.label: Project output-styles/
nodes.rationale: Output styles are usually personal and live in ~/.claude/output-styles/, but a project-level output-styles/ is for a style the team shares, such as a review mode everyone uses. It is applied at session start when selected via the outputStyle setting, and a project style takes precedence over a global one with the same name.

nodes.label: agents/ directory (subagents)
nodes.rationale: Each markdown file in agents/ defines a subagent with its own system prompt, tool access and optionally its own model. Subagents run in a fresh context window separate from the main session, keeping the main conversation clean, and are useful for parallel or isolated work; you delegate by typing @ and picking one from the autocomplete, or Claude spawns one itself.

nodes.label: tools: frontmatter restricts a subagent
nodes.rationale: A subagent's tools: frontmatter field limits which tools it can reach — the code-reviewer example is restricted to Read, Grep and Glob so it can inspect code but never edit it — while the description field tells Claude when to delegate automatically and the body becomes the subagent's system prompt.

nodes.label: workflows/ directory
nodes.rationale: Each .js file in workflows/ is a dynamic workflow: a script the runtime executes to spawn and coordinate many subagents. Workflows are written by Claude and saved from /workflows (pressing s on a run) rather than authored from scratch; they load at startup and each file becomes a /<name> command.

nodes.label: Project .claude/agent-memory/
nodes.rationale: Subagents declaring memory: project get a dedicated directory under .claude/agent-memory/<agent-name>/, where the subagent itself creates and maintains MEMORY.md. The first 200 lines (capped at 25KB) of that file are loaded into the subagent's system prompt when it runs; the directory is created only for subagents that set the memory: frontmatter field.

nodes.label: memory: project | local | user scopes
nodes.rationale: The memory: frontmatter value picks where a subagent's memory is written: project shares it with the team in .claude/agent-memory/, local keeps it out of version control in .claude/agent-memory-local/, and user makes it cross-project in ~/.claude/agent-memory/.

nodes.label: ~/.claude.json
nodes.rationale: ~/.claude.json holds app state that does not belong in settings.json: theme, OAuth session, per-project trust decisions, personal MCP servers and UI toggles such as autoConnectIde and externalEditorContext. It is read at session start and written back when settings change via /config or a trust prompt is approved; its projects key tracks per-project trust acceptance and last-session metrics.

nodes.label: ~/.claude/ directory
nodes.rationale: ~/.claude/ is the global counterpart to a project's .claude/ directory, holding personal configuration that applies to every project: CLAUDE.md, settings.json, keybindings.json, themes/, projects/ (auto memory), rules/, skills/, commands/, output-styles/, agents/, workflows/ and agent-memory/.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: The global CLAUDE.md is loaded at the start of every session in every project, alongside that project's own CLAUDE.md, so both are in context together. It should stay short and hold only preferences that apply everywhere — response style, commit format, personal conventions.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md files are both loaded, not merged
nodes.rationale: Global and project CLAUDE.md files are both loaded into context rather than merged key by key, and when their instructions conflict the project-level instruction takes priority. This is explicitly different from settings.json, where matching keys are overridden.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/settings.json
nodes.rationale: The global settings.json takes the same keys as a project's — permissions, hooks, model, environment variables — and supplies the user's defaults for every project, such as permissions always allowed, a preferred model, or a notification hook that runs regardless of project.

nodes.label: keybindings.json
nodes.rationale: keybindings.json rebinds keyboard shortcuts in the interactive CLI, is read at session start and hot-reloaded when edited, and is created or opened with /keybindings. Bindings are grouped by a context field (e.g. Chat) and unbound by setting a key to null; Ctrl+C, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+M and Caps Lock are reserved and cannot be rebound.

nodes.label: themes/ directory
nodes.rationale: Each .json file in ~/.claude/themes/ defines a custom color theme as a built-in base preset plus an overrides map of color tokens. Themes are read at session start, hot-reloaded on change, listed in /theme, and selecting one stores custom:<slug> as the theme preference.

nodes.label: Auto memory (~/.claude/projects/)
nodes.rationale: Auto memory lets Claude accumulate knowledge across sessions without the user writing anything — build commands, debugging insights, architecture notes — with each project getting its own memory directory keyed by repository path. It is on by default and toggled with /memory or the autoMemoryEnabled setting.

nodes.label: Auto memory MEMORY.md index
nodes.rationale: MEMORY.md is the index Claude creates and updates itself and reads at the start of every session; the first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded. The user does not write it, though they may edit or delete it — Claude keeps updating it.

nodes.label: Auto memory topic files
nodes.rationale: When MEMORY.md grows too long Claude splits detail into topic files such as debugging.md, architecture.md or build-commands.md, naming them after what it split out. These are read on demand when the current task relates to them, never at startup.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/rules/
nodes.rationale: User-level rules behave exactly like project .claude/rules/ but apply to every project, and are meant for conventions the user wants across all their work such as personal code style or commit message format.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/skills/
nodes.rationale: Personal skills use the same folder-with-SKILL.md structure as project skills but are scoped to the user account, so they are invocable with /skill-name in any project.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/commands/
nodes.rationale: Personal single-file commands work like project commands/ but are scoped to the user account: each markdown file becomes a /command-name available in every project.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/output-styles/
nodes.rationale: Each markdown file here defines an output style: a section appended to the system prompt that by default also drops the built-in software-engineering task instructions, adapting Claude Code for non-coding uses or teaching and review modes. keep-coding-instructions: true retains the default task instructions; built-in styles are Default, Proactive, Concise, Explanatory and Learning; changes take effect only in the next session because the system prompt is fixed at startup for caching.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/agents/
nodes.rationale: Subagents defined in ~/.claude/agents/ use the same format as project agents and are available across all of the user's projects, invoked by Claude delegating or by an @-mention in any project.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/workflows/
nodes.rationale: Workflow scripts saved in ~/.claude/workflows/ are available across all projects and each becomes a /<name> command at startup; a project workflow of the same name in .claude/workflows/ takes precedence over the personal one.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/agent-memory/
nodes.rationale: Subagents declaring memory: user store knowledge in ~/.claude/agent-memory/, where it persists across all projects and is loaded into the subagent's system prompt when the subagent starts.

nodes.label: Related files the explorer does not show
nodes.rationale: The explorer covers files a user authors and edits; a few related files live elsewhere and are listed separately: managed-settings.json, CLAUDE.local.md, and the installed-plugins tree under ~/.claude/plugins.

nodes.label: managed-settings.json
nodes.rationale: managed-settings.json is a system-level file whose location varies by OS, holding enterprise-enforced settings a user cannot override apart from narrow security-key exceptions where the stricter value applies.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.local.md
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.local.md sits at the project root and holds private preferences for that project, loaded alongside CLAUDE.md. It must be created manually and added to .gitignore by the user.

nodes.label: ~/.claude/plugins
nodes.rationale: ~/.claude/plugins holds cloned marketplaces, installed plugin versions and per-plugin data, managed by the claude plugin commands. For a plugin installed from a marketplace command source in link mode, Claude Code stores links there instead of a copy and the plugin's files stay in the directory the command prints.

nodes.label: Choose the right file (task-to-file table)
nodes.rationale: A lookup table maps an intent to the file that expresses it: project context to CLAUDE.md; allowing or blocking tool calls to settings.json permissions or hooks; keeping personal overrides out of git to settings.local.json; a /name capability to skills/<name>/SKILL.md; a specialized subagent to agents/*.md; orchestrating many subagents to workflows/*.js; external tools to .mcp.json; response formatting to output-styles/*.md.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting configuration
nodes.rationale: When a setting, hook or file is not taking effect, the Debug your configuration page supplies the inspection commands and a symptom-first lookup table.

nodes.label: Application data written during sessions
nodes.rationale: Beyond authored config, ~/.claude holds data Claude Code writes during sessions: full conversation transcripts at projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl, subagent transcripts, spilled tool results, pre-edit file snapshots, plans, debug logs, paste and image caches, uploads, session env, tasks, shell snapshots, backups, feedback bundles and usage data. Anything that passes through a tool lands in a transcript on disk.

nodes.label: Retention cleanup sweep
nodes.rationale: Claude Code deletes the listed application-data paths once they are older than the retention period, as long as it can safely determine that period. The same age cutoff also drives automatic removal of orphaned worktrees, and legacy directories todos/, statsig/ and logs/ have their contents and then the empty directory removed.

nodes.label: cleanupPeriodDays
nodes.rationale: cleanupPeriodDays sets the retention age for swept files: the default is 30 days, the minimum is 1, and setting 0 fails with a validation error. A sibling setting, desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays, gives Claude Desktop and Cowork transcripts an age limit.

nodes.label: Paths with their own retention rule
nodes.rationale: Three areas sit outside the age-based sweep: sessions/ files are removed when their session exits with crash leftovers cleared at next launch; a project's auto memory directory is excluded and removed only after being empty for the whole retention period (before v2.1.228 the sweep could delete files beneath it); and Claude Desktop and Cowork transcripts are kept at any age unless desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays or a managed cleanupPeriodDays is set, which requires v2.1.248 or later.

nodes.label: When the sweep does not run
nodes.rationale: Claude Code skips the sweep in bare mode (claude -p with --bare) and pauses it whenever it cannot safely determine the retention period; the retention_sweep telemetry event lists each pausing configuration. Unreadable settings, or settings errors with cleanupPeriodDays or desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays explicitly set, also raise a warning in /status until fixed, and managed settings supplying cleanupPeriodDays make the sweep run at the managed value regardless.

nodes.label: Data kept until you delete it
nodes.rationale: Five paths are outside the sweep and kept indefinitely: history.jsonl (every prompt typed, with timestamp and project path, used for up-arrow recall), stats-cache.json (token and cost totals for /usage), remote-settings.json and policy-limits.json (organization caches, both deleted at logout), and cache/changelog.md (the cached changelog shown by /release-notes).

nodes.label: Plaintext storage risk
nodes.rationale: Transcripts and prompt history are not encrypted at rest and OS file permissions are the only protection: if a tool reads a .env file or a command prints a credential, that value is written into projects/<project>/<session>.jsonl.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY and session persistence off
nodes.rationale: Setting the CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY environment variable skips writing transcripts and prompt history in any mode. Non-interactively you can instead pass --no-session-persistence alongside -p, or set persistSession: false in the TypeScript Agent SDK; the Python SDK has no equivalent option.

nodes.label: Deny reads of credential files with permission rules
nodes.rationale: One of the recommended reductions of plaintext exposure is to use permission rules to deny reads of credential files, so their contents never enter a tool result and therefore never reach the transcript on disk.

nodes.label: claude project purge
nodes.rationale: claude project purge deletes the state Claude Code holds for one project: transcripts and auto memory under projects/, per-session tasks/, debug/ and file-history/ entries, matching prompt lines in history.jsonl, and the project's entry in ~/.claude.json. It prints the full deletion plan and asks for confirmation; --dry-run previews, --yes skips the prompt, -i steps through item by item, and --all purges every project (deleting history.jsonl outright rather than filtering it). It leaves shell-snapshots/ and backups/ alone because they are not project-scoped, and exits with status 1 if no state matches the path.

nodes.label: What deleting each data path costs you
nodes.rationale: Any application-data path can be deleted by hand without affecting new sessions, but a table records what is lost for past ones: projects/ costs resume, continue, rewind and all auto memory; history.jsonl costs up-arrow recall; file-history/ costs checkpoint restore; stats-cache.json costs historical /usage totals. Caches such as remote-settings.json, cache/changelog.md and policy-limits.json cost nothing because they are re-fetched.

nodes.label: Paths never to delete
nodes.rationale: ~/.claude.json, ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/plugins/ must not be deleted: they hold authentication, preferences and installed plugins.

nodes.label: Committed / gitignored / local / Claude-writes badges
nodes.rationale: Every file in the explorer carries a badge stating its handling: committed (share with the team), gitignored, local only, or 'Claude writes' for autogenerated files such as MEMORY.md that the model creates and maintains itself.

nodes.label: Claude Security plugin
nodes.rationale: The Claude Security plugin runs a multi-agent vulnerability scan of a codebase from inside a Claude Code session, and can turn the findings you choose into patches you review and apply yourself. It scans a whole repository or only a set of changes such as a branch diff, a pull request diff, or a single commit.

nodes.label: Multi-agent vulnerability scan
nodes.rationale: A team of Claude agents maps the architecture, builds a threat model, hunts for vulnerabilities, and independently reviews every finding before writing the report. The scan reports each stage as it starts, with detail available under /workflows.

nodes.label: Architecture map and threat model
nodes.rationale: Before hunting for vulnerabilities, the agent team maps the codebase's architecture and builds a threat model from it. This is the first stage of the scan pipeline.

nodes.label: Independent verifier agents
nodes.rationale: Findings only appear in the report after independent verifier agents analyze them, which keeps reports short and worth reading. Every finding is independently reviewed before the report is written.

nodes.label: Local execution and plan usage limits
nodes.rationale: The plugin runs locally in the session, uses whichever models you have access to in Claude Code, and each scan counts against your plan's usage limits. A scan may take a while, may use a significant number of tokens, and needs Claude Code left open while it completes.

nodes.label: Claude Security managed product
nodes.rationale: The hosted Claude Security product, available on the Enterprise plan, monitors connected repositories and can run scans on Claude Mythos 5. It is the managed alternative to running the plugin locally.

nodes.label: Plugin reaches code the managed product cannot
nodes.rationale: Because it runs locally in the session, the plugin reaches code the managed product can't reach: repositories hosted on GitLab or Bitbucket, or on networks that don't allow inbound connections.

nodes.label: Security guidance plugin
nodes.rationale: The in-session layer of the security stack: it reviews code as Claude writes it, catching common vulnerabilities and fixing them in the same session.

nodes.label: /security-review command
nodes.rationale: The on-demand single-pass layer: /security-review runs one time-boxed security pass over the current branch, in contrast to the plugin's deep multi-agent scan.

nodes.label: Code Review (pull-request layer)
nodes.rationale: Code Review, on Team and Enterprise plans, is the pull-request stage of the stack: a multi-agent correctness and security review with full codebase context.

nodes.label: Defense-in-depth security stack
nodes.rationale: The plugin is the on-demand deep-scan layer in a defense-in-depth stack whose stages are: in session, on demand single pass, on demand deep scan, on pull request, managed, and in CI. Each stage covers a different moment in the development lifecycle.

nodes.label: Existing static analysis and dependency scanners
nodes.rationale: The CI stage of the stack: language-specific rules, supply-chain checks, and policy enforcement. The plugin does not replace them; it reasons about code the way a human security researcher would, complementing their deterministic checks.

nodes.label: Paid plan for dynamic workflows
nodes.rationale: A paid plan is required for the dynamic workflows the scan uses to orchestrate its agents. On Pro, dynamic workflows are turned on from the Dynamic workflows row in /config.

nodes.label: python3 3.9 or later on PATH
nodes.rationale: Python 3.9 or later must be available on PATH as python3, checked with python3 --version. The plugin's tooling uses only the Python standard library, so nothing is installed.

nodes.label: Git for change scans and patches
nodes.rationale: Git is required for change scans and for turning findings into patches; those jobs do not support other version control systems. A full scan works in any directory, with or without version control.

nodes.label: Supported operating systems
nodes.rationale: The plugin runs on Linux, macOS, or Windows.

nodes.label: /plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official
nodes.rationale: The plugin is installed from the official Anthropic marketplace with /plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official. The command opens the plugin's details, where you choose an installation scope to start the install.

nodes.label: Marketplace-not-found remedy
nodes.rationale: If the install reports Marketplace "claude-plugins-official" not found, add the marketplace with /plugin marketplace add anthropics/claude-plugins-official and retry. If it reports it can't find the plugin in the marketplace, check the plugin name for a typo.

nodes.label: /reload-plugins activation
nodes.rationale: When the install summary reports 'Run /reload-plugins to activate.', running /reload-plugins applies the pending change without restarting Claude Code.

nodes.label: Uninstalling the plugin
nodes.rationale: The plugin is removed either from the /plugin menu or by running claude plugin uninstall claude-security in the terminal.

nodes.label: /claude-security command menu
nodes.rationale: The plugin adds exactly one command, /claude-security, which opens a menu of its three jobs: scanning the codebase, scanning a set of changes, and suggesting patches.

nodes.label: Scan codebase job
nodes.rationale: The full-scan job: pick Scan codebase from the /claude-security menu, choose what to scan, confirm the run, and read the report. A full scan reads the working tree and works in any directory, versioned or not.

nodes.label: Scope selection with cost stated
nodes.rationale: The plugin reads the repository first, then offers the whole repository or a focused area, with each option's file count and relative cost stated. Answering 'I don't know' lets the plugin pick a sensible default for the repository's size.

nodes.label: Explicit run confirmation
nodes.rationale: Nothing runs until you confirm, because a scan may take a while, may use a significant number of tokens, and needs Claude Code left open while it completes.

nodes.label: Auto permission mode
nodes.rationale: The plugin works best in auto mode, which lets the scan's agents proceed without a permission prompt at each step.

nodes.label: Direct and plain-language invocation
nodes.rationale: You do not have to start from the menu: a job can be asked for directly as arguments to the command, such as /claude-security scan my branch, or in plain language, such as 'scan commit abc1234' or 'fix finding F3'.

nodes.label: Scan only your changes
nodes.rationale: When a branch has commits its base doesn't, the menu offers to scan only that diff, so a branch can be checked before merging. An open pull request or a single named commit can also be scanned.

nodes.label: Only committed changes are scanned
nodes.rationale: A change scan reads only committed changes: in-progress edits must be committed or stashed first, or a full scan run instead, since the full scan reads the working tree.

nodes.label: Pull-request lookup is the only network step
nodes.rationale: Finding your open pull requests is the one step that reaches the network, and it is offered only when the session already has permission to run the GitHub CLI and gh is signed in.

nodes.label: Scoping large repositories
nodes.rationale: On a large repository, scan one area at a time rather than the whole tree: pick a focused scope such as the API layer or authentication code and the run sizes itself to it. The report's coverage section states what was and was not examined, and another area can be scanned anytime.

nodes.label: CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/ results directory
nodes.rationale: Every scan writes its results into a timestamped CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/ directory in the repository. That directory is the only change a scan makes to your checkout.

nodes.label: CLAUDE-SECURITY-RESULTS.md report
nodes.rationale: The human-readable report, giving each finding an ID such as F1 plus its impact, exploit scenario, severity, confidence, and recommendation.

nodes.label: CLAUDE-SECURITY-RESULTS.jsonl
nodes.rationale: The same findings in machine-readable form, one JSON object per line.

nodes.label: CLAUDE-SECURITY-RESULTS.sarif (SARIF 2.1.0)
nodes.rationale: The same findings as a SARIF 2.1.0 log for GitHub code scanning and any other tool that reads the standard. The scan classifies findings under their CWE weakness categories.

nodes.label: CLAUDE-SECURITY-REVISION-<commit>.json stamp
nodes.rationale: The revision stamp records which commit was scanned, at what effort, whether uncommitted changes were part of the scanned tree, and how thoroughly the run was verified, so a report is always tied to the code it describes. A scan outside version control stamps UNVERSIONED in place of the commit.

nodes.label: Self-ignoring results directory
nodes.rationale: The results directory carries its own .gitignore, so a stray git add never sweeps a report into a commit. To keep a report in history for an audit trail, delete that one .gitignore file and commit the directory like any other.

nodes.label: Scans are nondeterministic
nodes.rationale: Two scans of the same code can surface different findings. The guidance is to run scans regularly and use the revision stamps to attribute each report to the exact code and settings it covered.

nodes.label: Suggest patches job
nodes.rationale: The fix flow: pick Suggest patches from the /claude-security menu, or ask in plain language, then choose which findings from the report to address. Patches are built against committed code.

nodes.label: Stale findings are skipped, not patched
nodes.rationale: The report has to still describe the code you have: findings whose code has since changed are skipped with a note, and the plugin offers a fresh scan instead of patching from a stale report.

nodes.label: Patches drafted in a scratch copy
nodes.rationale: Each patch is drafted in a scratch copy of the repository, so your source files stay untouched until you apply a patch yourself.

nodes.label: Independent patch reviewer
nodes.rationale: Before delivery each patch is reviewed by an agent independent of the one that wrote it, which runs the project's tests against the change when the code has them and reads the diff on its own terms. A patch is written only when that review can vouch that it addresses the one finding, introduces no new vulnerability, and leaves behavior otherwise unchanged; otherwise you get a short note explaining why instead of a patch.

nodes.label: F<n>.patch files in patches/
nodes.rationale: Reviewed patches land in the report's patches/ folder, one F<n>.patch per finding with a note beside it explaining the change.

nodes.label: Patches are never applied automatically
nodes.rationale: Applying a patch is always the user's decision; the plugin never applies one automatically. Each patch should be applied in its own pull request so it can be reviewed and tested on its own.

nodes.label: Applying a patch with git apply
nodes.rationale: A patch is applied from the shell with git apply CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/patches/F1.patch, or by asking Claude to apply it and open a pull request.

nodes.label: Note when the patched code has no tests
nodes.rationale: When the patched code has no tests, the patch's note says so, so you know its review ran without a test pass.

nodes.label: Python warning on the menu
nodes.rationale: When python3 cannot be found at all the menu warns that Claude Security won't work until one is installed; when the first python3 on PATH is older than 3.9 the warning names the version it found. The fix is to install Python 3 or put a newer python3 first on PATH, then start a new session.

nodes.label: Fable safeguard flag and Opus downgrade
nodes.rationale: On a Fable model you may see "Fable 5.1's safeguards flagged this message" or the Fable 5 equivalent. Due to Fable's cybersecurity safety classifiers certain model activities are blocked and automatically downgraded to Opus; this is expected and the scan should still complete successfully.

nodes.label: Claude Code CLI reference
nodes.rationale: The complete reference for the Claude Code command-line interface, covering both the subcommands that start, pipe, resume and manage sessions and the flags that customize a session's behavior.

nodes.label: CLI commands surface
nodes.rationale: The set of `claude` subcommands used to start sessions, pipe content, resume conversations and manage updates, installs, auth, plugins, MCP servers, background sessions and self-hosted infrastructure.

nodes.label: CLI flags surface
nodes.rationale: The command-line flags that customize Claude Code's behavior for one invocation, spanning working directories, tools and permissions, models and effort, output formats, plugins, MCP, and session lifecycle.

nodes.label: claude (interactive session)
nodes.rationale: Running `claude` with no arguments starts an interactive session. It is the default entry point that every other subcommand and flag modifies.

nodes.label: claude "query" (initial prompt)
nodes.rationale: `claude "query"` starts an interactive session seeded with an initial prompt, e.g. `claude "explain this project"`.

nodes.label: --print / -p (print mode)
nodes.rationale: `claude -p "query"` queries via the SDK and exits, printing the response without interactive mode. Print mode is the gate for a large family of flags that are documented as print-mode only.

nodes.label: Piped input to print mode
nodes.rationale: `cat file | claude -p "query"` processes piped content, e.g. `cat logs.txt | claude -p "explain"`, making the CLI usable as a shell filter.

nodes.label: --continue / -c
nodes.rationale: Loads the most recent conversation in the current directory, skipping background sessions, sessions created with `claude -p` or the Agent SDK, and sessions whose first prompt was `/loop`. `claude -p --continue` includes those, and the search includes sessions that added this directory with `/add-dir`.

nodes.label: --resume / -r
nodes.rationale: Resumes a session by ID or name, or shows an interactive picker. Given a session ID, Claude Code searches the current project directory and its git worktrees, then every other project on the machine; before v2.1.223 the ID search covered only the current project and its worktrees. Background sessions appear in the picker marked `bg`.

nodes.label: claude update
nodes.rationale: `claude update` updates the installation to the latest version.

nodes.label: claude gateway
nodes.rationale: Starts the self-hosted Claude apps gateway server for administrators deploying SSO and policy in front of Claude Code on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry. Requires `--config` pointing at a `gateway.yaml`, and Claude Code v2.1.195 or later.

nodes.label: claude install [version]
nodes.rationale: Installs or reinstalls the native binary, accepting an explicit version like `2.1.118`, or the aliases `stable` or `latest`.

nodes.label: claude auth (login / logout / status)
nodes.rationale: `claude auth login` signs in to an Anthropic account, with `--email` to pre-fill, `--sso` to force SSO, and `--console` to sign in with Anthropic Console for API billing instead of a subscription. `claude auth logout` logs out; `claude auth status` prints JSON (`--text` for human-readable) and exits 0 if logged in, 1 if not.

nodes.label: claude agents (agent view)
nodes.rationale: Opens agent view to monitor and dispatch parallel background sessions. `--cwd <path>` limits it to sessions started under that directory and `--json` prints active sessions as a JSON array for scripting (`--json --all` also includes completed ones). `--permission-mode`, `--model`, `--effort` and `--agent` set defaults for dispatched sessions; opening the view requires an interactive terminal.

nodes.label: Background session
nodes.rationale: A Claude Code session that runs detached from the terminal, identified by a short id such as `7c5dcf5d`, hosted by the supervisor process, visible in agent view, and manageable from the shell.

nodes.label: Background-session shell commands
nodes.rationale: `claude attach <id>` attaches to a background session in the terminal, `claude logs <id>` prints its recent output, `claude respawn <id>` restarts it with the conversation intact (`--all` restarts every running session, e.g. to pick up an updated binary), `claude stop <id>` (also `claude kill`) stops it, and `claude rm <id>` removes it from the list while the transcript stays locally available through `claude --resume`.

nodes.label: Background-session supervisor
nodes.rationale: A supervisor process hosts background sessions; it has state, a version, a socket directory and a worker count, and can become unresponsive, which is what the `claude daemon` subcommands exist to inspect and recover from.

nodes.label: claude daemon status
nodes.rationale: Prints the background-session supervisor's state, version, socket directory and worker count for diagnostics, and exits 1 if the supervisor isn't running.

nodes.label: claude daemon stop --any
nodes.rationale: Stops the supervisor and the sessions it hosts; `--keep-workers` leaves background sessions running so the next supervisor reconnects to them, and `--any` confirms stopping an on-demand supervisor (the default). It is the documented recovery for an unresponsive supervisor.

nodes.label: claude auto-mode defaults
nodes.rationale: Prints the built-in auto mode classifier rules as JSON; `claude auto-mode config` shows the effective config with settings applied, and `--label <prefix>` prints only rules whose label starts with that prefix, matched case-insensitively. Requires v2.1.208 or later.

nodes.label: claude auto-mode reset
nodes.rationale: Restores the default auto mode configuration by removing the `autoMode` section from the user settings file, prompting for confirmation unless `-y`/`--yes` is passed. Rules from managed settings or `--settings` still apply. Requires v2.1.212 or later.

nodes.label: claude doctor
nodes.rationale: Prints read-only installation and settings diagnostics from the terminal without starting a session, including install health, settings-file validation errors and Remote Control eligibility. The in-session `/doctor` is the variant that can also apply fixes.

nodes.label: claude import [codex|gemini]
nodes.rationale: Starts an interactive session that runs `/import` to bring configuration from other coding agents (codex, gemini) into Claude Code, accepting `--dry-run` and `--yes`. It is unavailable on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS, and when feature-flag fetching is turned off. Requires v2.1.213 or later.

nodes.label: claude mcp
nodes.rationale: `claude mcp` configures Model Context Protocol servers; the CLI reference defers the subcommand detail to the Claude Code MCP documentation.

nodes.label: claude mcp login / logout
nodes.rationale: `claude mcp login <name>` runs a configured MCP server's OAuth flow without opening the interactive `/mcp` panel, works for HTTP, SSE and claude.ai connector servers, and takes `--no-browser` over SSH to print the authorization URL for pasting the redirect back. `claude mcp logout <name>` clears stored OAuth credentials. Both require v2.1.186 or later.

nodes.label: claude plugin
nodes.rationale: Manages Claude Code plugins (alias `claude plugins`), e.g. `claude plugin install code-review@claude-plugins-official`; subcommands are documented in the plugin reference.

nodes.label: claude project purge
nodes.rationale: Deletes all local Claude Code state for a project — transcripts, task lists, debug logs, file-edit history, prompt history lines, and the project's entry in `~/.claude.json`. Omitting the path opens an interactive list; flags are `--dry-run`, `-y`/`--yes`, `-i`/`--interactive` and `--all`.

nodes.label: claude remote-control (server mode)
nodes.rationale: Starts a Remote Control server so Claude Code can be driven from Claude.ai or the Claude app. It runs in server mode with no local interactive session, and after the server is stopped the sessions it was serving can be brought back.

nodes.label: --remote-control / --rc
nodes.rationale: Starts an *interactive* session with Remote Control enabled so it can also be controlled from claude.ai or the Claude app, optionally taking a session name. `--remote-control-session-name-prefix <prefix>` sets the prefix for auto-generated names, defaulting to the machine's hostname (e.g. `myhost-graceful-unicorn`); `CLAUDE_REMOTE_CONTROL_SESSION_NAME_PREFIX` has the same effect.

nodes.label: claude self-hosted-runner
nodes.rationale: Starts a runner process that registers a machine or container with a self-hosted environment and hosts Claude Code cloud sessions on your own infrastructure. Sub-verbs are `setup` (guided operator walkthrough), `doctor` (diagnose a deployed runner) and `orchestrator` (spawn on-demand runners). Requires v2.1.224 or later.

nodes.label: claude setup-token
nodes.rationale: Generates a long-lived OAuth token for CI and scripts, printing it to the terminal without saving it. It requires a Claude subscription.

nodes.label: claude ultrareview
nodes.rationale: Runs ultrareview non-interactively, printing findings to stdout and exiting 0 on success or 1 on failure. `--json` returns the raw payload, `--timeout <minutes>` overrides the 30-minute default, and `--post` on a github.com pull request target posts the findings to the PR as one plain comment from your GitHub account (`--no-post` is the default). Requires v2.1.227 or later.

nodes.label: Mistyped-subcommand suggestion
nodes.rationale: If a subcommand is mistyped, Claude Code suggests the closest match and exits without starting a session — `claude udpate` prints `Did you mean claude update?` rather than treating the typo as a prompt.

nodes.label: Leading-flag routing to daemon subcommands
nodes.rationale: As of v2.1.199, `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions daemon <subcommand>` actually runs the daemon subcommand; earlier versions treated `daemon <subcommand>` as the prompt for a new interactive session, so the subcommand never ran when the flag came first — a common setup when `claude` is aliased to include the flag. Only a leading `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or `--allow-dangerously-skip-permissions` routes this way.

nodes.label: `claude --help` is not exhaustive
nodes.rationale: `claude --help` does not list every flag, so a flag's absence from `--help` does not mean it is unavailable. The documented flag table, not the help output, is the authority on what exists.

nodes.label: --add-dir
nodes.rationale: Adds additional working directories Claude may read and edit. It grants file access only — most `.claude/` configuration is not discovered from those directories — validates each path exists as a directory, and persists across sessions only via the `permissions.additionalDirectories` setting.

nodes.label: --advisor <model>
nodes.rationale: Enables the server-side advisor tool for the session with a model alias (`fable`, `opus`, `sonnet`) or a full model ID, taking precedence over the `advisorModel` setting for that session; `fable` requires Fable access.

nodes.label: --agents / --agent
nodes.rationale: `--agent` selects an agent for the current session, overriding the `agent` setting. `--agents` defines custom subagents dynamically via JSON using the fields listed for CLI-defined subagents; Claude Code validates that JSON at startup and exits on an invalid value, with validation requiring v2.1.242 or later.

nodes.label: --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions
nodes.rationale: Adds `bypassPermissions` to the `Shift+Tab` mode cycle without starting in it, so a session can begin in another mode such as `plan` and switch to bypass later.

nodes.label: --dangerously-skip-permissions
nodes.rationale: Skips permission prompts and is equivalent to `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. For sessions started with `--bg`, the mode persists when the supervisor restarts the session.

nodes.label: --allowedTools / --allowed-tools
nodes.rationale: Names tools that execute without prompting for permission, using the permission rule syntax for pattern matching (e.g. `"Bash(git log *)"`). Naming a task-tracking tool here also opts the session in to task tracking. It grants auto-approval, not availability.

nodes.label: --disallowedTools / --disallowed-tools
nodes.rationale: Deny rules with two distinct behaviors: a bare tool name removes matching tools from Claude's context (`"Edit"` removes Edit, `"*"` every tool, `"mcp__*"` every MCP tool), while a scoped rule such as `Bash(rm *)` leaves the tool available and denies only matching calls.

nodes.label: --tools
nodes.rationale: Restricts which built-in tools Claude can use: `""` disables all, `"default"` allows all, or an explicit list like `"Bash,Edit,Read"`. It does not affect MCP tools — denying those needs `--disallowedTools "mcp__*"` — and naming a task-tracking tool opts the session in.

nodes.label: EndConversation tool exception
nodes.rationale: EndConversation resists ordinary tool restriction: a `--tools` list that omits it does not remove it, `""` removes it only when no MCP tools remain, and a `--disallowedTools` rule naming it cannot remove it while any other tool remains.

nodes.label: --append-subagent-system-prompt
nodes.rationale: Appends custom text to the end of every subagent's system prompt, nested subagents included, except a forked subagent which reuses the conversation's own prompt. It only applies in non-interactive mode with `-p` and requires v2.1.205 or later.

nodes.label: System prompt flags (the four)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code provides four flags for customizing the system prompt — `--system-prompt`, `--system-prompt-file`, `--append-system-prompt`, `--append-system-prompt-file` — and all four work in both interactive and non-interactive modes. They apply only to the current invocation.

nodes.label: Replacement system-prompt flags
nodes.rationale: `--system-prompt` replaces the entire default prompt with custom text and `--system-prompt-file` replaces it with file contents; the two are mutually exclusive. Replacing drops all of the default prompt, including tool guidance and safety instructions, so the author takes responsibility for whatever the task still needs.

nodes.label: Appending system-prompt flags
nodes.rationale: `--append-system-prompt` and `--append-system-prompt-file` add text (inline or from a file) to the end of the default prompt, preserving the default tool guidance, safety instructions and coding conventions so only the difference is supplied. The append flags can be combined with either replacement flag.

nodes.label: Append-vs-replace decision rule
nodes.rationale: Choose based on whether Claude Code's default identity still fits the task: append when Claude should remain a coding assistant that also follows extra rules (per-invocation instructions, output formatting, domain context for a `-p` script); replace when the surface, identity, or permission model differs — for example a non-coding agent in an unwatched pipeline.

nodes.label: Persistent alternatives to prompt flags
nodes.rationale: Because the system-prompt flags apply only to the current invocation, persistent personas that can be switched and shared across a project belong in output styles, and project conventions Claude should always follow belong in CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: --autocompact <auto|tokens>
nodes.rationale: Sets the auto-compact window for the session without changing saved settings, accepting the same values as the `/autocompact` command (e.g. `500k`). Requires v2.1.221 or later.

nodes.label: --ax-screen-reader
nodes.rationale: Renders screen-reader friendly output — flat text with no decorative borders or animations — forcing the classic renderer so the `tui` setting has no effect, though attached background sessions still render fullscreen. It takes precedence over `CLAUDE_AX_SCREEN_READER` and the `axScreenReader` setting; requires v2.1.181 or later.

nodes.label: --bare (minimal mode)
nodes.rationale: Skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md so scripted calls start faster, leaving Claude with Bash, file read and file edit tools. Skills in a directory passed with `--add-dir` still load. It sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE`.

nodes.label: --safe-mode
nodes.rationale: Starts with all customizations disabled to troubleshoot a broken configuration — CLAUDE.md, skills, plugins, hooks, MCP servers, custom commands and agents, output styles, workflows, themes, keybindings, status line, file-suggestion commands, LSP servers and auto memory do not load — while authentication, model selection, built-in tools and permissions keep working. Managed settings policy still applies (including policy hooks, status line and file-suggestion commands) but managed plugins, skills, CLAUDE.md and policy MCP servers do not. Sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SAFE_MODE`.

nodes.label: --restricted
nodes.rationale: Starts in restricted mode for an evaluation harness driving `claude` on a shared machine: Claude Code removes the built-in tools that run commands or code plus WebFetch unless named individually in `--tools` (not via the `default` preset), confines file tools to the working directories, loads only managed settings and `--settings`, refuses `bypassPermissions`, and refuses to create cloud sessions. Requires v2.1.248 or later.

nodes.label: --bg / --background
nodes.rationale: Starts the session as a background agent and returns immediately, printing the session ID and management commands. It combines with `--exec` to run a shell command as a background job instead of a Claude session, or with `--agent` for a specific subagent, and cannot be combined with `-p`/`--print`.

nodes.label: --exec
nodes.rationale: Runs a shell command as a PTY-backed background job instead of starting a Claude session, used with `--bg` to launch it from the shell (e.g. `claude --bg --exec 'pytest -x'`).

nodes.label: --channels (research preview)
nodes.rationale: Names the MCP servers whose channel notifications Claude should listen for in this session, as a space-separated list of `plugin:<name>@<marketplace>` entries, and requires Anthropic authentication through claude.ai or a Console API key. `--dangerously-load-development-channels` enables channels off the approved allowlist for local development and prompts for confirmation.

nodes.label: --chrome / --no-chrome
nodes.rationale: `--chrome` enables Chrome browser integration for web automation and testing; `--no-chrome` disables it for the session.

nodes.label: --cloud
nodes.rationale: With a task description, creates a new web session on claude.ai; with a session ID (`session_...` or `cse_...`) or a claude.ai/code URL, it queues a message into that existing session instead, used with `-p`.

nodes.label: --remote (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: `--remote` is a deprecated alias for `--cloud`, including the existing-session form.

nodes.label: --debug
nodes.rationale: Enables debug mode with optional category filtering such as `--debug='mcp,startup'` or `--debug='!1p'`. The filter binds only in the `=` form; a space-separated filter enables debug mode without filtering.

nodes.label: --debug-file <path>
nodes.rationale: Writes debug logs to a specific file path, implicitly enabling debug mode, and takes precedence over `CLAUDE_CODE_DEBUG_LOGS_DIR`.

nodes.label: --effort
nodes.rationale: Sets the session's effort level to `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max` or `ultracode`, with available levels depending on the model. `ultracode` starts at `xhigh` with ultracode turned on and needs v2.1.203 or later. The flag overrides the `modelSettings` and `effortLevel` settings for the session and does not persist.

nodes.label: --environment <environment-id>
nodes.rationale: Creates a new cloud session that runs on the self-hosted environment with the given ID; environment IDs start with `ccpool_`. Dispatch behavior and the flag combinations it rejects are documented separately. Requires v2.1.224 or later.

nodes.label: --ref <branch>
nodes.rationale: Used with `--environment`, bases the new session's checkout on a named ref instead of the local `HEAD`.

nodes.label: --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections
nodes.rationale: Moves per-machine sections — working directory, environment info, memory paths, git-repo flag — out of the system prompt and into the first user message. It only applies with the default system prompt and is ignored when `--system-prompt` or `--system-prompt-file` is set; intended for `-p` scripted, multi-user workloads.

nodes.label: Prompt-cache reuse across machines
nodes.rationale: Keeping per-machine detail out of the system prompt improves prompt-cache reuse across different users and machines running the same task — the stated payoff of `--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections`.

nodes.label: --fallback-model
nodes.rationale: Enables automatic fallback to the specified model(s) when the primary model is overloaded or unavailable — for example a retired model — accepting a comma-separated list tried in order. It overrides the `fallbackModel` setting, which is how a chain persists across sessions.

nodes.label: --fork-session
nodes.rationale: When resuming, creates a new session ID instead of reusing the original; used with `--resume` or `--continue`.

nodes.label: --forward-subagent-text
nodes.rationale: Emits subagent text and thinking blocks in the output stream as `assistant` and `user` messages with `parent_tool_use_id` set, so each subagent's transcript can be reconstructed; without it Claude Code emits only subagent `tool_use` and `tool_result` blocks. Nested subagent messages are forwarded too (v2.1.219+), and `CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT` enables the same behavior. Requires v2.1.211 or later.

nodes.label: --from-pr
nodes.rationale: Opens the session picker filtered to sessions linked to a specific pull request, accepting a PR number, a GitHub or GitHub Enterprise PR URL, a GitLab merge request URL, or a Bitbucket pull request URL. Sessions are linked automatically when Claude creates the pull request.

nodes.label: --init / --init-only / --maintenance
nodes.rationale: `--init` runs Setup hooks with the `init` matcher before the session and `--maintenance` runs them with the `maintenance` matcher, both print mode only; `--init-only` runs Setup and `SessionStart` hooks and then exits without starting a conversation.

nodes.label: --include-hook-events
nodes.rationale: Includes hook lifecycle events in the output stream. `SessionStart` and `Setup` events are always included, while `Notification`, `SessionEnd`, `PreCompact` and `PostCompact` never produce a `hook_started` event even with the flag — for those Claude Code still emits `hook_progress` when a command hook runs over a second with output, and `hook_response` only when a background hook finishes. Requires `--output-format stream-json`.

nodes.label: --include-partial-messages
nodes.rationale: Includes partial streaming events in the output; requires `--print` and `--output-format stream-json`.

nodes.label: --input-format / --output-format
nodes.rationale: Print mode's I/O shape: `--input-format` accepts `text` or `stream-json`, and `--output-format` accepts `text`, `json` or `stream-json`. `stream-json` is the mode the streaming and instrumentation flags are documented as requiring.

nodes.label: --json-schema
nodes.rationale: Returns validated JSON output matching a JSON Schema after the agent completes its workflow (print mode only). Claude Code exits with an error on an invalid schema and accepts the `format` keyword as an annotation without client-side validation.

nodes.label: --max-budget-usd
nodes.rationale: Caps the dollar amount spent on API calls before stopping (print mode only). Subagent spend counts toward the cap; once reached, spawning another subagent fails with `Budget limit reached` and Claude Code stops background subagents still running. The cap-enforcement behaviors require v2.1.217 or later.

nodes.label: --max-turns
nodes.rationale: Limits the number of agentic turns (print mode only) and exits with an error when the limit is reached; there is no limit by default. With `--input-format stream-json`, a message still queued when the limit ends a turn stays queued and starts a new turn with its own limit.

nodes.label: --mcp-config
nodes.rationale: Loads MCP servers from JSON files or strings (space-separated). Passed with `-p`, Claude Code waits for still-pending servers to connect before the first turn, up to the `MCP_TIMEOUT` startup timeout; a server with a cached tool list skips the wait and connects on first use. The wait requires v2.1.221 or later.

nodes.label: MCP startup connect wait (MCP_TIMEOUT)
nodes.rationale: Before the first turn, Claude Code waits for pending MCP servers to connect, bounded by the `MCP_TIMEOUT` startup timeout, 30 seconds by default. The same bounded wait governs `--mcp-config` with `-p` and `--permission-prompt-tool`.

nodes.label: --strict-mcp-config
nodes.rationale: Uses only the MCP servers from `--mcp-config`, ignoring all other MCP configurations; its behavior under a managed MCP file is documented in the managed-mcp reference.

nodes.label: --model
nodes.rationale: Sets the model for the current session using an alias such as `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku` or `fable`, or a model's full name, overriding both the `model` setting and the `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` environment variable.

nodes.label: --name / -n
nodes.rationale: Sets a display name for the session, shown in `/resume` and the terminal title, and a named session can be resumed with `claude --resume <name>`. In an interactive session, if another live session on the machine already uses the name, Claude Code applies a variant of it; `/rename` changes the name mid-session.

nodes.label: --no-session-persistence
nodes.rationale: Disables session persistence so sessions are not saved to disk and cannot be resumed; print mode only. The `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` environment variable does the same in any mode.

nodes.label: --permission-mode
nodes.rationale: Begins the session in a specified permission mode: `default`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, or `manual` as an alias for `default` (v2.1.200+, listed by `--help` in place of `default`, both values working). It overrides `defaultMode` from settings files; without it or `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, a `-p` session starts in `default` when nothing is configured.

nodes.label: --permission-prompt-tool
nodes.rationale: Specifies an MCP tool to handle permission prompts in non-interactive mode, with Claude Code waiting for that tool's server to connect before the first turn up to `MCP_TIMEOUT`. The prompt tool cannot approve an MCP tool marked as requiring user interaction — Claude Code converts an `allow` result for one into a deny (v2.1.199+).

nodes.label: --plugin-dir / --plugin-url
nodes.rationale: `--plugin-dir` loads a plugin from a directory or `.zip` archive for the session only, one path per flag and repeatable; `--plugin-url` fetches a plugin `.zip` from a URL for the session only, repeatable or given as space-separated URLs in one quoted value.

nodes.label: --prompt-suggestions
nodes.rationale: Emits a `prompt_suggestion` message with a predicted next user prompt after each turn that generates one — very short conversations can produce none. Requires `--print`, `--output-format stream-json`, and `--verbose`.

nodes.label: --replay-user-messages
nodes.rationale: Re-emits user messages from stdin back on stdout for acknowledgment; requires both `--input-format stream-json` and `--output-format stream-json`.

nodes.label: --session-id
nodes.rationale: Uses a specific session ID for the conversation; the value must be a valid UUID.

nodes.label: --settings / --setting-sources
nodes.rationale: `--settings` takes a settings JSON file path or inline JSON string whose values override the same keys in `settings.json` for the session while omitted keys keep their file values; the file must be a regular file no larger than 2 MiB. `--setting-sources` takes a comma-separated list of sources to load (`user`, `project`, `local`).

nodes.label: --teleport
nodes.rationale: Resumes a web session (Claude Code on the web) in the local terminal.

nodes.label: --teammate-mode
nodes.rationale: Sets how agent-team teammates display: `in-process` (default), `auto`, `tmux`, or `iterm2` (added in v2.1.186). It overrides the `teammateMode` setting for the session.

nodes.label: --tmux
nodes.rationale: Creates a tmux session for the worktree and requires `--worktree`. It uses iTerm2 native panes when available; `--tmux=classic` forces traditional tmux.

nodes.label: --worktree / -w
nodes.rationale: Starts Claude in an isolated git worktree at `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>`, generating a name if none is given. Passing `#<number>`, a GitHub pull request URL, or a GitLab merge request URL fetches that PR or MR from `origin` and branches the worktree from it; the GitLab form requires v2.1.233 or later.

nodes.label: --verbose
nodes.rationale: Enables verbose logging showing full turn-by-turn output, and overrides the `viewMode` setting for the session. Several streaming flags list it among their requirements.

nodes.label: --disable-slash-commands
nodes.rationale: Disables all skills and commands for the session.

nodes.label: --betas
nodes.rationale: Adds beta headers to API requests, e.g. `claude --betas interleaved-thinking`. It is available to API key users only.

nodes.label: --enable-auto-mode (removed)
nodes.rationale: `--enable-auto-mode` was removed in v2.1.111: auto mode is now in the `Shift+Tab` cycle by default, and `--permission-mode auto` is what starts a session in it.

nodes.label: --ide
nodes.rationale: Automatically connects to an IDE on startup if exactly one valid IDE is available.

nodes.label: Cloud environment
nodes.rationale: A cloud environment is the configurable container every Claude Code cloud session runs in. It can allow or deny network access, set environment variables for the session, store API credentials sessions use without seeing them, and run a setup script before Claude starts working.

nodes.label: Cloud session
nodes.rationale: A cloud session is one run of Claude Code inside a cloud environment. The same environments apply wherever a session is started: Claude Code on the web, the terminal with `claude --cloud`, Claude Tag, routines, the mobile app, and the Desktop app.

nodes.label: Claude Code on the web research preview
nodes.rationale: Cloud environments require Claude Code on the web, which is in research preview for Pro, Max, and Team users, and for Enterprise users with premium seats or Chat + Claude Code seats.

nodes.label: The Default environment
nodes.rationale: Onboarding creates a **Default** environment when you have none — automatically via CLI flows such as `/web-setup` and via web onboarding on Pro and Max, or through a create form on Team and Enterprise. Default carries no configuration of its own: Trusted network access, no environment variables, and no setup script.

nodes.label: Environment selector at claude.ai/code
nodes.rationale: Environments are created, edited, and archived from the environment selector at claude.ai/code — the cloud icon in the row above the message box. There is no settings page or direct URL for the selector. The dialog holds the name, network access level, environment variables, and setup script; editing an existing environment also exposes API credentials.

nodes.label: Environment variables (.env format)
nodes.rationale: An environment's variables use `.env` format, one KEY=value per line, with `#` starting a comment in an unquoted value. Each session copies the values once at startup, so edits affect only sessions started afterward. Anyone who uses the environment can read the values, so secrets do not belong there.

nodes.label: API credential
nodes.rationale: An API credential is a key or token stored on a cloud environment so Claude can call that API from any session without seeing the key; the key never reaches Claude, the commands it runs, or the session's environment variables. Credentials are added one at a time from an existing environment's editor, cannot be edited or viewed again, and are changed by deleting and re-adding.

nodes.label: Anthropic agent proxy
nodes.rationale: Anthropic's agent proxy adds a stored credential to requests for the hosts listed on it, after each request has left the session's VM. It attaches the key when the request host matches, lets sessions reach those hosts even when the network access level would not, and sends only one of two credentials whose hosts overlap without matching exactly.

nodes.label: API credential requirements
nodes.rationale: Four conditions govern credentials: an organization admin role (Owners on Team/Enterprise, yourself on Pro/Max); an Anthropic-hosted environment that already exists (self-hosted environments have no API credentials); an API reachable from the internet, because requests leave from Anthropic's network; and no customer-managed encryption keys, which block saving credentials.

nodes.label: Requests that never get the credential
nodes.rationale: The agent proxy never attaches a stored credential to GitHub requests (the GitHub proxy authenticates those), to the Anthropic API and public package registries (api.anthropic.com, registry.npmjs.org, jsr.io, npm.jsr.io, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, index.crates.io, proxy.golang.org), or to setup-script requests, because Claude Code connects to the agent proxy only after the setup script has run.

nodes.label: /remote-env command
nodes.rationale: `/remote-env` opens a picker of existing environments and saves the choice to `remote.defaultEnvironmentId` in user settings, applying in every project until changed unless a higher-precedence settings layer sets the same key. It only sets the default: it does not start a session and cannot add or edit environments.

nodes.label: --environment <environment-id> flag
nodes.rationale: Passing `--environment <environment-id>` with a self-hosted environment's `ccpool_` ID when dispatching a session overrides both the `/remote-env` pick and the fallback for that invocation. Claude Code rejects Anthropic-hosted `env_` IDs passed to the flag, and the flag requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.

nodes.label: CLI environment selection and fallback
nodes.rationale: From the CLI, Claude Code uses the `/remote-env` pick, or falls back to the Anthropic-hosted environment when the list has one, and otherwise to the first environment that is not a bridge environment — the entry Remote Control registers to represent your own machine. On the web, Desktop, and mobile, sessions instead use the environment shown in the selector, pre-filled by an organization default.

nodes.label: Archiving an environment
nodes.rationale: Environments can be archived but never deleted. Archiving affects new sessions only: running sessions continue and keep their attached API credentials, the environment disappears from the selector and `/remote-env`, and no new session can start in it on any surface — anything configured with it explicitly, such as a routine, must be repointed.

nodes.label: Organization-shared environments
nodes.rationale: On Team and Enterprise plans an Owner can create cloud environments shared with every member, managed from the **Cloud environments** admin page (the Admin role cannot open it). Shared environments appear in each member's selector as read-only, letting a team standardize on one configuration; their variables are readable by every member, so secrets belong in an API credential instead.
