nodes.label: Claude Tag channel environment
nodes.rationale: In Claude Tag channels Claude works as the organization's shared identity rather than as a member, so channel sessions use organization-level environments only — either shared or self-hosted. A channel is pointed at one by setting the organization default at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-code or by pinning an environment to the channel in Claude Tag admin settings.

nodes.label: Network access levels
nodes.rationale: Each environment sets exactly one of four outbound network levels: **None** (no outbound access through the session's network), **Trusted** (allowlisted domains only — package registries, GitHub, cloud SDKs), **Full** (any domain), and **Custom** (your own allowlist, optionally including the defaults).

nodes.label: Default allowed domains (Trusted list)
nodes.rationale: With Trusted access, sessions reach a published allowlist grouped by category: Anthropic services, version control (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket), container registries, cloud platforms, language package managers (npm, PyPI, RubyGems, crates.io, Go, Maven/Gradle, Composer, NuGet, Hex, CPAN, CocoaPods, Hackage, Swift), Linux distributions, developer tooling, monitoring, CDNs, schema hosts, and `*.modelcontextprotocol.io`. A leading `*` denotes wildcard subdomain matching.

nodes.label: Custom allowed domains
nodes.rationale: Selecting **Custom** takes one domain per line in **Allowed domains**, where a leading `*.` matches every subdomain. Checking *Also include default list of common package managers* keeps the Trusted domains; leaving it unchecked allows only what is listed.

nodes.label: Artifacts host *.frame.claudeusercontent.com
nodes.rationale: Sessions that work with artifacts need `*.frame.claudeusercontent.com` in a custom allowlist, because Claude Code fetches artifact content from that host. Leaving it out means Claude cannot read artifacts in sessions run in that environment.

nodes.label: No organization-level network allowlist
nodes.rationale: Each environment has its own allowed-domains list and there is no organization-level allowlist an admin can push to every member's environments. Server-managed settings still apply inside cloud sessions, but none of them adds domains to an environment's network allowlist.

nodes.label: GitHub proxy
nodes.rationale: In Anthropic-hosted environments every GitHub operation goes through a dedicated proxy that keeps real GitHub credentials outside the session VM, independent of the access level. It swaps a scoped git credential for the real token, substitutes credentials on API requests, restricts `git push` to the session's current branch, limits API and release-asset access to attached repositories (403 otherwise), and serves only a pinned set of GraphQL operations — rejecting the rest with `This GraphQL query is not enabled for this session`, so GraphQL-only APIs such as Projects v2 are unreachable.

nodes.label: Security proxy
nodes.rationale: All outbound internet traffic from an Anthropic-hosted cloud session passes through an HTTP/HTTPS security proxy providing protection against malicious requests, rate limiting and abuse prevention, content filtering, and a DNS-level audit trail of requested hostnames. In a self-hosted environment traffic leaves through the organization's own network boundary instead.

nodes.label: Bun proxy incompatibility
nodes.rationale: Some package managers do not work correctly behind the Anthropic-hosted security proxy; Bun is the named example — it is pre-installed but has known proxy compatibility issues for package fetching.

nodes.label: MCP connector traffic
nodes.rationale: MCP connectors enabled on a session or routine work without adding their hosts to Allowed domains, because connector traffic travels through Anthropic's servers rather than the session's network. Connectors are configured per session or per routine, so removing unneeded ones limits which tools Claude can reach.

nodes.label: Session VM (Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64)
nodes.rationale: In Anthropic-hosted environments each session gets a fresh virtual machine running Ubuntu 24.04 on x86_64 regardless of the user's own OS and CPU architecture, with the repository cloned and common toolchains pre-installed. Dependencies that ship precompiled binaries must use their x86_64 Linux build to match the VM.

nodes.label: Resource limits
nodes.rationale: Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions run with approximate ceilings that may change over time: 4 vCPUs, 16 GB of RAM, and 30 GB of disk. The VM may stop tasks needing significantly more memory, such as large builds or memory-intensive tests.

nodes.label: Pre-installed tools
nodes.rationale: Cloud sessions ship with Python 3.x (pip, poetry, uv, black, mypy, pytest, ruff), Node.js 20/21/22 (npm, yarn, pnpm, bun, eslint, prettier, chromedriver), Ruby 3.1–3.3, PHP 8.3 with Composer, OpenJDK 21 with Maven and Gradle, Go, Rust, C/C++ toolchains, Docker, PostgreSQL 16 and Redis 7.0, and utilities (git, gh, jq, yq, ripgrep, tmux, vim, nano). Toolchains outside this list, such as the .NET SDK, are not pre-installed.

nodes.label: check-tools command
nodes.rationale: `check-tools` is a shell command installed on the session VM — not a slash command — that reports the versions of most pre-installed tools; you ask Claude to run it because Claude runs all VM commands for you. For tools it does not report (Ruby, PHP, bun, PostgreSQL, Redis) ask Claude to run the tool's own version command.

nodes.label: Node.js version paths
nodes.rationale: Node.js is installed at `/opt/node20`, `/opt/node21`, and `/opt/node22`, with 22 on PATH by default. To use another version, ask Claude to prepend that version's `bin` directory, such as `/opt/node20/bin`, to PATH.

nodes.label: What carries over from your setup
nodes.rationale: Repo-committed configuration reaches cloud sessions — CLAUDE.md, `.claude/settings.json` hooks, `.mcp.json`, `.claude/rules/`, skills, agents, commands, and plugins declared in the repo. Machine-local configuration does not: `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, user skills/agents/commands, user-scoped `enabledPlugins`, MCP servers added at local or user scope, transport variables such as `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, and interactive auth like AWS SSO.

nodes.label: Fresh repository clone
nodes.rationale: Cloud sessions start from a fresh clone of the repository: anything committed to the repo is available, and anything installed or configured only on the user's own machine is not. The remedy for making local configuration available is to commit it to the repo.

nodes.label: Server-managed settings in cloud sessions
nodes.rationale: An organization's server-managed settings are fetched from Anthropic's servers when a session starts, arriving separately from the repo clone. Settings deployed to a device via MDM or managed settings files do not apply, because the session runs on an Anthropic-managed VM; self-hosted sessions additionally read the runner image's managed settings file.

nodes.label: Built-in GitHub tools
nodes.rationale: Cloud sessions include built-in GitHub tools that let Claude read issues, list pull requests, fetch diffs, and post comments without setup. They authenticate through the GitHub proxy using whichever GitHub authentication option was configured, so the token never enters the container; the `gh` CLI is pre-installed for commands the built-in tools do not cover.

nodes.label: GH_TOKEN and the proxy-injected placeholder
nodes.rationale: You may set `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` yourself — it passes through unchanged and is readable by anyone using the environment — or leave both unset, in which case they read as the placeholder string `proxy-injected` and the proxy substitutes real credentials on outbound requests. A script that reads `GITHUB_TOKEN` directly gets the placeholder, not a usable token; `echo $GH_TOKEN` shows which case applies.

nodes.label: Session URL and CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID
nodes.rationale: Each cloud session has a transcript URL on claude.ai and can read its own ID from `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE_SESSION_ID`. Commits include a `Claude-Session: <url>` git trailer and PR bodies carry the session URL (v2.1.179+; disable with `attribution.sessionUrl` false, v2.1.182+); for other outputs, convert the `cse_` prefix to `session_` to build the transcript link.

nodes.label: Setup script
nodes.rationale: A setup script is a Bash script that runs as root on Ubuntu 24.04 when a new cloud session starts, before Claude Code launches, so `apt install` and most language package managers work. It is entered in the environment dialog's **Setup script** field and is the way to install toolchains that are not pre-installed.

nodes.label: Setup script constraints
nodes.rationale: Three constraints govern a setup script: it must exit zero or the session fails to start (append `|| true` to non-critical commands); it must finish within roughly five minutes so the environment cache can build (parallelize with `&`/`wait`, or move a long download into a background SessionStart hook); and package installs need network access, which fails entirely at the **None** level.

nodes.label: Environment caching
nodes.rationale: After the setup script completes on the first session, Anthropic snapshots the filesystem and reuses it for later sessions, which start with dependencies, tools and Docker images on disk and skip the setup step. The snapshot keeps files but loses anything only running, and is rebuilt when the setup script or allowed hosts change or after roughly seven days; resuming an existing session never re-runs the script.

nodes.label: SessionStart hook
nodes.rationale: A SessionStart hook is configured in a settings file such as the repo's `.claude/settings.json` and runs after Claude Code launches, on every session — local and cloud, including resumed ones. It is the right tool for project setup that should run everywhere, such as `npm install`, whereas a setup script provisions the VM itself.

nodes.label: Cloud-only dependency install pattern
nodes.rationale: To install dependencies only in cloud sessions, pair a SessionStart hook matched on `startup|resume` running `bash "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"/scripts/install_pkgs.sh` with a script that exits early unless `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` is `true`. Together the two files give every cloud session a fresh `npm install` and `pip install` while leaving local sessions untouched.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE environment variable
nodes.rationale: The session VM's environment carries `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` as `true`, and it is never `true` locally. Checking it is what scopes a hook's work to cloud sessions, since hooks themselves offer no cloud-only matcher.

nodes.label: SessionStart hook limitations in the cloud
nodes.rationale: Four caveats apply to SessionStart hooks in cloud sessions: no cloud-only scoping (check `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE`), a hard requirement for network access so installs fail at the None level, proxy-compatibility problems for some package managers, and added startup latency because hooks run every start or resume without the benefit of environment caching.

nodes.label: Running tests, services and packages
nodes.rationale: There is no shell into the session VM — Claude runs every command, so tasks are phrased as prompt requests. PostgreSQL and Redis are pre-installed but not running (`service postgresql start`, `service redis-server start`), Docker is available for `docker compose up`, and image pulls follow the environment's access level.

nodes.label: Remote Control sessions
nodes.rationale: Remote Control connects the web and mobile interfaces to a session on your own machine, using that machine's network and files rather than a cloud environment. It registers a bridge environment entry in the environment list, and is the recommended route for workloads beyond the cloud VM's resource ceilings.

nodes.label: Self-hosted environment
nodes.rationale: Sessions an organization routes to a self-hosted environment run on its own runners with the tools its runner image provides, identified by a `ccpool_` ID. Self-hosted environments have no API credentials, authenticate git with deployment-provided credentials, send outbound traffic through the organization's own network boundary, and additionally run hooks seeded from the runner host and its managed settings file.

nodes.label: Claude Code commands
nodes.rationale: Commands control Claude Code from inside a session, giving a quick way to switch models, manage permissions, clear context, run a workflow, and more. Typing / shows the commands available to you, and typing / followed by letters filters the menu.

nodes.label: Commands recognized only at message start
nodes.rationale: A command is only recognized at the start of your message; text that follows the command name becomes its arguments.

nodes.label: Chained skill invocations
nodes.rationale: As of v2.1.199 skills are the exception to the one-command rule: a skill invocation followed by more skills, such as /skill-a /skill-b do XYZ, loads every skill named at the start and passes the trailing text to each as arguments. Up to six skills can be chained.

nodes.label: Queuing while Claude responds
nodes.rationale: A command sent while Claude is responding is queued and runs after the current turn finishes. Some commands run immediately without interrupting the response, such as /status, /tasks and /usage; in fullscreen rendering, dialog commands such as /theme and /help also open immediately (before v2.1.234 those dialogs were queued).

nodes.label: Per-user command availability
nodes.rationale: Not every command appears for every user: availability depends on platform, plan and environment. /desktop only shows on macOS and x64 Windows when signed in with a Claude subscription, and /upgrade does not show on Enterprise plans.

nodes.label: Argument notation in the command table
nodes.rationale: In the command reference table, <arg> indicates a required argument and [arg] indicates an optional one.

nodes.label: Bundled skill commands
nodes.rationale: A command marked Skill is a bundled skill: it works like skills you write yourself, a prompt handed to Claude. /verify runs only when you invoke it; before v2.1.215 Claude could also run /verify on its own.

nodes.label: Bundled workflow commands
nodes.rationale: A command marked Workflow is a bundled dynamic workflow that fans work out across many subagents and runs in the background. /deep-research runs only when you invoke it; before v2.1.218 Claude could also start it on its own.

nodes.label: Adding your own commands
nodes.rationale: To add your own commands you write skills; the Skills documentation is the create-your-own-commands path, and bundled skill commands use the same mechanism.

nodes.label: First session in a repo
nodes.rationale: For a first session in a repo the doc prescribes /init to generate a starter CLAUDE.md, /memory to refine it, /mcp to set up any servers the project needs, asking Claude to create subagents, and /permissions to set approval rules.

nodes.label: Commands during a task
nodes.rationale: During a task: /plan switches into plan mode before a large change, /model and /effort adjust the model and how much reasoning it applies, /context shows what is filling the window and /compact summarizes it, and /btw asks a side question that should not add to the conversation history.

nodes.label: Running work in parallel
nodes.rationale: Claude delegates side tasks to subagents; /tasks lists the current session's background work including finished subagents, /background detaches the whole session to keep running as a background agent, and /batch decomposes a codebase-spanning change into independent units each run in its own worktree.

nodes.label: Before you ship
nodes.rationale: Before shipping: /diff shows what changed, /code-review checks the current diff for correctness bugs and cleanups and can apply findings with --fix (a PR number reviews a pull request instead), /review is an alias, /code-review ultra runs a multi-agent cloud review, and /security-review checks the diff for security vulnerabilities.

nodes.label: Between sessions
nodes.rationale: Between sessions: /clear starts fresh while keeping project memory, /resume returns to an earlier conversation, /branch branches the current one, /fork copies it into a new background session, /teleport pulls a web session into the terminal, and /remote-control continues the local session from another device.

nodes.label: When something is wrong
nodes.rationale: When something is wrong: /rewind rolls code and conversation back to a checkpoint or summarizes part of the conversation, /doctor runs a setup checkup that diagnoses and can fix installation and configuration issues, /debug diagnoses runtime issues, and /feedback reports a bug with session context attached.

nodes.label: /init
nodes.rationale: Initializes a project with a CLAUDE.md guide. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 gives an interactive flow that also walks through skills, hooks and personal memory files. If it finds configuration from a coding agent that /import supports, it offers to carry it over.

nodes.label: /memory
nodes.rationale: Edits CLAUDE.md files, enables or disables auto memory, and views auto memory entries.

nodes.label: /permissions
nodes.rationale: Manages allow, ask and deny rules for tool permissions through an interactive dialog: view rules by scope, add or remove rules, manage working directories, review recent auto mode denials, and edit auto mode classifier rules. Run mid-response it opens immediately and applies from Claude's next tool call (queued before v2.1.234). Alias: /allowed-tools.

nodes.label: /mcp
nodes.rationale: Manages MCP server connections and OAuth authentication. With no argument it opens the interactive list; reconnect <server> reconnects one disconnected server, and enable/disable with a server name or all changes connection state without the dialog. In non-interactive mode (-p) with no argument it prints a text summary; requires v2.1.205 or later.

nodes.label: /plan
nodes.rationale: Enters plan mode directly from the prompt; an optional description enters plan mode and immediately starts with that task, for example /plan fix the auth bug.

nodes.label: /model
nodes.rationale: Switches the AI model and saves it as the default for new sessions; left/right arrows adjust effort level for models that support it, and pressing s on a row switches for the current session only. Also available in -p with a model argument, where it applies to the current session only and is not saved as the default (requires v2.1.205 or later).

nodes.label: /effort
nodes.rationale: Sets the effort level: low to xhigh, max, ultracode, or auto; status prints it. max and ultracode are session-only while the ultracode settings key persists. Run mid-turn it applies the new level to the next request in that turn once the cache warning is confirmed.

nodes.label: /context
nodes.rationale: Visualizes current context usage as a colored grid with optimization suggestions for context-heavy tools, memory bloat and capacity warnings. When the conversation exceeds the context window the output includes a warning showing how far over the limit you are and which command frees space. In fullscreen the per-item breakdown collapses; pass all to expand.

nodes.label: /compact
nodes.rationale: Frees up context by summarizing the conversation so far, optionally with focus instructions for the summary.

nodes.label: /autocompact
nodes.rationale: Sets the auto-compact window — how full the context window gets before Claude Code compacts automatically. Accepts a size such as 500k, or auto to return to the window tuned for your model; the value is saved to user settings and applied to the current session. Requires v2.1.221 or later.

nodes.label: /btw
nodes.rationale: Asks a side question about the current session without adding to the conversation. With no question it shows your most recent side question so you can browse earlier answers, or prints a usage line if you have not asked one; before v2.1.212 /btw required a question.

nodes.label: /tasks
nodes.rationale: Views and manages background work in the current session, including subagents that have finished. Also available as /bashes.

nodes.label: /background
nodes.rationale: Detaches the current session to run as a background agent and frees the terminal; an optional prompt sends one more instruction before detaching. Monitor with claude agents. Alias: /bg.

nodes.label: /batch
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that orchestrates large-scale changes across a codebase in parallel: it researches the codebase, decomposes the work into 5 to 30 independent units, presents a plan, and on approval spawns one background subagent per unit in an isolated git worktree that implements its unit, runs tests and opens a pull request. Requires a git repository.

nodes.label: /fork
nodes.rationale: Copies the current conversation into a new background session while you keep working here. With a prompt the copy starts immediately; without one it waits in agent view. Except when the copy edits in place, Claude Code instructs it to create its own worktree before making code changes. Requires v2.1.212 or later.

nodes.label: /subtask
nodes.rationale: Spawns a forked subagent — a background subagent that inherits the full conversation and works on the task while you keep working — whose result returns to this conversation when it finishes. Requires v2.1.212 or later; on v2.1.161 through v2.1.211 this command is /fork.

nodes.label: /branch
nodes.rationale: Creates a branch of the current conversation at this point so you can try a different direction without losing the conversation as it stands. It switches you into the branch and preserves the original, which you can return to with /resume.

nodes.label: /clear
nodes.rationale: Starts a new conversation with empty context; a name labels the previous conversation in the /resume picker. The previous conversation can be resumed with /resume or, in the same process, restored from the rewind menu's previous-session entry. Aliases: /reset, /new.

nodes.label: /resume
nodes.rationale: Resumes a conversation by ID or name, or opens the session picker. Background sessions appear marked with bg; one still running cannot be resumed here, so attach to it from claude agents or stop it there first. Alias: /continue.

nodes.label: /teleport
nodes.rationale: Pulls a Claude Code on the web session into this terminal: opens a picker, then fetches the branch and conversation. Also available as /tp; requires a claude.ai subscription.

nodes.label: /remote-control
nodes.rationale: Makes this session available for Remote Control from claude.ai. Run while signed out it prints that Remote Control requires a claude.ai subscription and how to sign in; before v2.1.206 it reported Unknown command. Alias: /rc.

nodes.label: /rewind
nodes.rationale: Rewinds the conversation and/or code to a previous point, or summarizes from a selected message. Aliases: /checkpoint, /undo.

nodes.label: /doctor
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that runs a setup checkup which diagnoses issues and can fix them: installation health, duplicate installs, PATH problems, unparseable settings, unused skills/MCP servers/plugins versus their context cost, slow hooks, and newer versions on your release channel. It deduplicates and trims CLAUDE.md files and reports findings before changing anything. Alias: /checkup.

nodes.label: /debug
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that enables debug logging for the current session and troubleshoots issues by reading the session debug log. Debug logging is off by default unless started with claude --debug, so running /debug mid-session captures logs only from that point forward.

nodes.label: /feedback
nodes.rationale: Sends product feedback about Claude Code, opening the same dialog as /bug with the same consent step, sending rules and mid-turn behavior. In sessions with Claude-drafted feedback, /feedback with no argument opens the drafts queue where you review, edit, send or discard the drafts Claude queued.

nodes.label: /bug
nodes.rationale: Reports a bug or shares your conversation: you choose how much session history to include and confirm on a consent screen before anything is sent. Signed in to Anthropic on a first-party connection the report goes to Anthropic; otherwise Claude Code writes it to a local archive under ~/.claude/feedback-bundles/ that you forward yourself. Alias: /share.

nodes.label: /code-review
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that reviews the current diff, or a PR number, branch or path you pass, for correctness bugs and cleanup opportunities. --fix applies findings, --comment posts them as inline GitHub PR comments, and ultra runs a deep cloud review; with ultra on a github.com PR target, --post preselects posting the findings to the PR. Alias: /review.

nodes.label: /review
nodes.rationale: An alias of /code-review taking the same effort levels and flags. With no level given the review reuses the last low-through-max level you typed. Before v2.1.223 /review was a separate command that ran a single-pass read-only review of a GitHub pull request by number.

nodes.label: /ultrareview
nodes.rationale: Runs a deep, multi-agent code review in a cloud sandbox; a PR reference reviews that pull request and a branch name changes the comparison base. The preferred invocation is now /code-review ultra, with /ultrareview remaining as an alias. Includes 3 free runs on Pro and Max, then requires usage credits.

nodes.label: /security-review
nodes.rationale: Analyzes the changes on the current branch for security vulnerabilities, reviewing the diff between your branch and origin's default branch and identifying risks like injection, auth issues and data exposure. It needs an origin remote.

nodes.label: /simplify
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that reviews the changed code for cleanup opportunities and applies the fixes: four review agents run in parallel covering reuse of existing helpers, simplification, efficiency, and whether the change is at the right level of abstraction. It does not look for correctness bugs.

nodes.label: /diff
nodes.rationale: Opens an interactive diff viewer showing uncommitted changes and per-turn diffs. Claude Code computes these diffs from raw git blob content, so diff drivers and textconv filters configured in .gitattributes or git config do not apply. The open viewer auto-refreshes when the repository's git state changes outside the session (requires v2.1.198 or later).

nodes.label: /deep-research
nodes.rationale: A bundled workflow that fans out web searches on a question, fetches and cross-checks sources, and synthesizes a cited report.

nodes.label: /verify
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that confirms a code change does what it should by building your project's app, running it and observing the result, rather than relying on tests or type checks.

nodes.label: /run
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that launches and drives your project's app to see a change working, not only passing tests.

nodes.label: /run-skill-generator
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that teaches /run and /verify how to build, launch and drive your project's app from a clean environment by writing a per-project skill.

nodes.label: /dataviz
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill giving design guidance for charts, graphs and dashboards: Claude picks the chart form for the data, assigns color by role, validates the palette for colorblind safety and contrast with a bundled script, and applies mark, interaction and accessibility rules. Requires v2.1.198 or later.

nodes.label: /design
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that drafts UI mockups, screen flows, landing pages or posters as artboards on one canvas, published as an artifact running a research preview of Claude Design's editor. Requires a session where artifacts are available and Claude Code v2.1.234 or later.

nodes.label: /design-sync
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that converts your repo's React design system and uploads it to Claude Design so designs it produces use your real components. A first-time sync verifies every component and can take a few hours on a large repo.

nodes.label: /design-login
nodes.rationale: Authorizes design-system access for /design-sync with your claude.ai account.

nodes.label: /claude-api
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that loads Claude API and Managed Agents reference material for your project's language, and activates automatically when your code imports anthropic or @anthropic-ai/sdk. Subcommands: migrate, upgrade, managed-agents-onboard, prompt-audit and cost-optimize (which requires v2.1.247 or later).

nodes.label: /loop
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that runs a prompt repeatedly while the session stays open. Omitting the interval lets Claude self-pace between iterations; omitting the prompt runs the built-in maintenance prompt or your loop.md. Alias: /proactive.

nodes.label: /schedule
nodes.rationale: Creates, updates, lists or runs routines, which execute in the cloud; Claude walks you through the setup conversationally and can report a routine's recent runs. Alias: /routines.

nodes.label: /workflows
nodes.rationale: Opens the workflow progress view to watch, pause, resume or save running and completed workflows.

nodes.label: /workflow-authoring
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that loads the reference for writing dynamic workflow scripts: the script API, resume behavior, quality patterns and worked examples. Claude normally loads it on its own before writing a script; run it yourself before editing a saved script by hand. Requires v2.1.248 or later.

nodes.label: /add-dir
nodes.rationale: Adds a working directory for file access during the current session, with tab-completed directory suggestions. Most .claude/ configuration is not discovered from the added directory. A successful add runs your DirectoryAdded hooks.

nodes.label: /cd
nodes.rationale: Moves this session to a new working directory while keeping the conversation, with tab-completed directory suggestions (suggestions require v2.1.206 or later). Requires Claude Code v2.1.169 or later.

nodes.label: /advisor
nodes.rationale: Enables or disables the advisor tool, which consults a second model for guidance at key moments during a task. It accepts fable, opus, sonnet or a full model ID; fable requires Fable access. Without an argument it opens a picker.

nodes.label: /agents
nodes.rationale: As of v2.1.198, running /agents prints a reminder to ask Claude to create or manage subagents, or to edit .claude/agents/ or ~/.claude/agents/ directly. On v2.1.197 and earlier it opened an interactive interface for creating and managing subagent configurations.

nodes.label: /artifacts
nodes.rationale: Lists the artifacts you own or that are shared with you, then attaches one to the session, opens it in your browser, or copies its link. Requires Claude Code v2.1.208 or later; attaching with Enter requires v2.1.216.

nodes.label: /auto-mode-setup
nodes.rationale: Drafts autoMode.environment entries from your project and recent sessions, then lets you review the draft and save it to your user settings. Requires a Pro, Max or Team plan and Claude Code v2.1.228 or later (v2.1.233 on native Windows).

nodes.label: /autofix-pr
nodes.rationale: Spawns a Claude Code on the web session that watches the current branch's PR and pushes fixes when CI fails or reviewers leave comments. It detects the open PR from the checked-out branch with gh pr view, so watching a different PR means checking out its branch first. Requires the gh CLI.

nodes.label: /config
nodes.rationale: Opens the Settings interface to adjust theme, model, output style and other preferences. From v2.1.181 one or more key=value pairs set a setting directly without opening the interface; the key=value form also works in -p and via Remote Control, but cannot turn ON a setting that needs confirmation in the panel. Alias: /settings.

nodes.label: /usage
nodes.rationale: Shows session cost, plan usage limits and activity stats, including a breakdown of what counts against your plan limits on Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plans. /cost and /stats are aliases, with /stats opening on the Stats tab.

nodes.label: /rate-limit-options
nodes.rationale: Shows ways to keep working when a claude.ai usage limit blocks a request: wait and continue automatically when the limit resets, add usage credits, or upgrade your plan. Claude Code can open this menu on its own when you hit a limit at your own terminal.

nodes.label: /usage-credits
nodes.rationale: Configures usage credits, or requests them from your admin, when you hit a limit. It opens usage-credits billing settings in the browser, except that Team and Enterprise members without billing access send a request to their admin from the CLI. Previously /extra-usage.

nodes.label: /plugin
nodes.rationale: Manages Claude Code plugins: with no argument it opens the plugin menu, or a subcommand such as list, install, enable or disable acts directly. Claude Code can activate a plugin during the install, and the install summary tells you whether it did or whether to run /reload-plugins.

nodes.label: /reload-plugins
nodes.rationale: Reloads all active plugins to apply pending changes without restarting, reporting counts for each reloaded component and flagging load errors. When the reload would change which MCP tools are loaded and invalidate the prompt cache, it warns and skips unless you pass --force.

nodes.label: /reload-skills
nodes.rationale: Re-scans skill and command directories so skills added or changed on disk during the session become available without restarting, reporting how many skills are available and how many were added or removed.

nodes.label: /skills
nodes.rationale: Lists available skills, filterable by name, description or source. Press t to sort by token count and Space or Enter to cycle a skill's visibility to Claude and the / menu; plugin skills, skills with disable-model-invocation: true, and skills with a skillOverrides entry cannot be cycled.

nodes.label: /list-agents
nodes.rationale: Lists the subagents, agent team teammates and other Claude Code sessions Claude can message, with the name to use for each. Also available as /peers; requires v2.1.224 or later, and teammate rows plus this session's own name require v2.1.239. Available only where cross-session messaging is enabled.

nodes.label: /import
nodes.rationale: Brings configuration from other coding agents on your machine — currently OpenAI Codex and Google Gemini CLI — into Claude Code, including instruction files, MCP servers, commands, subagents and skills. --dry-run previews without writing and --yes skips the picker. Requires Claude Code v2.1.213 or later.

nodes.label: /heapdump
nodes.rationale: Writes a JavaScript heap snapshot and a memory breakdown to ~/Desktop for diagnosing high memory usage. Attach only the -diagnostics.json file when reporting a memory issue: the .heapsnapshot contains your full conversation and credentials, so do not share it.

nodes.label: /insights
nodes.rationale: Generates an HTML report analyzing your recent sessions on this machine: which projects you work in, how you use Claude Code, where things go wrong, and features to try. Not available in cloud sessions.

nodes.label: /team-onboarding
nodes.rationale: Generates a team onboarding guide from your Claude Code usage history: Claude analyzes your sessions, commands and MCP server usage from the past 30 days and produces a markdown guide a teammate can paste as a first message. Subscribers on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise also get a share link.

nodes.label: /fewer-permission-prompts
nodes.rationale: A bundled skill that scans your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then adds a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

nodes.label: /goal
nodes.rationale: Sets a goal: Claude keeps working across turns until the condition is met or the goal clears for another reason. With no argument it shows the current or most recently achieved goal; clear, stop, off, reset, none or cancel removes an active goal early.

nodes.label: /status
nodes.rationale: Opens the Settings interface on the Status tab, showing version, model, account and connectivity. A Session kind row reads background job attached or unattended in a background session and interactive in any other; it works while Claude is responding.

nodes.label: /focus
nodes.rationale: Toggles the focus view, which shows only your last prompt, a one-line tool-call summary with edit diffstats, and the final response. The selection persists across sessions and the viewMode setting overrides it. Only available in fullscreen rendering.

nodes.label: /tui
nodes.rationale: Sets the terminal UI renderer and relaunches into it with your conversation intact; fullscreen enables the flicker-free alt-screen renderer, and with no argument it prints the active renderer.

nodes.label: /sandbox
nodes.rationale: Toggles sandbox mode; available on supported platforms only.

nodes.label: /setup-bedrock
nodes.rationale: Configures Amazon Bedrock authentication, region and model pins through an interactive wizard. It is hidden from the command menu until CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 is set; first-time Bedrock users can also reach the wizard from the login screen.

nodes.label: /setup-vertex
nodes.rationale: Configures Google Cloud's Agent Platform authentication, project, region and model pins through an interactive wizard. It is hidden from the command menu until CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1 is set; first-time users can also reach it from the login screen.

nodes.label: Removed commands
nodes.rationale: Some table entries document removals: /pr-comments was removed in v2.1.91 (ask Claude to view PR comments instead), /ultraplan was removed in favor of plan mode, and /vim was removed in v2.1.92 in favor of /config then Editor mode.

nodes.label: Third-party provider unavailability
nodes.rationale: On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS several commands are unavailable: artifacts are not available there so /design cannot run, /design-sync's underlying tool cannot reach claude.ai, and /import is not available.

nodes.label: Feature-flag fetching dependency
nodes.rationale: Some behavior depends on Claude Code fetching feature flags from Anthropic: /import is unavailable when feature-flag fetching is turned off, and before v2.1.242 /effort, /fast and /model decided from a fetched flag whether to run mid-turn, always queuing in sessions that do not fetch flags, such as on a third-party provider.

nodes.label: How the command menu matches what you type
nodes.rationale: Claude Code filters the / menu as you type; the doc enumerates four behaviors you might notice while filtering — highlighting, what happens after a typo, commands not available to you, and hidden commands.

nodes.label: Menu highlighting rules
nodes.rationale: Claude Code highlights the top suggestion only when the letters after the / match a command's name or alias, from the start of the name or from a word within it, ignoring the :, _ and - separators. Typing /adddir highlights /add-dir and /new highlights /clear through its alias. These rules require v2.1.236 or later.

nodes.label: Menu behavior after a typo
nodes.rationale: After a typo Claude Code highlights nothing: close matches stay listed and can be picked with Tab or the arrow keys, but Enter submits your text as typed and reports Unknown command.

nodes.label: Unavailable commands in the menu
nodes.rationale: Commands that are not available to you are left out of the menu, and when nothing matches Claude Code shows 'No commands match /name'. Most unavailable commands return Unknown command when submitted; a few, such as /schedule on a Console API key, answer with their own availability message, as do commands an organization's policy disables.

nodes.label: Hidden commands
nodes.rationale: Claude Code keeps a few available commands out of the menu by design. A partial name never brings a hidden command into the menu — the same no-match message appears — and the command is listed only once you have typed its full name, which then runs it.

nodes.label: MCP prompts as commands
nodes.rationale: MCP servers can expose prompts that appear as commands in Claude Code.

nodes.label: Communications kit
nodes.rationale: A page for administrators and engineering leads rolling Claude Code out to a team, providing copy-ready launch announcements, a tips-and-tricks drip campaign, and one-line FAQ responses for the questions they will be asked most.

nodes.label: Treat everything as draft copy
nodes.rationale: Everything on the page is draft copy, not finished copy: rewrite each message in the organization's voice, swap example tasks for real bugs and modules from your own codebase, and replace the bracketed placeholders. The announcements that drive adoption read like someone at your company wrote them.

nodes.label: Before-you-send checklist
nodes.rationale: A six-item checklist to work through before the announcement goes out. Each item closes a gap that would otherwise turn into a launch-day support thread.

nodes.label: #claude-code channel
nodes.rationale: A dedicated #claude-code channel must be created and linked in the announcement so that questions have one place to land. It is also where the tips campaign is dripped and where champions are recruited from.

nodes.label: Install command tested in your environment
nodes.rationale: Test the install command on at least one machine in your environment before launch. This catches proxy or firewall issues before the whole organization hits them at once.

nodes.label: Security and data-handling link ready
nodes.rationale: Have the Data usage page (or your internal equivalent) linked and ready before sending, because 'Where does my code go?' will be the first reply to the announcement.

nodes.label: One concrete first task
nodes.rationale: Choose one concrete first task — a real bug or file in your own codebase — to hand readers. Generic examples do not convert; 'fix the flaky test in auth_test.go' does.

nodes.label: Named channel owner for 48 hours
nodes.rationale: Name an owner who watches the channel for the first 48 hours after launch, because unanswered launch-day questions kill momentum.

nodes.label: C-suite sponsor
nodes.rationale: Line up a C-suite sponsor to send or co-sign the announcement: exec-sent launches consistently see higher first-week adoption than admin-sent ones, signalling a company priority rather than an optional experiment.

nodes.label: The standard announcement
nodes.rationale: The standard org-wide rollout message, offered in Email and Slack/Teams formats. It covers what Claude Code is, gives a two-minute install path, hands readers one concrete task to try, and answers 'where does my code go?' before anyone has to ask.

nodes.label: Two-minute install path
nodes.rationale: The install path quoted in every announcement variant: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`, then `cd <your-repo>`, then `claude`. It is presented as a two-minute (or ten-minute, in the exec ask) commitment.

nodes.label: /init
nodes.rationale: Run `/init` once per repo: Claude reads the project structure and writes a CLAUDE.md with build commands, architecture, and conventions, so engineers stop re-explaining the basics every session. The docs frame it as thirty seconds that pays off every session after.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md project memory
nodes.rationale: A CLAUDE.md file holding a repo's build commands, architecture, and conventions; every future session in that repo starts from it automatically. Keep it under two screens — it is a cheat sheet, not documentation.

nodes.label: "Where your code goes" answer
nodes.rationale: The copy-ready data-handling paragraph: Claude Code runs in your terminal and talks directly to Anthropic's API with no third-party servers in the loop, asks before editing files or running commands, and under an Enterprise agreement Anthropic does not use your code or prompts to train its models.

nodes.label: VS Code extension and JetBrains plugin
nodes.rationale: For engineers who prefer their editor, there is a VS Code extension and a JetBrains plugin with the same features embedded in the editor — the same agent, no terminal required.

nodes.label: Agent, not autocomplete
nodes.rationale: The positioning line of the announcement: Claude Code is an AI coding agent that runs in the terminal, reads the actual codebase, and works through real tasks end to end — debugging, refactors, tests, PRs. It is not autocomplete and not a chat window; it edits files, runs commands, and asks permission before anything risky.

nodes.label: Executive sponsor variant
nodes.rationale: An announcement variant sent from the sponsoring executive (CTO, CIO, or SVP Engineering) under their own name and account. It is deliberately stripped to one ask — install it and run it on one real task — leaving the 'how' to the standard announcement and the #claude-code channel.

nodes.label: Pilot group variant
nodes.rationale: An announcement variant for a phased rollout, sent to the pilot cohort only. The ask is one real task that week plus a candid note in #claude-code-pilot on what worked, what was annoying, and what surprised them, which decides how the wider rollout proceeds.

nodes.label: Champion recruitment DM
nodes.rationale: After launch, DM the two or three people most active in #claude-code and offer to make their advocacy semi-official — low lift, mostly keep posting, plus first crack at new features and a direct line to the Anthropic team.

nodes.label: Tips and tricks drip campaign
nodes.rationale: Ready-to-paste Slack or Teams messages that drive feature activation after launch. Each follows one pattern — a hook, the payoff, a 'try it now' prompt, and a docs link — dripped one or two a week in #claude-code, standing alone with no required order.

nodes.label: Match the model to the moment
nodes.rationale: Claude Code runs on the same models as the Claude app and the model can be switched mid-session with `/model`. Using Opus to fix a typo burns compute; using Haiku for a twelve-file refactor invites a re-do.

nodes.label: Fable
nodes.rationale: The most capable model, for the hardest, longest-running tasks. It is opt-in only and not the default — select it with `/model fable` — and cybersecurity or biology content falls back to Opus automatically.

nodes.label: Opus
nodes.rationale: The model for large-scale refactors, complex debugging, architecture decisions, and high-stakes changes. On Opus 5, cybersecurity or biology content triggers automatic model fallback or a refusal.

nodes.label: Sonnet
nodes.rationale: The workhorse and recommended default: everyday feature work, bug fixes, tests, documentation, and code review. The tip's call to action is to type `/model` and pick Sonnet if you have not already.

nodes.label: Haiku
nodes.rationale: The model to drop to for quick questions, formatting, mechanical edits, and rapid iteration — cases where speed wins.

nodes.label: Automatic model fallback
nodes.rationale: Content-triggered model switching: cybersecurity or biology content on Fable falls back to Opus automatically, and Opus 5 runs its own checks so flagged cybersecurity content switches models while flagged biology content is refused.

nodes.label: Three things to try in your first 10 minutes
nodes.rationale: Three zero-setup starters for a newly installed user: fix something annoying (a flaky test), get oriented in code you did not write ('walk me through how [module] works'), and sanity-check a working diff before pushing.

nodes.label: @-references
nodes.rationale: Typing `@` followed by a file path pulls that file directly into context instead of pasting its contents; it works for whole directories too, and `@` then Tab autocompletes every file in reach.

nodes.label: Permission modes (Shift+Tab)
nodes.rationale: Shift+Tab cycles how much Claude can do without asking: Manual (the `default` setting value) asks before file edits and most shell commands; acceptEdits lets file edits and common filesystem commands flow through while still checking other shell commands; plan proposes changes for approval before anything is touched.

nodes.label: Plan mode
nodes.rationale: The permission mode in which Claude lays out exactly what it intends to do before touching a file. It is described as the trust-builder and the fastest way to calibrate how much to trust the agent, so it is the recommended starting point for anything touching multiple files.

nodes.label: Checkpointing and /rewind
nodes.rationale: `/rewind` rolls the conversation back to an earlier point, including the file changes Claude made along the way; pressing Esc twice opens the rewind menu. Checkpointing is automatic and requires no setup.

nodes.label: MCP connectors
nodes.rationale: One config file, `.mcp.json` at the project root, wires Claude into GitHub, Jira, Linear, or another tracker, so asking for the top-priority issue and then fixing it happen in the same conversation instead of pasting tickets.

nodes.label: Skills
nodes.rationale: A SKILL.md file in `.claude/skills/<name>/` becomes a reusable prompt invoked by typing `/name`. The advice is to make one the second time you type a multi-step prompt you have typed before, and the easiest path is to ask Claude to write it.

nodes.label: Hooks
nodes.rationale: Hooks are shell commands that fire on Claude Code events; a Stop hook sending a desktop notification lets you kick off a long refactor, walk away, and be pinged when it finishes.

nodes.label: Screenshots and images
nodes.rationale: Drag a screenshot straight into the terminal and Claude sees it — error dialogs, UI mockups, whiteboard photos, Figma exports. Ctrl+V pastes from the clipboard, or Alt+V on Windows and WSL.

nodes.label: Git workflows
nodes.rationale: Claude handles the full git ceremony — conventional commit messages, branches, and PRs with proper summaries — from a single ask, and can walk you through someone else's diff when given a PR URL.

nodes.label: Plugins
nodes.rationale: Skills get bundled and shared as plugins; `/plugin` browses what is available and installs in one step. Five minutes of browsing can save an hour of building a command someone already made.

nodes.label: Permission-first security architecture
nodes.rationale: Permission-first by design: every file edit, shell command, and external call is gated by user approval. The CLI runs in the terminal and talks directly to Anthropic's API with no third-party servers, supports optional OS-level sandboxing for shell commands, and under an Enterprise plan code and prompts are not used for training.

nodes.label: Four habits of daily users
nodes.rationale: The four habits that separate people who tried it once from people who use it daily: start in plan mode for anything multi-file, run /init early because context compounds, review diffs before committing because Claude can be confidently wrong, and verify changes on critical paths — treat it like a sharp junior, not an oracle.

nodes.label: FAQ one-line responses
nodes.rationale: A quick-reference table of one-line replies to the six questions administrators will be asked most, each with a docs link: editor support, whether configuration is needed, where code goes, repo visibility, the Copilot comparison, and what to try first.

nodes.label: What Claude can see of your repo
nodes.rationale: Claude reads what it is given access to: file reads inside the working directory do not prompt, while permission prompts gate edits, non-read-only shell commands, and file-tool reads outside that directory. A built-in set of read-only shell commands such as `ls` and `cat` runs without prompting and can be restricted with sandbox `denyRead` rules.

nodes.label: Difference from Copilot
nodes.rationale: The FAQ answer to 'How is this different from Copilot?': Copilot autocompletes lines, while Claude Code is an agent that reads files, runs commands, and makes multi-file edits.

nodes.label: Starter prompt templates
nodes.rationale: Eight starter prompts to share with engineers who have installed but do not know what to ask — fix a bug, understand code, safe refactor, write tests, review before commit, open a PR, make a skill, debug a stack trace — each phrased as it would be typed into a real session, with bracketed pieces replaced by files from your own repo.

nodes.label: Verify version-specific details before distributing
nodes.rationale: Claude Code ships frequently, so version-specific details in this kit must be verified against the documentation home page before the copy is distributed internally.

nodes.label: Computer use in the Claude Code CLI
nodes.rationale: Computer use lets Claude open apps, control the screen, and work on the machine the way the user would, from inside the same CLI conversation that wrote the code. It is a research preview on macOS that can compile a Swift app, launch it, click through every button, and screenshot the result.

nodes.label: macOS-only in the CLI
nodes.rationale: Computer use in the CLI runs only on macOS; it is not available on Linux or Windows. Windows users are directed to computer use in the Desktop app instead.

nodes.label: Pro or Max plan requirement
nodes.rationale: Computer use requires a Pro or Max plan and is explicitly not available on Team or Enterprise plans. `/status` confirms the current subscription.

nodes.label: Interactive session requirement
nodes.rationale: Computer use requires an interactive Claude Code session and is therefore unavailable in non-interactive (headless) mode with the `-p` flag.

nodes.label: claude.ai authentication requirement
nodes.rationale: Computer use requires authentication through claude.ai and is not available with third-party providers such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry; users on those providers need a separate claude.ai account.

nodes.label: Eligibility checklist for the computer-use server
nodes.rationale: The `computer-use` server appears in `/mcp` only on eligible setups. When it is missing, the documented checks are: macOS, a Pro or Max plan, claude.ai authentication, and an interactive session.

nodes.label: GUI-only task use cases
nodes.rationale: Computer use handles tasks that require a GUI: building and validating native apps, end-to-end UI testing without a Playwright config or test harness, debugging visual and layout issues, and driving GUI-only tools such as design apps, hardware control panels, and the iOS Simulator.

nodes.label: Tool precedence ladder
nodes.rationale: Computer use is the broadest and slowest way for Claude to interact with an app, so Claude tries the most precise tool first: an MCP server for the service, then Bash for shell tasks, then Claude in Chrome for browser work, and only then computer use.

nodes.label: Prefer a dedicated MCP server
nodes.rationale: If an MCP server exists for the service in question, Claude uses that rather than screen control — it is the most precise rung of the ladder.

nodes.label: Prefer Bash for shell tasks
nodes.rationale: If the task is a shell command, Claude uses the Bash tool rather than driving a terminal window through screen control.

nodes.label: Prefer Claude in Chrome for browser work
nodes.rationale: If the task is browser work and Claude in Chrome is set up, Claude uses that instead of computer use.

nodes.label: Screen control as last resort
nodes.rationale: Screen control is reserved for things nothing else can reach: native apps, simulators such as the iOS Simulator, and tools that have no API. It is the final rung when no MCP server, shell command, or browser path applies.

nodes.label: Built-in `computer-use` MCP server
nodes.rationale: Computer use ships as a built-in MCP server named `computer-use`, which is off by default until the user enables it.

nodes.label: Enabling via the /mcp menu
nodes.rationale: In an interactive session, running `/mcp` lists `computer-use` as disabled; selecting it and choosing Enable turns it on. The setting persists per project, so it is done once per project.

nodes.label: macOS permission grants
nodes.rationale: The first time Claude tries to use the computer, a prompt asks for two macOS permissions with links to the relevant System Settings panes. After granting both, the user selects Try again; macOS may require restarting Claude Code after Screen Recording is granted.

nodes.label: Accessibility permission
nodes.rationale: The macOS Accessibility permission is what lets Claude click, type, and scroll on the user's machine.

nodes.label: Screen Recording permission
nodes.rationale: The macOS Screen Recording permission is what lets Claude see what is on the screen. macOS sometimes requires the requesting process to restart after it is granted, which is why the permission prompt can reappear.

nodes.label: Per-session app approval
nodes.rationale: Enabling the server does not grant access to every app. The first time Claude needs a specific app in a session, a terminal prompt names which apps it wants to control, any extra permissions such as clipboard access, and how many other apps will be hidden. Approvals last only for the current session.

nodes.label: Sentinel warnings for broad-reach apps
nodes.rationale: Apps with broad reach carry an extra warning in the approval prompt: 'Equivalent to shell access' for terminals and IDEs (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, Warp), 'Can read or write any file' for Finder, and 'Can change system settings' for System Settings. These apps are not blocked — the warning exists so the user can judge whether the task warrants that access.

nodes.label: Per-category control tiers
nodes.rationale: Claude's level of control varies by app category: browsers and trading platforms are view-only, terminals and IDEs are click-only, and everything else gets full control.

nodes.label: How Claude works on your screen
nodes.rationale: The on-screen flow is documented so users can anticipate what Claude will do and how to intervene: a machine-wide lock, hiding of other apps, automatic screenshot downscaling, and a global stop key.

nodes.label: One session at a time (machine-wide lock)
nodes.rationale: A session takes a machine-wide lock at its first computer use action and releases it only when the session exits, not when the task finishes. A second session's computer use fails with an error naming the session holding the lock.

nodes.label: Other apps hidden during control
nodes.rationale: When Claude starts controlling the screen, other visible apps are hidden so it interacts only with approved apps; hidden apps are restored automatically when the turn finishes. In the CLI this auto-unhide is always on, unlike the Desktop app where it is an optional toggle.

nodes.label: Terminal excluded from screenshots
nodes.rationale: The user's terminal window stays visible to the human but is excluded from screenshots, so Claude never sees its own output and on-screen prompts in the session cannot feed back into the model.

nodes.label: Automatic screenshot downscaling
nodes.rationale: Claude Code downscales every screenshot before sending it to the model — a 16-inch MacBook Pro captures at 3456x2234 and downscales to roughly 1372x887, preserving aspect ratio. There is no setting for the target size; if text is too small to read, enlarge it in the app rather than lowering display resolution.

nodes.label: Global Esc abort
nodes.rationale: A macOS notification announces 'Claude is using your computer - press Esc to stop'. Esc from anywhere (or Ctrl+C in the terminal) aborts the current action immediately, unhides apps, and returns control; the key press is consumed so prompt injection cannot use it to dismiss dialogs. The session still holds the computer use lock until it exits.

nodes.label: The computer use trust boundary
nodes.rationale: Computer use runs on the actual desktop with access to the apps the user approved, so its trust boundary differs from other tools. Claude checks each action and flags potential prompt injection from on-screen content, and a separate safety guide carries best practices.

nodes.label: Sandboxed Bash tool
nodes.rationale: The sandboxed Bash tool isolates filesystem and network access; the doc contrasts it explicitly with computer use, which has no such sandbox and runs on the real desktop.

nodes.label: Prompt injection from on-screen content
nodes.rationale: Content visible on screen can attempt prompt injection. Claude checks each action and flags potential injection, the terminal is kept out of screenshots so session output cannot feed back in, and the Esc key press is consumed so injected content cannot use it to dismiss dialogs.

nodes.label: Built-in guardrails
nodes.rationale: Five guardrails reduce risk without configuration: per-app approval, sentinel warnings on shell/filesystem/system-settings apps, terminal exclusion from screenshots, a global Esc abort, and a lock file limiting control to one session.

nodes.label: Example: validate a native build
nodes.rationale: After changing a macOS or iOS app, Claude can compile and verify in one pass — running `xcodebuild`, launching the app, opening the preferences window, checking that an interval slider updates its label, and screenshotting the result.

nodes.label: Example: reproduce a layout bug
nodes.rationale: For a visual bug that only appears at certain window sizes, Claude resizes the app window until the clipped state reproduces, screenshots it, and then reads the relevant stylesheets to find the cause.

nodes.label: Example: test an iOS Simulator flow
nodes.rationale: Claude can drive the iOS Simulator with a mouse instead of writing XCTest — launching the app, tapping through onboarding screens, and reporting slow screens. In the Desktop app the same request opens the iOS Simulator pane rather than using screen control.

nodes.label: Computer use in the Desktop app
nodes.rationale: The CLI and Desktop surfaces share the same computer use engine but differ: Desktop runs on macOS and Windows, is enabled by a Settings toggle, has a configurable denied-apps list, an optional auto-unhide toggle, and Dispatch integration — none of which the CLI has.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting: lock held by another session
nodes.rationale: The error 'Computer use is in use by another Claude session' means another session holds the lock until it exits — the remedy is to exit that session. If the other session crashed, the lock releases automatically once Claude detects the process is gone.

nodes.label: Claude Code context window
nodes.rationale: The context window holds everything Claude knows about a session: the user's instructions, the files it reads, its own responses, and content that never appears in the terminal. The page's interactive simulation models a 200,000-token window filling from startup through compaction.

nodes.label: Pre-prompt startup load
nodes.rationale: A large amount loads before the user types anything: system prompt, auto memory, environment info, MCP tool names, skill descriptions, and both global and project CLAUDE.md. This startup content lives outside the message history, which is why it reloads after compaction.

nodes.label: System prompt
nodes.rationale: Core instructions for behavior, tool use, and response formatting, always loaded first and never shown to the user (~4,200 illustrative tokens). An output style or text from --append-system-prompt enters the system prompt the same way.

nodes.label: Auto memory (MEMORY.md)
nodes.rationale: Claude's notes to itself from previous sessions — build commands it learned, patterns it noticed, mistakes to avoid. The first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded into the conversation context.

nodes.label: Environment info block
nodes.rationale: Working directory, platform, shell, OS version, and whether the directory is a git repo. Git branch, status, and recent commits load as a separate block at the very end of the system prompt.

nodes.label: Deferred MCP tool schemas
nodes.rationale: By default only MCP tool NAMES are listed at startup so Claude knows what is available; full schemas stay deferred and Claude loads specific ones on demand via tool search when a task needs them.

nodes.label: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH setting
nodes.rationale: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=auto loads MCP tool schemas upfront when they fit within 10% of the context window; ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false loads everything upfront regardless.

nodes.label: Startup skill description index
nodes.rationale: One-line descriptions of available skills load at startup so Claude knows what it can invoke; full skill content loads only when a skill is actually used. Unlike the rest of the startup content, this listing is NOT re-injected after /compact — only skills actually invoked are preserved.

nodes.label: disable-model-invocation frontmatter
nodes.rationale: A skill with `disable-model-invocation: true` is absent from the startup skill index and costs zero context until the user invokes it with /name. The page recommends it for skills with side effects such as committing, deploying, or sending messages.

nodes.label: Global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: The user's global preferences, applying to every project and loaded alongside project instructions at the start of every conversation (~320 illustrative tokens).

nodes.label: Project CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: Project conventions, build commands, and architecture notes living in the project root, described as the most important file a user can create because the whole team gets the same instructions. It is re-injected from disk after compaction.

nodes.label: Keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines
nodes.rationale: The page's save-context tip: keep CLAUDE.md under 200 lines and move reference content to skills or path-scoped rules so it only loads when needed.

nodes.label: File reads dominate context
nodes.rationale: Every file Claude reads grows the context: the terminal shows a one-line 'Read auth.ts' while thousands of tokens of content enter context invisibly. The page states file reads dominate context usage and advises specific prompts and subagents to reduce them.

nodes.label: Path-scoped rules
nodes.rationale: A rule in .claude/rules/ with a `paths:` pattern loads automatically when Claude reads a matching file; the terminal shows only a 'Loaded' notice, not the rule content. Because they load into message history they are summarized away by compaction and reload only when a matching file is read again — dropping `paths:` or moving the rule to project-root CLAUDE.md makes it persist.

nodes.label: Nested CLAUDE.md in subdirectories
nodes.rationale: A CLAUDE.md in a subdirectory loads into message history when Claude reads a file in that subdirectory, so compaction summarizes it away; Claude Code reloads it as Claude reads files there again.

nodes.label: PostToolUse hook
nodes.rationale: A PostToolUse hook configured in settings.json fires after every matching tool event — e.g. running prettier after each file edit — and fires again for every subsequent matching event. For PostToolUse, exit code 2 surfaces stderr as an error but cannot block, since the tool already ran.

nodes.label: hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext
nodes.rationale: A hook reports back to Claude via the JSON field hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, which is the field that actually enters Claude's context. Plain stdout on exit 0 does NOT — it is written to the debug log only.

nodes.label: 10,000-character hook output cap
nodes.rationale: Hook output over 10,000 characters is saved to a file; Claude receives a preview and the file path instead of the full output.

nodes.label: ! shell-mode prefix
nodes.rationale: Running a shell command with the ! prefix puts both the command and its output into context as part of the user's message — useful for grounding Claude in command output without Claude running the command itself.

nodes.label: Subagent's separate context window
nodes.rationale: A spawned subagent works in a fresh, separate context window. It loads CLAUDE.md and the same MCP and skill setup, but starts without the main conversation history or the main session's auto memory; its file reads fill its own context, not the caller's.

nodes.label: Subagent system prompt
nodes.rationale: The subagent gets its own system prompt, shorter than the main session's — for the general-purpose agent, a brief prompt plus environment details (~900 illustrative tokens). The main session's auto memory is not included.

nodes.label: Subagent's own CLAUDE.md copy
nodes.rationale: The subagent loads the same project CLAUDE.md — same file, same content — but it counts against the subagent's context rather than the main session's.

nodes.label: Subagent tool restrictions
nodes.rationale: A subagent gets most of the parent's tools minus several that do not apply in a nested context — plan-mode controls, background-task tools, and by default the Agent tool itself, to prevent recursion.

nodes.label: Only the subagent's summary returns
nodes.rationale: Only the subagent's final text response returns to the caller's context, plus a small metadata trailer with token counts and duration. In the simulation the subagent read 6,100 tokens of files and returned a 420-token result — that gap is the context savings.

nodes.label: Custom agent memory: frontmatter
nodes.rationale: If a custom agent declares `memory:` in its frontmatter, it loads its own separate MEMORY.md in place of the main session's auto memory, which is never inherited.

nodes.label: Explore and Plan agents skip CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: The built-in Explore and Plan agents skip loading the project CLAUDE.md in order to run with a smaller context.

nodes.label: Compaction
nodes.rationale: Compaction replaces the verbatim conversation with one structured summary that keeps requests and intent, key technical concepts, files examined or modified with important snippets, errors and their fixes, pending tasks, and current work. Full tool outputs and intermediate reasoning are gone; the summarization itself never appears in the terminal.

nodes.label: /compact command
nodes.rationale: /compact is the user-invoked trigger for compaction, summarizing older exchanges to free space; the terminal shows only a 'Conversation compacted' message. The page advises running it when context starts affecting performance or before a long new task.

nodes.label: What survives compaction (table)
nodes.rationale: The page's per-mechanism table: what happens to each kind of content after compaction depends on how it was loaded — system prompt and output style unchanged (not part of message history); project-root CLAUDE.md, unscoped rules, auto memory and the plan-mode plan re-injected from disk; path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md reloaded on the next matching read; hook-added context summarized with the conversation.

nodes.label: Post-compaction re-read of five files
nodes.rationale: Right after compaction Claude Code re-reads up to five of the files read or edited during the session, choosing the most recently modified first, and reloads the path-scoped rules and nested CLAUDE.md files that apply to them.

nodes.label: 5,000-token Referenced file fallback
nodes.rationale: A re-read file over 5,000 tokens comes back as a path reference without its content, shown as `Referenced file` instead of `Read`. Its associated rules still reload.

nodes.label: Skill body re-injection caps
nodes.rationale: After compaction Claude Code re-injects the body of each skill that was invoked, capped at 5,000 tokens per skill and 25,000 tokens in total, with the oldest invoked skills dropped once the total budget is exceeded.

nodes.label: Skill truncation keeps the file start
nodes.rationale: When a large skill is truncated to fit the per-skill re-injection cap, truncation keeps the START of the file — so the most important instructions belong near the top of SKILL.md.

nodes.label: SessionStart hook with compact source
nodes.rationale: SessionStart hooks that match the `compact` source are run by Claude Code after compaction and their output is added to the compacted context — the documented way to re-inject arbitrary context that compaction would otherwise summarize away.

nodes.label: Summarization inherits extended thinking
nodes.rationale: As of v2.1.198 the summarization request inherits the session's extended-thinking configuration: it reasons with thinking enabled when the session has it enabled and stays off otherwise. Thinking affects only how the summary is produced; session settings are unchanged afterward.

nodes.label: Automatic compaction
nodes.rationale: Claude Code compacts automatically as the session approaches the limit, so a full context window does not end the session; the automatic pass works the same way as a manual /compact.

nodes.label: /compact with focus instructions
nodes.rationale: Running /compact with instructions — e.g. `/compact focus on the auth bug fix` — makes the summary keep what the user chooses instead of what the automatic pass guesses is important.

nodes.label: /rewind partial summarization
nodes.rationale: /rewind lets the user select a message and choose 'Summarize from here' or 'Summarize up to here', compacting only part of the conversation rather than all of it.

nodes.label: /autocompact token threshold
nodes.rationale: Running /autocompact with a token count, e.g. `/autocompact 500k`, sets how full the context window gets before the automatic pass runs.

nodes.label: /clear between unrelated tasks
nodes.rationale: Running /clear when switching to unrelated work discards the old conversation, which otherwise crowds out the files needed next and costs tokens on every message.

nodes.label: Delegate large reads to a subagent
nodes.rationale: Sending research to a subagent keeps the file contents in the subagent's context window rather than the main one — the page's recommended lever for research-heavy tasks.

nodes.label: 1M token context models
nodes.rationale: Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6 and later, and Sonnet 4.6 support a 1 million token context window, selected via a `[1m]` model variant — except Sonnet 5, which runs at 1M with no `[1m]` variant to select. Compaction works the same way at the larger limit.

nodes.label: Per-model auto-compact thresholds
nodes.rationale: The point at which automatic compaction runs depends on the model and configuration; the docs carry default auto-compact thresholds per model, and Sonnet 5 has its own thresholds plus an LLM gateway exception.

nodes.label: Gateway/custom model ID window correction
nodes.rationale: When Claude Code assumes the wrong context window for a model ID — such as an LLM gateway alias — the model-config docs describe how to correct the window for that gateway or custom model ID.

nodes.label: /context live breakdown
nodes.rationale: Because the visualization uses representative numbers, actual usage is read with /context — a live breakdown by category with optimization suggestions, including which CLAUDE.md and auto memory files loaded. /memory opens and edits those files.

nodes.label: Terminal visibility tiers
nodes.rationale: Every context event falls into one of three visibility tiers: hidden ('invisible in your terminal'), brief ('a one-liner in your terminal'), and full ('the actual content appears'). Most of what fills the window — system prompt, memory, rules, hooks, file contents — is hidden or brief.

nodes.label: Illustrative token counts
nodes.rationale: The simulation's numbers are explicitly illustrative against a 200,000-token maximum: actual values vary with CLAUDE.md size, MCP servers, and file lengths.

nodes.label: Claude Code charges by API token consumption
nodes.rationale: Claude Code charges by API token consumption; subscription plan pricing (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) is separate and published at claude.com/pricing. Per-developer costs vary widely with model selection, codebase size, and usage patterns such as running multiple instances or automation.

nodes.label: Enterprise per-developer cost benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Across enterprise deployments the average cost is around $13 per developer per active day and $150-250 per developer per month, with costs staying below $30 per active day for 90% of users.

nodes.label: Pilot-group baseline before rollout
nodes.rationale: To estimate spend for a team, start with a small pilot group and use the tracking tools to establish a baseline before wider rollout, rather than extrapolating from published averages.

nodes.label: /usage command
nodes.rationale: `/usage` is the in-CLI cost and usage screen: a Session block of API token statistics, plus (on a plan) usage bars, activity stats, a plan usage breakdown, and a usage-credits row.

nodes.label: Session block in /usage
nodes.rationale: The Session block at the top of `/usage` shows total cost, API and wall duration, code changes, and per-model input/output/cache-read/cache-write token counts for the current session. It reports API token usage and is intended for API users; Max and Pro subscribers have usage included in their subscription, so the session cost figure is not relevant for their billing.

nodes.label: Local list-price cost computation
nodes.rationale: Claude Code computes every dollar figure it shows locally from token counts at list price. The figure is an estimate, not an invoice; the authoritative billing source is the Usage page in the Claude Console.

nodes.label: modelPricing managed setting
nodes.rationale: `modelPricing` makes Claude Code report costs at an organization's contracted rates instead of list price, via a flat `multiplier`, per-model `overrides`, or both. It changes only what Claude Code reports, never what Anthropic charges, and requires v2.1.242 or later; when in effect the `Total cost` line carries the note `at your organization's configured rates`.

nodes.label: Managed-settings-only delivery
nodes.rationale: Contracted rates must be delivered as managed settings — server-managed settings, an MDM policy, `managed-settings.json`, or a policy helper. Claude Code ignores the key in user, project, and local settings and in `--settings`, and does not fetch rates from the Console, so the setting must be updated when the contract changes.

nodes.label: /clear resets session totals
nodes.rationale: Session totals reset when `/clear` starts a new session, so the next session's total cost starts at $0. Before v2.1.211 they kept accumulating across `/clear` for the lifetime of the Claude Code process.

nodes.label: 1.1x data residency rate
nodes.rationale: For a Claude API response billed at the 1.1x data residency rate, Claude Code multiplies that response's list-price token cost by 1.1 in the session cost figure. Before v2.1.239 it did not, so the reported session cost was lower than the actual bill.

nodes.label: --max-budget-usd
nodes.rationale: Claude Code compares the same session cost total it shows in `/usage` and the status line against the `--max-budget-usd` CLI flag, making that flag a per-session spend ceiling expressed in the locally computed figure.

nodes.label: Status line cost field
nodes.rationale: The status line's cost field reports the same session total as the `/usage` Session block, giving a continuously visible view of the same locally computed estimate.

nodes.label: Prompt cache (main) line
