nodes.rationale: A workflow where the AI reads files, runs commands and makes changes autonomously while the human watches, redirects or steps away — as opposed to chat assistants that only return text the human must apply. Claude Code is agentic because it has tools that let it act rather than only advise.

nodes.label: Agentic harness
nodes.rationale: The tools, context management and execution environment that turn a language model into a capable coding agent. Claude Code is the harness and Claude is the model inside it; the harness supplies file access, shell execution, permission gating, memory loading, and the loop that chains actions together.

nodes.label: Agentic loop
nodes.rationale: The cycle Claude works through for every task: gather context, take action, verify results, repeat until done. Each tool use returns information that informs the next step, the loop can be interrupted at any point to redirect, and most extension points (hooks, skills, MCP) plug into specific phases of it.

nodes.label: Artifact
nodes.rationale: A live, interactive web page Claude Code publishes from a session to a private URL on claude.ai so output can be seen visually or shared instead of read as terminal text. The page updates in place when the session republishes, and sharing scope depends on plan: public links on Pro and Max, organization sharing on Team and Enterprise unless an Owner enables public links.

nodes.label: Auto memory
nodes.rationale: Notes Claude writes for itself from the user's corrections and preferences, stored per git repository under ~/.claude/projects/, with all worktrees of a repository sharing one directory. The first 200 lines or 25 KB of the MEMORY.md index loads at the start of every session; it is the Claude-written counterpart to the user-written CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Auto mode
nodes.rationale: A permission mode in which a separate classifier model reviews actions instead of the user, so most run without asking, while explicit ask rules still prompt. It is the built-in starting mode for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions on Pro, Max and Team; the classifier blocks scope escalation, untrusted infrastructure and prompt injection, and sees tool results stripped so hostile content cannot manipulate it directly.

nodes.label: Bare mode
nodes.rationale: With --bare, Claude Code starts without loading hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory or CLAUDE.md — apart from skills in a directory passed with --add-dir. It is recommended for CI and scripted calls that need the same result on every machine.

nodes.label: Bundled skills
nodes.rationale: Prompt-based playbooks shipped with Claude Code, such as /batch, /code-review, /debug and /loop. Unlike built-in commands, which execute fixed logic, a bundled skill gives Claude a detailed prompt and lets it orchestrate the work, so it can spawn agents, read files and adapt to the codebase.

nodes.label: Channel
nodes.rationale: An MCP server that pushes events into a running session so Claude can react to things that happen while the user is away from the terminal. Channels can be two-way — Claude reads an inbound event and replies through the same channel — and Telegram, Discord and iMessage are included in the research preview.

nodes.label: Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: A restore point created at each prompt sent; Claude Code snapshots files before every edit so a checkpoint can revert them. Esc twice or /rewind restores code, conversation, or both. Checkpoints are saved with the conversation so a resumed session can still rewind, but they are separate from git and do not track changes made through the Bash tool.

nodes.label: .claude directory
nodes.rationale: The directory where Claude Code reads project-scoped configuration — settings, hooks, skills, subagents, rules and auto memory. A project has .claude/ at its root; user-level defaults live at ~/.claude/.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: A markdown file of persistent user-written instructions loaded at the start of every session as a user message after the system prompt. It can sit at project scope (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md), user scope (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), or as managed policy; all discovered files are concatenated from broadest to most specific rather than overriding each other, and the project-root file survives compaction and is re-read fresh from disk.

nodes.label: Command
nodes.rationale: A reusable instruction invoked by typing /name at the prompt; built-ins such as /clear, /model and /compact control the session, and custom ones are files in .claude/commands/ or come from a plugin. Two unrelated uses of the word are `claude` CLI subcommands such as `claude mcp add`, and the `command` field of a stdio MCP server entry naming the executable to launch.

nodes.label: Compaction
nodes.rationale: Automatic summarization of the conversation when the context window approaches its limit: older tool outputs are cleared first, then the conversation is summarized. Project-root CLAUDE.md and auto memory survive and reload from disk while instructions given only in conversation may be lost; /compact triggers it manually, optionally with a focus.

nodes.label: Connector
nodes.rationale: An MCP server added to a claude.ai account rather than configured in Claude Code. Signing in to Claude Code with that account makes connectors appear in /mcp alongside locally added servers, and organizations can provision connectors and set per-tool controls on them.

nodes.label: Context window
nodes.rationale: The working memory for a session, holding conversation history, file contents, command outputs, CLAUDE.md, auto memory, loaded skills and system instructions. It fills as work proceeds until compaction summarizes it; /context shows what is using space.

nodes.label: Dispatch
nodes.rationale: A phone-initiated task router that spawns a Claude Code session in the Desktop app when a coding task is sent from the Claude mobile app; the prompt routes to the right tool automatically. Available on Pro and Max plans.

nodes.label: Effort level
nodes.rationale: A setting controlling how much of the adaptive-reasoning thinking budget Claude uses each turn: higher effort means more thinking tokens and deeper reasoning, lower effort is faster and cheaper. Effort is supported on Fable 5.1 and Fable 5, Opus 4.6 and later, and Sonnet 4.6 and later.

nodes.label: Extended thinking
nodes.rationale: Visible step-by-step reasoning the model performs before responding, shown in gray italic text in the terminal. It is adjusted with the effort level, or capped with MAX_THINKING_TOKENS on models that have a fixed thinking budget.

nodes.label: Hook
nodes.rationale: A user-defined handler that executes automatically at a specific point in Claude Code's lifecycle — before a tool runs, after a file edit, at session start. Handlers can be a shell command, HTTP endpoint, MCP tool, LLM prompt or subagent, and hooks are deterministic: they fire at fixed lifecycle points rather than at the model's discretion.

nodes.label: Hook event
nodes.rationale: The first of the three levels of a hook configuration: the lifecycle point at which the hook can fire.

nodes.label: Hook matcher
nodes.rationale: The second level of a hook configuration: the filter deciding which events actually fire the hook.

nodes.label: Hook handler
nodes.rationale: The third level of a hook configuration: what actually runs when the hook fires — a shell command, HTTP endpoint, MCP tool, LLM prompt or subagent.

nodes.label: Managed settings
nodes.rationale: Settings enforced org-wide by IT or DevOps, delivered from Anthropic's servers through the admin console or deployed to devices at an OS-level path outside ~/.claude. User and project settings cannot override them, making them the tool for security policies, compliance requirements and standardized fleet tooling.

nodes.label: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
nodes.rationale: An open standard for connecting AI tools to external data sources and services. MCP servers give Claude new tools for Slack, Jira, databases, browsers and hundreds of other integrations; servers are connected via /mcp or by adding them to .mcp.json.

nodes.label: MCP server
nodes.rationale: A program that gives Claude tools, prompts or resources over MCP, added with `claude mcp add`, in .mcp.json, through a plugin, or as a claude.ai connector. A local stdio server runs as a process Claude Code starts from the `command` and `args` fields of its configuration, which are unrelated to the slash commands typed at the prompt.

nodes.label: MCP Tool Search
nodes.rationale: A context-saving mechanism that defers MCP tool schemas until needed: only tool names and server instructions load at startup, and Claude fetches a full schema on demand when it decides to use that tool. This keeps idle MCP servers from consuming much context.

nodes.label: Non-interactive mode
nodes.rationale: A mode that executes a single prompt and exits, invoked with -p or --print, used for CI, scripts and piping. The run is still saved as a resumable session unless --no-session-persistence is passed; the Agent SDK is the Python and TypeScript equivalent. It was formerly called headless mode.

nodes.label: Output style
nodes.rationale: A configuration that modifies Claude's system prompt to change response behavior, tone or format. It differs from CLAUDE.md, which Claude Code delivers as a user message after the system prompt, because an output style changes the system prompt itself.

nodes.label: Permission mode
nodes.rationale: The baseline approval behavior for a session, cycled with Shift+Tab in the CLI or chosen in the VS Code, Desktop and claude.ai mode selector. The modes are default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk and bypassPermissions; default is labeled Manual in the CLI, VS Code, JetBrains and desktop app, and `manual` is accepted as an alias.

nodes.label: Permission rule
nodes.rationale: A settings entry that allows, asks about, or denies a tool invocation based on the tool name and argument pattern. Rules are evaluated deny then ask then allow, first match wins, and they are fine-grained controls layered on top of the broader permission mode.

nodes.label: Plan mode
nodes.rationale: A permission mode in which Claude researches and proposes changes without editing source files: it can read, search and run exploration commands, then presents a plan for approval before touching anything. Entered with /plan or Shift+Tab.

nodes.label: Plugin
nodes.rationale: A bundle of skills, hooks, subagents and MCP servers packaged as a single installable unit. Plugin skills are namespaced as plugin-name:skill-name so multiple plugins coexist, and plugins are distributed across teams via a marketplace.

nodes.label: Project trust
nodes.rationale: A dialog accepting a directory before Claude Code loads its configuration. Acceptance is saved per project directory except the home directory, where trust lasts only for the current session; until a directory is trusted Claude Code holds back some repository-supplied content such as project allow rules and marketplaces from .claude/settings.json.

nodes.label: Prompt injection
nodes.rationale: Hostile instructions embedded in a file, web page or tool result that try to redirect Claude toward actions the user never asked for. Claude Code's defenses are the permission system, command injection detection and trust verification; auto mode adds a server-side probe scanning tool results and a classifier that reviews actions with tool results stripped.

nodes.label: Remote Control
nodes.rationale: A way to continue a local Claude Code session from a phone or browser via claude.ai: code execution and files stay on the local machine and only the interface is remote. It differs from Claude Code on the web, which runs in a cloud sandbox.

nodes.label: Rules
nodes.rationale: Modular instruction files in .claude/rules/ that load alongside CLAUDE.md. A rule can be path-scoped with YAML `paths:` frontmatter so it loads only when Claude reads a matching file, keeping context lean until it is relevant.

nodes.label: Sandboxing
nodes.rationale: OS-level filesystem and network isolation for the Bash tool: commands run inside a boundary defined upfront so Claude can work freely within it without per-command approval prompts. Sandboxing is a separate layer from permission rules.

nodes.label: Session
nodes.rationale: A conversation tied to the current directory with its own independent context window. Sessions resume with `claude -c`, fork with --fork-session to preserve history under a new session ID, or run in parallel across terminals; /clear starts a new one while the previous stays available via /resume, and each transcript is stored under ~/.claude/projects/.

nodes.label: Settings layers
nodes.rationale: The hierarchy Claude Code reads configuration from, highest to lowest: managed policy, command-line arguments, local settings at .claude/settings.local.json, project settings at .claude/settings.json, then user settings at ~/.claude/settings.json. Arrays merge across layers while scalars at a higher layer override lower ones.

nodes.label: Skill
nodes.rationale: A SKILL.md file containing instructions, knowledge or a workflow that Claude adds to its toolkit, loaded automatically when relevant or invoked directly with /skill-name. Skills follow the Agent Skills open standard (Claude Code extends it with invocation control and subagent execution) and are the recommended successor to custom commands; .claude/commands/deploy.md and .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy.

nodes.label: Subagent
nodes.rationale: A specialized AI assistant running in its own context window with a custom system prompt, specific tool access and independent permissions; it works a delegated task and returns a summary to the main conversation. A subagent stays inside the session that spawned it, and built-ins include Explore, Plan and general-purpose.

nodes.label: Surface
nodes.rationale: Any place Claude Code is accessed — CLI, VS Code, JetBrains, Desktop or claude.ai — all sharing the same engine. Local sessions read local CLAUDE.md, settings and skills, while cloud sessions start from a fresh clone and do not read ~/.claude/; Slack and the Chrome extension are integrations connecting to a surface rather than surfaces themselves.

nodes.label: Teleport
nodes.rationale: The /teleport command pulls a cloud Claude Code session into the local terminal: Claude fetches the branch, loads the conversation history and resumes from the web session's last state. The reverse direction is --cloud, which sends a local task to run on the web.

nodes.label: Tool
nodes.rationale: An action Claude can take — read a file, edit code, run a shell command, search the web, spawn a subagent. Tools are what make Claude Code agentic; without them Claude can only respond with text, and each tool use returns a result that informs the next decision in the agentic loop.

nodes.label: Turn
nodes.rationale: One complete response from Claude within a session: it begins when the user sends a message and ends when Claude finishes responding, with any number of tool calls in between. Stop hooks fire at the end of each turn; a session consists of many turns and the agentic loop describes what happens inside one.

nodes.label: Verification loop
nodes.rationale: How a session knows work is actually done rather than merely plausible: the user gives Claude a check it can run — a test suite, a build, a screenshot comparison — and Claude iterates until it passes instead of stopping after one attempt. It is the prerequisite for /goal, unattended runs and dynamic workflows, because without one the only thing deciding the agent is finished is the agent itself.

nodes.label: Worktree isolation
nodes.rationale: An isolation mode that runs Claude in a separate git worktree under .claude/worktrees/, enabled with the -w flag or `isolation: worktree` in subagent config. Changes stay on a separate branch in a separate directory so parallel agents do not overwrite each other's files.

nodes.label: Deprecated and renamed terms
nodes.rationale: A table mapping older terms still found in docs, blog posts and community content to their current names: headless mode is now non-interactive mode (same -p flag, same behavior), custom commands are now skills (.claude/commands/ files still work), and slash commands are now just commands with 'slash' dropped from product copy.

nodes.label: Agent SDK
nodes.rationale: The Agent SDK gives programmatic callers the same tools, agent loop, and context management that power Claude Code. It ships as a CLI for scripts and CI/CD, and as Python and TypeScript packages that add structured outputs, tool approval callbacks, and native message objects.

nodes.label: Non-interactive print mode (claude -p)
nodes.rationale: Adding `-p` (or `--print`) to any `claude` command runs it non-interactively with the prompt supplied on the command line, e.g. `claude -p "Find and fix the bug in auth.py" --allowedTools "Read,Edit,Bash"`. This is how the Agent SDK is used from the CLI.

nodes.label: CLI options commonly combined with -p
nodes.rationale: The options most often paired with `-p` are `--continue` for continuing conversations, `--allowedTools` for auto-approving tools, and `--output-format` for structured output.

nodes.label: Flags -p rejects
nodes.rationale: Not every CLI option combines with `-p`. Claude Code rejects `--bg`, and rejects `--cloud` with a task description, erroring with the name of the conflict; `--cloud` with a session ID plus `-p` instead queues a message into that cloud session and exits.

nodes.label: Exit codes and error reporting
nodes.rationale: Claude Code exits 0 on success and non-zero when the run fails, so scripts can branch on exit status. An invalid flag is reported to stderr before the run starts, while a failure inside the run (such as missing authentication) is printed as the result on stdout.

nodes.label: Bare mode (--bare)
nodes.rationale: `--bare` reduces startup time by skipping auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md. It is aimed at CI and scripts that need the same result on every machine, since a teammate's `~/.claude` hook or a project `.mcp.json` server is never read.

nodes.label: --add-dir partial exception in bare mode
nodes.rationale: A directory named with `--add-dir` is a partial exception to bare mode's skipping: bare mode loads skills from that directory's `.claude/skills/` folder, but still skips its `.claude/commands/` and `.claude/agents/` folders.

nodes.label: Repository content runs under -p without a trust dialog
nodes.rationale: Without `--bare`, a `-p` session runs the hooks in a project's `.claude/settings.json` and connects the servers in its `.mcp.json` even in a folder that has never been trusted. A `-p` session shows no workspace trust dialog and no per-server approval prompt.

nodes.label: Credential handling in bare mode
nodes.rationale: In bare mode Claude Code never reads OAuth credentials or the system keychain, so it does not use a subscription login. For the Anthropic API set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or supply an `apiKeyHelper` in the `--settings` JSON; Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry keep reading their own provider credentials.

nodes.label: Tools available in bare mode
nodes.rationale: In bare mode Claude has access to the Bash, file read, and file edit tools; anything else must be supplied explicitly by a flag.

nodes.label: Explicit context flags for bare mode
nodes.rationale: Context that bare mode skips must be passed by flag: `--append-system-prompt` / `--append-system-prompt-file` for system prompt additions, `--settings <file-or-json>` for settings, `--mcp-config <file-or-json>` for MCP servers, `--agents <json>` for custom agents, and `--plugin-dir <path>` / `--plugin-url <url>` for a plugin.

nodes.label: Bare mode is the recommended, future default
nodes.rationale: The docs state that `--bare` is the recommended mode for scripted and SDK calls, and will become the default for `-p` in a future release.

nodes.label: Five-second grace for background Bash tasks
nodes.rationale: A background Bash task started during a `claude -p` run (a dev server, a watch build) has its shell terminated about five seconds after Claude returns its final result and stdin closes; the grace period lets a task finishing just after the result still deliver output. Before v2.1.163 a never-exiting background process held the invocation open indefinitely.

nodes.label: Background subagent wait ceiling
nodes.rationale: Background subagents and workflows are exempt from the five-second grace because their result is part of the final output, so `claude -p` waits for them. From v2.1.182 that wait is capped at ten minutes of continuous idle waiting by default, adjustable via `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (0 waits without a limit).

nodes.label: SIGTERM stops a run with exit code 143
nodes.rationale: Stopping a `claude -p` run with SIGTERM (via `kill` or a process supervisor) makes Claude Code exit with code 143, leaving the in-progress turn unfinished and recording no result for it. To end the turn instead, send SIGINT or call the Agent SDK's `interrupt()` before stopping the process.

nodes.label: SIGTERM shutdown sequence
nodes.rationale: On SIGTERM Claude Code terminates the process tree of any still-running Bash command, then runs `SessionEnd` hooks and exits. While exiting it starts no new tool call, sends no new model request, and runs no hook other than `SessionEnd`; a command in flight is recorded in the session as killed.

nodes.label: Pending permission prompt at SIGTERM
nodes.rationale: If SIGTERM arrives while waiting for an answer to a permission prompt, Claude Code leaves the prompt unanswered. If the program instead closes the session through the Agent SDK, the SDK ends Claude Code's input before sending any signal and the prompt is cancelled as soon as the input ends.

nodes.label: Resuming continues a SIGTERM-interrupted turn
nodes.rationale: When the session is resumed, Claude Code continues the turn that SIGTERM left unfinished — the unfinished turn is recoverable rather than lost.

nodes.label: Piping data through Claude
nodes.rationale: Non-interactive mode reads stdin, so data can be piped in and the response redirected out like any other command-line tool, e.g. `cat build-error.txt | claude -p 'concisely explain the root cause of this build error' > output.txt`.

nodes.label: 10MB piped-stdin cap
nodes.rationale: Piped stdin is capped at 10MB; exceeding it makes Claude Code exit with a clear error and a non-zero status. Larger inputs should be written to a file whose path is referenced in the prompt instead of being piped.

nodes.label: Unreadable stdin degrades to a warning
nodes.rationale: If Claude Code cannot read stdin — for example because the starting process disconnected its end — it prints a warning to stderr and continues with the prompt from the command line. Before v2.1.211 an unreadable stdin on Windows crashed the session or made it exit silently with no output.

nodes.label: Per-invocation cost reporting
nodes.rationale: With `--output-format json` the response payload includes `total_cost_usd` and a per-model cost breakdown, letting scripted callers track spend per invocation without the usage dashboard. Both figures are client-side estimates and can differ from the actual bill.

nodes.label: Claude as a project-specific linter in a build script
nodes.rationale: A non-interactive call can be wrapped in a script to act as a project-specific linter or reviewer — e.g. a `package.json` `lint:claude` script piping `git diff main` into `claude -p` to report typos. Piping the diff means Claude needs no Bash permission to read it, and escaped double quotes keep the script portable to Windows.

nodes.label: --output-format (text, json, stream-json)
nodes.rationale: `--output-format` controls how responses are returned: `text` (default) is plain text, `json` is structured JSON with the result, session ID and metadata (the text result sits in the `result` field), and `stream-json` is newline-delimited JSON for real-time streaming.

nodes.label: Schema-conforming output via --json-schema
nodes.rationale: Pairing `--output-format json` with `--json-schema` and a JSON Schema definition returns output conforming to that schema: the response carries request metadata (session ID, usage) with the structured value in the `structured_output` field, which `jq '.structured_output'` can extract.

nodes.label: JSON Schema validation and the format keyword
nodes.rationale: An invalid schema makes `claude` exit with `Error: --json-schema is not a valid JSON Schema` plus the validator's diagnostic. Schemas using the `format` keyword (e.g. `"format": "email"`) are accepted but `format` is treated as an annotation and not enforced. Before v2.1.205 an invalid schema was silently ignored and returned unstructured text, and any schema containing `format` was treated as invalid.

nodes.label: Token streaming with stream-json
nodes.rationale: `--output-format stream-json` with `--verbose` and `--include-partial-messages` emits tokens as they are generated, one JSON event object per line; the last line is a `result` message carrying the final response text, cost, and session metadata. A `jq -rj` filter on `stream_event` text deltas renders the streaming text alone.

nodes.label: Exit wait while stream output drains
nodes.rationale: If the consumer reads the stream slowly, Claude Code waits for the queued output to drain before exiting, scaling the wait with how much is still queued and capping it at 30 seconds. Before v2.1.214 the exit wait was capped at about two seconds, which could cut off the end of a large response.

nodes.label: Subagent messages in the stream
nodes.rationale: Subagent messages appear as `assistant`/`user` messages whose `parent_tool_use_id` is the spawning tool call's ID (main-conversation messages carry `null`). By default only subagent `tool_use`/`tool_result` blocks are emitted; `--forward-subagent-text` or `CLAUDE_CODE_FORWARD_SUBAGENT_TEXT` (v2.1.211+) also emits text and thinking blocks, and forwards messages at every nesting depth so the nesting tree can be rebuilt (nested subagents were absent before v2.1.219).

nodes.label: system/api_retry event
nodes.rationale: When an API request fails with a retryable error Claude Code emits a `system/api_retry` event before retrying, carrying `attempt`, `max_retries`, `retry_delay_ms`, `error_status` (null for connection errors), an `error` category such as `rate_limit` or `overloaded`, `uuid`, and `session_id`. On v2.1.246+ a `401`/`403` rejecting an `apiKeyHelper` credential makes the first two retries quiet — no event, though they still count toward `attempt`.

nodes.label: system/init session metadata event
nodes.rationale: The `system/init` event reports session metadata including the model, tools, MCP servers and loaded plugins, and is the first event in the stream unless startup events precede it — `plugin_install` events, or `hook_started`/`hook_progress`/`hook_response` events while a `SessionStart` or `Setup` hook runs (batched after the hook in v2.1.169–v2.1.203; live delivery restored in v2.1.204).

nodes.label: capabilities array for feature detection
nodes.rationale: `system/init` optionally carries a `capabilities` array naming protocol behaviors this Claude Code version implements, such as `interrupt_receipt_v1` or `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1`. Consumers should feature-detect from it instead of comparing version strings, and ignore unrecognized values; the field requires v2.1.205 or later and is absent from earlier versions.

nodes.label: plugins and plugin_errors fields
nodes.rationale: `system/init` carries `plugins` (each loaded plugin's `name` and `path`) and `plugin_errors` (each load-time error's `plugin`, `type`, `message`, including unsatisfied dependency versions and `--plugin-dir` failures such as a missing path or invalid archive). Affected plugins are demoted and absent from `plugins`; the `plugin_errors` key is omitted when there are no errors, so CI can fail on it.

nodes.label: mcp_servers and mcp_server_errors fields
nodes.rationale: `mcp_servers` lists each server's `name` and `status`, while `mcp_server_errors` lists `--mcp-config` entries skipped by config validation with `name`, `type` (a skip category such as `unknown_type`, `url_missing_type`, `invalid_config`, `reserved_name`) and `message`; the key is omitted when empty so a CI gate can fail on a non-empty array (v2.1.219+). With `--mcp-config` under `-p`, Claude Code waits for pending servers up to `MCP_TIMEOUT` (30s default, v2.1.221+), except remote servers with a cached tool list.

nodes.label: Skipped-MCP warning is terminal-only
nodes.rationale: Run by hand in a terminal, Claude Code prints a startup warning to stderr such as `Warning: 1 MCP server skipped due to invalid config:` with a reason per entry. When stderr is redirected or captured by a CI runner or SDK host, no warning is printed and the skipped entries are reported only in `mcp_server_errors` (warning requires v2.1.219+).

nodes.label: system/plugin_install events
nodes.rationale: When `CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_PLUGIN_INSTALL` is set, Claude Code emits `system/plugin_install` events while marketplace plugins install before the first turn, with `status` of `started`/`completed` bracketing the overall install and `installed`/`failed` reporting individual marketplaces (plus optional `name` and `error`, and `uuid`/`session_id`).

nodes.label: --allowedTools auto-approval
nodes.rationale: `--allowedTools` lets Claude use named tools without prompting, e.g. `claude -p "Run the test suite and fix any failures" --allowedTools "Bash,Read,Edit"`, so a scripted run completes without a permission prompt.

nodes.label: Permission rule prefix matching
nodes.rationale: `--allowedTools` uses permission rule syntax where a trailing ` *` enables prefix matching: `Bash(git diff *)` allows any command starting with `git diff`. The space before `*` matters — `Bash(git diff*)` would also match `git diff-index`.

nodes.label: Permission modes under -p
nodes.rationale: A permission mode sets a session-wide baseline instead of listing individual tools; for `-p` the built-in starting mode is Manual on every plan, so the wanted mode must be passed. `auto` has a classifier review most actions; `dontAsk` denies anything outside `permissions.allow` or the read-only command set (and always denies `AskUserQuestion`, org-`ask` connector tools, and `requiresUserInteraction` MCP tools); `acceptEdits` writes files and auto-approves common filesystem commands like `mkdir`, `touch`, `mv`, `cp`.

nodes.label: --append-system-prompt customization
nodes.rationale: `--append-system-prompt` adds instructions while keeping Claude Code's default behavior — e.g. a `review.sh` script piping `gh pr diff "$1"` into `claude -p` with a security-engineer instruction and `--output-format json`. `--system-prompt` fully replaces the default prompt instead.

nodes.label: --continue and --resume
nodes.rationale: `--continue` continues the most recent conversation (skipping background sessions), while `--resume` with a session ID continues a specific one. With multiple conversations in flight, capture the ID — `session_id=$(claude -p "Start a review" --output-format json | jq -r '.session_id')` — and pass it to `--resume`.

nodes.label: Machine-wide session lookup by ID
nodes.rationale: The starting and resuming commands can run from different directories: Claude Code finds a session by its ID in any project on the machine. Before v2.1.223 it looked only in the current project directory and its git worktrees, so both commands had to run from the same directory.

nodes.label: Skills and slash commands in -p mode
nodes.rationale: User-invoked skills and custom commands work in `-p` mode by including `/skill-name` in the prompt string, which Claude Code expands before running. Terminal-only built-ins such as `/login` are unavailable; `/model`, `/effort`, `/fast`, `/color` and `/rename` take a value argument and `/mcp` with no argument prints server status (v2.1.205+), and `/config key=value` changes a setting.

nodes.label: Claude Code hooks
nodes.rationale: Hooks are user-defined shell commands that Claude Code runs at specific points in its lifecycle. They are used to enforce project rules, automate repetitive tasks, and integrate Claude Code with existing tools.

nodes.label: Deterministic control over LLM choice
nodes.rationale: The value proposition of hooks is that certain actions always happen rather than relying on the LLM to choose to run them. For decisions that need judgment instead of deterministic rules, prompt-based or agent-based hooks that call a Claude model are the documented alternative.

nodes.label: Hook lifecycle events
nodes.rationale: Claude Code fires named hook events at points in its lifecycle: SessionStart, Setup, UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Notification, MessageDisplay, SubagentStart/Stop, TaskCreated/Completed, Stop, StopFailure, TeammateIdle, InstructionsLoaded, ConfigChange, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, FileChanged, WorktreeCreate/Remove, PreCompact, PostCompact, PreModelSwitch, PostModelSwitch, Elicitation, ElicitationResult and SessionEnd.

nodes.label: Notification event
nodes.rationale: The Notification event fires when Claude Code sends a notification, such as when Claude is waiting for input or permission. It is the event behind the guide's first walkthrough hook, a desktop notification.

nodes.label: Notification matcher values
nodes.rationale: An empty Notification matcher fires on all notification types; specific values narrow it to permission_prompt, idle_prompt, auth_success, the four elicitation_* types, agent_needs_input, agent_completed, and quota_auto_resume_fired/stale/disabled. Several carry version floors: agent_needs_input and agent_completed need v2.1.198+, the quota_auto_resume_* set needs v2.1.234+, sandboxed-network permission_prompt needs v2.1.246+, and a teammate terminal-setup agent_needs_input needs v2.1.248+.

nodes.label: PreToolUse event
nodes.rationale: PreToolUse fires before a tool call executes and can block it. Its matcher filters on tool name, and it receives hook_event_name, tool_name and tool_input on stdin.

nodes.label: PostToolUse event
nodes.rationale: PostToolUse fires after a tool call succeeds and filters by tool name. It uses a top-level decision: "block" field rather than PreToolUse's permissionDecision.

nodes.label: PermissionRequest event
nodes.rationale: PermissionRequest fires when Claude Code is about to ask the user for a permission decision, and its decision lives at hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior. In plain -p runs, or with --permission-prompt-tool, that prompt does not exist unless the Agent SDK canUseTool callback supplies it, so PreToolUse should be used for automated decisions there.

nodes.label: SessionStart event
nodes.rationale: SessionStart fires when a session begins or resumes, and its matcher filters on how the session started: startup, resume, clear, compact or fork. Its stdout on exit 0 is added to Claude's context as plain text.

nodes.label: ConfigChange event
nodes.rationale: ConfigChange fires when an external process or editor modifies a configuration file during a session, so changes can be logged for compliance or blocked. Its matcher filters by configuration source: user_settings, project_settings, local_settings, policy_settings or skills.

nodes.label: CwdChanged event
nodes.rationale: CwdChanged fires when the working directory changes, for example when Claude runs a cd command. It supports no matcher and is documented as the hook for reactive environment management with tools like direnv.

nodes.label: FileChanged event
nodes.rationale: FileChanged fires when a watched file changes on disk, whatever wrote it, including a Bash command. Its matcher lists literal filenames separated by |, which Claude Code splits into filenames rather than evaluating as a regex.

nodes.label: Stop event
nodes.rationale: Stop fires when Claude finishes responding. It supports no matcher, uses a top-level decision: "block" field, and is the recommended place to scan the working tree once per turn when a hook must see every file change including ones made by shell commands.

nodes.label: Command hook type
nodes.rationale: "type": "command" is the default hook type and runs a shell command. Command hooks communicate only through stdin, stdout, stderr and exit codes; they cannot trigger slash commands or tool calls, and they are the recommended type for production workflows.

nodes.label: Prompt-based hook
nodes.rationale: "type": "prompt" sends the prompt plus the hook's input data to a Claude model (Haiku by default, overridable with the model field) for a single-turn decision returned as JSON with ok and reason. On Stop and SubagentStop a false ok feeds the reason back so Claude keeps working, unless the response also sets impossible: true.

nodes.label: Agent-based hook
nodes.rationale: "type": "agent" spawns a subagent that can read files, search code and run tools before returning an ok/reason decision, with a 60-second default timeout and up to 50 tool-use turns. Agent hooks are experimental, do not support the prompt hook's impossible field, have no continueOnBlock field, and behave as if continueOnBlock were true on ok: false.

nodes.label: HTTP hook
nodes.rationale: "type": "http" POSTs the same JSON a command hook would get on stdin to a URL and reads the decision from the HTTP response body in the same JSON format; HTTP status codes alone cannot block an action. Header values interpolate $VAR_NAME only for variables listed in allowedEnvVars.

nodes.label: MCP tool hook type
nodes.rationale: "type": "mcp_tool" calls a tool on an already-connected MCP server instead of running a shell command. It shares the 10-minute default timeout of command and http hooks.

nodes.label: hooks block in a settings file
nodes.rationale: A hook is created by adding a hooks block to a settings file, where each event name is a key inside the single hooks object holding an array of matcher/handler groups. When a hooks key already exists, a new event must be added as a sibling rather than replacing the whole object, and edits to settings files are normally picked up by the file watcher while Claude Code runs.

nodes.label: /hooks browser
nodes.rationale: Typing /hooks opens a read-only browser listing every hook event with a count of configured hooks, and selecting one shows its event, matcher, type, source file and command. It cannot add, modify or remove hooks — that requires editing the settings JSON directly or asking Claude to do it.

nodes.label: Desktop notification hook recipe
nodes.rationale: A Notification hook with an empty matcher fires a native desktop alert: osascript on macOS, notify-send on Linux, or a PowerShell MessageBox on Windows. Known failure modes are Script Editor lacking notification permission on macOS, a missing notification daemon or libnotify-bin on Linux, and the Windows dialog opening behind the terminal.

nodes.label: Auto-format after edits recipe
nodes.rationale: A PostToolUse hook with an Edit|Write matcher runs `jq -r '.tool_input.file_path' | xargs npx prettier --write` so formatting stays consistent without manual intervention. A successful run shows nothing in the conversation, so confirmation comes from the reformatted file or debug logging; to catch rewrites made by Bash commands, a FileChanged hook is used instead.

nodes.label: Block edits to protected files recipe
nodes.rationale: A PreToolUse hook on Edit|Write calls .claude/hooks/protect-files.sh, which reads tool_input.file_path, normalizes Windows backslashes, matches it against patterns such as .env, package-lock.json and .git/, and exits 2 with a Blocked: message on stderr. The script must be made executable with chmod +x, and Claude receives the stderr as feedback so it can adjust.

nodes.label: Re-inject context after compaction recipe
nodes.rationale: Compaction summarizes the conversation to free context space and can lose important details; a SessionStart hook with a compact matcher re-injects critical context after every compaction by writing plain text to stdout. Any dynamic command works, such as git log --oneline -5, while CLAUDE.md is preferred for context needed on every session start.

nodes.label: Configuration-change audit log recipe
nodes.rationale: A ConfigChange hook appends one JSON line per change — timestamp, source and file path — to ~/claude-config-audit.log using jq. To block a change from taking effect instead of only recording it, the hook exits 2 or returns {"decision": "block"}.

nodes.label: direnv environment reload recipe
nodes.rationale: Claude's Bash tool does not pick up direnv-style per-directory environment changes on its own, so a SessionStart hook loads the launch directory's variables and a CwdChanged hook reloads them on every directory change, both running `direnv export bash > "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE"`. direnv allow must be run once per directory with an .envrc, and devbox shellenv works the same way.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE names a file that Claude Code runs as a script preamble before each Bash command, so a hook writing environment exports there changes the environment of subsequent Bash tool calls.

nodes.label: Auto-approve ExitPlanMode recipe
nodes.rationale: A PermissionRequest hook matched narrowly to ExitPlanMode can echo {"hookSpecificOutput": {"hookEventName": "PermissionRequest", "decision": {"behavior": "allow"}}} so Claude Code answers the prompt on the user's behalf, showing "Allowed by PermissionRequest hook" in the transcript. The hook path always keeps the current conversation and cannot start a fresh implementation session the way the dialog can, and the matcher must stay narrow because .* or an empty matcher would auto-approve every tool prompt.

nodes.label: updatedPermissions setMode
nodes.rationale: A PermissionRequest hook's allow decision can carry an updatedPermissions array with a setMode entry naming any permission mode (default, acceptEdits, bypassPermissions); destination: "session" applies it for the current session only.

nodes.label: bypassPermissions precondition
nodes.rationale: Setting bypassPermissions from a hook only applies if the session was launched with bypass mode already available (--dangerously-skip-permissions, --permission-mode bypassPermissions, --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, or permissions.defaultMode) and not disabled by permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode or restricted mode. It is never persisted as defaultMode.

nodes.label: Parallel execution of matching hooks
nodes.rationale: When an event fires, Claude Code runs all matching hooks in parallel and every hook's command runs to completion before results are merged. One hook returning deny does not stop sibling hooks from executing, so a deny must never be relied on to suppress another hook's side effects — in the worked example the logging hook still writes its line while the guardrail hook denies rm -rf.

nodes.label: Most-restrictive decision precedence
nodes.rationale: After all matching hooks finish, Claude Code combines their outputs; for PreToolUse permission decisions the most restrictive answer wins in the order deny, defer, ask, allow. Text from additionalContext is kept from every hook and passed to Claude together.

nodes.label: additionalContext injection
nodes.rationale: UserPromptSubmit hooks inject text into Claude's context via hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, which is delivered as a system reminder Claude reads as plain text. It must be nested inside hookSpecificOutput — placed at the top level of the JSON, Claude Code silently ignores it.

nodes.label: Hook input JSON on stdin
nodes.rationale: When an event fires, Claude Code passes event-specific data as JSON on the script's stdin. Common fields include session_id and cwd; a PreToolUse hook additionally gets hook_event_name, tool_name and tool_input, while UserPromptSubmit gets prompt and SessionStart gets a source of startup, resume, clear, compact or fork.

nodes.label: Exit code 0
nodes.rationale: Exit 0 reports no objection through the exit code. For PreToolUse it does not approve the tool call — the normal permission flow still applies — and for UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, SessionStart and PostModelSwitch, stdout treated as plain text is added to Claude's context.

nodes.label: Exit code 2 blocks the action
nodes.rationale: Exit 2 makes Claude Code block the action, with the reason written to stderr. Where the reason lands is event-dependent: some events feed it to Claude as feedback, some show it to the user, ConfigChange and Elicitation surface no message, and events such as SessionStart cannot be blocked at all — exit 2 shows stderr to the user and execution continues.

nodes.label: Other exit codes and non-blocking errors
nodes.rationale: For any other exit code the outcome depends on stdout: a parsed object that passes schema validation makes the exit code irrelevant and the JSON alone decides; a parsed object that fails validation, or stdout that looks like JSON but is not valid, is a non-blocking error carrying the validation or parse message; plain-text or empty stdout lets the action proceed as a non-blocking error showing a "<hook name> hook error" notice and the first line of stderr prefixed with "Failed with non-blocking status code:".

nodes.label: Structured JSON output
nodes.rationale: Exit codes only let a hook block or stay silent; for finer control the hook exits 0 and prints a JSON object to stdout, typically under hookSpecificOutput with hookEventName. The guide says to pick one approach per hook — exit 2 with a stderr message, or exit 0 with JSON — rather than mixing them.

nodes.label: PreToolUse permissionDecision values
nodes.rationale: On PreToolUse, "allow" skips the interactive prompt while deny and ask rules including enterprise managed deny lists still apply; "deny" cancels the tool call and sends permissionDecisionReason back to Claude; "ask" shows the normal permission prompt.

nodes.label: defer decision
nodes.rationale: A fourth permissionDecision value, "defer", is available only in non-interactive mode with -p. It exits the process with the tool call preserved so an Agent SDK wrapper can collect input and resume.

nodes.label: PreModelSwitch decision control
nodes.rationale: A PreModelSwitch hook returns the same permissionDecision field: "allow" lets the model switch proceed and "deny" cancels it. "ask" prompts for confirmation when /model is run in an interactive session and is treated as a refusal everywhere else.

nodes.label: matcher field
nodes.rationale: Without a matcher a hook fires on every occurrence of its event; a matcher narrows it at the group level, and what it filters differs per event — tool name for the tool events, session source for SessionStart, notification type for Notification, agent type for SubagentStart/Stop, and so on. Matchers are case-sensitive, "Edit|Write" alternation is supported, and from v2.1.191 a comma separates alternatives the same way; UserPromptSubmit, PostToolBatch, Stop, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, CwdChanged and MessageDisplay support no matcher at all.

nodes.label: Matching MCP tool names
nodes.rationale: MCP tools are named mcp__<server>__<tool>, and plugin-bundled servers use a scoped server segment such as mcp__plugin_my-plugin_db__query. A regex matcher like mcp__github__.* targets one server, and a pattern like mcp__.*__write.* matches across servers.

nodes.label: if field
nodes.rationale: The if field uses permission rule syntax such as "Bash(git *)" or "Edit(*.ts)" to filter a handler by tool name and arguments together, so the hook process spawns only on a matching tool call. It works only on the tool events PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest and PermissionDenied — adding it to any other event prevents the hook from running — and multiple tool names need separate handlers or matcher-level alternation.

nodes.label: Best-effort Bash subcommand filtering
nodes.rationale: Whether an if pattern fires depends on the command shape: each subcommand of a chain and commands inside $() or backticks are checked, so `npm test && git push` and `echo $(git log)` both match Bash(git *), while a pattern specifying more than the command name runs the hook anyway on $(), backticks or $VAR. When Claude Code cannot determine which commands the input runs, it runs the hook regardless — so the filter is best-effort and the permission system, not a hook, must enforce a hard allow or deny.

nodes.label: Hook location determines scope
nodes.rationale: Where a hook is declared sets its scope and shareability: ~/.claude/settings.json covers all your projects but is machine-local; .claude/settings.json is a single project and committable; .claude/settings.local.json is a single project and gitignored; managed policy settings are organization-wide; a plugin's hooks/hooks.json applies while the plugin is enabled; skill frontmatter applies for the rest of the session once the skill is invoked; and subagent frontmatter applies while that subagent runs.

nodes.label: disableAllHooks
nodes.rationale: Setting "disableAllHooks": true in a settings file turns hooks off. Claude Code reads the value left after settings precedence applies, so a project's settings file can override yours, and hooks configured in managed settings still run unless disableAllHooks is also set there.

nodes.label: Hook timeouts by type
nodes.rationale: Timeouts vary by hook type and are overridable per hook with the timeout field in seconds: command, http and mcp_tool default to 10 minutes (lowered to 30 seconds for UserPromptSubmit, PreModelSwitch and PostModelSwitch, and 10 seconds for MessageDisplay), prompt to 30 seconds, and agent to 60 seconds. SessionEnd hooks of any type share a 1.5-second budget, raised to match a longer configured per-hook timeout up to 60 seconds.

nodes.label: PostToolUse cannot undo actions
nodes.rationale: A PostToolUse hook cannot undo an action because the tool has already executed by the time it fires.

nodes.label: Stop hooks fire on every response
nodes.rationale: Stop hooks fire whenever Claude finishes responding, not only at task completion, and they do not fire on user interrupts. A turn ended by an API error fires StopFailure instead.

nodes.label: updatedInput last-writer race
nodes.rationale: When several PreToolUse hooks return updatedInput to rewrite a tool's arguments, the last one to finish takes effect; because hooks run in parallel the order is non-deterministic, so more than one hook should not modify the same tool's input.

nodes.label: Hooks tighten but never loosen permissions
nodes.rationale: PreToolUse hooks fire before any permission-mode check in every permission mode including dontAsk, so a deny blocks the tool even under bypassPermissions or --dangerously-skip-permissions, letting policy survive a user's mode change. The reverse does not hold: an allow does not bypass settings deny rules and cannot suppress prompts for MCP tools marked requiresUserInteraction or connector tools an organization set to ask.

nodes.label: Stop hook block cap
nodes.rationale: Claude Code overrides a Stop hook after it blocks eight times in a row without progress and ends the turn with a warning. The hook script should parse the stop_hook_active field from its JSON input and exit 0 early when it is true; a hook that legitimately needs more iterations raises the cap with CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP.

nodes.label: Shell profile output breaks hook JSON
nodes.rationale: A shell-form command hook is run by sh -c, Git Bash, or PowerShell, and although the shell is non-interactive some configurations still source the profile; an unconditional echo there is prepended to the hook's stdout so the output no longer starts with { and Claude Code treats all of it as plain text, silently ignoring the JSON. The fix is to guard profile echoes with a `[[ $- == *i* ]]` interactive check.

nodes.label: Hook debugging and transcript view
nodes.rationale: Ctrl+O opens the transcript view, where a successful hook run shows nothing, a blocking error shows the decision reason or the hook's stderr, and a non-blocking error shows a "<hook name> hook error" notice. Full execution details — which hooks matched, their exit codes, stdout and stderr — require the debug log, enabled with `claude --debug-file /tmp/claude.log` or `/debug` mid-session.

nodes.label: jq as the JSON parser in examples
nodes.rationale: The guide's Bash examples parse the hook's stdin JSON with jq, installed via brew or apt; a "jq: command not found" error means installing it or using Python/Node.js instead. Building output with a JSON encoder such as jq rather than string concatenation is also the documented fix for stdout that fails to parse as JSON.

nodes.label: Exec form via args
nodes.rationale: Adding "args": [] switches a command hook to exec form, spawning the script directly without a shell and avoiding shell quoting entirely. A "command not found" error otherwise calls for absolute paths or ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, and a script that never runs usually needs chmod +x.

nodes.label: Shell commands bypass tool matchers
nodes.rationale: Claude can create or modify files by running shell commands, so an Edit|Write matcher misses those changes. For compliance scanning or audit logging, add a Stop hook that scans the working tree once per turn, or for per-call coverage also match Bash|PowerShell and list modified and untracked files with git status --porcelain; a FileChanged hook covers a specific file whatever wrote it.

nodes.label: Claude Code hooks
nodes.rationale: Hooks are user-defined shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, LLM prompts, or subagents that execute automatically at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle. Claude Code fires the same hook events wherever it runs: terminal sessions, IDE extensions, the Desktop app, and Claude Code on the web.

nodes.label: Three hook cadences
nodes.rationale: Hook events fall into three cadences: once per session (SessionStart, SessionEnd), once per turn (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, StopFailure), and on every tool call inside the agentic loop (PreToolUse, PostToolUse) — except EndConversation calls, which skip both tool events.

nodes.label: How a hook resolves
nodes.rationale: Resolution runs in five steps: the event fires and Claude Code sends JSON on stdin; the matcher is tested against the event's field; the optional `if` condition narrows further; the handler spawns and prints a decision; Claude Code acts on it. Exit code 0 with no output means no decision, so the call continues through the normal permission flow — a hook can deny, but staying silent does not approve.

nodes.label: Three-level hook configuration
nodes.rationale: Hooks are defined in JSON settings files with three levels of nesting: a hook EVENT to respond to, a MATCHER GROUP that filters when it fires, and one or more HOOK HANDLERS that run when matched. The docs reserve those three terms precisely; "hook" alone means the feature.

nodes.label: Hook locations and scope
nodes.rationale: Where a hook is defined determines its scope: ~/.claude/settings.json (all projects, not shareable), .claude/settings.json (one project, committable), .claude/settings.local.json, managed policy settings (organization-wide), a plugin's hooks/hooks.json, skill frontmatter (rest of the session once invoked), and subagent frontmatter (while that subagent runs).

nodes.label: Hooks also fire inside subagents
nodes.rationale: Hooks from settings files, managed policy settings, and plugins also run inside subagents: when a subagent calls a tool, PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire the same configured hooks as in the main conversation, and the input carries `agent_id` and `agent_type`.

nodes.label: allowManagedHooksOnly
nodes.rationale: Enterprise administrators can set `allowManagedHooksOnly` to block user, project, local, and plugin hooks — hooks from plugins force-enabled in managed settings `enabledPlugins` are exempt. It also narrows statusLine/fileSuggestion/subagentStatusLine to managed settings and disables plugins with a `command` source unless `disableCommandPluginSources` is false.

nodes.label: Hook entries merge across settings levels
nodes.rationale: Hook entries merge across settings levels rather than replacing each other: user, project, and local settings add their own hooks without removing managed ones, and `disableAllHooks` cannot disable managed hooks from outside managed settings.

nodes.label: HTTP hook allowlists
nodes.rationale: `allowedHttpHookUrls` and `httpHookAllowedEnvVars` apply to hooks from every source, including managed policy settings: when defined at any level, Claude Code runs an HTTP hook only if its URL matches the merged allowlist, and interpolates only the listed environment variables into hook headers.

nodes.label: Matcher pattern evaluation
nodes.rationale: How a `matcher` is evaluated depends on the characters it contains: `"*"`, `""`, or omitted matches everything; a value of only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,` and `|` is an exact string or a `|`/`,`-separated list of exact strings; anything else is an unanchored JavaScript regular expression tested with RegExp.prototype.test, so `Edit.*` also matches `NotebookEdit`.

nodes.label: FileChanged and StopFailure use a narrower exact-match set
nodes.rationale: `FileChanged` and `StopFailure` use a narrower exact-match set of letters, digits, `_` and `|` only; a hyphen, space, or comma in their matcher keeps it on the regular-expression path and only `|` separates alternatives. Comma separators need v2.1.191+ and hyphens in the exact set need v2.1.195+.

nodes.label: Each event matches on a different field
nodes.rationale: Tool events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionRequest, PermissionDenied) match on tool name; SessionStart on how the session started; SessionEnd on why it ended; Notification on notification type; SubagentStart/Stop on agent type; PreCompact/PostCompact on compaction trigger; ConfigChange on configuration source; and several events (UserPromptSubmit, PostToolBatch, Stop, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated, TaskCompleted, WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, MessageDisplay, CwdChanged) have no matcher support at all. A matcher added to an event without support is silently ignored.

nodes.label: Matching MCP tools
nodes.rationale: MCP server tools appear as regular tools named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, so `mcp__memory__.*` matches every tool from the memory server. The trailing `.*` is required: a bare `mcp__memory` contains only exact-match characters and matches no tool. Plugin-bundled servers use the scoped form `mcp__plugin_<plugin-name>_<server-name>__<tool>`.

nodes.label: The `if` handler condition
nodes.rationale: `if` uses permission-rule syntax to filter an individual handler against the tool name and arguments together, such as `"Bash(git *)"` or `"Edit(*.ts)"`. It holds exactly one rule — there is no `&&`, `||`, or list syntax — and it is evaluated only on tool events; on any other event a handler with `if` set never runs.

nodes.label: Bash `if` matching is best-effort
nodes.rationale: For Bash patterns, leading `VAR=value` assignments are stripped, each `&&`-chained subcommand is checked, and commands inside `$()` and backticks are checked. When Claude Code cannot determine which commands the input runs — `$TOOL git push`, or a pattern more specific than the command name — it runs the hook regardless. Because `if` is best-effort, use the permission system, not a hook, to enforce a hard allow or deny.

nodes.label: Five hook handler types
nodes.rationale: Each object in the inner `hooks` array is a hook handler, and there are five types: `command`, `http`, `mcp_tool`, `prompt`, and `agent`. All matching hooks run in parallel; a handler defined in more than one settings file runs once, while a plugin's or skill's copy stays separate.

nodes.label: Command hooks
nodes.rationale: `type: "command"` runs a shell command. The script receives the event's JSON input on stdin and communicates results back through exit codes and stdout.

nodes.label: HTTP hooks
nodes.rationale: `type: "http"` sends the event's JSON input as an HTTP POST body to a URL with `Content-Type: application/json`. The endpoint communicates results back through the response body using the same JSON output format as command hooks.

nodes.label: MCP tool hooks
nodes.rationale: `type: "mcp_tool"` calls a tool on an already-connected MCP server; the tool's text output is read like command-hook stdout. The server must already be connected — the hook never triggers an OAuth or connection flow — and if it is not connected, or the tool returns `isError: true`, the hook produces a non-blocking error.

nodes.label: Prompt hooks
nodes.rationale: `type: "prompt"` sends a prompt to a Claude model (Haiku by default) for single-turn evaluation; the model returns its decision as structured JSON which Claude Code processes automatically.

nodes.label: Agent hooks
nodes.rationale: `type: "agent"` spawns a subagent that can use tools like Read, Grep, and Glob to verify conditions over up to 50 turns before returning a decision. Agent hooks are experimental and may change; production workflows should prefer command hooks.

nodes.label: Common handler fields
nodes.rationale: All hook types accept `type` (required), `if`, `timeout`, `statusMessage` (custom spinner text), and `once`. `once: true` removes the hook after its first successful run and is honored only for hooks declared in skill frontmatter — ignored in settings files and agent frontmatter; a run that fails, blocks with exit 2, or times out leaves the hook in place.

nodes.label: Per-type and per-event timeout defaults
nodes.rationale: Timeout defaults are 600 seconds for `command`, `http`, and `mcp_tool`, 30 for `prompt`, and 60 for `agent`. Claude Code lowers the command/http/mcp_tool default to 30 on UserPromptSubmit, PreModelSwitch and PostModelSwitch, and to 10 on MessageDisplay; SessionEnd hooks share a 1.5-second budget that a longer per-hook timeout raises up to 60 seconds. Timeout is not enforced on a command hook running with `async: true`.

nodes.label: Exec form (`args` present)
nodes.rationale: A command hook runs in exec form when `args` is set: Claude Code resolves `command` as an executable on PATH and spawns it directly with `args` as the argument vector. There is no shell, so each element is one argument exactly as written and special characters pass through verbatim. Prefer exec form for any hook referencing a path placeholder.

nodes.label: Shell form (`args` omitted)
nodes.rationale: Shell form runs when `args` is absent: the `command` string is passed to `sh -c` on macOS and Linux, Git Bash on Windows, or PowerShell when Git Bash is missing, and the shell tokenizes, expands variables, and interprets pipes, `&&`, redirects, and globs. Use it when you need shell features, and wrap each path placeholder in double quotes.

nodes.label: `async: true` background hooks
nodes.rationale: Setting `"async": true` on a `type: "command"` hook runs it in the background while Claude keeps working. Async hooks cannot block or control behavior — `decision`, `permissionDecision` and `continue` have no effect — and their `additionalContext` and `systemMessage` are delivered to Claude on the next conversation turn without being shown to the user.

nodes.label: `asyncRewake`
nodes.rationale: `asyncRewake: true` runs the hook in the background and wakes Claude on exit code 2: the hook's stderr, or stdout if stderr is empty, is shown to Claude as a system reminder so it can react to a long-running background failure. Unlike a plain `async` hook, `timeout` is still enforced on an `asyncRewake` hook.

nodes.label: `shell` field
nodes.rationale: The `shell` field selects `"bash"` or `"powershell"` for one command hook, defaulting to bash or to powershell on Windows when Git Bash is absent. It does not require CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL because hooks spawn PowerShell directly, and it is ignored when `args` is set.

nodes.label: HTTP hook fields
nodes.rationale: HTTP hooks accept `url` (required), `headers` whose values support `$VAR`/`${VAR}` interpolation, and `allowedEnvVars` — the list of environment variable names that may be interpolated. References to unlisted variables are replaced with empty strings, so `allowedEnvVars` is required for any env-var interpolation to work.

nodes.label: MCP tool hook fields
nodes.rationale: MCP tool hooks accept `server` (a configured server name, or the scoped `plugin:<plugin-name>:<server-name>` form for a plugin-bundled server), `tool`, and `input` whose string values support `${path}` substitution from the hook's JSON input, such as `"${tool_input.file_path}"`.

nodes.label: Prompt and agent hook fields
nodes.rationale: Prompt and agent hooks accept `prompt` (required) and `model` (defaults to a fast model). `$ARGUMENTS` is the placeholder for the hook input JSON, and a backslash escapes literal text such as `\$1.00`.

nodes.label: Path placeholders
nodes.rationale: `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` is the project root where the session started, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` the plugin's installation directory (which changes on each update), and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` the plugin's persistent data directory. All three are also exported as environment variables on the spawned process in both exec and shell form.

nodes.label: Placeholders vs worktrees
nodes.rationale: If Claude enters a worktree mid-session, `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` stays at the project root where the session started, while the `cwd` field in the hook's input JSON follows Claude — it is the worktree root, and the new directory after a `cd`. Read `cwd` when a hook needs to know which directory Claude is working in.

nodes.label: Hooks in skill and subagent frontmatter
nodes.rationale: Hooks can be declared in skill and subagent YAML frontmatter using the same configuration format. Subagent hooks run only while that subagent runs, and a `Stop` hook there is converted to `SubagentStop`; skill hooks register when the skill is invoked and keep running for the rest of the session unless `once: true` is set. Project subagent frontmatter hooks require accepting the workspace trust dialog, while project skill frontmatter hooks follow the settings-file rule.

nodes.label: The `/hooks` menu
nodes.rationale: `/hooks` opens a read-only browser for configured hooks: every event with a count, drill-down into matchers, and full handler details labeled with a `[type]` prefix and a source (User Settings, Project Settings, Local Settings, Plugin Hooks, Session Hooks). It is read-only — to change hooks you edit the settings JSON.

nodes.label: Disabling hooks
nodes.rationale: `"disableAllHooks": true` temporarily disables all hooks; Claude Code reads the value left after settings precedence, so a project `false` overrides a user `true`, and `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` turns hooks off for one run. Only `disableAllHooks` set at the managed level can disable managed hooks, and there is no way to disable an individual hook while keeping it configured.

nodes.label: Common hook input fields
nodes.rationale: Every hook event receives `session_id`, `prompt_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode`, `effort`, and `hook_event_name` as JSON — on stdin for command hooks, as the POST body for HTTP hooks. The transcript file is written asynchronously and may lag the in-memory conversation, so hooks needing the turn's final assistant text should read `last_assistant_message` on Stop/SubagentStop rather than the transcript.

nodes.label: `agent_id` and `agent_type` input fields
nodes.rationale: When running with `--agent` or inside a subagent, hooks additionally receive `agent_id` (unique identifier, present only inside a subagent call) and `agent_type` (the agent name). For subagents, the subagent's type takes precedence over the session's `--agent` value.

nodes.label: The `effort` input field
nodes.rationale: `effort` is an object with a `level` field holding the effort level in effect — low, medium, high, xhigh, or max — reporting the level Claude Code actually ran if the model does not support the requested one, and reporting Ultracode as `"xhigh"`. It is present for events inside a tool-use context and is also exposed to hook commands as `$CLAUDE_EFFORT`.

nodes.label: There is no $CLAUDE_MODEL environment variable
nodes.rationale: Only SessionStart hooks can receive a `model` field, and Claude Code does not always include it; PreModelSwitch and PostModelSwitch receive `from_model` and `to_model` instead. There is no `$CLAUDE_MODEL` environment variable, and `$ANTHROPIC_MODEL` does not change when you switch models with `/model` mid-session.

nodes.label: Hook process environment
nodes.rationale: A hook process inherits the parent environment apart from the `OTEL_*` exporter variables Claude Code removes from every subprocess, and the variables stripped when `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB=1`. `$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` is `"true"` in remote web environments, and v2.1.199+ sets `$CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID` during an active Remote Control connection.

nodes.label: Hooks have no controlling terminal
nodes.rationale: On macOS and Linux, command hooks run in their own session without a controlling terminal, so the hook and its children cannot open /dev/tty or send escape sequences directly to the interface; Windows has no /dev/tty at all. Surface a message with `systemMessage`, and trigger a desktop notification, window title, or bell with `terminalSequence`.

nodes.label: Exit code output model
nodes.rationale: The hook's exit code tells Claude Code whether the action should proceed, be blocked, or be ignored — but it does not act alone: Claude Code reads JSON output fields from stdout on every exit code, and for events using the standard decision model a parsed, schema-valid object takes effect alongside the code. Exit 2's block is the one outcome JSON cannot override.

nodes.label: Exit code 0
nodes.rationale: Exit 0 means success and is the intended code when printing JSON for structured control. For most events stdout goes only to the debug log; the exceptions are UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, SessionStart, and PostModelSwitch, where plain-text stdout is added as context Claude can see. Stderr from a hook that exits 0 goes to the debug log only and Claude never sees it.

nodes.label: How stdout is read as JSON or plain text
nodes.rationale: Ignoring surrounding whitespace: stdout that starts with `{` and ends with `}` is parsed as JSON; stdout that starts with `{` but does not end with `}` is plain text; anything else, including a JSON array or a quoted JSON string, is plain text. A parsed object that fails schema validation, or stdout Claude Code tries and fails to parse, is a non-blocking error on every exit code other than 2.

nodes.label: Exit code 2
nodes.rationale: Exit 2 is a blocking error: on events that can block it blocks whether or not JSON is printed, and even a JSON `permissionDecision: "allow"` cannot override it. The blocking message is the reason from a blocking JSON decision when there is one, and stderr otherwise. On Elicitation and ElicitationResult an exit-2 hook's `hookSpecificOutput` is ignored.

nodes.label: Other exit codes
nodes.rationale: Any other exit code does not block on its own for most events; the outcome depends on stdout. A schema-valid parsed object makes the JSON alone decide and the exit code is ignored; plain text or empty stdout is a non-blocking error whose transcript notice carries the first stderr line prefixed `Failed with non-blocking status code:`. A hook that cannot start (rc 127, bad path) lands in the same bucket, which is how a mistyped policy hook goes silently disabled.

nodes.label: Exit 1 does not block
nodes.rationale: Without valid JSON on stdout, Claude Code treats exit code 1 as a non-blocking error and proceeds with the action, even though 1 is the conventional Unix failure code. A hook meant to enforce a policy must use `exit 2`. The exception is WorktreeCreate, where any non-zero exit aborts worktree creation.

nodes.label: Timeout behavior
nodes.rationale: Apart from an `async: true` command hook, a command, HTTP, or MCP-tool hook that reaches its timeout is canceled and its output discarded, so on most events a timed-out hook renders no decision. On PreModelSwitch a canceled hook BLOCKS the model switch; on PreToolUse a timed-out command/http/mcp_tool hook does NOT block the tool call, while an Agent SDK callback hook that exceeds its timeout does.

nodes.label: Exit code 2 behavior per event
nodes.rationale: Exit 2 blocks on PreToolUse (the tool call), UserPromptSubmit (blocks and erases the prompt), UserPromptExpansion, Stop, SubagentStop, TeammateIdle, TaskCreated (rolls back creation), TaskCompleted, ConfigChange (except policy_settings), PostToolBatch (stops the agentic loop), PreCompact, PreModelSwitch, Elicitation (denies), ElicitationResult (becomes decline), and WorktreeCreate (any non-zero code). It does not block on PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionDenied, Notification, SubagentStart, SessionStart, Setup, SessionEnd, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, FileChanged, PostCompact, PostModelSwitch, StopFailure, WorktreeRemove, InstructionsLoaded, or MessageDisplay.

nodes.label: HTTP response handling
nodes.rationale: HTTP hooks use status codes and bodies instead of exit codes: 2xx with an empty body is success; 2xx with a JSON object body is parsed with the same schema as command hooks; 2xx with any other body, a non-2xx status, and a connection failure are all non-blocking errors. HTTP hooks cannot signal a blocking error through status codes alone — to block, return 2xx with a JSON body carrying the decision fields.

nodes.label: Universal JSON output fields
nodes.rationale: The JSON object supports universal fields — `continue` (false stops Claude entirely and takes precedence over event-specific decisions), `stopReason`, `suppressOutput` (accepted but has no effect), `systemMessage`, and `terminalSequence` — plus top-level `decision`/`reason` for some events and a nested `hookSpecificOutput` requiring a `hookEventName` field. Hook output strings are capped at 10,000 characters, beyond which the text is written to a file and replaced with a preview and path.

nodes.label: terminalSequence
nodes.rationale: Because hooks have no controlling terminal, a hook returns an escape sequence in `terminalSequence` and Claude Code emits it through its own terminal write path — race-free, and working inside tmux, screen, and Windows. Only OSC 0/1/2/9/99/777 and bare BEL are allowlisted; anything else, including OSC 8 hyperlinks and OSC 52 clipboard writes, is rejected and the field ignored. It is written only in an interactive session with the interface on screen, never under `-p` or the Agent SDK.

nodes.label: additionalContext
nodes.rationale: `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` passes a string into Claude's context wrapped in a system reminder inserted where the hook fired; Claude reads it on the next model request but it is not a chat message. Write it as factual statements rather than imperative system instructions — text framed as out-of-band commands can trigger Claude's prompt-injection defenses. On resume, Claude Code replays saved text rather than re-running the hook, so timestamps and SHAs go stale.

nodes.label: Decision control patterns per event
nodes.rationale: Events express decisions differently: a top-level `decision: "block"` plus `reason` (UserPromptSubmit, UserPromptExpansion, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PostToolBatch, Stop, SubagentStop, ConfigChange, PreCompact); `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` (PreToolUse, PreModelSwitch); `decision.behavior` (PermissionRequest); `retry` (PermissionDenied); a path return (WorktreeCreate); `action`/`content` (Elicitation, ElicitationResult); `displayContent` (MessageDisplay); context only (SessionStart, SubagentStart, PostModelSwitch); and no decision control at all for Setup, WorktreeRemove, Notification, SessionEnd, PostCompact, InstructionsLoaded, StopFailure, CwdChanged, DirectoryAdded, and FileChanged.

nodes.label: Rewriting content rather than allowing or blocking
nodes.rationale: A few events can rewrite content: PreToolUse's `updatedInput` replaces a tool's arguments before it runs, PermissionRequest's `updatedInput` sits inside the `decision` object, and PostToolUse's `updatedToolOutput` replaces the tool's result. UserPromptSubmit cannot replace the prompt — it only injects `additionalContext` alongside it. Intercept at PreToolUse for outbound inputs and PostToolUse for inbound results.

nodes.label: SessionStart event
nodes.rationale: SessionStart runs when a session begins or resumes, with matcher values `startup`, `resume`, `clear`, `compact`, and `fork` (forked sessions reported `resume` before v2.1.214). Only `command` and `mcp_tool` handler types are supported, and because it runs on every session the hooks must stay fast. Input adds `source` and optionally `model`, `agent_type`, and `session_title`.

nodes.label: SessionStart resume-cost input fields
nodes.rationale: When `source` is `resume` or `fork` and the transcript holds at least one Claude response, SessionStart also receives `seconds_since_last_response`, `context_tokens` (tokens the first request re-sends), `prompt_cache_likely_expired`, and `estimated_cache_write_usd`, so a hook can report what resuming a stale conversation costs before the first request. Requires v2.1.251 or later.

nodes.label: SessionStart decision control
nodes.rationale: SessionStart has no blocking control but adds plain-text stdout to Claude's context and accepts `additionalContext`, `initialUserMessage` (becomes the first user turn in `-p` mode), `sessionTitle` (applies on startup/resume/fork, ignored on clear/compact), `watchPaths` (paths for FileChanged), and `reloadSkills` (re-scan skill and command directories after the hooks complete, so skills the hook installed work in the same session).

nodes.label: CLAUDE_ENV_FILE
nodes.rationale: SessionStart, Setup, CwdChanged, and FileChanged hooks receive `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`, a file path where `export` statements can be appended to persist environment variables into subsequent Bash commands for the session. Use append (`>>`) to preserve variables set by other hooks; no other hook types have access to it.

nodes.label: Setup event
nodes.rationale: Setup fires only for `claude --init-only`, or `--init`/`--maintenance` in `-p` mode, with matchers `init` and `maintenance` and a `trigger` input field. It never fires on normal startup, so a plugin needing a dependency installed cannot rely on it — check on first use and install on miss instead. Setup cannot block, and its JSON output fields are discarded on every exit code.

nodes.label: InstructionsLoaded event
nodes.rationale: InstructionsLoaded fires when a CLAUDE.md or `.claude/rules/*.md` file is loaded into context — at session start and again on lazy loads.
