Input carries `file_path`, `memory_type` (User/Project/Local/Managed), `load_reason` (session_start, nested_traversal, path_glob_match, include, compact), `globs`, `trigger_file_path`, and `parent_file_path`. It runs asynchronously for observability and has no decision control; its JSON output is discarded.

nodes.label: UserPromptSubmit event
nodes.rationale: UserPromptSubmit runs when a prompt is submitted, before Claude processes it, receiving the `prompt` text. Its default command/http/mcp_tool timeout is 30 seconds rather than 600 because it blocks model processing; on timeout the output including `additionalContext` is discarded and the prompt reaches Claude without it — but an Agent SDK callback hook that times out here BLOCKS the prompt, because a callback can be a policy gate that must not fail open.

nodes.label: UserPromptSubmit decision control
nodes.rationale: Context can be added two ways on exit 0: plain-text stdout, or JSON `additionalContext`; neither produces a visible transcript entry. `decision: "block"` prevents processing and ERASES the prompt from context, `reason` is shown to the user but not added to context, `sessionTitle` names the session, and `suppressOriginalPrompt` omits the original text from the block message.

nodes.label: UserPromptExpansion event
nodes.rationale: UserPromptExpansion runs when a user-typed command expands into a prompt before reaching Claude, matching on `command_name` and receiving `expansion_type` (`slash_command` or `mcp_prompt`), `command_args`, `command_source`, and the original `prompt`. It covers the path PreToolUse misses: a PreToolUse hook on the Skill tool fires only when Claude calls the tool, while typing `/skillname` directly bypasses it. `decision: "block"` prevents the expansion.

nodes.label: MessageDisplay event
nodes.rationale: MessageDisplay runs while assistant message text streams: each batch of newly completed lines fires the hook once and Claude Code renders the hook's replacement in their place. Input carries `turn_id`, `message_id`, `index`, `final`, and `delta`; treat `final`, not a non-empty delta, as the end-of-message signal. In `-p` and Agent SDK runs it fires once per message with the whole text.

nodes.label: MessageDisplay output is display-only
nodes.rationale: MessageDisplay hooks return `displayContent` to replace the delta on screen and have no decision control: the transcript and what Claude sees keep the original text, verbose mode shows the original, and `systemMessage` and `continue` are discarded. Claude Code holds each batch until the hook returns, and displays the original text if the hook fails or times out — the default timeout here is 10 seconds.

nodes.label: PreToolUse event
nodes.rationale: PreToolUse runs after Claude creates tool parameters and before the tool call is processed, matching any tool name except `EndConversation`. It does NOT fire for files referenced with `@` in a prompt, because Claude Code inserts their contents while building the prompt with no tool call — a `Read` deny rule is the way to block those paths.

nodes.label: PreToolUse file paths are absolute and platform-native
nodes.rationale: For Write, Edit, and Read, `tool_input.file_path` is always absolute: Claude Code expands `~` and relative paths before hooks run, so a path-matching hook cannot be bypassed by a different spelling. On Windows the path arrives with backslashes even under Git Bash, so a forward-slash comparison silently never matches and the call proceeds as if the hook had nothing to block; normalize separators and match a path segment rather than anchoring with `^`.

nodes.label: Per-tool `tool_input` schemas
nodes.rationale: The `tool_input` fields depend on the tool: Bash and PowerShell carry `command`, `description`, `timeout`, and `run_in_background`; Write carries `file_path` and `content`; Edit adds `old_string`, `new_string`, `replace_all`; Read adds `offset`/`limit`; Glob uses `pattern`/`path`; Grep uses `pattern`, `path`, `glob`, `output_mode`, `-i`, `multiline`; WebFetch `url`/`prompt`; WebSearch `query` plus domain filters; Agent `prompt`, `description`, `subagent_type`, `model`; AskUserQuestion `questions`/`answers`; ExitPlanMode `plan`, `planFilePath`, and the deprecated `allowedPrompts`.

nodes.label: Agent tool response telemetry
nodes.rationale: When a foreground Agent call completes, PostToolUse receives the subagent's final text and run telemetry in `tool_response`: `status`, `agentId`, `content`, `resolvedModel`, `modelsUsed`, `totalTokens`, `totalDurationMs`, `totalToolUseCount`, and `usage`. `totalTokens` and `usage` cover the FINAL API request only, not the whole run — use the token and cost counters filtered to `query_source: "subagent"` for rollups. Background subagents return `status: "async_launched"` with no usage fields.

nodes.label: PreToolUse decision control
nodes.rationale: PreToolUse returns its decision inside `hookSpecificOutput`: `permissionDecision` of `allow`, `deny`, `ask`, or `defer`, plus `permissionDecisionReason`, `updatedInput` (replaces the ENTIRE input object, and permission rules are re-evaluated against it), and `additionalContext`. When several hooks disagree, precedence is deny > defer > ask > allow, and deny/ask permission rules still apply regardless of what the hook returns. Top-level `decision`/`reason` are deprecated for this event.

nodes.label: Allow paired with updatedInput for interactive tools
nodes.rationale: `AskUserQuestion` and `ExitPlanMode` require user interaction and normally block in `-p` mode; returning `permissionDecision: "allow"` TOGETHER WITH `updatedInput` satisfies that requirement, so the hook collects the answer through its own UI and the tool runs without prompting. `"allow"` alone is not sufficient. Since v2.1.199 an MCP tool marked `_meta["anthropic/requiresUserInteraction"]` cannot have its prompt skipped at all.

nodes.label: Deferring a tool call
nodes.rationale: `permissionDecision: "defer"` is for integrations running `claude -p` as a subprocess: the tool does not execute, the process exits with `stop_reason: "tool_deferred"` and a `deferred_tool_use` payload, the caller collects input through its own UI, then resumes with `--resume` and returns `allow` with the answer in `updatedInput`. It is honored only in `-p` mode, works only when Claude makes a SINGLE tool call in the turn, and has no timeout or retry limit.

nodes.label: PermissionRequest event
nodes.rationale: PermissionRequest runs when Claude Code is about to ask for permission to use a tool, or when it would otherwise auto-deny a call it cannot prompt for — in sessions that cannot show a prompt, if no hook returns a decision the tool call is DENIED. It receives `tool_name`, `tool_input` (no `tool_use_id`), and an optional `permission_suggestions` array holding the "always allow" options the dialog would show.

nodes.label: PermissionRequest decision control
nodes.rationale: PermissionRequest returns a `decision` object with `behavior` (allow/deny), `updatedInput` and `updatedPermissions` for allow, and `message`/`interrupt` for deny. Exit code 2 is NOT honored for this event — a hook that exits 2 without a `decision` object leaves the permission flow unchanged and its stderr is discarded; only the `decision` object can grant or deny.

nodes.label: Permission update entries
nodes.rationale: `updatedPermissions` and `permission_suggestions` share one entry shape whose `type` picks its fields: `addRules`, `replaceRules`, `removeRules`, `setMode`, `addDirectories`, and `removeDirectories`. `destination` decides where the change lands — `session` (in-memory), `localSettings`, `projectSettings`, or `userSettings`. `setMode` with `bypassPermissions` takes effect only if the session was launched with bypass mode available, and is never persisted as `defaultMode`.

nodes.label: PostToolUse event
nodes.rationale: PostToolUse runs immediately after a tool completes successfully, matching on tool name, and receives both `tool_input` and `tool_response` plus an optional `duration_ms` that excludes time spent in permission prompts and PreToolUse hooks. To react to a file changing no matter what wrote it, use FileChanged — Claude Code does not run an `Edit|Write` PostToolUse hook when a Bash command or an outside process rewrites the file.

nodes.label: PostToolUse decision control
nodes.rationale: PostToolUse accepts `decision: "block"` with `reason` (added next to the tool result; Claude still sees the original output), `additionalContext`, `classifierContext`, `updatedToolOutput`, and the MCP-only `updatedMCPToolOutput`. `updatedToolOutput` changes only what Claude sees — the tool has already run, and telemetry captured the original — and a value that does not match a built-in tool's output shape is ignored.

nodes.label: classifierContext
nodes.rationale: `classifierContext` sends a short note about a call's result to the auto-mode classifier rather than to Claude, which is the supported way to tell it something about a result it never sees. Notes from hooks configured in Claude Code are treated as unverified application context and never establish user intent; notes are capped at 2,000 characters per tool call, ignored from background hooks, and discarded for calls the classifier does not record. Requires v2.1.236+.

nodes.label: PostToolUseFailure event
nodes.rationale: PostToolUseFailure runs when a tool that started executing fails, adding `error`, `is_interrupt`, and `duration_ms` to the PostToolUse-style input, and supports only `additionalContext` as decision control. It does NOT fire for calls rejected before execution — unknown tool names, schema-validation failures, or permission denials — and the `error` string format varies by tool, so key on `tool_name`, `is_interrupt`, and the `Exit code N` first line rather than parsing the rest.

nodes.label: PostToolBatch event
nodes.rationale: PostToolBatch runs exactly once after every tool call in a batch resolves, before the next model request, receiving a `tool_calls` array. It is the right place for context depending on the SET of tools that ran, since PostToolUse fires concurrently per tool. Its `tool_response` shape differs from PostToolUse's: it carries the serialized `tool_result` content the model sees, not the tool's structured Output object. `decision: "block"` or `continue: false` stops the agentic loop.

nodes.label: PermissionDenied event
nodes.rationale: PermissionDenied runs when AUTO MODE denies a tool call, including denials with no classifier verdict. It does not fire when you manually deny a dialog, when a PreToolUse hook blocks, or when a deny rule matches. Input adds `reason` — usually the fixed text `Blocked by classifier`, or `Classifier unavailable`, or a no-verdict message beginning `Auto mode could not evaluate this action`.

nodes.label: PermissionDenied retry
nodes.rationale: `hookSpecificOutput.retry: true` tells the model it may retry the denied tool call; Claude Code does not reverse the denial itself, and without JSON or with `retry: false` the denial stands. Claude Code IGNORES `retry: true` for no-verdict denials, because the rejection message already tells the model whether to retry. Exit code and stderr are ignored on this event since the denial already happened.

nodes.label: Notification event
nodes.rationale: Notification runs when Claude Code sends a notification, matching on notification type. Hooks fire even with desktop notifications turned off — `preferredNotifChannel` changes only how you are alerted. Notification hooks cannot block or modify notifications; `systemMessage` and `continue` are discarded, but `terminalSequence` is still emitted.

nodes.label: Notification types
nodes.rationale: The matcher values are `permission_prompt`, `idle_prompt`, `auth_success`, `elicitation_dialog`, `elicitation_url_dialog`, `elicitation_complete`, `elicitation_response`, `agent_needs_input`, `agent_completed`, `quota_auto_resume_fired`, `quota_auto_resume_stale`, and `quota_auto_resume_disabled`. Several are gated on inactivity: `permission_prompt` and the elicitation dialogs wait about six seconds without a keystroke, and `idle_prompt` about 60 seconds after Claude finishes.

nodes.label: SubagentStart event
nodes.rationale: SubagentStart runs when a subagent is spawned via the Agent tool, matching on agent type — the built-in name, a custom subagent's frontmatter `name`, or a plugin-scoped identifier such as `my-plugin:reviewer` whose colon forces the regular-expression path, so anchor it as `^my-plugin:reviewer$`. It cannot block creation but can inject `additionalContext` into the subagent before its first prompt.

nodes.label: SubagentStop event
nodes.rationale: SubagentStop runs when a subagent finishes, receiving `stop_hook_active`, `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `agent_transcript_path` (the subagent's own nested transcript), `last_assistant_message`, and the parent session's `background_tasks` and `session_crons`. It uses the same decision control as Stop: `decision: "block"` with a `reason` keeps the subagent running and delivers the reason as its next instruction.

nodes.label: TaskCreated event
nodes.rationale: TaskCreated runs when a task is being created via the `TaskCreate` tool, with no matcher support, receiving `task_id`, `task_subject`, and optionally `task_description`, `teammate_name`, and the deprecated `team_name`. Either exit code 2 or `decision: "block"` makes Claude Code DELETE the task and return the message to Claude as the tool's error; `continue: false` is ignored.

nodes.label: TaskCompleted event
nodes.rationale: TaskCompleted fires when any agent marks a task completed through `TaskUpdate`, or when an agent-team teammate finishes its turn with in-progress tasks. Exit code 2 leaves the task incomplete and feeds stderr back to the model; `{"continue": false, "stopReason": …}` stops a teammate entirely but is IGNORED when the `TaskUpdate` tool triggered the event.

nodes.label: Stop event
nodes.rationale: Stop runs when the main agent has finished responding; it does not run on a user interrupt, and API errors fire StopFailure instead. `stop_hook_active` is true when Claude Code is already continuing because of a stop hook — check it to avoid blocking on a condition that never resolves — and Claude Code overrides the hook and ends the turn after 8 consecutive blocks. `/goal` is a built-in shortcut for a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook.

nodes.label: Stop decision control
nodes.rationale: Stop and SubagentStop accept `decision: "block"` with a REQUIRED `reason` telling Claude why to continue, and `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` for non-error feedback: it keeps the conversation going through the same loop protections (`stop_hook_active` and the 8-continuation cap) but the transcript labels it `Stop hook feedback` rather than raising a hook error.

nodes.label: background_tasks and session_crons
nodes.rationale: Stop and SubagentStop input carry `background_tasks` and `session_crons` so a hook can distinguish "session is done" from "session is paused waiting for background work". Each background task reports `id`, `type` (shell, subagent, monitor, workflow, teammate, cloud session, MCP task), `status`, `description`, and type-specific fields; each cron reports `id`, `schedule`, `recurring`, and `prompt`.

nodes.label: StopFailure event
nodes.rationale: StopFailure runs INSTEAD of Stop when the turn ends due to an API error, matching on the `error` type (`rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `account_on_hold`, `billing_error`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `unknown`). Claude Code ignores the hook's output and exit code apart from `terminalSequence`, and here `last_assistant_message` holds the API error string itself.

nodes.label: TeammateIdle event
nodes.rationale: TeammateIdle runs when an agent-team teammate is about to go idle after finishing its turn, with no matcher support, receiving `teammate_name` and the deprecated `team_name`. Exit code 2 feeds stderr back and the teammate keeps working; `{"continue": false, "stopReason": …}` stops the teammate entirely. Use it for quality gates before a teammate stops.

nodes.label: ConfigChange event
nodes.rationale: ConfigChange runs when a settings file, managed policy file, or skill file changes during a session, matching `user_settings`, `project_settings`, `local_settings`, `policy_settings`, or `skills`, and receiving `source` and `file_path`. Exit code 2 or `decision: "block"` prevents the change from applying — except `policy_settings`, which can never be blocked so enterprise-managed settings always take effect. A blocked change surfaces no message; only a debug-log line.

nodes.label: CwdChanged event
nodes.rationale: CwdChanged runs when the working directory changes, for example when Claude runs `cd`, with no matcher support, receiving `old_cwd` and `new_cwd`. It cannot block the change; Claude Code reads `watchPaths` and `systemMessage` from its output and discards `continue`. It has `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` access and pairs with FileChanged for per-directory environment tools like direnv.

nodes.label: DirectoryAdded event
nodes.rationale: DirectoryAdded runs after a working directory is added mid-session by `/add-dir` (`slash_command`) or an SDK `register_repo_root` control request, receiving `directory` and `source`. It does NOT fire for `--add-dir` at startup, for the `/permissions` Workspace tab, or for an already-added directory. Claude Code fires it after refreshing sandbox and permission state, does not wait for it, and it cannot block the add.

nodes.label: FileChanged event
nodes.rationale: FileChanged runs when a watched file changes on disk, detected by a filesystem watcher rather than by inspecting tool calls, so it fires no matter what wrote the file — an Edit, a Bash command, or a process outside Claude Code. Input carries `file_path` and `event` (`change`, `add`, `unlink`). It has no decision control and cannot block the change, but can return `watchPaths` and has `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` access.

nodes.label: The FileChanged matcher serves two roles
nodes.rationale: For FileChanged the matcher both BUILDS the watch list — split on `|`, each segment registered as a literal filename in the working directory — and FILTERS which hook groups run against the changed file's basename. Regex is useless for the first role: `^\.env` would watch a file literally named `^\.env`, and a `"*"` matcher registers a literal file named `*`. Give a dynamic-path group an OMITTED matcher, which matches every watched file and adds nothing to the list.

nodes.label: WorktreeCreate event
nodes.rationale: WorktreeCreate runs when a worktree is being created — from `--worktree`, a subagent with `isolation: "worktree"`, or a background session — and configuring it REPLACES Claude Code's default `git worktree` behavior, enabling SVN, Perforce, or Mercurial. Because the replacement is total, `.worktreeinclude` is not processed and any local file copying must happen inside the hook script.

nodes.label: WorktreeCreate output contract
nodes.rationale: WorktreeCreate does not use the allow/block model: a command hook prints the worktree path as the last non-empty line of stdout (ANSI codes stripped, everything else redirected to stderr), while an HTTP hook returns `hookSpecificOutput.worktreePath`. Any failure or missing path fails creation, and Claude Code refuses an absolute path containing `.`/`..` segments or one passing through a symlink below the repository root. A command hook therefore cannot return JSON at all.

nodes.label: WorktreeRemove event
nodes.rationale: WorktreeRemove is the cleanup counterpart to WorktreeCreate, firing when a `--worktree` session is removed, a `isolation: "worktree"` subagent finishes, or a background session is deleted. It receives `worktree_path`, cannot block removal, has its JSON output discarded, and logs failures in debug mode only. Without one, a non-git worktree directory is left on disk.

nodes.label: PreCompact event
nodes.rationale: PreCompact runs before a compact operation, matching `manual` (`/compact`) or `auto`, and receiving `trigger` and `custom_instructions` (null for auto, and null for manual when nothing was passed). Exit 2 or `decision: "block"` blocks compaction — blocking a proactive auto-compaction just skips it, while blocking one triggered to recover from a context-limit error makes the underlying error surface and the request fail.

nodes.label: PostCompact event
nodes.rationale: PostCompact runs after a compact operation completes, with the same `manual`/`auto` matchers, receiving `trigger` and `compact_summary` — the conversation summary the compaction generated. It has no decision control and its `systemMessage` and `continue` are discarded; use it to log the summary or update external state.

nodes.label: PreModelSwitch event
nodes.rationale: PreModelSwitch (v2.1.251+) runs before Claude Code applies a model switch you or a client requested — `/model`, the pickers, the `/config` Model setting, fast mode, or an SDK `set_model` request. It does NOT run for switches Claude Code makes on its own, such as an automatic fallback or restoring a model on resume; those reach PostModelSwitch only. The matcher compares the CANONICAL name of the target model, ignoring any `[1m]` suffix, so `claude-opus-5` covers every spelling of Opus 5.

nodes.label: PreModelSwitch cost input fields
nodes.rationale: Input adds `from_model`, `to_model`, `requested_model`, `source` (command/picker/sdk), and five cost fields: `context_tokens`, `prompt_cache_warm`, `cache_ttl`, `estimated_cache_write_usd`, and `pricing` (configured/catalog/default), so a hook can show what re-sending the conversation to the new model costs before the switch happens.

nodes.label: PreModelSwitch decision control
nodes.rationale: Exit 2 or top-level `decision: "block"` cancels the switch; for finer control, `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision` accepts `allow`, `deny`, and `ask` — but not `defer`, `updatedInput`, or `additionalContext` — with precedence deny > ask > allow. Only `/model` in an interactive session can show the `"ask"` prompt; everywhere else `"ask"` is treated as a refusal. A hook that does not respond before its 30-second timeout BLOCKS the switch, unlike PreToolUse.

nodes.label: PostModelSwitch event
nodes.rationale: PostModelSwitch (v2.1.251+) runs after the session's model changes, including changes Claude Code makes itself: an automatic fallback, `opusplan` entering or leaving plan mode, or restoring the model on resume. It does not run when a fallback-chain model serves a single turn without changing the session's model, and it cannot block. Its `source` adds `"auto"` and `"resume"` to the PreModelSwitch values.

nodes.label: PostModelSwitch context delivery
nodes.rationale: Claude Code takes the hook's plain-text stdout on exit 0, or `additionalContext` from JSON, and delivers it to Claude with the next request after the switch — the intended use is model-specific guidance without editing every CLAUDE.md. If the hook has not finished within five seconds after the next prompt is sent, that request goes without the output and it is attached to the following one; after several switches only the last target model's output is delivered.

nodes.label: SessionEnd event
nodes.rationale: SessionEnd runs when a session terminates, matching the exit `reason`: `clear`, `resume`, `logout`, `prompt_input_exit`, or `other` (`bypass_permissions_disabled` was removed in v2.1.234). It cannot block termination and its JSON output fields are discarded. Its default timeout is 1.5 seconds, raised automatically to the highest per-hook settings-file timeout up to 60 seconds, or overridden with `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSIONEND_HOOKS_TIMEOUT_MS`.

nodes.label: Elicitation event
nodes.rationale: Elicitation runs when an MCP server requests user input mid-task, matching the MCP server name and receiving `mcp_server_name`, `message`, and optional `mode` (`form` or `url`), `url`, `elicitation_id`, and `requested_schema`. A hook can answer programmatically and skip the dialog entirely by returning `hookSpecificOutput` with `action` (accept/decline/cancel) and `content`; exit code 2 denies it and the stderr is shown nowhere.

nodes.label: ElicitationResult event
nodes.rationale: ElicitationResult runs after a user responds to an MCP elicitation and before the response goes back to the server, so a hook can observe, modify, or block it. It receives `mcp_server_name`, `action`, and optional `mode`, `elicitation_id`, and `content`, and can override the user's answer with its own `action` and `content`. Exit code 2 blocks the response, changing the effective action to `decline`.

nodes.label: Which hook types each event supports
nodes.rationale: Thirteen events support all five handler types: PermissionDenied, PermissionRequest, PostToolBatch, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PreToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, TaskCompleted, TaskCreated, TeammateIdle, UserPromptExpansion, and UserPromptSubmit. Seventeen more support only `command`, `http`, and `mcp_tool`. SessionStart and Setup support `command` and `mcp_tool` alone — no `http`, `prompt`, or `agent`.

nodes.label: Prompt hook response schema
nodes.rationale: A prompt hook's model must return `{"ok": true|false, "reason": …, "impossible": true|false}`; `reason` is required when `ok` is false. `impossible` is returned with `ok: false` when the model judges the condition can never be satisfied — on Stop and SubagentStop Claude Code then lets the turn end instead of feeding the reason back, and agent hooks and every other event ignore it.

nodes.label: continueOnBlock
nodes.rationale: `continueOnBlock` (prompt hooks only, default false) decides what `ok: false` does on the events it applies to: on PreToolUse it returns the reason to Claude as the tool error so it can adjust and continue rather than ending the turn, and on PostToolUse and TeammateIdle it feeds the reason back instead of stopping. Some events ignore it entirely — PostToolUseFailure and TaskCreated always continue, while PostToolBatch, UserPromptSubmit and UserPromptExpansion always end the turn.

nodes.label: Events where a prompt hook's ok:false has no effect
nodes.rationale: On PermissionRequest, `ok: false` has no effect — denying requires a command hook returning `hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior: "deny"`. On PermissionDenied it also has no effect because the denial already happened, and the only output that event reads is `hookSpecificOutput.retry`, which prompt and agent hooks cannot set; they run there but their output is discarded.

nodes.label: How agent hooks execute
nodes.rationale: An agent hook spawns a subagent with the prompt and the hook's JSON input, lets it use Read, Grep, and Glob to investigate for up to 50 turns, then returns `{"ok": true/false}`. On `ok: false` Claude Code handles the block the way it handles a prompt hook with `continueOnBlock: true` on that event; agent hooks have no `continueOnBlock` field and do not support `impossible`. They earn their cost when verification needs actual files or test output.

nodes.label: Async hook limitations
nodes.rationale: Async hook output is delivered on the next conversation turn, so an idle session waits for the next user interaction — the exception being an `asyncRewake` hook exiting 2, which wakes Claude immediately. Each firing creates a separate background process with no deduplication, and under `-p` Claude Code kills any async hook still running at teardown and finalizes it `cancelled`. Malformed fields are dropped after schema validation rather than delivered.

nodes.label: Hooks run with your full user permissions
nodes.rationale: Command hooks execute shell commands with the user's full permissions and can modify, delete, or access any file that account can reach. Review and test every hook command before adding it to a configuration.

nodes.label: Workspace trust gates settings-file hooks
nodes.rationale: Claude Code checks workspace trust before running any hook from a settings file. In an interactive session it holds back hooks from EVERY settings file, including ~/.claude/settings.json, until the workspace trust dialog is accepted; in a `-p` or SDK session it never shows the dialog and treats the folder as trusted, so hooks committed in a repository's .claude/settings.json run in a folder you have never trusted.

nodes.label: Hook security best practices
nodes.rationale: Validate and sanitize inputs rather than trusting them; always quote shell variables as `"$VAR"`; block path traversal by checking for `..`; use absolute paths via `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`; and skip sensitive files such as `.env`, `.git/`, and keys.

nodes.label: Windows PowerShell hooks
nodes.rationale: Setting `"shell": "powershell"` runs one command hook in PowerShell; Claude Code auto-detects `pwsh.exe` and falls back to `powershell.exe`. As of v2.1.198 it rewrites the `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}`/`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`/`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` placeholders to PowerShell's `${env:NAME}` form everywhere. Never write the bare `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` spelling: PowerShell resolves it to `$null`, silently dropping the project-root prefix.

nodes.label: Debugging hooks
nodes.rationale: Hook execution details — which hooks matched, exit codes, and full stdout and stderr — go to the debug log: start with `claude --debug-file <path>`, or `claude --debug` and read `~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt`. The `--debug` flag does not print to the terminal. Set `CLAUDE_CODE_DEBUG_LOG_LEVEL=verbose` for matcher counts and query-matching lines.

nodes.label: Handler working-directory fallback
nodes.rationale: Handlers run in the current directory with Claude Code's environment. If that directory no longer exists — a worktree or temp directory another shell deleted mid-session — Claude Code runs command hooks from the first surviving option among the session's starting directory, the project root, the home directory, and the system temp directory, recording a warning naming the fallback in the debug log.

nodes.label: Claude Code authentication
nodes.rationale: Claude Code supports multiple authentication methods depending on the setup: individuals log in with a Claude.ai account, while teams use Claude for Teams or Enterprise, the Claude Console, or a cloud provider such as Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry.

nodes.label: First-launch browser login
nodes.rationale: Running `claude` on first launch opens a browser window to log in; pressing `c` copies the login URL when the browser does not open. If the browser shows a login code instead of redirecting back, it is pasted at the `Paste code here if prompted` prompt — common in WSL2, SSH sessions, and containers where the browser cannot reach Claude Code's local callback server.

nodes.label: Supported account types
nodes.rationale: You can authenticate with a Claude Pro or Max subscription, a Claude for Teams or Enterprise account, a Claude Console account, a cloud provider (Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry), or a self-hosted Claude apps gateway.

nodes.label: /logout resets setup state
nodes.rationale: Typing `/logout` at the Claude Code prompt logs out and re-authenticates. Logging out also resets first-launch setup state, so the next `claude` run walks through login and setup again.

nodes.label: Claude for Teams
nodes.rationale: Claude for Teams is the self-service plan with collaboration features, admin tools, and billing management, best for smaller teams. Members get both Claude Code and Claude on the web with centralized billing.

nodes.label: Claude for Enterprise
nodes.rationale: Claude for Enterprise adds SSO, domain capture, role-based permissions, a compliance API, and managed policy settings for organization-wide Claude Code configuration — aimed at larger organizations with security and compliance requirements.

nodes.label: Claude Console authentication
nodes.rationale: Organizations preferring API-based billing set access up through the Claude Console: create or reuse a Console account, add users by bulk invite or SSO, assign roles, and have each user accept the invite, install Claude Code, and log in with Console credentials.

nodes.label: Console roles: Claude Code vs Developer
nodes.rationale: When inviting Console users an admin assigns either the Claude Code role, whose users can only create Claude Code API keys, or the Developer role, whose users can create any kind of API key.

nodes.label: Sign in to Console without an API key
nodes.rationale: From Claude Code v2.1.242, choosing the Anthropic Console account at `/login` offers two routes: the recommended keyless sign-in keeps the OAuth token as an Anthropic profile and creates no API key, while the legacy route creates and stores a Console API key. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` must be unset first, `/logout` removes and revokes the credential written, and Claude Code refuses the sign-in if the target profile is a federation profile.

nodes.label: When keyless sign-in is not offered
nodes.rationale: Claude Code creates an API key without asking when running against a cloud provider or Claude Platform on AWS, when any settings file sets `forceLoginOrgUUID` or sets `forceLoginMethod` to `claudeai` or `console`, or when a managed settings source exists but cannot be read and no other managed source supplies a policy.

nodes.label: Anthropic profile credential
nodes.rationale: A profile is a named credential configuration file in the Anthropic configuration directory (`~/.config/anthropic` on macOS/Linux, `%APPDATA%\Anthropic` on Windows). Its auth mode is `oidc_federation` when configured for Workload Identity Federation, or `user_oauth` when written by `ant auth login` or by a keyless Console sign-in.

nodes.label: API key as a static credential
nodes.rationale: A profile stores an OAuth login while an API key is a static credential: Claude Code refreshes the profile's login automatically, and when refresh fails requests fail with `Anthropic profile login expired` until you sign in again.

nodes.label: Cloud provider authentication
nodes.rationale: Teams on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry follow the provider setup, distribute the required environment variables and credential instructions, and install Claude Code; selecting '3rd-party platform' at the login prompt launches an interactive setup wizard for Bedrock and Vertex AI, and no browser login is needed.

nodes.label: Claude apps gateway session
nodes.rationale: A self-hosted Claude apps gateway signs developers in with corporate SSO through `/login` and routes inference to the configured cloud provider; the gateway-issued token is the session's only credential. A signed-in gateway session is a provider selection that outranks Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, and suppresses the bearer token, API key, apiKeyHelper, and profile sources.

nodes.label: forceLoginMethod
nodes.rationale: `forceLoginMethod`, set in managed settings, directs which login method developers use — for example `"claudeai"` to steer them to claude.ai sign-in, or `"gateway"` to select gateway sign-in. On the terminal's interactive login screen Claude Code only pre-selects the method without enforcing it, so a developer can still complete a Console login there.

nodes.label: forceLoginOrgUUID
nodes.rationale: `forceLoginOrgUUID` requires developers' claude.ai logins to belong to a specific Anthropic organization: Claude Code errors and exits at startup when the claude.ai credential in use belongs to an unlisted organization. For Console logins it only pre-selects the organization on the sign-in page and never checks which organization the resulting Console credential belongs to.

nodes.label: Login paths and key enforcement
nodes.rationale: Developers log in via the terminal `/login` flow, the VS Code extension, the Agent SDK, `claude setup-token`, `/install-github-app`, and gateway sign-in. From v2.1.212 every path applies `forceLoginMethod` (before that, only terminal logins applied either key), but only terminal, VS Code, and Agent SDK logins verify `forceLoginOrgUUID`; `claude setup-token` and `/install-github-app` can mint a token in a different organization, and gateway sign-in is outside organization checks entirely.

nodes.label: Deploying the login keys in both managed sources
nodes.rationale: Deploy the login keys through device management tooling; server-managed settings reach only already-authenticated accounts and cannot redirect a first login. Managed-settings sources do not merge and cached server-managed settings replace the device-managed file, except the `env` block (merged per key from v2.1.223) and the cross-source lock keys — so `forceLoginMethod` and `forceLoginOrgUUID`, being neither, must be set in both places.

nodes.label: Environment credentials blocked at startup
nodes.rationale: When the login keys are set, a session credentialed by `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper` is blocked at startup because organization membership cannot be verified for an environment credential. Cloud provider sessions are not blocked (restrict those with cloud IAM policies), and profile or federation credentials are not blocked and are not organization-checked.

nodes.label: Credential management
nodes.rationale: Claude Code securely manages authentication credentials: where they are stored per platform, which authentication types are supported, custom credential scripts, refresh intervals, and failure behavior. `.credentials.json` is managed through `/login` and `/logout`; to route requests through a custom API endpoint set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` instead of editing it.

nodes.label: macOS Keychain storage and fallback
nodes.rationale: On macOS credentials live in the encrypted Keychain; when the Keychain rejects the write — for example when locked in an SSH session — Claude Code falls back to `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with mode `0600`, the same storage used on Linux. A Console login that creates an API key fails until the Keychain is writable.

nodes.label: Linux and Windows credential files
nodes.rationale: On Linux credentials are stored in `~/.claude/.credentials.json` with file mode `0600`. On Windows they are stored in `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json` and inherit the access controls of the user profile directory, which restricts the file to that user account by default.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocation
nodes.rationale: Setting `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` keeps `.credentials.json` (including the macOS fallback file) under that directory and keys the macOS Keychain entry to it, so a session with a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` reads a different credential entry.

nodes.label: Supported credential types
nodes.rationale: Supported authentication types are Claude.ai credentials, Claude API credentials, Microsoft Foundry Auth, Bedrock Auth, Vertex Auth, Anthropic profile and Workload Identity Federation credentials, and Claude apps gateway session tokens.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper script
nodes.rationale: The `apiKeyHelper` setting names a shell script that returns an API key, used for dynamic or rotating credentials such as short-lived tokens fetched from a vault.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper refresh interval
nodes.rationale: Claude Code re-runs `apiKeyHelper` after five minutes by default; `CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS` sets a custom refresh interval.

nodes.label: Slow helper notice
nodes.rationale: If `apiKeyHelper` takes longer than 10 seconds to return a key, Claude Code shows a warning notice in the prompt bar with the elapsed time, a signal that the credential script should be optimized.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper failure behavior
nodes.rationale: When the helper script errors, times out, or prints nothing, requests fail with `Your apiKeyHelper script is failing` within three attempts. Before v2.1.208 helper failures surfaced as a generic 401 after about ten silent retries.

nodes.label: Which surfaces read env credentials
nodes.rationale: `apiKeyHelper`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` apply to the CLI and the surfaces wrapping it — the VS Code extension, the Agent SDK, and GitHub Actions. Claude Desktop and cloud sessions neither call the helper nor read those variables: they use OAuth, except desktop sessions running a third-party inference configuration.

nodes.label: Expiring-login warning
nodes.rationale: Within three days of a `/login` credential expiring, Claude Code shows `Your login expires in 3 days · run /login to renew` at startup (v2.1.203+; the window was five days before v2.1.217). The warning is informational, never blocks a request, and appears only when a claude.ai or Claude Console login is the active credential — not for cloud providers, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, or `apiKeyHelper`.

nodes.label: Login expired failure and /status row
nodes.rationale: Once a stored login expires and cannot be refreshed, every model request fails with `Login expired · Please run /login` until you sign in again (before v2.1.206 this was reported as a model error). `/status` shows a `Login` row reading `Expired — log in again` with the saved organization and email, requiring v2.1.210 or later.

nodes.label: Unattended sessions stall on expiry
nodes.rationale: Renewing early matters most for unattended work: a background session in agent view or a Remote Control session that outlives its login stops making progress once the credential expires and cannot recover until you sign in again.

nodes.label: Authentication precedence order
nodes.rationale: With multiple credentials present Claude Code chooses in this order: cloud provider credentials, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `apiKeyHelper` output, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, Anthropic profile and federation credentials, then subscription OAuth credentials from `/login`.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is sent as the `Authorization: Bearer` header and is used when routing through an LLM gateway or proxy that authenticates with bearer tokens rather than Anthropic API keys. It ranks second in the precedence order.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
nodes.rationale: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is sent as the `X-Api-Key` header for direct Anthropic API access. In interactive mode you approve or decline the key once and the choice is remembered, changeable via the 'Use custom API key' toggle in `/config` (visible only while the variable is set); in non-interactive `-p` mode the key is always used when present.

nodes.label: API key overrides an active subscription
nodes.rationale: With an active subscription and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set, the API key takes precedence once approved, which causes authentication failures if the key belongs to a disabled or expired organization. `unset ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` falls back to the subscription, and `/status` confirms the active method via the `Login method` and `API key` rows.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` holds a long-lived OAuth token for CI pipelines and scripts where browser login is unavailable. Running `/login` while it is set switches the current session to the new login, but every new session reads the variable again until it is removed from the shell profile or a settings file's `env` block.

nodes.label: claude setup-token
nodes.rationale: `claude setup-token` generates a one-year OAuth token through the same browser authorization flow as `/login`, prints it to the terminal, and saves it nowhere — you copy it into `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. The token can only make model requests, so it cannot establish Remote Control sessions or fetch claude.ai connectors, though locally configured MCP servers still work.

nodes.label: Bare mode credential limits
nodes.rationale: Bare mode does not read `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, and Claude Code reads no profiles or federation variables in bare mode, Claude Desktop, or cloud sessions (where `/status` shows no `Profile` row). Scripts passing `--bare` must authenticate with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or an `apiKeyHelper`.

nodes.label: Profile source selection order
nodes.rationale: Claude Code checks three profile sources in order and stops at the first set: a named profile from `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE` (ranks above `/login` in either auth mode), the federation variables `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID` plus `ANTHROPIC_ORGANIZATION_ID` (above `/login`), and the active profile from `active_config` or one named `default` — above `/login` when `oidc_federation`, below a working `/login` credential when `user_oauth`.

nodes.label: Workload Identity Federation
nodes.rationale: Workload Identity Federation gives a profile the `oidc_federation` auth mode; when exchanging an identity token Claude Code also reads the other WIF environment variables, such as `ANTHROPIC_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE`.

nodes.label: The user_oauth ranking rule
nodes.rationale: Ranking a `user_oauth` active profile below a working `/login` credential keeps a leftover `ant auth login` profile from moving requests off the account you signed in to with `/login`.

nodes.label: Diagnosing which profile source was chosen
nodes.rationale: `/status` names the chosen source in a `Profile` row that replaces the `Login method` row; starting with `--debug` also writes a `Using Anthropic profile auth` line with the source name to `~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt`, plus a warning when a `user_oauth` active profile is passed over in favor of a working claude.ai login.

nodes.label: Features needing a claude.ai login
nodes.rationale: Features that need a claude.ai login — claude.ai connectors and `/schedule` — are unavailable while a profile or federation source is selected. To stop selection, unset `ANTHROPIC_PROFILE` or either federation variable, or for an active profile run `/logout`, `ant auth logout`, or delete the profile file from `configs/`.

nodes.label: Subscription OAuth credentials from /login
nodes.rationale: Subscription OAuth credentials written by `/login` sit last in the precedence order and are the default for Claude Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users.

nodes.label: Claude Code on the Web credentials
nodes.rationale: Claude Code on the Web always uses your subscription credentials: setting `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` in the sandbox environment does not override them.

nodes.label: Interactive mode reference
nodes.rationale: The page is the complete reference for keyboard shortcuts, input modes, and interactive features in Claude Code sessions. It covers shortcuts, vim mode, command history, background bash, message queueing, prompt suggestions, emoji shortcodes, spell checking, /btw side questions, the task list, session recap, usage-limit waiting, and PR/MR status badges.

nodes.label: Keyboard shortcuts
nodes.rationale: Keyboard shortcuts may vary by platform and terminal. In fullscreen rendering, pressing `?` in the transcript viewer lists the shortcuts available there. The shortcut tables are grouped into general controls, text editing, theme and display, multiline input, quick commands, transcript viewer, and voice input.

nodes.label: Option as Meta on macOS
nodes.rationale: On macOS, the Option/Alt shortcuts `Alt+B`, `Alt+F`, `Alt+D`, `Alt+Y` and `Alt+P` require configuring Option as Meta in the terminal emulator. Option+T (toggle extended thinking) is the exception: it works on macOS without that configuration.

nodes.label: Ctrl+C interrupt or clear input
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+C` interrupts a running operation. If nothing is running, the first press clears the prompt input and a second press exits Claude Code.

nodes.label: Ctrl+X Ctrl+K stop background subagents
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+X Ctrl+K` stops all running background subagents in the session and turns off artifact auto-replies for the rest of it. It must be pressed twice within 3 seconds to confirm.

nodes.label: Ctrl+D exit session
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+D` exits the Claude Code session: the first press shows a confirmation hint and a second press within 800ms exits. When the prompt already contains text, `Ctrl+D` deletes the character after the cursor instead.

nodes.label: Open prompt in external editor
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+G`, or the readline-native binding `Ctrl+X Ctrl+E`, opens the prompt or a custom response in the default text editor. Turning on 'Show last response in external editor' in `/config` prepends Claude's previous reply as `#`-commented context, which Claude Code strips when the file is saved.

nodes.label: Ctrl+L redraw screen
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+L` forces a full terminal redraw while keeping input and conversation history, and is the recovery path when the display becomes garbled or partially blank.

nodes.label: Ctrl+O toggle transcript viewer
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+O` toggles the transcript viewer, which shows detailed tool usage and execution with a timestamp and the model used on each assistant message, and expands lines that collapse by default such as MCP calls and messages from other sessions.

nodes.label: Ctrl+R reverse history search key
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+R` activates interactive reverse search through previous commands. In vim NORMAL mode, `/` opens the same reverse history search.

nodes.label: Paste image from clipboard
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+V`, `Cmd+V` in iTerm2, or `Alt+V` on Windows and WSL pastes an image from the clipboard, inserting an `[Image #N]` chip at the cursor so it can be referenced positionally in the prompt. On WSL both `Ctrl+V` and `Alt+V` are bound.

nodes.label: Ctrl+B background running tasks
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+B` moves running Bash commands and agents to the background. Tmux users must press it twice because of tmux's prefix key.

nodes.label: Ctrl+T toggle task checklist
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+T` shows or hides Claude's to-do checklist in the status area, displaying up to five tasks at a time. It is not the background-task view; `/tasks` shows running shells and subagents.

nodes.label: Ctrl+S stash or restore prompt
nodes.rationale: With text in the input, `Ctrl+S` stashes it and clears the prompt; pressed again on an empty prompt it restores the stashed text, cursor position, and pasted content.

nodes.label: Ctrl+Z suspend Claude Code
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+Z` is Unix only and suspends the Claude Code process to the shell; `fg` resumes it.

nodes.label: Tab accept suggestion or comment on permission
nodes.rationale: While autocomplete suggestions are showing, `Tab` accepts the selected suggestion. On most permission prompts, with Yes or No focused, `Tab` opens a comment field on that option and pressing it again closes the field.

nodes.label: Arrow keys move cursor or navigate history
nodes.rationale: `Up`/`Down` or `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+N` first move the cursor when the input spans more than one visual row; once the cursor is on the first or last visual row, pressing again navigates command history. While messages are queued, `Up` from the first row takes them back instead.

nodes.label: Esc interrupt Claude or close dialog
nodes.rationale: `Esc` stops the current response or tool call mid-turn while keeping the work done so far, closes an open dialog, and on a permission prompt declines the action the same as No without a comment. If messages are queued, Claude Code sends them next.

nodes.label: Double Esc clear draft or rewind
nodes.rationale: When the prompt contains text, double `Esc` clears it and saves the draft to history so `Up` recalls it. When the input is empty, double `Esc` opens the rewind menu to restore or summarize code and conversation from a previous point.

nodes.label: Shift+Tab cycle permission modes
nodes.rationale: `Shift+Tab`, or `Alt+M` on Windows when the Node or Bun runtime does not enable VT input mode, cycles through `default` (labeled Manual), `acceptEdits`, `plan`, and where available `bypassPermissions` and then `auto`; from `auto` the first press returns to `default`. On a file permission prompt the same key closes an open comment field or selects the session-wide allow option.

nodes.label: Option+P switch model
nodes.rationale: `Option+P` on macOS or `Alt+P` on Windows/Linux switches models without clearing the prompt.

nodes.label: Option+T toggle extended thinking
nodes.rationale: `Option+T` (macOS) or `Alt+T` (Windows/Linux) enables or disables extended thinking mode. It has no effect on Fable 5.1 or Fable 5, which always use extended thinking, and it works on macOS without configuring Option as Meta.

nodes.label: Option+O toggle fast mode
nodes.rationale: `Option+O` (macOS) or `Alt+O` (Windows/Linux) enables or disables fast mode.

nodes.label: Text editing shortcuts
nodes.rationale: The prompt input supports emacs-style editing keys: `Ctrl+A`/`Ctrl+E` for line start and end, `Ctrl+K` delete to end of line, `Ctrl+U` delete to line start, `Ctrl+W` delete previous word, `Alt+B`/`Alt+F` word navigation, `Alt+D` delete next word, and `Ctrl+_` or `Ctrl+Shift+-` to undo the last input edit.

nodes.label: Paste deleted text and cycle paste history
nodes.rationale: `Ctrl+K`, `Ctrl+U` and `Ctrl+W` store the deleted text; `Ctrl+Y` pastes it back, and under `keybindingFlavor: "readline"` text deleted by `Alt+D` too. `Alt+Y` after `Ctrl+Y` cycles through previously deleted text.

nodes.label: keybindingFlavor readline setting
nodes.rationale: Setting `keybindingFlavor` to `"readline"` in `~/.claude/settings.json` makes the prompt's editing keys follow GNU readline conventions: `Ctrl+W` deletes back to the previous whitespace and a word is a run of letters and digits, so punctuation separates words. The default is `"classic"`; the setting requires v2.1.238 or later, and before v2.1.239 it applied only to `Ctrl+W`.

nodes.label: keybindings.json is a separate mechanism
nodes.rationale: The `keybindingFlavor` setting is separate from the keybindings configuration file: the word-editing commands are not actions in `keybindings.json`, so they cannot be remapped there. Transcript-viewer keys such as `transcript:toggleShowAll` and `transcript:exit` can be rebound in that file.

nodes.label: Toggle syntax highlighting in /theme
nodes.rationale: Inside the `/theme` picker menu only, `Ctrl+T` toggles syntax highlighting for code blocks, controlling whether code in Claude's responses uses syntax coloring.

nodes.label: Multiline input methods
nodes.rationale: Multiline prompts can be entered with `\` + `Enter` (works in all terminals), `Option+Enter` after enabling Option as Meta on macOS, `Shift+Enter` natively in iTerm2, WezTerm, Ghostty, Kitty, Warp, Apple Terminal and Windows Terminal, `Ctrl+J` in any terminal without configuration, or by pasting directly for code blocks and logs.

nodes.label: Quick command prefixes
nodes.rationale: Leading characters change how input is interpreted: `/` opens a command or skill, `!` enters shell mode, `@` triggers file path autocomplete (and, with cross-session messaging, suggests other live sessions after at least one letter), `:` inserts an emoji shortcode, and `?` on an empty input toggles the shortcut help panel.

nodes.label: Transcript viewer
nodes.rationale: Inside the transcript viewer, `?` toggles the shortcut help panel, `{`/`}` jump between user prompts like vim paragraph motion, `Ctrl+E` toggles show-all in the classic renderer only, `[` writes the conversation to native scrollback so `Cmd+F` and tmux copy mode can search it, `v` opens it in `$VISUAL`/`$EDITOR`, and `q`, `Ctrl+C` or `Esc` exit. Several of these require fullscreen rendering; `/tui` with no argument reports the active renderer.

nodes.label: Voice dictation input
nodes.rationale: Holding or tapping `Space` starts voice dictation when the voice dictation feature is enabled. Hold to record, or run `/voice tap` for tap-to-toggle; the dictation key is rebindable.

nodes.label: Slash command menu
nodes.rationale: Typing `/` lists built-in commands, bundled and user-authored skills, and commands contributed by plugins and MCP servers; typing letters after it filters. Some built-in commands are not visible to every user because they depend on platform or plan, and a few are hidden from the menu by design and run only when typed in full. In fullscreen rendering the `/` and `@` suggestion lists respond to the mouse.

nodes.label: Vim editor mode
nodes.rationale: Vim-style editing is enabled via `/config` → Editor mode (or `"editorMode": "vim"` in settings). Claude Code preserves the vim mode and cursor position when the transcript viewer is toggled with `Ctrl+O` or a panel such as `/config` is opened and closed.

nodes.label: Vim mode switching commands
nodes.rationale: `Esc` or `Ctrl+[` enters NORMAL mode from INSERT or VISUAL (in Kitty-keyboard-protocol terminals `Ctrl+[` requires v2.1.242 or later); from NORMAL mode `i`, `I`, `a`, `A`, `o` and `O` enter INSERT at various positions, and `v`/`V` start character-wise or line-wise visual selection.

nodes.label: vimInsertModeRemaps
nodes.rationale: `vimInsertModeRemaps` maps a two-printable-character INSERT-mode sequence to Escape, such as `{"jj": "<Esc>"}`; `"<Esc>"` is the only supported target and other lengths or targets are ignored. The second character must follow within one second, otherwise both characters stay as literal text. Claude Code reads it only from user settings, `--settings`, and managed settings, so a checked-out repository cannot remap keystrokes.

nodes.label: Vim NORMAL-mode navigation
nodes.rationale: NORMAL mode supports `h/j/k/l`, `Space`, `w`/`e`/`b`, `0`, `$`, `^`, `gg`, `G`, the `f`/`F`/`t`/`T` character jumps with `;` and `,` to repeat, and `/` to open reverse history search. When the cursor cannot move further, `j`/`k` and the arrows navigate command history instead, and `←` on an empty prompt opens agent view.

nodes.label: Vim NORMAL-mode editing
nodes.rationale: NORMAL mode supports the delete, change and yank operators (`x`, `dd`, `D`, `dw/de/db`, `df{char}`/`dt{char}`, `cc`, `C`, `cw/ce/cb`, `yy/Y`, `yw/ye/yb`), paste with `p`/`P`, indent `>>`/`<<`, join `J`, undo `u`, and repeat `.`. `s` and `S` substitute a character or a line and require Claude Code v2.1.211 or later.

nodes.label: Vim text objects
nodes.rationale: Text objects work with operators like `d`, `c` and `y`: `iw`/`aw` for a word, `iW`/`aW` for a whitespace-delimited WORD, and inner/around variants for double quotes, single quotes, parentheses, brackets and braces.

nodes.label: Vim visual mode
nodes.rationale: `v` starts character-wise and `V` line-wise selection; motions extend the selection and operators act on it directly. Visual mode supports delete `d`/`x`, yank `y`, change `c`/`s`, replace with register `p`, `r{char}`, case toggling `~`/`u`/`U`, indent `>`/`<`, join `J`, swap cursor and anchor `o`, text-object selection, and `v`/`V` to toggle or exit.

nodes.label: Block-wise visual mode unsupported
nodes.rationale: Block-wise visual mode with `Ctrl+V` is not supported in Claude Code's vim implementation.

nodes.label: Command history
nodes.rationale: Input history is stored per working directory and Up-arrow recall reaches prompts from past sessions of the same project. `/clear` starts a new session whose prompts list first; repeating a prompt records one entry; recalling a prompt with pasted text resends the full pasted content; and `!` history expansion is disabled by default.

nodes.label: Reverse search behavior
nodes.rationale: The classic renderer's inline search always searches prompts from all projects, newest first with duplicates collapsed: `Ctrl+R` cycles older matches, `Tab`/`Esc` accepts, `Enter` accepts and executes, and `Ctrl+C` or Backspace on an empty search cancels. In fullscreen rendering `Ctrl+R` opens a dialog where `Ctrl+S` cycles scope through this session, this project, and all projects, and results fill in as history loads.

nodes.label: Background Bash commands
nodes.rationale: A backgrounded command runs asynchronously and immediately returns a background task ID, so Claude Code can respond to new prompts while it executes. Output is written to a file that Claude can retrieve with the Read tool. Commands are backgrounded either by prompting Claude or by pressing `Ctrl+B`; common cases are build tools, package managers, test runners, dev servers, and long-running processes such as docker or terraform.

nodes.label: Background task lifecycle and reaping
nodes.rationale: Background tasks are cleaned up when Claude Code exits, or handed to the background session if the session is backgrounded, and are terminated when output exceeds 5GB. On macOS and Linux they are terminated on OS memory pressure after 30 minutes idle with no turn or subagent running, disabled by `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_SHELL_PRESSURE_REAP=1` (v2.1.193+); subagent-owned commands are instead terminated after 60 minutes, configurable with `CLAUDE_SUBAGENT_BG_SHELL_MAX_MS`.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS
nodes.rationale: Setting the `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS` environment variable to `1` disables all background task functionality.

nodes.label: Shell mode with the ! prefix
nodes.rationale: Prefixing input with `!` runs a shell command directly without Claude interpreting or approving it, adds the command and its output to conversation context, shows real-time output, and supports `Ctrl+B` backgrounding, history-based `Tab` autocomplete, and live file path autocomplete triggered by `/` (v2.1.193+). Exit with `Escape`, `Backspace`, or `Ctrl+U` on an empty prompt; pasting text starting with `!` enters shell mode automatically.

nodes.label: respondToBashCommands setting
nodes.rationale: Claude responds automatically to shell-mode command output once it lands in the transcript, at the same cost as sending a normal prompt. Setting `respondToBashCommands` to `false` in `settings.json` restores the pre-v2.1.186 behavior where output is added to context without a response.

nodes.label: Queue messages while Claude works
nodes.rationale: Typing a message and pressing `Enter` while Claude is working queues it instead of interrupting the turn, and the queued entries are listed above the input box until they are sent. Shell `!` commands and most slash commands can be queued the same way.

nodes.label: When queued entries are sent
nodes.rationale: A queued message is passed to Claude as soon as the running tool calls finish, within the same turn; if the turn ends with messages still queued, only the oldest is sent as the next turn and the rest follow the same rule. Queued commands and shell commands are held until the turn ends and then run one at a time.

nodes.label: Commands that run immediately instead of queueing
nodes.rationale: Some commands, among them `/model`, `/effort` and `/fast`, run as soon as they are sent rather than being queued. `/model` and `/effort` apply to the next request in the current turn once any cache warning is confirmed, while `/fast` keeps the fast-mode setting the turn started with and applies from the next turn.

nodes.label: Take back what you queued
nodes.rationale: Pressing `Up` from the first line of the input box removes queued messages and commands from the queue and places them in the input box, one per line, ahead of any typed text. Queued shell commands are taken back only when the input box is empty and nothing else is queued, and Claude Code then switches the input box to shell mode.

nodes.label: Prompt suggestions
nodes.rationale: A new session shows a grayed-out example command picked from the project's git history, and after Claude responds Claude Code can suggest the next prompt from conversation history. `Tab` or `Right arrow` places the suggestion in the input and `Enter` submits it; typing dismisses it. Each suggestion is generated by a background request that reuses the conversation's prompt cache, so the added cost is minimal.

nodes.label: When prompt suggestions are skipped
nodes.rationale: Suggestions are off by default in sessions that do not fetch feature flags and in a first session after install or upgrade, and individual suggestions are skipped when the prompt cache is cold, sometimes after the first turn, after an error, in plan mode, near the usage limit (overridable with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=true`), and in agent-team teammates' sessions. In print mode none are generated unless `--prompt-suggestions` is passed with `-p` and stream-json output.

nodes.label: Turn prompt suggestions off
nodes.rationale: Prompt suggestions can be disabled by turning off Prompt suggestions in `/config`, setting `promptSuggestionEnabled` to `false`, or exporting `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_PROMPT_SUGGESTION=false`, which takes precedence over the setting. Organizations set `promptSuggestionEnabled` to `false` in managed settings and must also set the env var under the managed `env` key so users cannot re-enable it.

nodes.label: Emoji shortcodes
nodes.rationale: Typing a complete `:shortcode:` replaces it with the emoji on the closing `:`, and typing `:` plus at least two characters opens a suggestion popup accepted with `Tab` or `Enter`. The shortcode must start the input or follow a space. Requires v2.1.217 or later, and `emojiCompletionEnabled: false` disables both the popup and the inline replacement.

nodes.label: Spell checking in the prompt input
nodes.rationale: Claude Code can underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, checking only the input box and never Claude's replies or your files. It is off by default, requires v2.1.235 or later, checks nothing in screen reader mode, and checks nothing while the input is in shell mode, `Ctrl+R` history search, or voice dictation.

nodes.label: Spell checker prerequisites
nodes.rationale: Spell checking requires aspell, hunspell, or ispell installed and on `PATH`; Claude Code runs the first of the three it finds, in that order, on every platform including a `.cmd` shim on Windows. `aspell --version`, `hunspell --version`, or `ispell -v` confirms availability.

nodes.label: spellcheck setting sources and precedence
nodes.rationale: The `spellcheck` setting is read from user settings, a `--settings` file, or managed settings, and is ignored in a project's `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json`. When more than one source defines it, Claude Code uses exactly one — managed settings, then `--settings`, then user settings — and never combines fields. Its fields are `enabled`, `checker`, `language`, and `color`.

nodes.label: What spell checking skips
nodes.rationale: Claude Code underlines unknown words shortly after typing pauses, leaves the word being typed alone, and never changes the text. It skips code-like text — commands, `@` mentions, URLs, file paths, flags, words with digits, underscores or a non-initial capital, and backticked text — plus Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Lao, Khmer and Myanmar text. Claude Code has no word list of its own; a word is misspelled when the checker says so, and new words are added to the checker's personal dictionary.

nodes.label: When spell checking underlines nothing
nodes.rationale: Nothing is underlined when no checker is installed or the named `checker` is missing, when the checker fails twice in a row (Claude Code restarts it once, then stops until restart), or when it takes over 15 seconds to answer three times. `claude --debug` plus the `[spellcheck]` lines in `~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt` name the program started and why checking stopped, including a missing-dictionary error for the `language` value.

nodes.label: Side questions with /btw
nodes.rationale: `/btw` asks a question about the current work without adding to conversation history: Claude answers from the messages, replies and tool results already in the session, the exchange appears in a dismissible overlay, and Claude Code replays the newest 20 earlier side questions with each ask. It can be run while Claude is working without interrupting the turn, and costs little while the prompt cache is warm. In the VS Code extension (v2.1.227+) it opens a panel whose thread survives window reloads.

nodes.label: /btw has no tool access
nodes.rationale: Side questions answer only from what is already in context: Claude cannot read files, run commands, or search when answering one, and there are no follow-up turns in the overlay. Use `/btw` to ask about what Claude already knows from the session and a subagent to go find out something new.

nodes.label: Fork a /btw answer into a subagent
nodes.rationale: Pressing `f` on a side-question answer starts a forked background subagent that inherits the parent conversation plus this question and answer, so it can continue with full tool access while you stay in the current session. It is available in local sessions only.

nodes.label: /btw overlay keys
nodes.rationale: In the answer overlay, `Space`/`Enter`/`Escape` dismiss, `Up`/`Down` scroll, `Left`/`Right` step between this and earlier answers (v2.1.187+), `c` copies the answer as raw Markdown rather than the hard-wrapped rendering, `f` forks to a subagent, and `x` clears the list of earlier exchanges. Running `/btw` with no question reopens the overlay on the most recent exchange.

nodes.label: Task list
nodes.rationale: The task list is Claude's to-do checklist for multi-step work, with pending, in-progress and complete indicators. It shows up to five tasks, restores its expanded state on `--resume`/`--continue` when tasks remain, persists across context compactions, and can be shared across sessions by setting `CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID` to a named directory in `~/.claude/tasks/`.

nodes.label: Task list availability by model
nodes.rationale: On Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5 and later versions of those families, Claude tracks multi-step work without a written checklist and Claude Code does not provide the tools that fill the list, so it stays empty. Opting in with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` restores it; on earlier models such as Opus 4.7 it works by default.

nodes.label: Session recap
nodes.rationale: Claude Code shows a one-line recap of the session when you return to an unfocused terminal, generated in the background once at least three minutes have passed since the last completed turn, only after three turns and never twice in a row. `/recap` generates one on demand; both forms are capped at 400 characters. It is on by default for every plan and provider, can be turned off in `/config`, and is always skipped in non-interactive mode.

nodes.label: Wait for a usage limit to reset
nodes.rationale: When a claude.ai usage limit stops Claude mid-task, Claude Code waits in the open session and continues the task on its own after the reset, sending a fixed continuation prompt rather than resending the last message. Automatic continue is on by default in interactive sessions signed in with a claude.ai subscription and requires v2.1.234 or later; after repeated limit hits it re-arms at most twice, then stops.

nodes.label: Cancel the usage-limit wait
nodes.rationale: `Esc` at an empty prompt, `Ctrl+C`, or `/rate-limit-options` → Don't continue automatically cancels the wait, and Claude Code confirms with a line starting 'Automatic continue cancelled'. The wait also ends without continuing when you send a prompt, exit, hand the conversation elsewhere (`/login`, clear, rewind, `/resume`, `/teleport`, `/tui`, desktop, background or cloud), when the setting turns off or the reset moves past 24 hours, or when a `UserPromptSubmit` hook blocks the continuation.

nodes.label: Start a usage-limit wait yourself
nodes.rationale: Claude Code does not start the wait on its own in Remote Control and agent-team teammate sessions, when a reset is more than 24 hours away, or on an Opus/Sonnet limit while running a model outside that family. In those cases it opens the usage-limit options menu once per reset window, and the row starting 'Wait here, then continue automatically' starts the wait; teammates run `/rate-limit-options` themselves.

nodes.label: Where the usage-limit wait is not offered
nodes.rationale: The wait is not offered at all in background sessions and `-p` runs, with API keys, cloud providers and usage-based billing (metered per request, so there is no reset to wait for), or through an LLM gateway without a saved claude.ai login.

nodes.label: autoContinueAtUsageLimit setting
nodes.rationale: Automatic continue is turned off in `/config` under 'Continue automatically at usage limit' or by setting `autoContinueAtUsageLimit` to `false` in user settings. `/config autoContinueAtUsageLimit=false` also works, including with `-p`, but that `key=value` form cannot turn it back on because the setting grants unattended execution.

nodes.label: PR review status badge
nodes.rationale: On a branch with an open pull request, Claude Code shows a clickable link such as 'PR #446' in the footer, underlined green for approved, yellow for pending review, red for changes requested, and gray for draft; it disappears once the PR merges or closes. Refresh is about every 90 seconds on the Anthropic API with feature-flag fetching on and every 60 seconds otherwise, plus immediately after a successful `git push` or a `gh pr` command, stopping after an hour without input.

nodes.label: gh CLI requirement for PR status
nodes.rationale: PR status for GitHub repositories requires the `gh` CLI to be installed and authenticated with `gh auth login`.

nodes.label: GitLab merge request badge
nodes.rationale: On a branch with an open GitLab merge request, Claude Code shows a clickable `MR !N` badge in the footer slot that otherwise holds the GitHub PR link, underlined green when GitLab reports it mergeable, yellow for any other open state, and gray for draft. It uses the same refresh schedule as the GitHub badge and refreshes after a successful `glab mr create` or `git push`.

nodes.label: glab CLI requirement for MR status
nodes.rationale: The MR badge needs Claude Code v2.1.234 or later, a remote pointing at gitlab.com or a self-managed GitLab host, and the `glab` CLI on `PATH` authenticated with `glab auth login`. Claude Code ignores `glab` token environment variables such as `GITLAB_TOKEN`, and looks for `glab` and its login once per session, so it must be restarted after installing or authenticating.

nodes.label: LLM gateway
nodes.rationale: An LLM gateway is a proxy an organization runs between Claude Code and the model provider. When an organization uses one, Claude Code authenticates to the gateway with a credential the organization issues instead of the developer's personal claude.ai login.

nodes.label: Gateway credential
nodes.rationale: The credential a gateway team issues: a key or token string, or a command that fetches one. It is supplied to Claude Code through ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or an apiKeyHelper, and it replaces the personal claude.ai login for gateway traffic.

nodes.label: Check for an existing configuration
nodes.rationale: Administrators can distribute the gateway address and credential through managed settings, device management, or an apiKeyHelper, so Claude Code picks them up at startup. The check is: start `claude` (a login screen means nothing was distributed), inspect /status, then send a test message.

nodes.label: Configure Claude Code yourself
nodes.rationale: The second path when no administrator configured the gateway: obtain the gateway's base URL and a credential from the gateway team, set the credential variable and base URL, verify the connection, configure each surface, and add any additional variables the gateway needs.

nodes.label: /status Status tab
nodes.rationale: `/status` opens on the Status tab, where an `Anthropic base URL` line appears only when a gateway address is set, and an `Auth token` or `API key` line naming ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper confirms a gateway credential is active. A `Login method` line naming a claude.ai account means no gateway credential was distributed.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
nodes.rationale: The environment variable that points Claude Code at the gateway's base URL, for example https://llm-gateway.example.com. It is one of the two variables every gateway connection needs, and its presence is what makes the `Anthropic base URL` line appear in /status.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN
nodes.rationale: The credential variable to use when the gateway team says 'bearer token' or 'Authorization header'; it is also the default to try when they did not say which kind. It sends the credential in `Authorization: Bearer` and takes precedence over a saved login immediately, with no approval prompt.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
nodes.rationale: The credential variable to use when the gateway team says 'API key' or 'x-api-key'; the value is sent in the `x-api-key` header. In interactive mode you are prompted once to approve the key before it takes over from a saved login.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper
nodes.rationale: A settings-file entry naming a shell command Claude Code runs to fetch the current gateway credential from stdout, for credentials that rotate or come from a vault or SSO. Its value is sent in both `Authorization` and `x-api-key`, and on v2.1.227+ any banner or log line printed alongside the key makes the helper fail.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper cache lifetime
nodes.rationale: Claude Code caches the helper's output for five minutes by default and re-runs the helper once the cache lifetime elapses. CLAUDE_CODE_API_KEY_HELPER_TTL_MS changes the lifetime in milliseconds, e.g. 900000 for 15 minutes.

nodes.label: Credential variable to header mapping
nodes.rationale: Each credential variable sends the value in a different HTTP header: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN in `Authorization: Bearer`, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in `x-api-key`, and apiKeyHelper in both. A credential in the wrong variable arrives in a header the gateway does not read and the request fails with 401.

nodes.label: Shell environment variables
nodes.rationale: Exporting ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and the credential variable applies only to that terminal session and programs started from it; an editor launched from the dock or Start menu will not see them, and shell-only exports do not reliably reach supervisor-hosted background agents. Adding the lines to ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc or the PowerShell $PROFILE makes them persist across terminals.

nodes.label: Settings file env block
nodes.rationale: Setting ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and the credential in a settings file's `env` block makes the configuration apply everywhere Claude Code runs, including background agents. When both a shell export and a settings-file env block set the same variable, the settings-file value applies.

nodes.label: Settings file scopes and credential safety
nodes.rationale: ~/.claude/settings.json applies to all projects (%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json on Windows); .claude/settings.local.json applies to one project and is gitignored when Claude Code writes it. The credential must never go in a project's committed .claude/settings.json, which is shared with everyone who clones the repository.

nodes.label: Verification request
nodes.rationale: A one-token POST to $ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL/v1/messages (curl or Invoke-RestMethod) sent before opening Claude Code, so a failure points at the gateway rather than at Claude Code's configuration. It reads the shell variables, so shell exports are required even when the values also live in a settings file.

nodes.label: Reading the verification response
nodes.rationale: A JSON response starting with {"id":"msg_ and carrying a "content":[...] field means the gateway is reachable and the credential works.
