An error naming an unknown model still proves URL and credential, because the gateway authenticated before rejecting the model; a 401 means the credential was rejected and the other variable should be tried.

nodes.label: Conflicts with an existing login
nodes.rationale: A gateway credential variable takes precedence over a saved claude.ai login or Console key; the saved login stays unused while the variable is set and returns when it is unset. `/logout` clears the saved login so only the gateway credential remains, and `/status` shows which credential source is active.

nodes.label: VS Code extension configuration
nodes.rationale: Gateway variables for the VS Code extension go in `claudeCode.environmentVariables` in VS Code's own user settings JSON. The extension checks credentials from that setting before launching, so values in ~/.claude/settings.json reach the spawned process but not the extension's own login check.

nodes.label: Desktop app third-party inference configuration
nodes.rationale: The desktop app reads gateway routing from its third-party inference configuration, not from ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL or settings.json; the configuration is either administrator-distributed (which makes the in-app form read-only) or entered via Developer mode. With it active the app runs sessions locally only — no SSH or Anthropic-hosted environments, and Remote Control is unavailable.

nodes.label: GitHub Actions gateway configuration
nodes.rationale: Claude Code GitHub Actions reads ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS from the workflow env block and takes the credential as the action's `anthropic_api_key` input, which it exposes as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the x-api-key header. For a bearer-token gateway the same secret is passed twice — as the input, only to satisfy the action's launch check, and as ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN in env, which is what fills the Authorization header.

nodes.label: Agent SDK env option
nodes.rationale: The Agent SDK has no gateway-specific options; it passes environment variables to the Claude Code process it spawns. In TypeScript, setting options.env replaces the environment entirely, so process.env must be spread in; in Python, ClaudeAgentOptions(env=...) merges on top of the inherited environment.

nodes.label: Slack and web are outside the gateway
nodes.rationale: Claude Code in Slack and Claude Code on the web are Anthropic-hosted products that always use Anthropic's API and are not part of a gateway deployment; gateway variables set in a cloud session's environment configuration are not applied. Organizations whose traffic must stay on the gateway should not enable these surfaces for those users.

nodes.label: Remote Control and voice dictation unavailability
nodes.rationale: Remote Control and voice dictation both rely on a claude.ai identity and are unavailable while ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or an apiKeyHelper is active; Remote Control is additionally disabled while ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a non-Anthropic host (behaviour introduced in v2.1.196). Restoring them means logging in with claude.ai and unsetting the credential, plus the base URL for Remote Control; `claude doctor` names what is blocking it.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS
nodes.rationale: Some gateways route or tag requests with a custom header such as a tenant identifier or routing key; ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS carries one `Name: Value` pair per line, using \n between pairs inside a settings-file env block. Routing and tenant header names count as headers that need approval, and project-settings values follow Claude Code's rules for when it applies env values.

nodes.label: Gateway model discovery
nodes.rationale: With CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1, Claude Code queries the gateway for its model list at startup and adds those names to the /model picker labelled `From gateway`. Discovery can be confirmed by running `claude --debug` and looking for `[gatewayDiscovery]` lines in ~/.claude/debug/<session-id>.txt, which record cached model counts, list changes, and any 404, timeout or redirect.

nodes.label: modelPicker replaceBuiltInOptions
nodes.rationale: If a modelPicker lineup sets replaceBuiltInOptions, Claude Code hides the gateway-discovered model names as well as the built-in entries, keeping only a row for the model the session is already using. It is one of the two causes of models missing from the /model picker.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC
nodes.rationale: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1 turns off background traffic outside the gateway path — version checks, telemetry, release notes — which otherwise fails and shows as blocked connections on gateway-only egress networks. It also disables auto-updates, suppresses the fast-mode availability check, and turns off gateway model discovery (previously cached models remain but are not refreshed).

nodes.label: Telemetry credential scoping
nodes.rationale: Claude Code attaches a credential to telemetry or usage-metrics requests only when the request goes to the host the credential belongs to, so while ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at a gateway it sends telemetry to Anthropic without the gateway credential, and it stops reporting usage metrics to the Console analytics dashboard. Before v2.1.246 it could attach the gateway credential to Anthropic-bound telemetry; model requests always went to the gateway.

nodes.label: skipWebFetchPreflight
nodes.rationale: The WebFetch tool's domain safety check still calls api.anthropic.com and is unaffected by disabling nonessential traffic; it must be turned off separately with `skipWebFetchPreflight: true` in settings when the network blocks that host.

nodes.label: Amazon Bedrock gateway route
nodes.rationale: For a gateway that speaks Bedrock's native request format, set ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL, CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_BEDROCK_AUTH=1 and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 in place of ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. The skip-auth variable tells Claude Code not to sign requests with provider credentials because the gateway holds them.

nodes.label: Google Cloud Agent Platform gateway route
nodes.rationale: For a Google Cloud Agent Platform gateway, set ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_PROJECT_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_VERTEX_AUTH=1, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1 and CLOUD_ML_REGION. Like Bedrock, this gateway accepts the provider's native request format rather than the Anthropic Messages format.

nodes.label: Microsoft Foundry gateway route
nodes.rationale: A Microsoft Foundry gateway takes ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL plus ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_API_KEY (sent as x-api-key) or ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_AUTH_TOKEN (sent as Authorization: Bearer, taking precedence when both are set), and requires v2.1.203 or later. A gateway that injects its own Authorization header instead uses CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_FOUNDRY_AUTH=1 with both credential variables unset; before v2.1.203 that combination left the Foundry client unable to send requests.

nodes.label: Claude Platform on AWS gateway route
nodes.rationale: For a Claude Platform on AWS gateway, set ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_AWS_WORKSPACE_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_ANTHROPIC_AWS_AUTH=1 and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_ANTHROPIC_AWS=1. Like Microsoft Foundry, this gateway accepts the Anthropic Messages format and differs only in which base URL variable reaches it.

nodes.label: Confirm the provider route
nodes.rationale: Starting `claude` from the shell holding a provider block and running /status shows rows such as `API provider: Amazon Bedrock`, `Bedrock base URL: …` and `AWS auth skipped`; other providers show equivalents such as `Vertex base URL` and `GCP auth skipped`. Foundry shows an auth-skipped row only with CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_FOUNDRY_AUTH set, a corporate proxy adds a `Proxy` row, and a missing base URL row means the variable did not reach the session.

nodes.label: Gateway error troubleshooting table
nodes.rationale: A table of the most common errors seen when running Claude Code through a gateway, each paired with its gateway-side cause and the fix. It is the referral target from the configuration-check, verification, and additional-configuration sections whenever a step fails.

nodes.label: Auth conflict startup warning
nodes.rationale: A startup warning naming two credential sources and ending in `auth may not work as expected` (older versions: `Auth conflict: Both a token (SOURCE) and an API key (SOURCE) are set`) means a gateway credential and a saved login are both active. The fix is to unset the variable to use the saved login, or run /logout to use the gateway credential.

nodes.label: 401 invalid or unrecognized token
nodes.rationale: 401 errors naming an invalid or unrecognized token mean the credential is not one the gateway issued, or it is in a header the gateway does not read. The fix is to confirm the variable matches the credential kind and to regenerate the key at the gateway if it was revoked.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper script is failing
nodes.rationale: `Your apiKeyHelper script is failing` means the configured command did not produce a usable key, so requests carry a placeholder key. The fix is to run the command directly to see why, and to re-authenticate with the credential provider if it reports an expired session.

nodes.label: ConnectionRefused / ENOTFOUND
nodes.rationale: `Connection refused — a firewall or proxy may be blocking it (ConnectionRefused)` or `Can't reach the API server (ENOTFOUND)`, often after a silent pause while Claude Code retries with backoff, means nothing answered at the base URL: a wrong address, or a VPN or firewall blocking the path. The curl verification request fails immediately with the same cause.

nodes.label: Empty or malformed response (HTTP 200)
nodes.rationale: `API returned an empty or malformed response (HTTP 200)` means the gateway or an intermediate proxy returned a non-API response, often an HTML error or login page. The fix is to reproduce it with the curl request and repair the gateway route that answers with something other than a Claude API response.

nodes.label: 400 on unrecognized request fields
nodes.rationale: 400 errors naming `context_management`, `Extra inputs are not permitted` or other unrecognized fields mean the gateway forwards to an upstream that rejects fields Claude Code sends to Anthropic-format endpoints. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1 suppresses most pre-release fields; for betas that flag does not gate, set the matching CLAUDE_CODE_USE_* provider variable.

nodes.label: 400 on thinking or adaptive
nodes.rationale: 400 errors naming `thinking` or `adaptive`, such as `Input tag 'adaptive' found`, mean the upstream model build does not accept the adaptive reasoning Claude Code requests for Claude 4.6 and later. Upgrading the gateway's upstream is the fix; on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING=1 works instead, and model-configuration capability variables apply only to provider configurations, not behind an ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateway.

nodes.label: Gateway-enforced context limit
nodes.rationale: 400 errors stating a context or token limit in the gateway's own words (`ContextWindowExceededError`, `prompt token count of N exceeds the limit of M`) mean the gateway enforces a smaller context than the model's native window and rewrites the upstream error, so Claude Code does not recognize it as a too-long error and does not auto-compact. /compact recovers the session; CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW prevents it but is clamped between 100,000 tokens and the model's window, and CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS should be set below the gateway's output limit.

nodes.label: Fast mode unavailable due to network connectivity
nodes.rationale: `/fast` reporting `Fast mode unavailable due to network connectivity issues` while inference works means the fast-mode availability check goes directly to api.anthropic.com and does not follow ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL; the same message appears on an open network when Anthropic rejects a gateway-issued key presented by the check. Allowlisting api.anthropic.com fixes blocked egress; for a rejected gateway key only the skip variables help.

nodes.label: Fast mode disabled by your organization
nodes.rationale: In a session authenticated with ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, /fast can report `Fast mode has been disabled by your organization` even when the organization has it enabled, because the availability check requires a claude.ai login or an Anthropic API key and Claude Code treats a bearer-token-only session as disabled without sending the check. CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_FAST_MODE_ORG_CHECK=1 is the fix.

nodes.label: Login prompt despite a working curl test
nodes.rationale: Claude Code asking you to log in while the curl test succeeds means the CLI has no credential of its own — a reachable base URL is not one — and that in an interactive session a project settings env block applies only after the first-run wizard and trust prompt. The credential must be somewhere read before first-run setup: a shell export, ~/.claude/settings.json's env block, or managed settings.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY set but ignored
nodes.rationale: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY being set but ignored with no prompt means the key needs its one-time interactive approval and a previously declined key is ignored without asking again. It is enabled under /config with the `Use custom API key` option.

nodes.label: Managed settings require a first-party login
nodes.rationale: `This machine's managed settings require a first-party login` means managed settings include forceLoginMethod or forceLoginOrgUUID, which cannot coexist with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or apiKeyHelper. An administrator must remove those managed settings to use gateway credentials; the two cannot be combined.

nodes.label: 403 from a WAF body inspection rule
nodes.rationale: A 403 with an HTML body while the gateway's own logs show no request received means a web application firewall or reverse proxy blocked the request body first. Claude Code prompts contain XML-style tags and source code that match cross-site-scripting body rules, so a short curl test passes while a real session fails; exempt the gateway's /v1/messages path from request-body inspection (AWS WAF's CrossSiteScripting_Body rule, or the equivalent OWASP CRS rules under ModSecurity).

nodes.label: TLS certificate errors behind inspection proxies
nodes.rationale: `SSL certificate verification failed` or `Self-signed certificate detected` while the curl test succeeds means Claude Code's runtime does not trust the same certificate authority curl uses, which is common behind corporate TLS-inspection proxies. Setting NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS to the CA bundle path is the fix.

nodes.label: Gateway protocol reference
nodes.rationale: The API contract between Claude Code and an LLM gateway: the endpoints Claude Code calls, the headers and body fields a gateway must forward, which features degrade when they are stripped, attribution headers for cost tracking, and model discovery. It is written for operators configuring a gateway product to work with Claude Code.

nodes.label: Forward unchanged vs consume
nodes.rationale: The page uses two terms for what a gateway does with each header and body field: 'forward unchanged' means pass it to the upstream byte-for-byte, and 'consume' means the gateway may read it for routing, attribution or tracing and need not forward it. Anything not marked forward unchanged is the gateway's to consume or ignore.

nodes.label: GET /protocol machine-readable contract
nodes.rationale: A running Claude apps gateway serves a machine-readable version of this contract at `GET /protocol`, covering the same forwarding requirements plus Claude apps gateway-specific endpoints for SSO sign-in, managed-settings delivery, and telemetry. Claude apps gateway runs from the same `claude` binary as the CLI, so its quickstart is the shortest path to an instance you can fetch the spec from.

nodes.label: API formats a gateway may expose
nodes.rationale: A gateway must expose at least one of three API formats to Claude Code clients: Anthropic Messages, Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel, or Google Cloud's Agent Platform rawPredict. A client picks a format and points Claude Code at the gateway with that format's selection variables.

nodes.label: Anthropic Messages format
nodes.rationale: Selected by `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`; endpoints are `/v1/messages` and the optional `/v1/messages/count_tokens`. The `anthropic-beta` and `anthropic-version` request headers must be forwarded unchanged. Inference requests post to `/v1/messages?beta=true`, so a gateway should match on the path rather than the full URL.

nodes.label: Amazon Bedrock InvokeModel format
nodes.rationale: Selected by `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL` with `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1`; endpoints are `/model/{model}/invoke`, `/model/{model}/invoke-with-response-stream`, and the optional `/model/{model}/count-tokens`. The `anthropic_beta` and `anthropic_version` request BODY fields must be forwarded unchanged.

nodes.label: Google Cloud Agent Platform rawPredict format
nodes.rationale: Google Cloud's Agent Platform is Google Cloud's Claude endpoint, formerly Vertex AI, and its variable names keep the `VERTEX` spelling: selected by `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_BASE_URL` with `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX=1`, with `:rawPredict`, `:streamRawPredict` and optional `count-tokens:rawPredict` method suffixes attached to the publisher model path. Both `anthropic-beta`/`anthropic-version` headers and the `anthropic_version` body field are forwarded unchanged.

nodes.label: Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS
nodes.rationale: Microsoft Foundry and the Claude Platform on AWS implement the Anthropic Messages format. Claude Code routes to them through their own variables, `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` and `ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL`, but a gateway fronting either implements the Anthropic Messages row.

nodes.label: anthropic-workspace-id header
nodes.rationale: A gateway fronting the Claude Platform on AWS must also forward the `anthropic-workspace-id` header, which that platform requires on every request. It joins `anthropic-version` and `anthropic-beta` in the forward-unchanged set for that upstream.

nodes.label: Optional token-counting endpoints
nodes.rationale: Token-counting endpoints are the only optional ones in every format: when absent, Claude Code falls back to counting context usage through the inference (messages) endpoint instead. Exposing the endpoint keeps token counts from consuming inference requests. Token counting has no beta pairing.

nodes.label: Best-effort startup traffic
nodes.rationale: A gateway sees best-effort startup traffic it can reject without breaking anything: an Anthropic Messages-format gateway receives a `HEAD /api/hello` connection-warming probe (skipped when an HTTP proxy or client certificate is configured), and a Bedrock-format gateway receives `GET /inference-profiles?type=SYSTEM_DEFINED` plus `GET /inference-profiles/{profile}` lookups when the configured model is an inference profile.

nodes.label: Checks that bypass the gateway
nodes.rationale: The fast mode availability check and the WebFetch domain safety check call `api.anthropic.com` directly rather than following `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, so they never appear in gateway logs. On a network blocking direct egress to `api.anthropic.com`, fast mode can report a connectivity error while inference through the gateway keeps working.

nodes.label: Stream inference responses
nodes.rationale: A gateway must stream inference responses: Claude Code reads the stream as it arrives, so a gateway that buffers complete responses before relaying them makes Claude Code stall.

nodes.label: Relay Bedrock event-stream unmodified
nodes.rationale: When the client speaks the Amazon Bedrock format, relay the `InvokeModelWithResponseStream` response body and its `Content-Type: application/vnd.amazon.eventstream` header unmodified, and do not convert the stream to server-sent events.

nodes.label: Keep-alive pings and the 300s byte watchdog
nodes.rationale: On `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` or `ANTHROPIC_AWS_BASE_URL` connections Claude Code counts every relayed byte, including SSE `ping` events and comment lines, and aborts a stream silent for 300 seconds by default; upstream pings are the only traffic during long thinking pauses, so stripping or buffering them aborts the stream. An upstream with no pings (Bedrock's binary event-stream) requires the gateway to emit its own `ping` events during silent gaps. Gateways reached via `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_VERTEX_BASE_URL` or `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` are not byte-watchdogged — a 5-minute idle timeout applies instead, and `CLAUDE_ENABLE_BYTE_WATCHDOG_BEDROCK` can add the watchdog on Bedrock connections.

nodes.label: Format mismatch with the upstream
nodes.rationale: The common failure mode is a mismatch between the format the client sends to the gateway and the format the upstream accepts. Speaking Bedrock or Agent Platform format, Claude Code sends only the subset those providers accept; speaking Anthropic Messages format it sends the full capability set even when the gateway forwards to a Bedrock or Agent Platform upstream. Bridging that difference is the gateway's job.

nodes.label: Claude Code request headers
nodes.rationale: Header names are case-insensitive on the wire. `anthropic-version` and `anthropic-beta` must be forwarded unchanged, plus `anthropic-workspace-id` when the upstream is the Claude Platform on AWS; the rest the gateway may consume for routing, attribution and tracing and need not forward.

nodes.label: Authorization and x-api-key credential headers
nodes.rationale: `Authorization` and `x-api-key` carry the developer's gateway credential, in one or both headers depending on which credential variable the developer set.

nodes.label: anthropic-version header
nodes.rationale: The API version header, currently `2023-06-01`. Bedrock- and Agent Platform-format requests also carry an `anthropic_version` BODY field whose value is the provider dialect string, not this header's value.

nodes.label: anthropic-beta header
nodes.rationale: Comma-separated capability values for the request. Forward the header verbatim and do not allowlist individual values, because the set changes with Claude Code releases.

nodes.label: OAuth capability inside anthropic-beta
nodes.rationale: When the developer authenticates with a claude.ai login — possible when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is set without a gateway credential variable — the `anthropic-beta` header also carries an OAuth capability the upstream requires, and stripping it fails those requests with `401`.

nodes.label: Session and agent identifier headers
nodes.rationale: `x-claude-code-session-id` uniquely identifies the session so requests can be aggregated without parsing bodies; `x-claude-code-agent-id` identifies a subagent that issued the request and pairs with the session ID to attribute cost to parallel agents; `x-claude-code-parent-agent-id` identifies the spawning agent for nested agents. Subagent IDs are fresh per spawn while teammate agents reuse a stable name-based ID, and in both cases the ID identifies an agent, not a person or device — so it must not be treated as a user identifier.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS
nodes.rationale: If developers set `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, those headers appear on API requests as well, and Claude Code also sends them on the model-discovery request.

nodes.label: Forward as open lists
nodes.rationale: Headers and body fields are open lists, not closed ones: Claude Code gains capabilities over releases and they arrive as new `anthropic-beta` values, new body fields, and occasionally new `anthropic-*` or `x-claude-code-*` headers. A gateway pinned to an observed list strips the next capability's header or field and breaks it on the release that introduces it.

nodes.label: System prompt attribution block
nodes.rationale: Claude Code prepends a short attribution block to the system prompt containing the client version and a fingerprint derived from the conversation. Anthropic and the cloud providers' Claude endpoints read the block for attribution.

nodes.label: Positional strip of the attribution block
nodes.rationale: The `api.anthropic.com` endpoint strips the attribution block before processing when it arrives unchanged as the first system block, so it does not affect first-party prompt caching; any other upstream receives it as part of the prompt. The strip is positional, so it only works when the gateway forwards the `system` array unchanged.

nodes.label: System array forwarding rules
nodes.rationale: Forward the `system` array exactly as received with the attribution block first — prepending another system block, reordering the array, or converting it to a single string defeats the strip and the block then reaches the model and the prompt cache key. Keep the block in its own array entry: the endpoint treats a merged block starting with the attribution header as attribution in its entirety and drops everything merged into it, including the rest of the system prompt.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0
nodes.rationale: If a gateway must reshape system content, set `CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0` so Claude Code omits the block at the client rather than the gateway stripping or moving it. The variable exists for gateway and third-party caching compatibility, not as a privacy control: on a direct connection the full request already goes to the Anthropic API either way.

nodes.label: Auto mode classifier exception
nodes.rationale: Claude Code keeps the attribution block on auto-mode classifier requests even with the variable set to `0`, but only when the requests go to `api.anthropic.com` (with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` unset or naming that host and no third-party provider) and the active credential is not an Anthropic profile or federation credential. Classifier requests skip the rest of the system prompt, so the block is their only Claude Code marker; before v2.1.229 this exception did not exist and setting `0` made auto mode fail on every action it sent to the classifier.

nodes.label: Attribution block stability from v2.1.181
nodes.rationale: From Claude Code v2.1.181 the block is stable for the lifetime of a conversation when requests route through a custom base URL, so a gateway-side prompt cache keyed on the full request body works without disabling it. Before v2.1.181 the block included a per-request token that changed the start of the system prompt on every request, so on those versions `CLAUDE_CODE_ATTRIBUTION_HEADER=0` should be set when the gateway caches on the request body or forwards to a third-party provider.

nodes.label: Feature pass-through
nodes.rationale: Claude Code treats an `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateway as an Anthropic-format endpoint and sends it the same beta headers and body fields it sends to `api.anthropic.com`, except a small release-varying set of diagnostics and defaults reserved for direct connections. The section enumerates which capabilities break, and how, when a gateway strips headers or body fields.

nodes.label: Header and body field pairing
nodes.rationale: Capabilities that add body fields pair them with a beta header and the pair travels together. A gateway that strips the header while passing the body, or forwards an Anthropic-format body to an upstream with a different schema, produces hard `400` errors; only when both halves are absent together does the feature turn off quietly. A gateway that rewrites or redacts request bodies for content inspection breaks the pairing the same way, so inspect without modifying.

nodes.label: Fine-grained tool streaming default
nodes.rationale: Fine-grained tool streaming is one of the direct-connection defaults: it is off by default whenever requests route through a custom base URL, and a gateway receives it only when developers set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_FINE_GRAINED_TOOL_STREAMING=1`.

nodes.label: Adaptive reasoning pass-through
nodes.rationale: Adaptive reasoning has no beta header: Claude Code sends `thinking: {"type": "adaptive"}` for Claude 4.6 and later and treats unrecognized model names, such as gateway aliases, as current models that receive the field. When the upstream model build does not accept it the symptom is a `400` naming the `thinking` field or the `adaptive` tag; the remedy is upgrading the upstream, or on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 setting `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING=1`.

nodes.label: Context management pass-through
nodes.rationale: The context management beta header pairs with the `context_management` body field. Breaking the pair produces a `400` with `Extra inputs are not permitted`, common when a gateway accepts Anthropic-format requests but forwards them to Amazon Bedrock; the remedy is forwarding both or setting `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1`.

nodes.label: Extended context and interleaved thinking
nodes.rationale: Extended context and interleaved thinking are beta headers only, with no body field. When the header is stripped they are silently unavailable — the upstream never sees the capability request — so the remedy is forwarding `anthropic-beta` verbatim.

nodes.label: Beta tool schema fields
nodes.rationale: Tool-related beta headers pair with tool schema fields such as `strict` and `defer_loading`. When the body passes through without its header the symptom is a `400` naming the unrecognized tool schema field; the remedy is forwarding both or `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1`.

nodes.label: output_config: effort and structured outputs
nodes.rationale: The `output_config` body field carries effort, structured-output format, and task budget settings, and each pairs with its own beta header. Breaking the pairing yields a `400` naming `output_config`, often `Extra inputs are not permitted`, on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform upstreams; forward the field and its headers together.

nodes.label: Prompt caching pass-through (cache_control)
nodes.rationale: Prompt caching has no beta pairing: Claude Code attaches `cache_control` markers to `system` blocks and to `messages` entries, including `role: "system"` entries appended mid-conversation. Breakage raises no error — the conversation bills as uncached input every turn, visible as high `input_tokens` with little cache activity in `usage` — so forward `cache_control` unchanged wherever it appears and do not convert block-form `system` or message content to plain strings.

nodes.label: Scope of ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES
nodes.rationale: The `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` variables declare model capabilities only in the provider configurations `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY` and `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE`. They have no effect behind an `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateway.

nodes.label: Automatic retry and capability disabling
nodes.rationale: When the upstream rejects the `thinking` field, a thinking signature, a mid-conversation system message, or a `cache_control` marker on one of those messages, Claude Code retries the request and disables the rejected capability for the rest of the conversation. It does NOT retry context management or tool schema field rejections; those `400` errors reach the developer.

nodes.label: Forward error response bodies unmodified
nodes.rationale: The retry logic matches on the upstream's error wording, so error response bodies must be forwarded unmodified. A gateway that wraps upstream errors in its own envelope breaks the recovery path even when it preserves the status code.

nodes.label: capability_rejected: token
nodes.rationale: An error envelope preserves the recovery path when its message carries a stable `capability_rejected:` token; Claude apps gateway substitutes those tokens for cloud providers' error wording, for example `capability_rejected: prompt_too_long`.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1
nodes.rationale: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1` stops Claude Code from sending pre-release capabilities and their body fields on every provider, including context management and the beta tool fields. It does not affect adaptive reasoning, which is selected by model rather than by beta, and it never suppresses the OAuth capability that subscription authentication requires.

nodes.label: MCP tool search override under the betas variable
nodes.rationale: On Claude Code v2.1.227 or later an organization can keep MCP tool search on under `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS` through managed settings. On a direct connection or an `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` gateway, Claude Code then keeps sending the tool-search beta header, `defer_loading` tool fields and `tool_reference` blocks while stripping the rest; on a cloud provider, or signed in through a Claude apps gateway, the override has no effect.

nodes.label: Gateway model discovery
nodes.rationale: When `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a gateway exposing the Anthropic Messages format, Claude Code can query the gateway's `/v1/models` endpoint at startup and add the returned models to the `/model` picker. Setting `replaceBuiltInOptions` in a `modelPicker` lineup hides the discovered models from the picker.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1
nodes.rationale: Developers enable discovery by setting `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1`, in their own environment or through managed settings. Discovery is off by default so that gateways backed by a shared API key do not surface every model the key can access to every user.

nodes.label: When discovery does not run
nodes.rationale: Discovery applies only to the Anthropic Messages format and does not run when any `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_*` provider variable is set (even alongside `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`), when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is unset or points at `api.anthropic.com`, or when nonessential traffic is disabled through `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC` or organization policy.

nodes.label: Discovery request: GET /v1/models?limit=1000
nodes.rationale: The request is `GET /v1/models?limit=1000` with a 3-second timeout, and any redirect is treated as failure so the credential cannot leak to a redirect target. A gateway that responds slowly or redirects `/v1/models` — even `http` to `https` — fails discovery silently, so the endpoint must be served directly at the configured base URL. Claude Code reads `id` and the optional `display_name` from each entry in the response's `data` array.

nodes.label: Discovery credential headers
nodes.rationale: Claude Code sends the discovery request with both credential headers and omits one whose value does not resolve: `Authorization` carries `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (or the `apiKeyHelper` value) as a bearer token, and `x-api-key` carries the resolved API key — a helper-only credential arrives in both. Sending both requires v2.1.248 or later; earlier versions sent only `Authorization` when `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` was set and only `x-api-key` otherwise. When neither resolves, Claude Code skips discovery and writes a `[gatewayDiscovery] skipped` line to the `claude --debug` log.

nodes.label: Discovery id substring filter
nodes.rationale: Claude Code keeps a discovered entry when its `id` contains `claude` or `anthropic` anywhere in the string, matched case-insensitively, and ignores the rest — so provider-prefixed IDs such as `vertex_ai/claude-sonnet-4-6` pass. Before v2.1.223 an entry was kept only when its `id` BEGAN with `claude` or `anthropic`, which hid provider-prefixed IDs.

nodes.label: Picker entries and ID folding
nodes.rationale: Each discovered entry is labeled "From gateway" and uses `display_name` when provided, bounded by the `availableModels` managed setting. A discovered ID is skipped when it exactly matches an existing picker row or is another spelling of the same Fable version, and an explicit ID folds into a built-in alias row when both resolve to the same model — so `claude-sonnet-5` collapses into the `sonnet` row while `claude-sonnet-4-6` adds its own row. Before v2.1.197 explicit IDs were not folded.

nodes.label: gateway-models.json discovery cache
nodes.rationale: Results are cached to `~/.claude/cache/gateway-models.json` (or `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\cache\gateway-models.json` on Windows, or under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` when set) and refreshed on each startup. If the request fails or the gateway does not implement `/v1/models`, the picker falls back to the previous startup's cached list or the built-in model list.

nodes.label: Managed settings
nodes.rationale: Managed settings are the settings an organization deploys to every developer's machine. Claude Code applies them above every other level, so no user, project, local, or --settings value overrides them.

nodes.label: Exceptions to managed-settings precedence
nodes.rationale: A few security-sensitive exceptions let a stricter value from a lower level still count against the managed policy. The exceptions only ever tighten, never loosen, what the managed value allows.

nodes.label: managed-settings.json
nodes.rationale: A managed-settings.json file holds the keys an administrator has decided to enforce, in the same JSON shape as settings.json. It is the quickest way to put a policy on each machine; the settings reference says for each key whether a managed source can set it.

nodes.label: Per-OS system directories
nodes.rationale: The managed settings file lives in a system directory that differs per OS: /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/ on macOS, /etc/claude-code/ on Linux and WSL, and C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\ on Windows. Claude Code does not read the legacy Windows path C:\ProgramData\ClaudeCode\managed-settings.json.

nodes.label: /status Setting sources line
nodes.rationale: Running /status inside Claude Code prints a Setting sources line that shows Enterprise managed settings with the source Claude Code selected in parentheses. It is the confirmation step before rolling a policy out to the rest of a fleet.

nodes.label: Managed settings delivery mechanisms
nodes.rationale: There are four ways to get managed settings onto a machine: server-managed settings, MDM or OS-level policy, a file-based managed-settings.json, and the Windows HKCU registry. Every mechanism carries the same policy keys as a settings.json file.

nodes.label: Server-managed settings
nodes.rationale: Server-managed settings are delivered from the claude.ai admin console or a self-hosted Claude apps gateway, fetched at startup and polled hourly. Claude Code keeps a local cache that it applies at startup and replaces on each successful fetch. Use it when you want one place to change policy for a claude.ai organization without touching each machine.

nodes.label: MDM or OS-level policy
nodes.rationale: MDM delivery uses a macOS configuration profile in the com.anthropic.claudecode managed preferences domain, or a Windows HKLM registry value named Settings under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode, pushed by Jamf, Intune, or Group Policy. Claude Code reads it at startup and checks for changes every 30 minutes.

nodes.label: File-based delivery
nodes.rationale: File-based delivery places managed-settings.json (plus an optional managed-settings.d/ directory and managed-mcp.json) in the OS system directory on each machine. Claude Code reads it at startup and reloads it when the file changes; it suits machines without MDM, Linux hosts, and self-built images.

nodes.label: HKCU registry fallback
nodes.rationale: The Windows HKCU registry holds the same Settings value under HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\ClaudeCode, for administrators who cannot write the machine-level HKLM key. Because it is user-writable it is not an admin source: Claude Code uses it only when no higher source delivers a policy key and no host-supplied parent settings supply a restrictive key.

nodes.label: Endpoint-managed settings
nodes.rationale: The MDM and file mechanisms are together called endpoint-managed settings, because the policy is stored on the developer's device, as opposed to server-managed settings, which Claude Code fetches.

nodes.label: Delivery control keys
nodes.rationale: policyHelper, wslInheritsWindowsSettings, and managedSourcesBehavior are the delivery controls: keys tied to particular sources, whose Scope line in the settings reference says where each may be set.

nodes.label: Gateway login keys
nodes.rationale: forceLoginGatewayUrl and the "gateway" value of forceLoginMethod are source-tied gateway login keys, listed alongside the delivery controls as keys whose usable source is restricted.

nodes.label: Per-group policy targeting
nodes.rationale: A managed settings file, an MDM profile, or the claude.ai console applies one policy to everyone it reaches, so a different group needs a different file or profile. The claude.ai console cannot target a group yet, while a self-hosted Claude apps gateway delivers managed settings per IdP group.

nodes.label: Surfaces that read managed settings
nodes.rationale: On the developer's machine, the terminal, the VS Code and JetBrains extensions, the desktop app's Code tab, and Agent SDK sessions all read the managed sources. Agent SDK sessions load managed settings even when settingSources excludes the user, project, and local files.

nodes.label: Cloud and self-hosted sessions
nodes.rationale: A session in an Anthropic-hosted environment reads no device MDM profile or file, so its policy has to come from server-managed settings. A self-hosted environment also reads the managed settings file in its runner image, by default only when server-managed settings deliver no policy key, apart from the keys read from every admin source.

nodes.label: Cowork sessions
nodes.rationale: Cowork in the Claude Desktop app runs its sessions on Claude Code, and never fetches server-managed settings from the claude.ai console even for Team or Enterprise accounts. On the user's machine it reads the device MDM policy and managed settings file; inside a full VM sandbox (requireCoworkFullVmSandbox) or on remote Anthropic-managed VMs there is no device policy to read.

nodes.label: Refresh behavior in running sessions
nodes.rationale: A running session picks up most policy changes on each mechanism's schedule without a restart. Claude Code reads forceRemoteSettingsRefresh and requiredMinimumVersion only at session start, arms a new or changed policyHelper entry at the next launch, and reads some user-editable keys once at session start.

nodes.label: Changes that need approval
nodes.rationale: A server-managed change to a setting that needs approval, such as a hook or an env variable, waits for the developer to accept a dialog in an interactive session, and applies for the current run in a session hosted by an IDE extension or the Agent SDK. Other server-managed changes apply on the next poll.

nodes.label: requiredMinimumVersion
nodes.rationale: requiredMinimumVersion blocks an outdated binary from starting but does not end a session that is already running, so a session left open for weeks can still lag a rollout. Together with requiredMaximumVersion it fails open by design: an invalid value is dropped rather than enforced.

nodes.label: managed-settings.d drop-in directory
nodes.rationale: When several teams own parts of one policy, each part goes in its own file in managed-settings.d/ beside managed-settings.json. Claude Code merges managed-settings.json first, then every *.json file in the directory in alphabetical order (numeric prefixes control the order), ignoring hidden files and non-.json files.

nodes.label: Drop-in file merge rules
nodes.rationale: When two drop-in files set the same key: single values are replaced by the later file, lists combine with duplicates removed, nested blocks merge key by key under the same rules, and fallbackModel, a same-named extraKnownMarketplaces entry, and modelPicker are each replaced whole by the later file.

nodes.label: managedSourcesBehavior
nodes.rationale: managedSourcesBehavior decides what Claude Code does when more than one managed source reaches the same machine: "first-wins" (the default) or "merge". It is a control key rather than a policy key, and Claude Code reads it only from the highest-ranked source that carries either it or a policy key.

nodes.label: first-wins source selection
nodes.rationale: Under the default "first-wins", Claude Code uses the highest-ranked source that delivers at least one policy key and ignores the rest rather than merging them, apart from the keys read from every admin source. It shows no warning for the sources it skips; /status names the source it used and the ones it skipped.

nodes.label: merge mode for managed sources
nodes.rationale: Setting managedSourcesBehavior to "merge" in the highest-ranked source deployed makes Claude Code apply every admin source that delivers a policy key, combined by kind of key; it requires v2.1.242 or later. A lower source cannot opt itself into merging, the HKCU registry never merges, and because lower sources' list entries are added, merge should be enabled only when every lower source is administrator-controlled.

nodes.label: Policy key
nodes.rationale: A policy key is any settings key other than the two control keys wslInheritsWindowsSettings and managedSourcesBehavior. A managed settings file or MDM policy containing only control keys does not count as delivering policy, and Claude Code moves on to the next source.

nodes.label: Admin source
nodes.rationale: An admin source is one of the first three ranked sources: remote settings, MDM or OS-level policy, and managed settings files. The HKCU registry is user-writable and is not an admin source, which is why the cross-source key scan leaves it out.

nodes.label: Managed source ranking
nodes.rationale: Claude Code checks the sources highest priority first: (1) remote settings from claude.ai or a gateway, (2) MDM or OS-level policies, (3) managed settings files including drop-ins, (4) the HKCU registry. Remote settings are fetched only when the session authenticates to Anthropic's API with an eligible login or key or signs in to a gateway; on other providers or a non-Anthropic ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, Claude Code starts at the next source.

nodes.label: Keys read from every admin source
nodes.rationale: A small set of cross-source keys are read from every admin source rather than only the selected one, so a lower-ranked MDM policy or file can still set them. They include the sandbox locks and binary paths, allowAllClaudeAiMcps, sandbox.filesystem.disabled, sandbox.network.strictAllowlist, useAutoModeDuringPlan, syncClaudeAiSkills, enableArtifact, commit-trailer opt-outs, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, and env.

nodes.label: Sandbox allowlist locks
nodes.rationale: sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly and sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly turn on when any admin source sets them true. While a lock is on, Claude Code unions the allowlist it locks — allowedDomains plus WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules, or filesystem.allowRead — across every admin source; without the lock, an unselected source's allowlist is ignored under first-wins.

nodes.label: Per-variable env merge
nodes.rationale: env is merged per variable across the admin sources under either behavior: each variable comes from the highest-priority source that defines it, so lower sources fill in variables the higher ones leave unset. This requires v2.1.223 or later; before that, Claude Code applied only the selected source's whole env block.

nodes.label: enableArtifact deny-only semantics
nodes.rationale: A false for enableArtifact from any admin source turns the Artifact tool off, and a false in the developer's user, project, or local settings turns it off too, with no source able to turn it back on. useAutoModeDuringPlan and syncClaudeAiSkills behave the same way: each key can only deny. enableArtifact requires v2.1.242 or later.

nodes.label: How merge combines each kind of key
nodes.rationale: Under "merge": lists such as permissions.allow, hooks and deniedMcpServers combine entries from every source; locks such as allowManagedHooksOnly and crossSessionInbound take the strictest value any source sets, with a looser value applying only from the highest source; restriction allowlists such as availableModels and allowedMcpServers are taken whole from the highest source that sets them; credential helpers, forceLoginOrgUUID, modelPicker and permissions.defaultMode are read from the highest-ranked source only; every other key takes the highest source's value.

nodes.label: policyHelper
nodes.rationale: A policyHelper is an executable named by an MDM policy or managed settings file that Claude Code runs at startup to compute managed settings. Claude Code selects the source at startup, and that selection decides whether a helper runs; a new or changed entry arms only at the next launch.

nodes.label: Helper output replaces all managed settings
nodes.rationale: When the selected source configures a policyHelper and the helper emits a managedSettings object, that object is the only managed settings for the session, including for the keys otherwise read from every admin source. The single exception is forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, which Claude Code checks in every admin source at startup before the helper runs.

nodes.label: Parent settings from an embedding host
nodes.rationale: When another application launches Claude Code — Claude Desktop, an IDE extension, or an Agent SDK app — that host can pass its own managed settings through the SDK managedSettings option; Claude Code calls these parent settings. By default Claude Code ignores parent settings whenever any admin source is present.

nodes.label: parentSettingsBehavior
nodes.rationale: Setting parentSettingsBehavior to "merge" in the highest-priority managed source makes Claude Code merge parent settings alongside an admin source, keeping only the host values that restrict what Claude can do. The gap to know: unless the allowManaged*Only locks are also set, the host's permission allow rules and sandbox allowlists still apply, and a policyHelper can turn parent merging off regardless of this key.

nodes.label: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly
nodes.rationale: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly makes Claude Code honor only the permission rules in the managed policy, ignoring user, project and local files and --allowedTools. When any admin source sets it, Claude Code also drops parent-supplied permission allow rules and additionalDirectories as it reads them, even when a higher-priority source leaves the key unset.

nodes.label: Restoring Cowork folder access
nodes.rationale: Cowork pre-approves writes to a session's connected folders through host-supplied allow rules, which allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly drops — Cowork cannot show the prompt, so Claude reports each write as blocked. The fix is to add allow rules for those folders (for example Edit(~/CoworkProjects/**)) to the managed source Claude Code selects on those machines, which on an MDM fleet is the MDM policy rather than a separate file.

nodes.label: What a developer can still change
nodes.rationale: Four things sit outside the rule that a developer cannot override a managed value: a managed model is a default that --model and ANTHROPIC_MODEL still override; a local administrator can edit the managed source itself; an edit to the server-managed cache lasts only until the next successful fetch; and managed settings bind Claude Code only, not another tool calling the API.

nodes.label: availableModels
nodes.rationale: Because a managed model key is only a default, availableModels is what actually restricts which models a session may pick. When present but invalid it is enforced as an empty allowlist so only the Default model is available, with non-string entries stripped and the valid subset enforced.

nodes.label: Checking that a policy is in force
nodes.rationale: Two commands on the developer's machine answer whether a policy applied: /status shows which managed source Claude Code selected, and claude doctor lists what Claude Code dropped. Use them when a developer reports a policy isn't applying or to confirm a rollout before pushing it to the fleet.

nodes.label: Setting sources labels
nodes.rationale: The parenthesised label on the Setting sources line names the selected source: (remote) for server-managed, (plist) or (HKLM) for MDM/OS policy, (file), (drop-ins) or (file + drop-ins) for the file mechanism, a list ending in ", merged" when sources were composed, (HKCU) for the user-writable fallback, (parent process) for an embedding host, and (helper) for a policyHelper.

nodes.label: Skipped sources line
nodes.rationale: When Claude Code found a managed source and did not select it, a second /status line named Skipped sources names each one, which distinguishes a policy that never reached the machine from one a higher-priority source overrode. It requires v2.1.242 or later.

nodes.label: Diagnosing a missing Setting sources line
nodes.rationale: A missing Setting sources line means Claude Code found no managed source delivering a policy key — check the file's path for the OS, that it is valid JSON, and that it holds a policy key rather than only control keys. A line naming a source other than the one you deployed means a higher-priority source is present and yours was skipped.

nodes.label: claude doctor
nodes.rationale: claude doctor lists each invalid managed entry with its source and field, and reports the server-managed fetch outcome when a policy was deployed that way. It is one of three places a dropped entry surfaces, alongside a startup dialog in interactive sessions and a stderr summary in non-interactive -p runs.

nodes.label: Managed schema-validation tolerance
nodes.rationale: When a managed file, MDM profile, registry value, or server-managed payload fails schema validation, Claude Code first skips the individual entries it can repair (with a warning for each), then drops any top-level key whose value still fails, and keeps enforcing every remaining valid key.

nodes.label: Stricter validation of helper output
nodes.rationale: Claude Code is stricter with the managedSettings a policyHelper emits: it makes the same per-entry repairs, but any schema violation that survives fails the whole helper run, and at startup Claude Code refuses to start, the same as for a helper that exits non-zero.

nodes.label: Unparseable managed file behavior
nodes.rationale: A managed settings file or drop-in that isn't valid JSON contributes no settings at all; Claude Code reports it with the other validation errors and reads the remaining sources as usual. If it can't be read or parsed and no other admin source supplies a policy, sessions signed in with claude.ai or Claude Console credentials exit at startup with a message to contact an administrator.

nodes.label: Keys that fail closed
nodes.rationale: A few enforcement keys are not dropped when invalid; Claude Code enforces a stricter fallback until the value is fixed. allowedMcpServers and availableModels become empty allowlists, allowManagedHooksOnly / allowManagedMcpServersOnly / disableCommandPluginSources / enforceAvailableModels are treated as true, forceLoginOrgUUID permits no organization, crossSessionInbound becomes refuse, and sandbox.credentials entries degrade to mode deny or are stripped.

nodes.label: Strict validation of lower-tier settings
nodes.rationale: The repair-and-keep-going tolerance applies only to managed settings. User, project, and local settings files stay strict: a file whose JSON or top-level shape fails validation is rejected as a whole and reported, while an individual failing entry such as a malformed permission rule is skipped with a warning and the rest of the file applies.

nodes.label: Keys only a managed source can set
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reads a set of keys only from a managed source; placing them in user or project settings has no effect. They cover permission, plugin and delivery controls — allowAllClaudeAiMcps, allowedChannelPlugins, allowManagedHooksOnly, allowManagedMcpServersOnly, allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly, blockedMarketplaces, channelsEnabled, disableCommandPluginSources, disableSideloadFlags, forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, managedSourcesBehavior, parentSettingsBehavior, pluginSuggestionMarketplaces, pluginTrustMessage, policyHelper, the sandbox locks, strictKnownMarketplaces, strictPluginOnlyCustomization and wslInheritsWindowsSettings.

nodes.label: The lock pattern
nodes.rationale: Most managed-only keys are locks: the value a lock governs — permission rules, sandbox.network.allowedDomains — is an ordinary key any level can set, and the lock tells Claude Code to honor only the managed value.

nodes.label: wslInheritsWindowsSettings
nodes.rationale: Set in the HKLM registry or a file under C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode, wslInheritsWindowsSettings makes WSL read the Windows policy chain and read /etc/claude-code only when no managed settings file or drop-in under that directory delivers a policy key. On WSL the HKCU registry applies only once HKLM or the Windows managed file turns this on and the HKCU value also sets it.

nodes.label: managed-mcp.json
nodes.rationale: Managed MCP servers are deployed alongside any delivery mechanism through a managed-mcp.json file in the same system directory. allowAllClaudeAiMcps controls whether the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself load alongside a deployed managed-mcp.json instead of being suppressed.

nodes.label: DISABLE_TELEMETRY via managed env
nodes.rationale: Claude Code sends Anthropic operational telemetry by default on sessions that use the Anthropic API, directly or through a gateway or custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. To turn it off for every developer without relying on each person's shell, deliver DISABLE_TELEMETRY through the env block of managed settings; a value of 1 applies without showing the user the approval dialog.

nodes.label: Consequences of disabling telemetry
nodes.rationale: Turning telemetry off stops the usage data that feeds the organization's analytics dashboard for the developers the policy reaches. It also turns off feature-flag fetching, making Remote Control, default auto mode, and other features that need feature-flag fetching unavailable for them.

nodes.label: MDM examples repository
nodes.rationale: Starter templates for Jamf, Iru, Intune, and Group Policy live in the MDM examples repository at github.com/anthropics/claude-code/tree/main/examples/mdm.

nodes.label: Org-wide Remote Control and web session controls
nodes.rationale: On Team and Enterprise plans an Owner enables or disables Remote Control and web sessions organization-wide in Claude Code admin settings. Remote Control can additionally be disabled per device with the disableRemoteControl setting, while web sessions have no per-device managed settings key.

nodes.label: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
nodes.rationale: MCP is an open source standard for AI-tool integrations that lets Claude Code connect to hundreds of external tools and data sources. MCP servers give Claude Code access to tools, databases, and APIs.

nodes.label: MCP servers in Claude Code
nodes.rationale: An MCP server is the connected system Claude Code reads and acts on directly instead of working from data you paste in. Connect one when you find yourself copying data into chat from another tool such as an issue tracker or a monitoring dashboard.

nodes.label: What you can do with MCP
nodes.rationale: With servers connected Claude Code can implement features from issue trackers, analyze monitoring data, query databases, integrate Figma designs, automate workflows such as Gmail drafts, and react to external events pushed in as channel messages.

nodes.label: Anthropic Directory of connectors
nodes.rationale: The Anthropic Directory at claude.ai/directory lists reviewed connectors. Directory connectors use the same MCP infrastructure as Claude Code, so any remote server listed there can be added with `claude mcp add`.

nodes.label: Prompt injection risk from untrusted servers
nodes.rationale: The docs warn to verify you trust each server before connecting it: servers that fetch external content can expose the session to prompt injection risk.

nodes.label: mcp-server-dev scaffolding plugin
nodes.rationale: The official `mcp-server-dev` plugin scaffolds a server for you. Install it with `/plugin install mcp-server-dev@claude-plugins-official`, run `/reload-plugins` if the install summary says to, then run `/mcp-server-dev:build-mcp-server`, which asks about your use case and scaffolds a remote HTTP or local stdio server.

nodes.label: The four MCP installation options
nodes.rationale: Claude Code installs MCP servers in four shapes: a remote HTTP server (recommended), a remote SSE server (deprecated), a local stdio server, and a remote WebSocket server. Each takes a different input — a URL, a launch command, or a JSON entry.

nodes.label: Remote HTTP transport
nodes.rationale: HTTP is the recommended and most widely supported transport for remote MCP servers, added with `claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url>`, optionally with `--header` for a Bearer token or API key.

nodes.label: `streamable-http` as an alias for `http`
nodes.rationale: In `.mcp.json`, `~/.claude.json`, or `claude mcp add-json`, the `type` field accepts `streamable-http` as an alias for `http`, because the MCP specification uses that name for the transport — so configurations copied from server documentation work unmodified.

nodes.label: A `url` entry with no `type` is a configuration error
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reads a JSON entry with no `type` as a stdio server, so an entry that has a `url` but no `type` is skipped with the message `MCP server "<name>" has a "url" but no "type"; add "type": "http" (or "sse" / "ws")`. Before v2.1.202 it reported `command: expected string, received undefined` instead.

nodes.label: `mcp_server_errors` in the stream-json init event
nodes.rationale: In `--output-format stream-json` runs, Claude Code reports a skipped `--mcp-config` entry in the `system/init` event's `mcp_server_errors` field, so scripts can detect that the server never loaded. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.

nodes.label: Remote SSE transport (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: The SSE (Server-Sent Events) transport is deprecated; use HTTP where available. Services that still expose only an SSE endpoint are added with the same command plus `--transport sse`.

nodes.label: Local stdio transport
nodes.rationale: Stdio servers run as local processes on your machine and suit tools needing direct system access or custom scripts. They are added with `claude mcp add [options] <name> -- <command> [args...]`.

nodes.label: `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` in the spawned server environment
nodes.rationale: Claude Code sets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` in a spawned stdio server's environment to the stable project root, so the server can resolve project-relative paths without depending on the working directory. It does not change when working directories are added or removed mid-session, and referencing it via `${VAR}` in a project- or user-scoped entry needs a default such as `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}`.

nodes.label: MCP `roots/list` for allowed directories
nodes.rationale: A server that limits its own filesystem access to a set of allowed directories should implement the MCP `roots/list` request. Claude Code answers with the session's launch directory plus every additional working directory granted via `--add-dir`, `/add-dir`, or `additionalDirectories`, and sends `notifications/roots/list_changed` when that set changes (v2.1.203 or later).

nodes.label: The `--` separator for stdio server arguments
nodes.rationale: For stdio servers, `--` separates Claude's own options (`--transport`, `--env`, `--scope`) from the command and arguments that run the server; everything after `--` is passed through untouched. `--env` accepts multiple `KEY=value` pairs, so at least one other option must sit between `--env` and the server name or the CLI reads the name as another pair.

nodes.label: Remote WebSocket transport
nodes.rationale: WebSocket servers hold a persistent bidirectional connection, suiting remote servers that push events to Claude unprompted. A `type: "ws"` entry accepts the same `url`, `headers`, `headersHelper`, `timeout`, and `alwaysLoad` fields as `http`, but `claude mcp add --transport` does not accept `ws` and WebSocket supports no OAuth.

nodes.label: Adding a server from another client's setup instructions
nodes.rationale: MCP servers are not Claude Code specific, so instructions written for Claude Desktop or Cursor give one of three inputs: a URL (remote), a launch command (local stdio), or an `mcpServers` JSON block. Each maps onto one of the four install options; a `url` with no `type` and a server key with characters outside letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores each need a repair first.

nodes.label: `claude mcp add-json`
nodes.rationale: `claude mcp add-json <name> '<json>'` adds a server from a JSON configuration conforming to the MCP server configuration schema. You pass the object inside `mcpServers`, not the wrapper, and can add `--scope user` or `--client-secret`.

nodes.label: Server management commands
nodes.rationale: Configured servers are managed with `claude mcp list` (all servers), `claude mcp get <name>` (details), `claude mcp remove <name>`, and the in-session `/mcp` panel for status.

nodes.label: Server health and configuration statuses
nodes.rationale: `claude mcp list` shows a health status per server such as `✔ Connected`, `! Needs authentication`, or `✘ Failed to connect`; a failure status means Claude Code could not connect, not that the command failed. Three statuses report a configuration decision without connecting: `⏸ Pending approval`, `✘ Rejected (see disabledMcpjsonServers)`, and `⊘ Disabled for this project`. WebSocket servers do not appear in `claude mcp list`.

nodes.label: Project server approvals and workspace trust
nodes.rationale: As of v2.1.196, `claude mcp list`/`get` read `.mcp.json` approvals from settings files not checked into the repository only after you trust the workspace, so a cloned repository cannot approve its own servers — committed `enableAllProjectMcpServers` or `enabledMcpjsonServers` is ignored in an untrusted folder. User settings, managed settings and `--settings` still apply; a `disabledMcpjsonServers` entry still rejects.

nodes.label: MCP discovery cache and the `cached` status
nodes.rationale: A remote HTTP or SSE server used before can show a status like `cached 2h ago · connects on first use · 5 tools`: Claude Code loaded the tool list from a discovery cache saved in a previous session and connects the server on the first tool call. Requires v2.1.221 or later. Reconnect keeps the entry on a cached server; Reconnect on a connected/failed server, and Clear authentication, discard it.

nodes.label: `MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE` environment variable
nodes.rationale: The discovery cache is off by default unless a gradual rollout enabled it for your account. Set `MCP_DISCOVERY_CACHE=1` to turn it on or `0` to keep it off even when the rollout enabled it. Before v2.1.238 the cache was on by default.

nodes.label: Failure detail is shown but credential-redacted
nodes.rationale: On `✘ Failed to connect`, `claude mcp list` appends the failure detail and `claude mcp get` shows an `Issue:` line with the HTTP status or error code plus the server's error text. Claude Code redacts credential-like text and never includes the expanded server URL; it appends no detail to `✘ Connection error` because that exception text could embed the URL. Post-auth failure messages show only the URL's origin, never path or query.

nodes.label: MCP configuration warnings
nodes.rationale: Claude Code warns about four configuration problems, each with a stated check and remedy: hidden whitespace in config values, the same server name in more than one scope, use of a reserved built-in server name, and a `${VAR}` reference to a variable that is not set.

nodes.label: Hidden whitespace in config values
nodes.rationale: Claude Code warns when an MCP config value carries hidden leading or trailing whitespace, often from pasting a token with a trailing newline. It checks `command`, `url`, each `args` entry, and the values and key names under `env` and `headers`, names the affected fields without echoing their values, does not trim, and uses the values exactly as written.

nodes.label: Same server name in more than one scope
nodes.rationale: Defining one server name in more than one scope with different endpoints raises a conflict warning. Claude Code stores OAuth sign-ins per endpoint, so authenticating one definition does not sign you in where a different definition loads. The warning quotes each scope's endpoint as written, with `${VAR}` references unexpanded, so it never shows a resolved secret.

nodes.label: Reserved built-in server names
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reserves the names of its built-in servers, including `workspace`, `claude-in-chrome`, `computer-use`, `Claude Preview`, and `Claude Browser`. A configuration defining a reserved name is skipped at load time with a rename warning, and `claude mcp add` rejects it outright. Before v2.1.205, `Claude Browser` was not reserved.

nodes.label: Missing environment variable warning
nodes.rationale: If a `${VAR}` reference names a variable that is not set and has no `:-default`, Claude Code warns in `claude mcp list` and `/mcp`, names the variable, and still loads the server with the `${VAR}` text unexpanded.

nodes.label: Waiting for a server that is still connecting
nodes.rationale: If a request needs tools from a server still connecting in the background, Claude waits. With tool search (the default) the wait happens inside the `ToolSearch` call; without it Claude uses the `WaitForMcpServers` tool. On a Microsoft Foundry deployment hosted on Azure Claude starts on the tool-search path because the server-side rejection is only visible from the API.

nodes.label: Disabling a server without removing it
nodes.rationale: Toggling a server off in `/mcp` stops Claude Code connecting to it without losing the configuration; the server is still listed, marked disabled. The choice is recorded per project in `~/.claude.json` in one of two lists covering disjoint sets of servers.

nodes.label: `disabledMcpServers` opt-out list
nodes.rationale: `disabledMcpServers` is the opt-out list for user-configured servers, plugin servers, the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself, and built-in servers that default to on. A connector disabled with the per-project `/mcp` toggle is written here under its display name, for example `claude.ai Slack`.

nodes.label: `enabledMcpServers` opt-in list
nodes.rationale: `enabledMcpServers` is the opt-in list for built-in servers that default to off, such as `computer-use`; Claude Code connects to a default-off server only when it is listed here.

nodes.label: `enabledMcpjsonServers` / `disabledMcpjsonServers`
nodes.rationale: These settings control approval of servers defined in a project's `.mcp.json` file. They are unrelated to `disabledMcpServers` and `enabledMcpServers`, which are the per-project on/off toggles.

nodes.label: MCP client runtimes v1 and v2
nodes.rationale: Claude Code connects through one of two client runtimes: v1 on MCP TypeScript SDK 1.x, and v2 — the same code on SDK 2.0, adding protocol revision 2026-07-28. On v2.1.232 or later it uses v2, picking a runtime at start and keeping it until exit; it falls back to v1 on Bedrock, AWS, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry, a Claude apps gateway login, or with feature-flag fetching off.

nodes.label: MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28
nodes.rationale: On the v2 runtime Claude Code asks HTTP and claude.ai connector servers whether they support revision 2026-07-28 and uses it with those that do; it asks stdio servers only when `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION` is `auto`. Anthropic can pin a specific server to the earlier protocol with a feature flag.

nodes.label: `MCP_SDK_GENERATION` environment variable
nodes.rationale: Set `MCP_SDK_GENERATION` to `v1` or `v2` to pick the client runtime yourself. Where Claude Code uses v1 by default, pinning `v2` does not by itself make it negotiate the newer revision — `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=auto` must be set too.

nodes.label: `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION` environment variable
nodes.rationale: `MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION` set to `auto` or `legacy` decides whether Claude Code asks a server about the newer protocol revision. Leaving it unset or setting `legacy` keeps stdio servers on the earlier handshake; in a Claude Code on the web session Claude Code asks its MCP connectors only when it is `auto`.

nodes.label: Dynamic tool updates via `list_changed`
nodes.rationale: Claude Code supports MCP `list_changed` notifications, so servers can update their available tools, prompts, and resources without a disconnect/reconnect. If a refresh request fails, Claude Code keeps the previously discovered capabilities until a later refresh succeeds; before v2.1.214 a transient refresh error replaced them with an empty list.

nodes.label: Notification streams on the v2 runtime
nodes.rationale: On the v2 runtime Claude Code receives `list_changed` notifications from a server on the newer revision over a stream it holds open, and reopens the stream when it closes with two limits: closing again within 10 seconds allows up to three reopens, then it stops; after five reopens in an hour of longer-lived streams it waits about six hours. Until it reopens you keep the last fetched tools, prompts, and resources.

nodes.label: Automatic reconnection
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reconnects a remote server that drops mid-session and retries an HTTP or SSE server's first connection after a transient error. Stdio servers are local processes and are not reconnected automatically.

nodes.label: Mid-session drop reconnection backoff
nodes.rationale: A dropped remote server is reconnected with exponential backoff: up to five attempts, starting at one second and doubling. Interactively `/mcp` shows the server pending, then failed or needing authentication after five failures, with a manual retry. In `claude -p` and Agent SDK sessions the same schedule runs with no panel to show it.

nodes.label: Retry of a failed first connection
nodes.rationale: When an HTTP or SSE server's first connection fails with a transient error — a 5xx, a connection refused, or a timeout — Claude Code retries up to three times, at startup and when a server is added mid-session. It does not retry a WebSocket first connection, nor an authentication or not-found error, except when a `headersHelper` is the only source of the `Authorization` header, since the helper re-runs each attempt.

nodes.label: Retry of failed capability discovery requests
nodes.rationale: After connecting, Claude Code sends discovery requests such as `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, and `resources/list`, retrying them up to three times with short backoff after a transient network or server error. It does not retry authentication errors, 4xx responses, or request timeouts.

nodes.label: How Claude learns that a server failed
nodes.rationale: With tool search on (the default) Claude Code tells Claude which server failed and its connection error, so Claude reports the failure and the same information appears in `ToolSearch` results that find no matching tool. In any configuration without tool search, Claude Code does not report failed server connections to Claude at all.

nodes.label: Push messages with channels
nodes.rationale: An MCP server can push messages directly into a session so Claude reacts to external events such as CI results, monitoring alerts, or chat messages. The server declares the `claude/channel` capability and you opt it in with the `--channels` flag at startup.

nodes.label: MCP timeout model
nodes.rationale: Several distinct timers bound an MCP server: `MCP_TIMEOUT` for startup, a per-server `timeout` or `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` as a wall-clock limit per tool call, a per-request timer to the first response byte for HTTP/SSE/connector servers, and an idle timeout for a call that sends nothing.

nodes.label: `MCP_TIMEOUT` startup timeout
nodes.rationale: `MCP_TIMEOUT` configures MCP server startup timeout in milliseconds, for example `MCP_TIMEOUT=10000 claude` for a ten-second timeout.

nodes.label: Per-server `timeout` field
nodes.rationale: A `timeout` field in milliseconds in a server's `.mcp.json` entry sets a hard wall-clock limit per tool call for that server, overriding `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`; progress notifications do not extend it. Values below 1000 are ignored and fall through to `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` or its ~28-hour default. Before v2.1.162 such values were floored to one second.

nodes.label: `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` environment variable
nodes.rationale: `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT` sets the per-tool-call wall-clock limit for servers without their own `timeout`; unset, it defaults to about 28 hours, and that default does not enter the per-request timer comparison.

nodes.label: MCP tool-call idle timeout
nodes.rationale: A tool call whose server sends no response and no progress notification for the idle window aborts with an error rather than waiting for the wall-clock limit. It requires v2.1.187 or later, applies to every server type except IDE and SDK in-process servers, and defaults to five minutes for HTTP/SSE/WebSocket/connector servers and 30 minutes for stdio servers. `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_TOOL_IDLE_TIMEOUT` changes it, or `0` disables the check.

nodes.label: Per-request timer for remote servers
nodes.rationale: For HTTP, SSE, and claude.ai connector servers a second timer covers each request through to the server's first response byte. Claude Code sets it to the greatest of 60 seconds, the tool timeout that applies to the server, and `MCP_TIMEOUT`; a value below 60 seconds does not shorten it. Stdio and WebSocket servers have no per-request timer.

nodes.label: Automatic backgrounding of long tool calls
nodes.rationale: A main-conversation MCP tool call still running after two minutes moves to a background task; Claude gets the task ID immediately and the result arrives as a task notification. Requires v2.1.212 or later; the task shows in `/tasks` and does not survive exiting. `CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_AUTO_BACKGROUND_MS` changes or disables the threshold. Subagent calls, IDE server calls, and non-interactive calls are never backgrounded by default.

nodes.label: Plugin-provided MCP servers
nodes.rationale: Plugins can bundle MCP servers in `.mcp.json` at the plugin root or inline in `plugin.json`; enabling the plugin starts them, and their tools are offered alongside manually configured ones. You add and remove them by installing or uninstalling the plugin, though an installed plugin server can still be toggled off in `/mcp`. Lifecycle events include session startup, `/reload-plugins`, a `/cd` move on v2.1.246+, and on-demand start in web sessions.

nodes.label: Plugin path placeholders
nodes.rationale: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` resolves to the plugin's installation directory, `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` to its persistent state directory, and `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` to the stable project root. Substitution applies to `command`, `args`, `env` for stdio servers and to `url`, `headers`, and `headersHelper` for http/sse/ws servers; before v2.1.195 `headersHelper` passed the placeholder through literally.

nodes.label: Plugin MCP tool and server naming
