nodes.rationale: A plugin-bundled server's tools are callable as `mcp__plugin_<plugin-name>_<server-name>__<tool-name>`, with any character outside `A-Za-z0-9_-` replaced by `_`; a hook matcher written against the bare server key never fires. The server itself registers as `plugin:<plugin-name>:<server-name>`, which is the name to use where a configured server name is expected.

nodes.label: MCP installation scopes
nodes.rationale: MCP servers are configured at three scopes: local (current project only, private, `~/.claude.json`), project (current project, shared via version control, `.mcp.json`), and user (all your projects, private, `~/.claude.json`). Administrators can additionally deploy servers at the enterprise level.

nodes.label: Local scope
nodes.rationale: Local scope is the default: the server loads only in the project where it was added and stays private, stored in `~/.claude.json` under that project's path. Use it for personal development servers, experimental configurations, or credentials you do not want in version control. It is distinct from general local settings in `.claude/settings.local.json`.

nodes.label: Project scope
nodes.rationale: Project-scoped servers live in a `.mcp.json` file at the project root and are meant to be checked into version control so the whole team gets the same MCP tools. Claude Code prompts for approval in interactive sessions before using them, resettable with `claude mcp reset-project-choices`; `claude -p`, Agent SDK, and cloud sessions cannot show that prompt and load them without asking.

nodes.label: User scope
nodes.rationale: User-scoped servers are stored in `~/.claude.json` and are available across all projects on your machine while staying private to your account — suited to personal utility servers and development tools you use everywhere.

nodes.label: Scope hierarchy and precedence
nodes.rationale: When one server is defined in more than one place Claude Code connects once, using the whole entry from the highest-precedence source with no field merging: local, then project, then user, then plugin-provided servers, then claude.ai connectors. The three scopes match duplicates by name; plugins and connectors match by endpoint.

nodes.label: `--strict-mcp-config`
nodes.rationale: Starting a session with `--strict-mcp-config` makes Claude Code use only the MCP servers passed with `--mcp-config`. Skipping the approval prompt for the project-scoped servers it is not loading requires v2.1.246 or later; before that a strict session still waited on approval, leaving background sessions stuck at startup.

nodes.label: `.mcp.json` project configuration file
nodes.rationale: `.mcp.json` at the project root holds project-scoped servers under an `mcpServers` key in a standardized format, created or updated automatically by `claude mcp add --scope project`, and intended to be committed.

nodes.label: Environment variable expansion in `.mcp.json`
nodes.rationale: `.mcp.json` supports `${VAR}` and `${VAR:-default}` expansion in `command`, `args`, `env`, `url`, and `headers`, letting teams share one configuration while keeping machine-specific paths and secrets out of it. An unset variable with no default still loads the config, with the `${VAR}` text used as-is.

nodes.label: Example: GitHub remote MCP server
nodes.rationale: GitHub's remote MCP server authenticates with a fine-grained personal access token passed as an `Authorization: Bearer` header to `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`. `claude mcp add` saves the configuration without validating credentials, so a placeholder is accepted and the server fails later; verify with `/mcp`, where bad credentials show `failed` plus the HTTP status such as 401.

nodes.label: Example: DBHub PostgreSQL stdio server
nodes.rationale: DBHub (`@bytebase/dbhub`) is an MCP server connecting Claude to a relational database via a connection string passed in `--dsn`. The docs advise using a read-only database user so the queries Claude runs cannot modify data, then confirming with `/mcp` that `db` shows `connected`.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.0 authentication with remote servers
nodes.rationale: Claude Code supports OAuth 2.0 for remote MCP servers: `/mcp` runs the browser sign-in, tokens are stored securely and refreshed automatically, and 'Clear authentication' revokes access. A server returning `WWW-Authenticate` pointing at its authorization server gets the same automatic discovery as any other remote server.

nodes.label: When a 401 or 403 flags a server as needing authentication
nodes.rationale: Claude Code marks a remote server as needing authentication on `401 Unauthorized` or `403 Forbidden`, but not for a claude.ai connector whose 401 comes from claude.ai rejecting your session token, and not for a server whose `Authorization` header you configured — those are reported as failed connections instead. On a 401 for an already signed-in OAuth server Claude Code refreshes the token, reconnects, and retries once.

nodes.label: `claude mcp login` from the command line
nodes.rationale: From v2.1.186, `claude mcp login <name>` runs a configured server's OAuth flow directly from the shell, with `claude mcp logout <name>` clearing stored credentials. As of v2.1.191 it detects a missing local browser (SSH, no display server) and prints the authorization URL for you to paste the redirect URL back; `--no-browser` forces that prompt.

nodes.label: `--callback-port` for a fixed OAuth callback
nodes.rationale: By default Claude Code picks a random available port for the OAuth callback; `--callback-port` fixes it to match a pre-registered redirect URI of the form `http://localhost:PORT/callback`. It can be used alone with dynamic client registration or together with `--client-id`.

nodes.label: Pre-configured OAuth credentials
nodes.rationale: Servers that do not support Dynamic Client Registration need credentials registered through the server's developer portal, passed with `--client-id` and `--client-secret` (masked prompt), via an `oauth` object in `add-json`, or via `MCP_CLIENT_SECRET` in CI. The secret is stored in the system keychain or a credentials file, and these flags apply only to HTTP and SSE transports. Claude Code also supports Client ID Metadata Documents.

nodes.label: `authServerMetadataUrl` discovery override
nodes.rationale: Setting `authServerMetadataUrl` in a server's `oauth` object points Claude Code at a specific OAuth authorization server metadata URL, bypassing the default chain of RFC 9728 protected resource metadata then RFC 8414 authorization server metadata. The URL must use `https://`, and its `scopes_supported` overrides what the upstream server advertises.

nodes.label: `oauth.scopes` scope pinning
nodes.rationale: `oauth.scopes` pins the scopes Claude Code requests as a single space-separated string, the supported way to restrict a server to a security-team-approved subset. As of v2.1.196, when it is unset Claude Code requests the scope from `WWW-Authenticate` or protected resource metadata rather than the full `scopes_supported` catalog, which had caused `invalid_scope` rejections. `offline_access` is appended when advertised, and a 403 `insufficient_scope` re-authenticates with the same pinned scopes.

nodes.label: `headersHelper` dynamic authentication headers
nodes.rationale: For authentication schemes other than OAuth — Kerberos, short-lived tokens, internal SSO — `headersHelper` names a command Claude Code runs at connection time whose stdout JSON object of string pairs is merged into the connection headers. It runs in a shell with a 10-second limit, is re-run fresh on each connection with no caching, overrides same-named static headers, and an `Authorization` it returns suppresses the OAuth fallback.

nodes.label: Where the `headersHelper` command runs
nodes.rationale: The helper's working directory comes from the configuration that declares the server: the plugin root for a plugin (v2.1.195+), the project directory for a project `.mcp.json` or local-scope server, the session's primary working directory for an in-project agent file, SDK or `--mcp-config` server, and your configuration directory (`~/.claude` unless `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set) for user-scope, managed MCP, connectors, and outside agent files.

nodes.label: Credential variables stripped from an untrusted helper
nodes.rationale: A `headersHelper` supplied by a repository or plugin is a command you did not write, so Claude Code runs it without credential-looking variables from your environment — any name containing `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD`, `KEY`, or `AUTH` in either case, plus a fixed list such as `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS`, excepting Git's `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>`. Stripping applies to project `.mcp.json`, plugin, and in-project agent-file servers, not to user/local scope, managed MCP, connectors, SDK, or `--mcp-config` servers.

nodes.label: Folder trust gates `headersHelper` execution
nodes.rationale: Because a `headersHelper` is an arbitrary shell command, Claude Code runs one declared in a project `.mcp.json` or at local scope only after you accept the trust dialog for that project directory. A parent folder's trust and the automatic trust a `claude -p`/SDK session gets for settings hooks do not count; until trusted, the server connects with static headers alone and prints a `headersHelper not run` line. Before v2.1.238 these helpers ran untrusted.

nodes.label: Import MCP servers from Claude Desktop
nodes.rationale: `claude mcp add-from-claude-desktop` reads Claude Desktop's configuration and offers an interactive dialog to select which servers to import. It works only on macOS and WSL, `--scope user` targets the user configuration, and duplicate names get a numerical suffix such as `server_1`.

nodes.label: Server names allow only letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores
nodes.rationale: Server names added through `claude mcp` commands may contain only letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. Claude Desktop does not enforce this, so a name containing a space cannot be imported; the import reports each rejected name and still imports the rest. Before v2.1.205 the first invalid name stopped the whole import.

nodes.label: claude.ai connectors in Claude Code
nodes.rationale: MCP servers added in claude.ai — connectors, managed at claude.ai/customize/connectors — are automatically available in Claude Code when your active authentication method is a claude.ai subscription login. They are not loaded under `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `apiKeyHelper`, a third-party provider, a profile/federation credential, or a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`. Never-used connectors collapse behind a `Show unused connectors` row.

nodes.label: How connectors reach a session
nodes.rationale: Which settings govern a connector depends on how it arrives: terminal, VS Code, JetBrains and Agent SDK sessions fetch them from claude.ai and are governed by this page's settings and managed MCP; cloud sessions get them passed in by the remote host and filtered by allowlist/denylist settings against rewritten URLs; the desktop app's local and SSH sessions get them delivered in-process as `type: "sdk"` servers that no MCP setting reaches.

nodes.label: Organization controls on connector tools
nodes.rationale: An organization can set per-tool controls on claude.ai connectors, read at startup and enforced locally. A tool set to `ask` prompts on every call with 'Your organization requires approval for this tool', even in `acceptEdits`, `auto`, and `bypassPermissions` modes, with no remember option, and is denied in `dontAsk` mode. A tool set to `blocked` is filtered out before Claude sees it, in Claude Code, the desktop app, and claude.ai chat alike.

nodes.label: Disabling claude.ai connectors
nodes.rationale: `disableClaudeAiConnectors: true` turns off the connectors Claude Code fetches itself, with any-source-true semantics so a project-level `false` cannot re-enable what a user or policy level `true` disabled; `--mcp-config` servers are unaffected. `ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false` has the same effect for one shell session, and individual connectors can be blocked by name or URL pattern in `deniedMcpServers`.

nodes.label: Claude Code as an MCP server (`claude mcp serve`)
nodes.rationale: `claude mcp serve` runs Claude Code itself as a stdio MCP server other applications can connect to. It prints nothing on start — a silent, blocked terminal means it is waiting for a client. The `command` field must reference the Claude Code executable (use `which claude` for a full path) or you get `spawn claude ENOENT`, and the client is responsible for user confirmation of individual tool calls.

nodes.label: MCP output limits and warnings
nodes.rationale: Claude Code warns when any MCP tool output exceeds 10,000 tokens and limits output to 25,000 tokens by default; `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` raises the maximum while the warning threshold is fixed. The variable applies to tools that do not declare their own limit, and tools returning image data are always subject to it.

nodes.label: `anthropic/maxResultSizeChars` per-tool annotation
nodes.rationale: An MCP server can set `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` in a tool's `tools/list` entry to raise that tool's persist-to-disk threshold, up to a hard ceiling of 500,000 characters, for inherently large outputs such as database schemas or file trees. It applies independently of `MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS` for text content and has no effect on image content.

nodes.label: Tool input schemas with a root-level combinator
nodes.rationale: The Claude API rejects `anyOf`, `oneOf`, or `allOf` at a schema root, so Claude Code flattens such a schema into a single object and prepends a sentence to the tool description naming which parameter groups belong together — merging properties from every branch and enforcing `required` only for `allOf`. Servers must keep validating the combination themselves. Versions before v2.1.195 skipped every such tool.

nodes.label: Excluding tools with invalid input schemas
nodes.rationale: Because the Claude API rejects a whole request when any one tool schema fails, Claude Code runs two of the API's checks itself at load time and excludes each failing tool: top-level property names must be 1-64 ASCII letters/digits/`_`/`.`/`-`, and the schema must validate against JSON Schema draft 2020-12 when it declares that dialect or none. It runs them after the combinator rewrite and tells Claude which tools it excluded and why.

nodes.label: Feature-flag fetching gates some MCP behavior
nodes.rationale: Some MCP behavior depends on feature flags Claude Code fetches from Anthropic. With flag fetching off, or on a machine such as an air-gapped one whose flags never arrived, Claude Code still runs the invalid-schema checks and logs which tool would be rejected but sends the schema anyway, and it falls back to the v1 client runtime. The root-level combinator handling keeps its own behavior in that state.

nodes.label: `anthropic/requiresUserInteraction` annotation
nodes.rationale: Setting `_meta["anthropic/requiresUserInteraction"]` to the JSON boolean `true` makes Claude Code show that tool's permission prompt on every call — even in `acceptEdits`, `auto`, and `bypassPermissions` modes, with no 'don't ask again' and no allow-rule bypass, and denied in `dontAsk` mode. Under `--permission-prompt-tool` an `allow` is converted to a deny; the Agent SDK's `canUseTool` callback can still approve. Requires v2.1.199 or later.

nodes.label: Server-declared `_meta` tool annotations
nodes.rationale: MCP server authors influence Claude Code's handling of individual tools through `_meta` entries in the `tools/list` response: `anthropic/maxResultSizeChars`, `anthropic/requiresUserInteraction`, and `anthropic/alwaysLoad`.

nodes.label: MCP elicitation requests
nodes.rationale: Servers can request structured input mid-task via elicitation; Claude Code shows an interactive dialog automatically with no configuration. Form mode renders server-defined fields; URL mode opens a browser URL, passed as a command-line argument with a length cap (~8,000 characters plain, ~4,000 when heavily percent-escaped, since each escaped character counts four times) beyond which you can only decline. The `Elicitation` hook can auto-respond.

nodes.label: MCP resources via @ mentions
nodes.rationale: Servers can expose resources referenced like files: type `@` to list them, and use `@server:protocol://resource/path` (for example `@github:issue://123`) to reference one, including several in one prompt. Resources are fetched automatically and included as attachments, paths are fuzzy-searchable, and Claude Code provides list/read tools when servers support them.

nodes.label: MCP tool search
nodes.rationale: Tool search keeps MCP context usage low by deferring tool definitions until Claude needs them: only tool names and server instructions load at session start, so adding servers has minimal context impact and there is no fixed per-server tool cap — the practical limit is your context budget. It is unsupported on Microsoft Foundry deployments hosted on Azure, which reject it server-side, and requires a model supporting `tool_reference` blocks.

nodes.label: `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` configuration
nodes.rationale: Tool search is on by default and disabled when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a non-first-party host. `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH` takes `true` (defer all), `false` (load all upfront), `auto` (defer once definitions reach 10% of the context window), or `auto:N` for a custom percentage. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS` keeps it off and cannot be overridden; the `ToolSearch` tool itself can be denied in permissions.

nodes.label: `alwaysLoad` exemption from deferral
nodes.rationale: Setting `alwaysLoad: true` on a server, available on all server types, loads every one of its tools into context at session start regardless of `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`; a server can also mark individual tools with `"anthropic/alwaysLoad": true`. It also makes startup wait for that server's tools, capped at the standard 5-second connect timeout, so it is meant for a small number of tools Claude needs every turn.

nodes.label: Server instructions for MCP server authors
nodes.rationale: With tool search enabled the server instructions field becomes more useful: it should explain what category of tasks the tools handle, when Claude should search for them, and the server's key capabilities, much as skills do. Claude Code truncates tool descriptions and server instructions at 2KB each, so critical details belong near the start.

nodes.label: MCP prompts as slash commands
nodes.rationale: Servers can expose prompts that appear as commands: typing `/` lists each as `/servername:promptname (MCP)`, and `/mcp__servername__promptname` also runs it. Arguments are passed space-separated and split on whitespace, so each is a single token; in the `mcp__` form any server-name character outside `A-Za-z0-9_-` is replaced with `_` while the prompt name is used as declared.

nodes.label: Managed MCP configuration
nodes.rationale: For organizations needing centralized control, managed MCP configuration covers deploying a fixed server set with `managed-mcp.json`, restricting servers with `allowedMcpServers` and `deniedMcpServers`, and what users see when a server is blocked.

nodes.label: Two cross-session memory mechanisms
nodes.rationale: Each Claude Code session begins with a fresh context window, and exactly two mechanisms carry knowledge across sessions: CLAUDE.md files that the user writes, and auto memory notes Claude writes for itself. Both are loaded at the start of every conversation.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md files
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md files are markdown files a user writes to give Claude persistent instructions for a project, a personal workflow, or an organization; Claude reads them at the start of every session. They hold instructions and rules — coding standards, workflows, project architecture.

nodes.label: Auto memory
nodes.rationale: Auto memory lets Claude accumulate learnings and patterns across sessions with no manual effort, writing notes about the user's preferences and corrections. It is scoped per repository, shared across worktrees, and on by default; Claude does not save something every session, only what it judges useful in a future conversation.

nodes.label: Memory is context, not enforced configuration
nodes.rationale: Claude treats both memory systems as context rather than enforced configuration, so there is no guarantee of strict compliance. The more specific and concise the instructions, the more consistently Claude follows them.

nodes.label: PreToolUse hook as hard enforcement
nodes.rationale: To block an action regardless of what Claude decides, the docs direct users to a PreToolUse hook instead of an instruction file. Hooks execute as shell commands at fixed lifecycle events and apply regardless of Claude's judgement, which makes them the right home for anything that must run before every commit or after each file edit.

nodes.label: When to add something to CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md is the place to write down what you would otherwise re-explain: add an entry when Claude repeats a mistake, when code review catches something Claude should have known, when you retype a correction from a previous session, or when a new teammate would need the same context. Multi-step procedures or instructions relevant to only part of the codebase belong in a skill or a path-scoped rule instead.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md scope hierarchy
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md files live at four scopes listed in load order from broadest to most specific — managed policy, user instructions, project instructions, and local instructions — so a project instruction appears in context after a user instruction.

nodes.label: Managed policy CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: An organization-wide CLAUDE.md deployed at /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md (macOS), /etc/claude-code/CLAUDE.md (Linux and WSL) or C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\CLAUDE.md (Windows) applies to every session on the machine in every repository, is distributed via MDM/Group Policy/Ansible, and cannot be excluded by individual settings.

nodes.label: User instructions (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md holds personal preferences that apply to all of a user's projects — code styling preferences, personal tooling shortcuts — and is shared with nobody else.

nodes.label: Project instructions (./CLAUDE.md)
nodes.rationale: A project CLAUDE.md lives at ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md and carries team-shared instructions — build and test commands, coding standards, architectural decisions, naming conventions — distributed through version control, so it should hold project-level standards rather than personal preferences.

nodes.label: Local instructions (CLAUDE.local.md)
nodes.rationale: ./CLAUDE.local.md holds personal project-specific preferences such as sandbox URLs or preferred test data and should be gitignored. Because it is gitignored it exists only in the worktree where it was created; sharing personal instructions across worktrees requires importing a file from the home directory instead.

nodes.label: /init generates a starting CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: Running /init makes Claude analyze the codebase and write a CLAUDE.md with the build commands, test instructions and conventions it discovers; if one already exists, /init suggests improvements rather than overwriting it. It also reads Cursor rules (.cursor/rules/, .cursorrules) and Copilot rules (.github/copilot-instructions.md) and folds the relevant parts in.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT interactive init
nodes.rationale: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 turns /init into an interactive multi-phase flow: it asks which artifacts to set up (CLAUDE.md files, skills, hooks), explores the codebase with a subagent, fills gaps with follow-up questions, and presents a reviewable proposal before writing files. It also makes /init read AGENTS.md, .devin/rules/, .windsurf/rules/ or .windsurfrules, and .clinerules.

nodes.label: Writing effective instructions
nodes.rationale: Because CLAUDE.md is context rather than enforced configuration, how it is written affects adherence: use markdown headers and bullets for structure, and make instructions concrete enough to verify ("Use 2-space indentation" over "Format code properly"). Contradicting rules across files let Claude pick one arbitrarily, so files should be reviewed periodically for conflicts.

nodes.label: 200-line CLAUDE.md size target
nodes.rationale: The docs set a target of under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file, because CLAUDE.md loads into the context window at the start of every session and longer files consume more context while reducing adherence.

nodes.label: Oversized CLAUDE.md problem
nodes.rationale: A CLAUDE.md over 200 lines consumes more context and may reduce adherence, and one over 4 MiB is skipped entirely. Splitting into @path imports helps organization but does NOT reduce context, since imported files still load at launch.

nodes.label: 4 MiB CLAUDE.md load ceiling
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads a CLAUDE.md file of up to 4 MiB in full and skips a larger one outright. This ceiling is distinct from the MEMORY.md read limit, which applies only to the auto-memory index.

nodes.label: @path import syntax
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md files import other files with @path/to/import syntax; imports are expanded and loaded into context at launch. Relative paths resolve against the importing file rather than the working directory, imports recurse to a maximum depth of four hops, and parsing skips markdown code spans and fenced blocks so a backticked `@README` stays literal.

nodes.label: External-import approval dialog
nodes.rationale: An import in a project-level memory file is external when its path resolves outside the working directory. The first time Claude Code meets external imports in a project it shows an approval dialog listing the files, and declining disables them permanently without re-prompting — a protection against files other people commit to a shared project. Imports in user-scope files such as ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md are trusted and load without the dialog.

nodes.label: Cowork import and symlink restrictions
nodes.rationale: In Cowork sessions on the desktop, Claude Code skips any import in a user-scope file resolving outside the session's working directory and loads the rest of the file; it also skips a ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md that is itself a symlink or hard link, and a symlinked ~/.claude/rules/ directory or rule file pointing outside the working directory.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md interoperability
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md. A repository already using AGENTS.md should add a CLAUDE.md containing `@AGENTS.md` (optionally with Claude-specific instructions appended below), or symlink the two with `ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` when no extra content is needed. On Windows a symlink needs Administrator or Developer Mode, so the import is preferred there.

nodes.label: /import for other agents' configuration
nodes.rationale: The /import command brings a supported coding agent's configuration into Claude Code: it appends a one-time copy of instruction files such as AGENTS.md to the matching CLAUDE.md and carries over MCP servers, commands, subagents and skills. It requires Claude Code v2.1.213 or later.

nodes.label: Directory-hierarchy load order
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md from the working directory and every directory above it, concatenating all discovered files rather than letting them override each other. Content is ordered from filesystem root down to the working directory, and within a directory CLAUDE.local.md is appended after CLAUDE.md, so the most local and most personal instructions are read last.

nodes.label: On-demand subdirectory memory files
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE.local.md files discovered in subdirectories below the working directory are not loaded at launch; they are included only when Claude reads files in those subdirectories.

nodes.label: HTML comments stripped from context
nodes.rationale: Block-level HTML comments in CLAUDE.md files are stripped before the content is injected into Claude's context, so they can carry notes for human maintainers without spending context tokens. Comments inside code blocks are preserved, and comments remain visible when the file is opened with the Read tool.

nodes.label: Memory from --add-dir directories
nodes.rationale: By default CLAUDE.md files from directories added with --add-dir are not loaded. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1 loads CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/*.md and CLAUDE.local.md from the additional directory; CLAUDE.local.md is skipped if `local` is excluded from --setting-sources.

nodes.label: .claude/rules/ project rules
nodes.rationale: The .claude/rules/ directory organizes instructions into one markdown file per topic, discovered recursively so rules can be grouped into subdirectories. Rules without `paths` frontmatter load at launch with the same priority as .claude/CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Path-scoped rules (paths frontmatter)
nodes.rationale: A rule with a YAML `paths` field of glob patterns applies only when Claude works with matching files, reducing noise and saving context. Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude READS a matching file, not on every tool use; as of v2.1.198 matching also works when the file is reached through a symlinked path into the project.

nodes.label: Brace-expansion pattern budget
nodes.rationale: Each brace group multiplies expanded patterns, so a rule's whole `paths` list shares one budget of 1,000 expanded patterns and 4 MiB; patterns without braces do not count against it. Any pattern that would exceed the budget is used unexpanded, and its literal braces then match no files. Before v2.1.217 a paths value with many brace groups stalled or crashed the CLI at startup.

nodes.label: Invalid bracket-expression globs
nodes.rationale: Glob syntax reads `[` as the start of a bracket expression, so a pattern like `photos [2024/**` is invalid: it matches nothing while the rule's other patterns keep working, and a literal bracket must be escaped as `photos \[2024/**`. Before v2.1.207 one invalid pattern made the Read tool fail for every file the rule was evaluated against.

nodes.label: Sharing rules across projects with symlinks
nodes.rationale: The .claude/rules/ directory supports symlinks, so one shared rule set can be linked into many projects — both whole directories and individual files. Symlinks are resolved and loaded normally, and circular symlinks are detected and handled gracefully.

nodes.label: User-level rules (~/.claude/rules/)
nodes.rationale: Personal rules in ~/.claude/rules/ apply to every project on the machine and suit preferences that are not project-specific. They are loaded before project rules, which gives project rules higher priority.

nodes.label: Skills as the on-demand alternative
nodes.rationale: Rules load into context every session or when matching files are opened; skills load only when invoked or when Claude judges them relevant to the prompt. Task-specific instructions that need not be in context all the time therefore belong in a skill rather than a rule.

nodes.label: --setting-sources exclusion of project rules
nodes.rationale: Project rules are skipped when `project` is excluded from --setting-sources. Before v2.1.211 the on-demand rules — path-scoped rules and rules in nested .claude/rules/ directories — loaded even when project was excluded.

nodes.label: Managed settings vs managed CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: Managed settings are enforced by the client regardless of what Claude decides, and own blocking tools/commands/paths (permissions.deny), sandbox isolation, env and provider routing, and login restrictions. Managed CLAUDE.md owns behavioral guidance — code style, compliance reminders — and is not a hard enforcement layer.

nodes.label: claudeMd key in managed settings
nodes.rationale: The claudeMd key puts managed CLAUDE.md content directly inside managed-settings.json instead of deploying a separate file. It has the same precedence as a managed CLAUDE.md file — loading before user and project CLAUDE.md — and is honored only in managed and policy settings; setting it in user, project or local settings has no effect.

nodes.label: claudeMdExcludes
nodes.rationale: In large monorepos claudeMdExcludes skips irrelevant ancestor CLAUDE.md files and rules directories by path or glob, matched against absolute paths; it can be set at any settings layer and the arrays merge across layers. For a rules file reached through a symlink, a pattern matching either the .claude/rules/ path or the link target excludes it — before v2.1.239 only the link target worked.

nodes.label: Four auto-memory note types
nodes.rationale: Claude saves four kinds of auto-memory note, recorded as a `type` field in the memory file's frontmatter: `user` (role, expertise, working preferences), `feedback` (corrections given and approaches confirmed), `project` (ongoing work, deadlines and decisions not derivable from code or git history), and `reference` (where to find information outside the project).

nodes.label: What auto memory deliberately skips
nodes.rationale: Claude skips saving anything it can derive from the codebase — architecture, file paths, debugging fixes — and anything the project's CLAUDE.md files already say. It also does not save every session, deciding instead whether the information would be useful in a future conversation.

nodes.label: Enabling and disabling auto memory
nodes.rationale: Auto memory is on by default. The /memory toggle writes autoMemoryEnabled to ~/.claude/settings.json; setting autoMemoryEnabled to false in a project's settings turns it off for that project, and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 disables it by environment variable.

nodes.label: Per-project memory directory
nodes.rationale: Each project gets its own memory directory at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/, where <project> is derived from the git repository, so all worktrees and subdirectories of one repo share a single auto-memory directory; outside a git repo the project root is used instead.

nodes.label: autoMemoryDirectory setting
nodes.rationale: autoMemoryDirectory relocates auto memory; its value must be an absolute path or start with ~/. It is read from any settings scope (user, project, local, policy or --settings), and when set in a project's .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json it is honored under the same workspace-trust rule as hooks in settings files.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME
nodes.rationale: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME beside CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR makes Claude Code use that name as the <project> directory under <config dir>/projects/ whatever repository it is launched in, so every project launched with that config directory shares one auto-memory directory. Requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later.

nodes.label: MEMORY.md index
nodes.rationale: MEMORY.md is the index of the memory directory — one line per memory — and is the only memory file loaded into every session. Claude reads and writes it throughout a session to track what is stored where, keeping it concise by moving detail into topic files.

nodes.label: Auto-memory topic files
nodes.rationale: The memory directory holds one topic file per memory beside MEMORY.md, such as user_role.md or feedback_testing.md. Claude Code does not load topic files at startup; Claude reads them on demand with its standard file tools when it needs the information.

nodes.label: 200-line / 25KB MEMORY.md read limit
nodes.rationale: Only the first 200 lines of MEMORY.md, or the first 25KB — whichever comes first — are loaded at the start of every conversation; content beyond that threshold is not loaded at session start. The limit applies only to MEMORY.md, not to CLAUDE.md.

nodes.label: Over-limit MEMORY.md write error
nodes.rationale: After Claude writes MEMORY.md, Claude Code measures it against the 200-line and 25KB limits: near a limit it reminds Claude to shorten (one line per entry, detail into topic files, merge or drop stale entries); over a limit the write still succeeds but Claude Code returns an error telling Claude to rewrite the index, because everything past the limit is dropped on the next load.

nodes.label: Memory excluded from the retention sweep
nodes.rationale: Claude Code deletes old session transcripts after the cleanupPeriodDays retention period but excludes the memory directory from that sweep; MEMORY.md and the topic files stay until the user or Claude edits or deletes them.

nodes.label: Subagent auto memory
nodes.rationale: The main conversation's auto memory is not loaded into subagents; the exception is a fork, which inherits the parent conversation and system prompt. A subagent can maintain its own auto memory via the subagent `memory` field, in a separate directory.

nodes.label: `modified` frontmatter timestamp
nodes.rationale: When Claude writes a memory file that begins with YAML frontmatter, Claude Code records the write time in a `modified` field as an ISO 8601 timestamp, showing how current the fact is to both the user and Claude on read-back. Any file that has frontmatter gets the field on its next write, including files created on earlier versions; Claude Code never adds frontmatter to a file that has none. Requires v2.1.214 or later.

nodes.label: /memory command
nodes.rationale: /memory lists CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md and other memory file locations across user and project scopes — including entries for files that do not exist yet, which are created on selection — toggles auto memory, and offers to open the auto-memory folder. GUI editors open in a separate window and leave the session usable; before v2.1.216 /memory waited for the file to close.

nodes.label: /context memory-files check
nodes.rationale: Running /context and reading the list under **Memory files** is the way to confirm which instruction files actually loaded into the current session. A file missing from that list is invisible to Claude.

nodes.label: Claude not following CLAUDE.md
nodes.rationale: CLAUDE.md content is delivered as a user message AFTER the system prompt, not as part of it, so there is no guarantee of strict compliance — especially for vague or conflicting instructions. Debugging means verifying the file loaded, checking it is in a loaded location, making instructions more specific, and hunting for conflicts across files.

nodes.label: --append-system-prompt
nodes.rationale: For instructions that must sit at the system-prompt level rather than arriving as a user message, --append-system-prompt is the mechanism. It must be passed on every invocation, so it suits scripts and automation better than interactive use.

nodes.label: InstructionsLoaded hook
nodes.rationale: The InstructionsLoaded hook logs exactly which instruction files are loaded, when they load, and why — the recommended tool for debugging path-specific rules and lazily loaded files in subdirectories.

nodes.label: /doctor CLAUDE.md trim check
nodes.rationale: The /doctor checkup proposes trims for a checked-in CLAUDE.md: it cuts content Claude can derive from the codebase — directory layouts, dependency lists, architecture overviews — and keeps pitfalls, rationale, and conventions that differ from tool defaults. The trim check requires Claude Code v2.1.206 or later.

nodes.label: What survives /compact
nodes.rationale: Project-root CLAUDE.md survives compaction — after /compact Claude re-reads it from disk and re-injects it. Nested CLAUDE.md files and rules with `paths:` frontmatter reload only as Claude reads files they apply to, so an instruction that disappeared was either conversation-only, in a nested file not yet reloaded, or a path-scoped rule that has not matched a file since.

nodes.label: Auto memory is machine-local
nodes.rationale: Auto memory is machine-local: all worktrees and subdirectories within the same git repository share one auto memory directory, but the files are not shared across machines or cloud environments.

nodes.label: model setting
nodes.rationale: The `model` setting in Claude Code accepts either a model alias or a model name. A model name is a full Anthropic API model name, an Amazon Bedrock inference profile ARN, a Microsoft Foundry deployment name, or a Google Cloud Agent Platform version name. The setting is an initial selection, not enforcement: users can still open `/model` and pick Default.

nodes.label: Model aliases
nodes.rationale: A model alias selects model settings without remembering exact version numbers. Aliases point to the recommended version for your provider and update over time; to pin a specific version, use the full model name such as `claude-opus-5` or the corresponding `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` environment variable.

nodes.label: `default` special value
nodes.rationale: `default` is a special value that clears any model override and reverts to the runtime default for your account. The docs state explicitly that it is not itself a model alias.

nodes.label: `best` alias
nodes.rationale: `best` uses the latest Fable model where it is available to you, and otherwise the same model as `opus`.

nodes.label: `fable` alias
nodes.rationale: `fable` uses the latest Fable model for the hardest and longest-running tasks. Unless `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` is set, it resolves to Fable 5.1; before v2.1.255 it resolved to Fable 5.

nodes.label: `sonnet` alias
nodes.rationale: `sonnet` uses the latest Sonnet model for daily coding tasks. Its resolved version is provider-dependent: Sonnet 5 on the Anthropic API, Sonnet 4.6 on Claude Platform on AWS, and Sonnet 4.5 on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry.

nodes.label: `opus` alias
nodes.rationale: `opus` uses the latest Opus model for complex reasoning tasks. It resolves to Opus 5 on the Anthropic API, Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and to Opus 4.6 on Microsoft Foundry.

nodes.label: `haiku` alias
nodes.rationale: `haiku` uses the fast and efficient Haiku model for simple tasks. Haiku models are always available under organization model restrictions and cannot be disabled, so every member keeps at least one usable model.

nodes.label: `[1m]` alias suffix
nodes.rationale: `sonnet[1m]` and `opus[1m]` select a 1 million token context window for long sessions, and the suffix can also be appended to a full model name such as `claude-opus-4-8[1m]`. `sonnet[1m]` has no effect when `sonnet` already resolves to Sonnet 5 with its native 1M window, but behind an LLM gateway it selects the 1M window for Sonnet 5.

nodes.label: `opusplan` alias
nodes.rationale: `opusplan` is a special mode that uses `opus` during plan mode and then switches to `sonnet` for execution.

nodes.label: Provider-dependent alias resolution
nodes.rationale: The version an alias resolves to depends on the provider: Anthropic API gives Opus 5 / Sonnet 5, Claude Platform on AWS Opus 5 / Sonnet 4.6, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform Opus 5 / Sonnet 4.5, and Microsoft Foundry Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.5. Where an alias resolves to an older model, newer models are reachable by full model name or an `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` variable.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL routes, does not select
nodes.rationale: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` changes where requests are sent, not which model answers them; routing Claude through an LLM gateway is a separate concern from model selection.

nodes.label: Minimum Claude Code version per model
nodes.rationale: Each model requires a minimum Claude Code version: Opus 5 needs v2.1.219 or later, Sonnet 5 v2.1.197, Opus 4.8 v2.1.154, Fable 5.1 v2.1.255, and Fable 5 v2.1.170. `claude update` upgrades; a request for a model from an older version fails with 'Claude Code does not support this model'.

nodes.label: Fable models in Claude Code
nodes.rationale: Claude Fable 5.1 and Fable 5 are the most capable models in Claude Code, suited to tasks larger than a single sitting: they sustain long autonomous sessions, investigate before acting, and verify their work more often than smaller models. Fable 5.1 is the newer release.

nodes.label: Fable must be selected explicitly
nodes.rationale: Neither Fable model is the account-type default on any plan or provider. Fable 5.1 is selected with `/model fable` or `claude --model fable`; Fable 5 is selected by model ID (`/model claude-fable-5` on the Anthropic API, or the provider's Fable 5 ID pinned with `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL` elsewhere).

nodes.label: One-time migration of a saved Fable 5 selection
nodes.rationale: If user settings hold `claude-fable-5` or `claude-fable-5[1m]` and you connect to the Anthropic API directly, the first run of v2.1.255 or later rewrites that saved value to the `fable` or `fable[1m]` alias and shows `(auto-updated)` once in the startup model line. A `claude-fable-5` value in project, local, or managed settings is left as it is.

nodes.label: Fable and usage credits
nodes.rationale: Depending on plan and seat tier, Fable usage can bill to usage credits instead of drawing on the plan's included limits. When it does, the `/model` picker shows 'Requires usage credits' on the Fable row.

nodes.label: Usage-credit consent prompt
nodes.rationale: In interactive sessions Claude Code shows a consent prompt before a Fable request bills usage credits; Enterprise plans with organization billing do not see it. Dismissing it keeps the current model in the picker, or continues the turn on the default model mid-session, and after you once choose to continue on Fable the prompt is not shown again.

nodes.label: dialogExpiry deadline for an unattended consent prompt
nodes.rationale: With Remote Control connected, in a background session, or in an agent-team teammate's session nobody may be at the terminal, so the mid-session consent prompt is held for the `dialogExpiry` deadline (five minutes by default). If unanswered, Claude Code ends the turn without sending the request, adds a transcript notice, leaves the model selection unchanged, and asks again on the next message.

nodes.label: Non-interactive credit billing without consent
nodes.rationale: In non-interactive mode with the `-p` flag and through the Agent SDK, Claude Code never shows the consent prompt: a Fable request that would bill to usage credits is billed without asking.

nodes.label: Server-side Fable availability check
nodes.rationale: On the Anthropic API the `/model` picker lists a Fable model only after the server reports it available for your organization, but typing `/model fable` or a Fable model ID checks availability with the server directly, so the selection can succeed before the picker lists the entry.

nodes.label: Getting the most from Fable
nodes.rationale: The guidance for Fable is to describe the outcome rather than the steps (and set a goal to hold it there), hand it ambiguous problems such as root-cause investigations and architecture decisions, skip verification reminders because it verifies its own work, and give it larger tasks you would otherwise break into pieces.

nodes.label: Model selection precedence order
nodes.rationale: Model configuration is resolved in priority order: `/model` during a session, `claude --model` at startup, the `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` environment variable, the `model` field in a settings file, and finally `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL` as the default for new sessions.

nodes.label: `/model` picker
nodes.rationale: `/model` with no argument opens the picker: `Enter` switches the model and saves it as your default by writing the `model` field in user settings, while `s` switches for the session only. Typing `/model <name>` behaves like `Enter`, except in non-interactive mode with `-p`, where the choice applies to the current session only.

nodes.label: `--model` and ANTHROPIC_MODEL are session-scoped
nodes.rationale: The `--model` flag and the `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` environment variable apply only to the session launched with them, so running different models in different terminals at the same time means launching each with its own `--model` flag rather than switching with `/model`.

nodes.label: Prices shown in the model picker
nodes.rationale: Prices appear in the `/model` picker only when Claude Code talks to the Anthropic API directly or through a proxying LLM gateway, and each row shows the price of the model that row selects. On third-party providers and the Claude apps gateway no price is shown because the provider decides billing; the price is a display label only.

nodes.label: Model on a resumed session
nodes.rationale: Sessions resumed with `--resume`, `--continue`, or `/resume` keep the model recorded in the transcript, so another session's `/model` choice cannot change it. If that model is retired or excluded by `availableModels` the session falls through to normal precedence, and on providers using provider-specific deployment IDs the transcript model is not restored at all.

nodes.label: Startup header names the settings source
nodes.rationale: When the active model at startup comes from project or managed settings rather than your own selection, the startup header shows which settings file set it; `/model` overrides for the session and the project or managed setting reapplies on the next launch.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST precedence
nodes.rationale: On platforms that embed Claude Code and set `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST`, the host's model configuration takes precedence over managed model settings, while a managed `availableModels` allowlist stays in force unless the host supplies its own.

nodes.label: Model-string validation on switch
nodes.rationale: A model switch requested through the Agent SDK `setModel()` or a host app is checked (v2.1.200+) against recognized strings on the Anthropic API — an alias, a picker entry, any name starting with `claude-`, or a configured custom option / `modelOverrides` value — and an unrecognized string is rejected with `Model "<name>" is not a recognized model id.` while the session keeps its model. The check does not cover `--model`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, the `model` setting, or non-Anthropic providers.

nodes.label: Retirement and remap warning
nodes.rationale: When the requested model has a scheduled retirement date or is automatically remapped to a newer version, Claude Code warns and names the requested model — as a startup notice interactively, and from v2.1.182 on stderr in non-interactive mode with the default text output. The warning covers a `model` in subagent frontmatter, is suppressed for JSON output formats, and the actual model is then read from the result message's `modelUsage` field.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL
nodes.rationale: `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL` (v2.1.236+) chooses the model new sessions start on, but only when `--model`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, a settings `model` value, and an organization default all fail to select one. It is ignored when set to `default`, `inherit`, `opusplan`, or `haiku`, when `enforceAvailableModels` is on, when an allowlist or organization restriction excludes the model, or when the model is unavailable to the account.

nodes.label: availableModels allowlist
nodes.rationale: Enterprise administrators use `availableModels` in managed or policy settings to restrict which models users can select. Entries match a model family (`sonnet`), a version prefix (`claude-sonnet-4-5`), or a full model ID; a version prefix also matches later IDs that extend it, so `claude-fable-5` permits both Fable 5 and Fable 5.1 while `claude-fable-5-1` permits Fable 5.1 only.

nodes.label: Surfaces the allowlist applies to
nodes.rationale: When set, `availableModels` applies everywhere a user can specify a model: the main session model (`/model`, `--model`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, the `model` setting, `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL`, the resumed model), alias resolution through the `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` variables, `/fast`, subagent and teammate models including `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL`, skill and command `model` frontmatter, `advisorModel` and `--advisor`, and the background-agent dispatch picker.

nodes.label: Newest-permitted-version alias substitution
nodes.rationale: On the Anthropic API and Claude Platform on AWS, a family alias resolves to its usual model when the allowlist permits it; when blocked, Claude Code substitutes the newest permitted version of that family and shows a notice naming both models. With `["sonnet", "claude-opus-4-6"]`, `/model opus` selects Opus 4.6. The substitution needs a permitted version to land on, otherwise the alias follows ordinary rejection behavior.

nodes.label: Handling of a blocked model selection
nodes.rationale: A blocked selection is handled by where it was set: `/model` is rejected with an error; `--model`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` or the `model` setting are replaced at startup with a warning and the session starts on the default; `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL` is ignored; a subagent or teammate override runs on a fallback model rather than failing; a skill or command override is ignored and it runs on the session model; `advisorModel` disables the advisor; and `--advisor` exits with an error at launch.

nodes.label: Allowlist checks on Claude Code's own model changes
nodes.rationale: Model changes Claude Code makes on your behalf are checked the same way: fallback-chain entries outside the allowlist are dropped, plan-mode upgrades use the newest permitted version of the upgrade family (or are skipped on provider-specific IDs), an automatic model fallback whose target is excluded does not run so the request ends in refusal, the auto-mode classifier falls back off Sonnet 5, and enabling fast mode is refused.

nodes.label: Allowlist surface coverage
nodes.rationale: Every surface enforces the allowlist it receives; what differs is which delivery mechanism reaches each surface. Model pickers on claude.ai and in the Desktop app hide or grey out excluded models as a convenience, but enforcement happens in the session.

nodes.label: Server-managed settings delivery
nodes.rationale: Server-managed settings from the admin console are enforced on CLI and IDE, Desktop local sessions, web/mobile/cloud sessions, and the Agent SDK, but are not delivered to Cowork or to third-party providers. They also require the session to authenticate with an eligible login or key, so fleets using an `apiKeyHelper` script must use MDM instead.

nodes.label: MDM / managed settings file delivery
nodes.rationale: MDM or managed settings files are enforced on CLI and IDE, Desktop local sessions, the Agent SDK and non-interactive runs, and Cowork where deployed, but are not delivered to Anthropic-hosted web/mobile/cloud sessions — only to self-hosted runner images. This is the delivery path to use on third-party providers, which never receive server-managed settings.

nodes.label: availableModels leaves Default alone
nodes.rationale: On its own, `availableModels` leaves the Default option on the account's runtime default until `enforceAvailableModels` is also set. An empty `availableModels` array never engages Default-model enforcement: named selections are blocked but the account-type Default remains usable.

nodes.label: enforceAvailableModels
nodes.rationale: `enforceAvailableModels: true` alongside a non-empty `availableModels` in managed settings (v2.1.175+) extends the allowlist to the Default option: when the account-type or organization default is not allowlisted, Default resolves to the first `availableModels` entry naming an allowed, available model. If no entry resolves, enforcement is skipped with a `--debug`-only warning, so keep at least one guaranteed-available entry.

nodes.label: Combining settings to control the model users run on
nodes.rationale: Fully controlling the model experience takes four settings together: `availableModels` restricts which named models users can switch to, `enforceAvailableModels` extends that to the Default option, `model` sets the initial selection, and the `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL` variables pin which version each permitted alias resolves to.

nodes.label: availableModels merge behavior
nodes.rationale: When applied managed settings define `availableModels`, that list alone applies — user, project and local entries cannot extend it and lists never merge across managed sources; otherwise lower-scope lists are concatenated and deduplicated. Within the effective list, a specific entry disables that family's wildcard, so `["sonnet", "claude-sonnet-4-5"]` allows only Sonnet 4.5 versions.

nodes.label: Mantle model IDs in availableModels
nodes.rationale: With the Amazon Bedrock Mantle endpoint enabled, `availableModels` entries starting with `anthropic.` are added to the `/model` picker as custom options and routed to Mantle — an exception to third-party alias matching. A Mantle ID embeds a family name, so it counts as a specific entry and disables that family's wildcard.

nodes.label: Organization model restrictions
nodes.rationale: Enterprise admins disable individual models in the claude.ai admin console; the restriction rides with account entitlements at authentication and the server enforces it independently at session creation (v2.1.187+). Restrictions apply org-wide or per role, Haiku can never be disabled, changes take effect on new requests within about a minute, and they reach only Anthropic API and LLM gateway sessions.

nodes.label: Organization default model
nodes.rationale: Enterprise admins can set a Claude Code default model org-wide or per custom role (v2.1.196+); the Default option then resolves to it and the picker's Default row shows the label 'Org default'. It is a starting point, not a restriction: `--model`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, managed/`--settings` `model`, and user/project/local `model` values all take precedence, and it is read once at startup.

nodes.label: Organization default overriding user selection
nodes.rationale: Admins can configure the organization default to override user selection: it then outranks the `model` value in user, project and local settings, so a `/model` choice applies for the current session and the org default returns on the next launch, with `/model` showing 'Your organization's default (<model>) applies on restart'. `--model`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, managed settings and `--settings` still take precedence, and availability is limited.

nodes.label: Organization effort limits
nodes.rationale: Enterprise admins can cap the maximum effort level per model for each custom role (v2.1.195+). Levels above the cap are absent from the `/effort` picker and a higher level named with `--effort` or `/effort` runs at the cap, warned in interactive and plain-text `--print` runs but clamped silently under JSON output or in background agents. Caps are per model, and the least restrictive of several roles applies.

nodes.label: Account-type Default model
nodes.rationale: `default` resolves by account type: Opus 5 on Max, Team Premium, Enterprise and the Anthropic API, and on Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud's Agent Platform; Sonnet 5 on Pro and Team Standard; Sonnet 4.5 on Microsoft Foundry. An organization default replaces the account-type default first, and Default-model enforcement then applies to the result.

nodes.label: `opusplan` hybrid mode
nodes.rationale: `opusplan` pairs Opus's reasoning for planning with Sonnet's efficiency for execution: Opus in plan mode, then an automatic switch to Sonnet for code generation. Its plan-mode Opus phase uses the same context window as `opus`, including the automatic 1M upgrade on subscription tiers, and `opusplan[1m]` forces 1M for both phases elsewhere.

nodes.label: Fallback model chains
nodes.rationale: When the primary model is overloaded, unavailable, or returns another non-retryable server error, Claude Code switches to a fallback model for the current turn only, set with `--fallback-model a,b` or the `fallbackModel` settings array (chains capped at three after dedup). Authentication, billing, rate-limit, request-size, transport errors and policy denials never trigger a switch, and Claude Code won't fall back to a smaller context window during compaction.

nodes.label: Automatic (content-based) model fallback
nodes.rationale: Fable models and Opus 5 run with safety classifiers that most often flag cybersecurity and biology content; when a classifier flags a request and the category has a fallback model, Claude Code re-runs the request on that model, shows a transcript notice, and the session continues on the fallback model until you run `/model`. Category-based fallback requires v2.1.219 or later.

nodes.label: Fallback targets per flagged category
nodes.rationale: From Fable 5.1 and Fable 5, biology-flagged requests re-run on Opus 5 and cybersecurity-flagged requests on Opus 4.8. From Opus 5, cybersecurity-flagged requests re-run on Opus 4.8 while biology-flagged requests end with a refusal, because Opus 5 runs its own biology classifiers with no fallback model.

nodes.label: Checking what triggered a fallback
nodes.rationale: Fallback can fire on the first request of a session because that request carries workspace context such as CLAUDE.md content and git status, and a repository holding security or biology material can trip the classifier on that context alone. `claude --safe-mode` disables customizations (CLAUDE.md, skills, MCP servers, hooks) to test whether they are the trigger; git status and directory names are not customizations and are still included.

nodes.label: switchModelsOnFlag — ask before switching
nodes.rationale: Turning off 'Switch models when a message is flagged' in `/config`, or setting `switchModelsOnFlag: false`, makes a flagged request pause the session with two options: switch to the fallback model, or edit the prompt and retry on the current model. No prompt is shown when the category has no fallback, when the fallback target is blocked by `availableModels`, or in non-interactive/SDK contexts — the request ends in a refusal instead.

nodes.label: Enabling fallback on Bedrock, Agent Platform, and Foundry
nodes.rationale: On providers with provider-specific model IDs, automatic fallback runs only when Claude Code can identify both models: the source is recognized when the ID contains `claude-fable-5`, matches `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL`, or is mapped through `modelOverrides`, and the target must resolve in the deployment (an `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` pin serves every category that has a fallback). If either cannot be identified, the flagged request ends with a refusal.

nodes.label: Security research and biology workloads
nodes.rationale: Offensive-security and biology workloads — penetration testing, CTF exercises, biology-adjacent codebases — trigger fallback frequently, often on the first request. On Fable the session moves to Opus 5 at the first biology flag and later biology flags there end in refusals; this is expected routing for these domains, not an account flag, and trusted access programs are the escalation path.

nodes.label: Effort levels
nodes.rationale: Effort levels control adaptive reasoning, letting the model decide whether and how much to think on each step based on task complexity. Lower effort is faster and cheaper for straightforward tasks; higher effort gives deeper reasoning for complex problems. The effort scale is calibrated per model, so the same level name is not the same underlying value across models.

nodes.label: Per-model effort level support
nodes.rationale: Fable 5.1/5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8 and Opus 4.7 support `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max`; Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 support `low`, `medium`, `high` and `max`; models not listed do not support effort. Setting an unsupported level falls back to the highest supported level at or below it, so `xhigh` runs as `high` on Opus 4.6.

nodes.label: Effort level resolution order
nodes.rationale: With `ultracode` off, the session effort resolves as: an explicit choice (`CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, `--effort`, or `/effort`); then a model-default hold on Fable 5, Opus 4.8 or Opus 4.7 that persists across sessions until you change effort once (Opus 5 and Fable 5.1 have no such hold); then your saved per-model level or `effortLevel`; then the model default, `high` everywhere except `xhigh` on Opus 4.7.

nodes.label: Per-model effort persistence in modelSettings
nodes.rationale: Setting `low`, `medium`, `high` or `xhigh` in an interactive local session saves the level per model under the `modelSettings` key in user settings and applies it in later sessions. `max` is the exception: unless set through `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, it applies to the current session only.

nodes.label: Non-interactive `/effort` is session-only
nodes.rationale: A level set with `/effort` in non-interactive mode (`-p`) applies to the current session only and isn't saved as your default. It also doesn't count as the one change that ends the model-default hold on Fable 5, Opus 4.8 or Opus 4.7 — while that hold is in effect a non-interactive `/effort` reports `Not applied`, so pass `--effort` at launch instead.

nodes.label: ultracode
nodes.rationale: Ultracode is a Claude Code setting rather than a model effort level: it sends `xhigh` to the model and additionally has Claude orchestrate dynamic workflows for substantive tasks. It is turned on via `/effort ultracode`, `--effort ultracode` (v2.1.203+), the `ultracode` settings key or SDK request, or the `/model` picker's effort slider; the `effortLevel` key and `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL` do not accept it, and where workflows are off it only sets `xhigh`.

nodes.label: Choosing an effort level
nodes.rationale: Each level trades token spend against capability: `low` for short, scoped, latency-sensitive and non-intelligence-sensitive tasks; `medium` for cost-sensitive work; `high` as the balanced default on every model except Opus 4.7; `xhigh` for deeper reasoning at higher spend and the default on Opus 4.7; `max` for demanding tasks, prone to diminishing returns and overthinking, so test before adopting broadly.

nodes.label: ultrathink keyword
nodes.rationale: Including `ultrathink` anywhere in a prompt requests deeper reasoning for that turn without changing the session effort setting: Claude Code recognizes the keyword and adds an in-context instruction while the effort level sent to the API is unchanged. Phrases such as 'think', 'think hard' and 'think more' are passed through as ordinary prompt text and are not keywords.

nodes.label: Ways to set the effort level
nodes.rationale: Effort can be changed with `/effort` (slider, a level name, or `auto` to clear the saved level), the `/model` picker's arrow-key slider, the `--effort` launch flag, `CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL`, a per-model `modelSettings` level or `effortLevel` key, a Remote Control device's effort control (v2.1.234+, session only), and `effort` in skill or subagent frontmatter. The current level is shown in the session header beside the model name.

nodes.label: Skill and subagent frontmatter effort
nodes.rationale: An `effort` value in a skill or subagent markdown file applies while that skill or subagent is active, overriding the session level but not the environment variable. The `effortLevel` key in managed settings is likewise a starting default rather than enforcement — users can change it per session and the managed value re-asserts in new sessions.

nodes.label: Adaptive reasoning vs fixed thinking budgets
nodes.rationale: Adaptive reasoning makes thinking optional on each step so Claude responds faster to routine prompts and reserves deeper thinking where it helps. Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Sonnet 5, and Opus 4.7 and later always use adaptive reasoning and ignore `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADAPTIVE_THINKING`; on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6 that variable reverts to the fixed thinking budget controlled by `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS`.

nodes.label: Extended thinking
nodes.rationale: Extended thinking is the reasoning Claude emits before responding; it is toggled per session with Option+T / Alt+T, defaulted globally via `/config` (`alwaysThinkingEnabled`), or disabled with `MAX_THINKING_TOKENS=0`. It cannot be turned off on Fable 5.1 or Fable 5. Output is collapsed by default (Ctrl+O for verbose), interactive Anthropic API sessions get redacted blocks unless `showThinkingSummaries: true`, and all thinking tokens are charged.

nodes.label: Extended (1M token) context
nodes.rationale: Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Sonnet 5, Opus 4.6 and later, and Sonnet 4.6 support a 1M token context window. On Max, Team and Enterprise plans Opus is automatically upgraded to 1M; Pro needs usage credits for Opus, and Sonnet 4.6 with 1M requires usage credits on every plan including Max. The window uses standard pricing with no premium beyond 200K, and the plan check runs only when connecting to the Anthropic API directly.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT
nodes.rationale: `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1` removes 1M model variants from the picker and treats models with a native 1M window, such as Sonnet 5 and the Fable models, as having 200K: with auto-compaction on they compact at the 200K boundary (raising the auto-compact window does not lift the hold, since it is capped at the model's window), and with it off they stop with the context-limit error. Before v2.1.223 only Sonnet 5, Opus 4.8 and Opus 5 were held.

nodes.label: Sonnet 5 context window
nodes.rationale: On the Anthropic API, Sonnet 5 always runs with the 1M context window — no 200K variant, no `[1m]` suffix to select, no usage credits on any plan — and auto-compacts at about 967K tokens by default. Two configurations budget it at 200K instead: an LLM gateway where 1M support can't be verified (select Sonnet 5 (1M context), which maps to `sonnet[1m]`), and `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1`.

nodes.label: Auto-compact window
nodes.rationale: The auto-compact window is how full the context window may get before Claude Code compacts the conversation. It is set with `/autocompact <value>` (saved as `autoCompactWindow`, but preempted by a higher-priority settings scope), the `--autocompact` launch flag (not preempted), or `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW` (which outranks all three). Values run 100K–1M as a token count, a `k`/`M` suffix, or a bare 100–1000 meaning thousands.

nodes.label: Default auto-compact thresholds
nodes.rationale: Without a configured window, Claude Code compacts at the model's context limit, except that cloud sessions compact as they approach it; Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 without extended context (and Opus 4.8/Opus 5 running at 200K on third-party providers) compact at 200K; models held by `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1` compact at 200K; Sonnet 5 compacts at the threshold for its configuration; and unrecognized model IDs compact at the window Claude Code assumes.

nodes.label: Correcting the window for a gateway or custom model ID
nodes.rationale: `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS` declares the window Claude Code should assume for a gateway or custom ID, and applies in three distinct cases: directly for an unrecognized ID without `[1m]`; only alongside `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT=1` for an unrecognized `[1m]` ID (which then shows an expected 'the 200K limit isn't enforced' startup warning); and only with `DISABLE_COMPACT` for an ID starting with `claude-` or resolving to a Claude model.

nodes.label: Checking your current model
nodes.rationale: The model in use is visible in two places: the status line, if one is configured, and `/status`, which also displays account information.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION
nodes.rationale: `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_MODEL_OPTION` adds a single custom entry to the `/model` picker without replacing built-in aliases, with optional `_NAME` and `_DESCRIPTION` companions; Claude Code skips validation for its model ID, so any string the endpoint accepts works. Gateway deployments can instead populate the picker from `/v1/models` with `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_GATEWAY_MODEL_DISCOVERY=1`.

nodes.label: modelPicker lineup
nodes.rationale: To list several models in your own order under labels you choose, set the `modelPicker` setting, which replaces the built-in picker lineup; rows appended through it come after any custom model option.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_*_MODEL variables
nodes.rationale: `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL`, `_OPUS_MODEL`, `_SONNET_MODEL` and `_HAIKU_MODEL` control the model each alias maps to, each value being a full model name or the provider's equivalent identifier. The Opus and Sonnet variables also back `opusplan` in and out of plan mode, the Haiku one backs background functionality, and `ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL` is deprecated in favor of `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL`.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL
nodes.rationale: `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` sets the default model for subagents, agent-team teammates, and workflow agents that aren't assigned a model another way, accepting an alias or a full model name. A per-invocation model or a definition's `model` field, including `inherit`, takes precedence over it.

nodes.label: Pinning models for third-party deployments
nodes.rationale: On Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, Microsoft Foundry and Claude Platform on AWS, pin model versions before rolling out to users: unpinned aliases resolve to a built-in per-provider default that can lag the newest release or be unenabled in an account, producing a fallback notice on Bedrock/Agent Platform and outright errors on Microsoft Foundry. Pinning lets you control when users move to a new model.

nodes.label: `[1m]` on a pinned provider model ID
nodes.rationale: Appending `[1m]` to the ID in `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL` or `ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL` enables the 1M window for all usage of that alias, including opusplan's plan-mode Opus phase. Claude Code strips the suffix before sending the ID; only append it where the model supports 1M; and it is read per variable, so the same model without the suffix in another variable uses 200K.

nodes.label: Pinned model display name and description
nodes.rationale: A pinned provider-specific ID appears as-is in the `/model` picker, so `_NAME` and `_DESCRIPTION` companion variables override the display name and description (defaulting to the model ID and `Custom Opus model`). These take effect on third-party providers, the `_NAME`/`_DESCRIPTION` pair also behind an LLM gateway, and none of them when connecting directly to api.anthropic.com.

nodes.label: _SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES declaration
nodes.rationale: Claude Code enables features by matching a model ID against known patterns, which provider-specific IDs such as Bedrock ARNs often fail, leaving supported features disabled. `_SUPPORTED_CAPABILITIES` declares them explicitly — `effort`, `xhigh_effort`, `max_effort`, `thinking`, `adaptive_thinking`, `interleaved_thinking` — enabling the listed ones and disabling the rest for that pinned model; unset, built-in ID detection applies.

nodes.label: modelOverrides
nodes.rationale: `modelOverrides` maps individual Anthropic model IDs to provider-specific strings, so administrators can route each model version to a specific Bedrock inference profile ARN, Agent Platform version name, or Foundry deployment name for governance, cost allocation, or regional routing. It also applies to IDs passed through `--model` and the environment variables (v2.1.200+), takes precedence over auto-discovered Bedrock inference profiles, and silences the `unrecognized_model` diagnostic when an ID maps to itself.

nodes.label: Prompt caching configuration
nodes.rationale: Claude Code uses prompt caching automatically. `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1` disables it for all models and takes precedence over the per-tier variables `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_HAIKU`, `_SONNET`, `_OPUS` and `_FABLE`, which disable caching for that model family only.

nodes.label: Claude Code OpenTelemetry monitoring
nodes.rationale: Claude Code tracks usage, costs and tool activity across an organization by exporting telemetry through OpenTelemetry: metrics as time series via the metrics protocol, events via the logs/events protocol, and optionally distributed traces via the traces protocol.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY
nodes.rationale: The required master switch for telemetry collection; set to 1. Without it no metrics, events or traces are exported, and turning it off in managed settings also removes a developer-set BETA_TRACING_ENDPOINT.

nodes.label: OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER
nodes.rationale: Selects the metrics exporter types as a comma-separated list: console, otlp, prometheus, or none to disable. It follows normal per-key settings precedence, so a developer can still disable or console-redirect metrics unless an administrator also sets the selector.

nodes.label: OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER
nodes.rationale: Selects the logs/events exporter types (console, otlp, none). Events are exported only when it is configured. Across admin sources it follows the telemetry unit, while the metrics and traces selectors merge per key; that behavior requires Claude Code v2.1.223 or later.

nodes.label: OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER
nodes.rationale: Beta selector choosing where spans are sent (console, otlp, none). It only takes effect once both CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 and CLAUDE_CODE_ENHANCED_TELEMETRY_BETA=1 are set.

nodes.label: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
nodes.rationale: The OTLP collector endpoint applied to all signals, for example http://localhost:4317. Per-signal endpoint variables such as OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT override it for that signal.

nodes.label: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL
nodes.rationale: Selects the OTLP wire protocol (grpc, http/json, http/protobuf) for all signals. Claude Code has NO default protocol, so this or the signal-specific protocol variable must be set for every otlp exporter enabled.

nodes.label: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS
nodes.rationale: Static authentication headers for OTLP, such as 'Authorization=Bearer token'. A per-signal headers variable is MERGED with this generic one for that signal rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: Per-signal variable precedence
nodes.rationale: A per-signal endpoint or protocol variable replaces the generic variable for that signal, while a per-signal headers variable is merged with the generic headers. This is the mechanism that lets metrics, logs and traces reach different collectors.

nodes.label: Export interval variables
nodes.rationale: OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL (default 60000 ms), OTEL_LOGS_EXPORT_INTERVAL (default 5000 ms) and OTEL_TRACES_EXPORT_INTERVAL (default 5000 ms) control batching cadence; shortening them is a debugging aid that should be reset for production.

nodes.label: Verifying a telemetry setup
nodes.rationale: To verify a metrics setup, check the backend for claude_code.session.count, emitted when a session starts; for a logs-only setup, submit a prompt and look for the claude_code.user_prompt event.

nodes.label: [3P telemetry] vs [Anthropic telemetry] debug lines
nodes.rationale: When nothing arrives, `claude --debug` shows exporter failures prefixed [3P telemetry] (third-party, i.e. your configured exporters). Lines prefixed [Anthropic telemetry] describe Anthropic's separate operational telemetry and do not indicate a problem with your setup.

nodes.label: Administrator configuration via managed settings
nodes.rationale: Administrators configure OpenTelemetry for all users by placing the OTEL_* variables in the managed settings file's `env` block, subject to the documented settings-precedence rules.

nodes.label: Managed settings lock the OTLP destination
