nodes.rationale: `/export` opens a menu to copy the current conversation to the clipboard or save it as a plain-text file, with messages and tool outputs rendered as readable text; passing a filename skips the menu and writes directly. It produces a RENDERED transcript for a person to read, not structured data for a script.

nodes.label: Script interfaces to session data
nodes.rationale: Four interfaces give a script structured session data, chosen by what triggers the script: `claude -p` with `--output-format json`/`stream-json` to capture a run's result, session ID, usage and cost; `claude -p --resume <session-id>` to ask an existing session a follow-up (e.g. `… --output-format json "summarize what we changed" | jq -r '.result'`); the `transcript_path` field hooks and status line commands receive (a `SessionEnd` hook can archive the transcript); and the Agent SDK to receive each message programmatically.

nodes.label: Where transcripts are stored
nodes.rationale: By default Claude Code stores transcripts as JSONL at `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session-id>.jsonl`, where `<project>` is the working directory path with non-alphanumeric characters replaced by `-`. A converted name over 200 characters is truncated to 200 characters with a hash of the full path appended, keeping the directory name within filesystem limits.

nodes.label: JSONL entry format is internal
nodes.rationale: Each transcript line is a JSON object for a message, tool use, or metadata entry, but the entry format is internal to Claude Code and changes between versions, so scripts parsing these files directly can break on any release. To build on session data, use `/export` or the documented script interfaces instead.

nodes.label: Transcript storage configuration
nodes.rationale: Location, retention and write behavior are configurable: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` moves storage off `~/.claude`, `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` names the `<project>` directory, `cleanupPeriodDays` changes the 30-day retention, `desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays` ages out Claude Desktop and Cowork transcripts, `CLAUDE_CODE_SKIP_PROMPT_HISTORY` suppresses transcript writes in all modes, and `--no-session-persistence` suppresses writes for one non-interactive run.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
nodes.rationale: The `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` environment variable moves session storage off `~/.claude`, e.g. to a per-tenant directory such as `/srv/tenant-a`, under which transcripts land in `<dir>/projects/<project>/`.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME
nodes.rationale: Setting `CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME` alongside `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` (v2.1.234+) replaces the path-derived `<project>` name with one you choose, storing that session's transcripts and auto memory under it whatever the working directory is — e.g. `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/srv/tenant-a CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME=work claude` writes to `/srv/tenant-a/projects/work/`. This suits a host that embeds Claude Code and gives each session its own config directory.

nodes.label: Rules for a pinned project directory name
nodes.rationale: Three rules govern the pinned name: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` must be set too (otherwise the fixed name would merge every project's transcripts and auto memory under `~/.claude`, so the variable is ignored); the value must be 1-64 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores and not a Windows device name such as `con`, or the derived name is used; and it must be set in the shell environment that starts `claude`, since it is read once at startup and cannot come from a settings-file `env` block. Launching later without it reads and writes the derived directory again, while `Ctrl+A` in the picker and `claude --resume <session-id>` still find sessions stored under either name.

nodes.label: cleanupPeriodDays retention
nodes.rationale: Transcripts are retained for 30 days by default; the `cleanupPeriodDays` setting in `settings.json` changes that window. A separate `desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays` setting ages out Claude Desktop and Cowork transcripts and lives in user settings, managed settings, or `--settings`.

nodes.label: Example settings files page
nodes.rationale: This page holds three realistic settings.json files, one for each place a setting can be saved: a developer's ~/.claude/settings.json, a team's committed .claude/settings.json, and an organization's managed-settings.json. The intent is that a reader copies one, keeps the keys they want, and changes the values.

nodes.label: User settings (~/.claude/settings.json)
nodes.rationale: One developer's personal settings file, saved at ~/.claude/settings.json, where it applies to every project they open. The example picks a model and effort level, adjusts the terminal, and pre-approves one read-only command and one file read; everything not listed keeps its default.

nodes.label: Team settings (.claude/settings.json, committed)
nodes.rationale: A team's shared settings file, saved at .claude/settings.json at the top of the repository and committed, so everyone who clones the repo gets the same permissions, hooks, telemetry, and plugin marketplace.

nodes.label: Managed settings (managed-settings.json)
nodes.rationale: An organization's managed-settings.json showing the shape of the managed keys with one plausible value for each. It is explicitly not a recommended policy: administrators pick the keys matching their own requirements and set their own values.

nodes.label: None of the examples is a recommended baseline
nodes.rationale: Each example is only a plausible file for that reader, meant to show the shape so parts can be copied; none of them is a recommended baseline. Every value comes from that key's entry on the settings reference, which carries its type, default, and where it can be set.

nodes.label: Two-tab pattern: copyable file vs annotated file
nodes.rationale: Each example has two tabs: 'Copyable settings file' is the file as you would save it, and 'What each key does' is the same file with a comment above each key. Claude Code does not accept comments in a settings file, so the copy must come from the first tab.

nodes.label: model and effortLevel keys
nodes.rationale: The developer example sets "model": "claude-sonnet-5" to start every session on Sonnet 5 and "effortLevel": "xhigh" to reason more deeply than the default high level on models with no saved level. /effort saves a level per model and --effort sets one for a single session.

nodes.label: Terminal personalization keys
nodes.rationale: The developer example adjusts the terminal with "editorMode": "vim" for vim keybindings in the prompt, "theme": "light-daltonized" for the colorblind-friendly light theme, "spinnerTipsEnabled": false to hide the rotating spinner tips, and "preferredNotifChannel": "terminal_bell" to ring the bell for notifications such as a finished task or a waiting permission prompt.

nodes.label: statusLine command block
nodes.rationale: The example configures a status line below the prompt with "statusLine": {"type": "command", "command": "jq -r ...", "padding": 2}, rendering the model display name and the percentage of the context window used.

nodes.label: Developer permissions.allow pre-approvals
nodes.rationale: The developer file pre-approves one read-only command and one file read via "permissions": {"allow": ["Bash(git diff *)", "Read(~/.zshrc)"]}, letting Claude Code run git diff and read the user's .zshrc without asking.

nodes.label: autoUpdatesChannel
nodes.rationale: The developer example sets "autoUpdatesChannel": "stable", meaning updates are taken from the stable channel.

nodes.label: cleanupPeriodDays retention
nodes.rationale: cleanupPeriodDays controls how long session transcripts and other local session data are kept before deletion. The developer example sets 20 days; the organization's managed file shortens retention to 7 days, so the same key appears at two scopes with different values.

nodes.label: Cloud sessions read the committed project file
nodes.rationale: A cloud session on Claude Code on the web starts from a clone of the repository, so a committed .claude/settings.json applies there as well as locally. This is one of three things to know before committing a team settings file.

nodes.label: Allow rules and marketplaces wait for folder trust
nodes.rationale: Allow rules and extraKnownMarketplaces entries in a committed project file take effect only after each person trusts that folder itself, not merely a parent folder. Deny and ask rules, by contrast, apply in every session, trusted or not.

nodes.label: The team hook is a script in the repository
nodes.rationale: The team example's hook is a PreToolUse entry matching Bash that runs ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/block-rm.sh — a script living in the repo that can block a command before it runs. Committing the settings file therefore also means committing the hook script it names.

nodes.label: permissions.ask for git push
nodes.rationale: The team example allows "Bash(npm run *)" without asking and puts "Bash(git push *)" in the ask list, so a push is always confirmed first.

nodes.label: permissions.deny for env files and secrets
nodes.rationale: The team example denies Read(./.env), Read(./.env.*) and Read(./secrets/**) so env files and the secrets folder are never read. The organization's managed file repeats the same idea with Read(./.env) and Read(./secrets/**) plus Bash(curl *).

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry env block
nodes.rationale: The team file's env block sets CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1, OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=otlp, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=grpc and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, sending OpenTelemetry metrics to the team's collector over gRPC; the endpoint is replaced with the team's own collector URL.

nodes.label: extraKnownMarketplaces
nodes.rationale: The team file registers the team's plugin marketplace on every clone with extraKnownMarketplaces, naming "acme-tools" whose source is the github repo acme-corp/claude-plugins.

nodes.label: enabledPlugins and the per-person install
nodes.rationale: enabledPlugins turns on one plugin from the registered marketplace ("code-formatter@acme-tools": true). A plugin from an external source such as a GitHub repository still requires each person to install it once.

nodes.label: Team sandbox block
nodes.rationale: The team file sandboxes commands with "sandbox": {"enabled": true, filesystem.allowWrite ["/tmp/build"], network.allowedDomains ["registry.npmjs.org", "*.example.com"]} — a writable build directory, npm and example.com pre-allowed, and other hosts still prompting.

nodes.label: plansDirectory
nodes.rationale: The team file sets "plansDirectory": "./plans" so plan files are kept inside the repository.

nodes.label: forceLoginMethod and forceLoginOrgUUID
nodes.rationale: The managed example pins the login method and organization: "forceLoginMethod": "claudeai" with a forceLoginOrgUUID list, allowing only claude.ai logins and only within that organization.

nodes.label: availableModels with enforceAvailableModels
nodes.rationale: availableModels restricts which models sessions can use — the example lists only "opus" and "sonnet" — and enforceAvailableModels: true makes even the Default option obey that list.

nodes.label: disableBypassPermissionsMode
nodes.rationale: Inside the managed permissions block, "disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable" removes the bypass-permissions mode from every session.

nodes.label: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly
nodes.rationale: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly: true makes the managed permission allowlist the only one that applies, so only managed permission rules take effect.

nodes.label: allowedMcpServers matched by URL
nodes.rationale: allowedMcpServers pins the MCP server by URL ("https://api.githubcopilot.com/*") rather than by name, because a user can name any server "github". Servers that do not match do not load — which includes every stdio server when the list holds only URL entries.

nodes.label: allowManagedMcpServersOnly
nodes.rationale: allowManagedMcpServersOnly: true locks the managed MCP allowlist so it is the only allowlist that counts, closing the gap that a locally-declared server could otherwise open.

nodes.label: strictKnownMarketplaces
nodes.rationale: strictKnownMarketplaces allows exactly one plugin marketplace — in the example the github repo acme-corp/approved-plugins — so plugins can come only from that source.

nodes.label: Managed sandbox lockdown
nodes.rationale: The managed sandbox block sandboxes every command with enabled: true, failIfUnavailable: true (refuse to start if the sandbox cannot be set up), allowUnsandboxedCommands: false (never let a blocked command retry outside the sandbox), a fixed network allowlist of registry.npmjs.org and github.com, and allowManagedDomainsOnly: true so users cannot add domains.

nodes.label: requiredMinimumVersion
nodes.rationale: requiredMinimumVersion sets a floor on the Claude Code version; the example uses "2.1.150", so Claude Code refuses to start on anything older.

nodes.label: companyAnnouncements
nodes.rationale: companyAnnouncements holds messages shown to every user at startup; the example greets users and points them at the organization's code guidelines.

nodes.label: One deployed managed file reaches every machine
nodes.rationale: Administrators deploy the file as managed-settings.json, or the same JSON through MDM or server-managed settings, and one deployed file applies to every machine or account it reaches. To give a group different values you deploy a different file or profile to that group, because server-managed settings do not support per-group policy yet.

nodes.label: Claude Code settings reference
nodes.rationale: A reference page listing every key Claude Code reads from a settings file, plus the short group of keys it keeps in ~/.claude.json instead. Each entry states the key's scope, type, default, any per-session override, and a paste-ready JSON example.

nodes.label: Settings scope model
nodes.rationale: Every key declares a Scope naming which files may set it: 'Any file' means all four settings files, and the narrower labels are 'User, local, or managed', 'User or managed', 'Managed', and 'Global config'. Narrow scopes exist so a cloned repository cannot set a key that steers the session.

nodes.label: User settings (~/.claude/settings.json)
nodes.rationale: The per-person settings file. Claude Code writes many keys here itself when you change them through /config, /model, /fast, /effort, /voice, /tui and similar commands.

nodes.label: Project settings (.claude/settings.json)
nodes.rationale: The repository-shared settings file. Because a cloned repository supplies it, several keys are ignored there entirely, and allow rules, additionalDirectories, extraKnownMarketplaces and env values from it take effect only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted.

nodes.label: Local settings (.claude/settings.local.json)
nodes.rationale: Per-machine overrides for one project, gitignored when Claude Code saves a setting there. Claude Code writes sandbox.enabled, disabledMcpjsonServers, enabledMcpjsonServers, enableAllProjectMcpServers and skillOverrides here from interactive dialogs.

nodes.label: Managed settings
nodes.rationale: What an organization deploys, delivered through server-managed settings, an MDM or OS policy, a managed-settings.json file, or a policy helper. Managed values outrank every other file and are the only source for the keys scoped 'Managed'.

nodes.label: Global config (~/.claude.json)
nodes.rationale: A short group of keys Claude Code reads only from ~/.claude.json and ignores in any settings.json: autoConnectIde, autoInstallIdeExtension, diffTool, externalEditorContext, permissionExplainerEnabled and the removed teammateDefaultModel. Several other keys also fall back to a value older versions left here.

nodes.label: Per-session overrides
nodes.rationale: Many entries carry a Per-session overrides line naming a CLI flag or environment variable that outranks the settings key for one session, such as --model and ANTHROPIC_MODEL over model, or --effort and CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL over effortLevel. For several safety keys the override can only turn a feature off, never back on.

nodes.label: Drop the bad entry, keep the rest
nodes.rationale: Claude Code repeatedly prefers partial validity over rejecting a settings file: it drops a modelPicker row or modelPricing rate it cannot parse, ignores unrecognized strictPluginOnlyCustomization surface names, drops an invalid forceLoginGatewayUrl on its own, and reports an invalid policyHelper as a dropped entry while still starting the session.

nodes.label: advisorModel
nodes.rationale: Picks which model answers when Claude calls the server-side advisor tool; unset turns the advisor off. The advisor must be at least as capable as the main model, and /advisor writes the pick to ~/.claude/settings.json rather than the user editing it by hand.

nodes.label: alwaysThinkingEnabled
nodes.rationale: Setting it false turns extended thinking off for every session; true changes nothing because thinking is already on. MAX_THINKING_TOKENS overrides it for one session in either direction, and on always-thinking models such as Fable, false has no effect.

nodes.label: availableModels
nodes.rationale: An allowlist of model aliases or IDs that constrains /model, --model and a developer's own model key for the main session, subagents, skills and the advisor. On its own it does not touch the picker's Default option.

nodes.label: enforceAvailableModels
nodes.rationale: Closes the gap availableModels leaves: with it true, a Default choice that would resolve outside the allowlist instead resolves to the first available model in the list. When any managed settings are deployed Claude Code reads this key from the managed source alone, and it has no effect when availableModels is unset.

nodes.label: effortLevel
nodes.rationale: A default reasoning effort of low, medium, high or xhigh for models with no saved level of their own. Since v2.1.251 an interactive /effort writes modelSettings instead of this key, and within one file a model's saved level wins over it.

nodes.label: modelSettings
nodes.rationale: Stores a saved effortLevel per model, written by /effort or the picker's effort slider. Across files Claude Code resolves each model separately: the highest-precedence file setting either that model's entry or effortLevel decides, so a managed effortLevel outranks a level saved in user settings.

nodes.label: fallbackModel
nodes.rationale: An ordered chain of backup models tried when the primary is overloaded, costing one turn with a cold prompt cache. Unlike most array settings it does not merge across files: the highest-precedence file that defines it supplies the whole chain, and at most three distinct allowed models are kept.

nodes.label: fastMode
nodes.rationale: Turns fast mode on where available, trading a higher cost per token for speed. Running /fast writes it to user settings; fast mode runs only on Opus 5 and Opus 4.8, so turning it on from another model switches to Opus.

nodes.label: fastModePerSessionOptIn
nodes.rationale: Stops a saved fastMode: true from turning fast mode on at session start, so each person must run /fast in each session. The saved fastMode key is left in place, so turning this key off restores the old behavior.

nodes.label: language
nodes.rationale: Added verbatim to the system prompt as an instruction to always respond in that language, so any language name Claude can read works and a misspelling reaches the model rather than erroring. The same value sets the voice dictation language, which does have a fixed supported list, and the language of auto-generated session titles.

nodes.label: model
nodes.rationale: Sets the model every new session starts with, without preventing a mid-session switch. --model and ANTHROPIC_MODEL outrank it for one session, including over a managed model, and an organization default model set to override user selection wins over it in user, project and local settings.

nodes.label: modelOverrides
nodes.rationale: Maps Anthropic model IDs to provider-specific IDs such as Bedrock inference-profile ARNs, so each picker entry calls the provider with its mapped value. Administrators use it on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform and Microsoft Foundry for governance, cost allocation or regional routing.

nodes.label: modelPicker
nodes.rationale: Replaces or extends the /model picker lineup with rows carrying a verbatim model value plus optional label and description, and an optional replaceBuiltInOptions flag. It is read only from managed settings, --settings and user settings, and lineups are never combined across sources; an unserviceable row is dropped and an unselectable one is grayed out.

nodes.label: modelPricing
nodes.rationale: Reports spend at an organization's contracted rates instead of list price, through an optional multiplier and an overrides map of per-million-token input, output, cacheRead and cacheWrite rates. It is managed-only, the administrator supplies the numbers, and the rates are applied to /usage, the status line, the SDK total_cost_usd, --max-budget-usd and OpenTelemetry cost metrics.

nodes.label: outputStyle
nodes.rationale: Names a built-in or custom output style, a saved set of system-prompt instructions that changes Claude's role, tone and output format. The style is built into the system prompt once per conversation, so an edit takes effect only after /clear or a new session.

nodes.label: promptCacheTtl
nodes.rationale: Chooses a 5m or 1h prompt-cache lifetime for the main conversation and the helpers run inline with it. The one-hour lifetime keeps the cache warm across longer breaks and bills each cache write at a higher rate.

nodes.label: subagentPromptCacheTtl
nodes.rationale: The sibling of promptCacheTtl for everything outside the main conversation: subagents, workflows, and Claude Code's own background and helper requests such as compaction and session titles. Setting both keys chooses a lifetime for every request Claude Code makes.

nodes.label: showThinkingSummaries
nodes.rationale: When false or unset the Anthropic API redacts thinking blocks and Claude Code shows a collapsed stub; true shows the full summaries on Ctrl+O. Redaction changes only what is displayed, not what the model generates, so lowering the thinking budget is the way to reduce spend.

nodes.label: switchModelsOnFlag
nodes.rationale: Decides what happens when a safety classifier flags a request: the default true switches to the fallback model and continues, while false pauses an interactive session for a choice and ends a -p run as an error.

nodes.label: ultracode
nodes.rationale: Starts sessions with ultracode on, so Claude plans a workflow for each substantive task unasked. Either way it runs the session at xhigh effort and takes precedence over effortLevel and modelSettings; Claude Code reads the key but never writes it.

nodes.label: permissions
nodes.rationale: The container object holding allow, ask, deny, additionalDirectories, defaultMode, disableBypassPermissionsMode and disableAutoMode. It decides which tools run without asking, which always prompt, which are blocked, and which permission mode a session starts in.

nodes.label: permissions.allow
nodes.rationale: Tool uses approved without a prompt. --allowedTools adds allow rules for one session, a deny rule from any file still blocks a named tool, and allow rules from a project's .claude/settings.json apply only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted.

nodes.label: permissions.ask
nodes.rationale: Tool uses that prompt for confirmation even in a mode that would otherwise approve them, such as acceptEdits or bypassPermissions. In dontAsk mode a matching tool use is denied instead of prompted.

nodes.label: permissions.deny
nodes.rationale: Blocked tool uses, and the documented way to keep secrets out of reach: matching files are excluded from discovery and search, reads are denied, and Edit and Write are blocked on those paths. Read and Edit deny rules cover Claude's file tools and recognized Bash file commands such as cat, head, tail and sed, but not arbitrary subprocesses, for which the sandbox is the OS-level enforcement.

nodes.label: Permission rule syntax
nodes.rationale: Rules take the form Tool or Tool(specifier), such as Bash, Bash(npm run *), Read(./.env) or WebFetch(domain:example.com). In an MCP rule a wildcard may appear only in the tool name after the mcp__<server>__ prefix, never in the server name, and tool names themselves accept globs so "*" denies every tool.

nodes.label: Deny, then ask, then allow
nodes.rationale: Claude Code evaluates deny rules first, then ask, then allow, and the first match decides regardless of how specific each rule is. Permission rules layer on top of every mode, so deny rules block even in bypassPermissions.

nodes.label: permissions.defaultMode
nodes.rationale: Sets the starting permission mode: default (reads only), acceptEdits (also edits and common filesystem commands), plan (blocks edits until a plan is approved), auto (everything with background safety checks), dontAsk (only pre-approved tools, auto-denying the rest), bypassPermissions (everything without asking), or manual as an alias for default. The auto value does not take effect from project or local settings.

nodes.label: permissions.additionalDirectories
nodes.rationale: Grants file access to working directories outside the one the session started in; --add-dir and /add-dir add them for one session. Most .claude/ configuration is not discovered from these directories, and project entries wait on the workspace trust dialog.

nodes.label: permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode
nodes.rationale: Set to the string "disable", it prevents anyone entering bypassPermissions mode: Claude Code rejects --dangerously-skip-permissions and ignores an agent definition's permissionMode: bypassPermissions, so the subagent runs with the parent's mode. Before v2.1.223 the frontmatter mode still applied.

nodes.label: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly
nodes.rationale: Makes managed settings the only source of allow, ask and deny rules: Claude Code ignores rules in other files and --allowedTools, hides always-allow choices, and stops saving new rules. Host-supplied parent settings are treated as part of the managed tier, keeping their deny and ask rules while their allow rules and additionalDirectories are dropped.

nodes.label: autoMode
nodes.rationale: Adds organization-specific environment, allow, soft_deny and hard_deny prose rules to the auto mode classifier so it stops blocking trusted internal operations. The literal string "$defaults" keeps the built-in rules at that position; omitting it replaces them, and arrays from several honored files concatenate.

nodes.label: autoMode.classifyAllShell
nodes.rationale: By default auto mode suspends only allow rules that could run arbitrary code, so a command matched by a narrow rule such as Bash(npm test) skips the classifier and an unanticipated destructive argument can pass unseen. Setting this true suspends every shell allow rule for the session so the classifier sees every Bash and PowerShell command.

nodes.label: disableAutoMode
nodes.rationale: Removes auto mode from the Shift+Tab cycle; any session that would have started in auto, whether from a flag, a settings file or the built-in default, starts in default instead. It is also accepted nested as permissions.disableAutoMode.

nodes.label: useAutoModeDuringPlan
nodes.rationale: With the default true the auto mode classifier reviews each shell command during plan mode instead of prompting; false gives a permission prompt for every command outside the built-in read-only set. Scoped to user, local or managed so a repository cannot turn it off for you.

nodes.label: Workspace trust gate
nodes.rationale: A repository's own files cannot take effect until the folder is trusted: project allow rules and additionalDirectories, extraKnownMarketplaces entries, autoMemoryDirectory, an apiKeyHelper command, a headersHelper command, project env values and the statusLine and fileSuggestion commands all wait on the trust dialog.

nodes.label: skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt
nodes.rationale: Skips the confirmation dialog shown before a session enters bypassPermissions mode, whether from --dangerously-skip-permissions or defaultMode. Claude Code writes true here in user settings once the dialog is accepted, and the sibling skipAutoPermissionPrompt does the same job for the one-time auto mode notice.

nodes.label: sandbox
nodes.rationale: The container that isolates the Bash commands Claude runs from the filesystem and network on macOS, Linux and WSL2, holding enabled plus the filesystem, network and credentials sub-objects. Boolean sub-keys take the value from the highest-precedence scope that sets them, while array sub-keys merge across every scope unless a managed-only lock applies.

nodes.label: sandbox.enabled
nodes.rationale: Turns Bash sandboxing on; the /sandbox panel writes it to .claude/settings.local.json for the current project, and setting it in user settings sandboxes every project. On Linux and WSL2 it needs bubblewrap and socat, and when the sandbox cannot start Claude Code warns and runs unsandboxed.

nodes.label: sandbox.failIfUnavailable
nodes.rationale: Makes Claude Code exit with an error at startup when sandbox.enabled is true but the sandbox cannot start, instead of degrading to unsandboxed execution. It is the hard gate an organization deploys in managed settings to require sandboxing.

nodes.label: sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed
nodes.rationale: Defaults to true, running sandboxed Bash commands with no permission prompt while deny rules and content-scoped ask rules such as Bash(git push *) still apply. Setting it false sends sandboxed commands through the regular permission flow, which the /sandbox Mode tab calls regular permissions mode.

nodes.label: sandbox.excludedCommands
nodes.rationale: Names command patterns that always run outside the sandbox; when any part of a compound command matches, the whole command runs unsandboxed. The docs call exclusion a convenience and not a security boundary, prefer filesystem.allowWrite where possible, and note there is no managed-only lock for this list.

nodes.label: sandbox.allowUnsandboxedCommands
nodes.rationale: Controls the unsandboxed-retry escape hatch: with the default true Claude may retry a blocked command with the dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter, and false makes Claude Code ignore that parameter so every command must be sandboxed or excluded. The /sandbox Overrides tab shows false as Strict sandbox mode.

nodes.label: sandbox.filesystem
nodes.rationale: Holds allowWrite, denyWrite, denyRead and allowRead plus allowManagedReadPathsOnly and disabled. By default sandboxed commands may write to the working directory, the session temp directory and added directories, and may read the rest of the filesystem including credential files.

nodes.label: Sandbox path prefixes
nodes.rationale: Sandbox paths resolve by prefix: / is absolute, ~/ is home-relative, and ./ or no prefix is relative to the project root for project settings or ~/.claude for user settings. This deliberately differs from Read and Edit permission rules, which use //path for absolute and /path for project-relative; a trailing slash and a trailing /** are stripped, and wildcards work in the write lists only on macOS.

nodes.label: sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite
nodes.rationale: Adds paths sandboxed commands may write beyond the defaults, for a subprocess such as kubectl or a build tool that writes outside the project. Entries merge across every scope and are joined by the paths from Edit allow rules, and no entry can lift a protected path.

nodes.label: sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite
nodes.rationale: Blocks writes to specific paths, including paths inside an otherwise writable directory, such as /etc or /usr/local/bin. Entries merge across scopes and pick up the paths from Edit deny permission rules.

nodes.label: sandbox.filesystem.denyRead
nodes.rationale: Blocks reads of specific paths, such as credential files the default read policy would otherwise expose. Entries merge across scopes and pick up Read deny rules, and they are not enforced when filesystem isolation is disabled.

nodes.label: sandbox.filesystem.allowRead
nodes.rationale: Re-opens reading inside a region denyRead blocks, the way to build workspace-only read access such as denyRead ~/ with allowRead ".". An exact or wildcard denyRead entry stays blocked inside a broader allowRead, and a wildcard denyRead matching a directory blocks its contents too.

nodes.label: sandbox.filesystem.allowManagedReadPathsOnly
nodes.rationale: Honors only the allowRead entries from managed settings so developers cannot re-open read access an organization blocked, while denyRead entries still merge from every scope. It is the read-path half of the managed-only locks.

nodes.label: sandbox.filesystem.disabled
nodes.rationale: Skips filesystem isolation while keeping network isolation, for the case where sandboxing exists to control where commands connect rather than what they write. With the layer off, denyRead and credentials.files deny entries are not enforced while envVars entries and applied mask entries keep working.

nodes.label: sandbox.ignoreViolations
nodes.rationale: Maps a command substring to violation substrings whose reports are suppressed, for paths a tool is expected to probe and be refused, such as /etc/hosts at startup. The sandbox still blocks the access; only the report to the user and to Claude is silenced.

nodes.label: Weaker-isolation sandbox switches
nodes.rationale: Three keys explicitly trade security for compatibility: enableWeakerNestedSandbox bind-mounts a container's existing /proc so bubblewrap runs unprivileged, enableWeakerNetworkIsolation lets Go tools reach macOS trustd to verify TLS behind a MITM proxy, and allowAppleEvents lets sandboxed commands launch other applications unsandboxed. Each documents the exposure it opens and points to excludedCommands as the narrower alternative.

nodes.label: sandbox.bwrapPath, socatPath and ripgrep
nodes.rationale: Point the sandbox at binaries outside PATH: bwrapPath and socatPath are managed-only absolute paths for Linux and WSL2, read only from managed settings so a project file cannot substitute a different binary, and ripgrep supplies a command plus optional args for a differently built rg.

nodes.label: sandbox.credentials
nodes.rationale: Declares the credential files and environment variables to protect from sandboxed commands, each with mode deny, which hides the credential, or mask, which shows a sentinel while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on outbound requests. Claude Code protects only what is listed; there is no built-in credential deny list.

nodes.label: sandbox.credentials.files
nodes.rationale: Protects credential files or directories: deny applies the same read block as filesystem.denyRead, while mask gives sandboxed commands a sentinel copy on Linux and WSL2 and makes the file unreadable on macOS. Mask entries are dropped from project and local settings, and mask fields on a deny entry are accepted but ignored.

nodes.label: sandbox.credentials.envVars
nodes.rationale: Protects environment variables: deny removes the variable from sandboxed commands, while mask shows a per-session sentinel and has the proxy substitute the real value on requests to the entry's injectHosts, so tools such as gh and npm authenticate without ever holding the credential. Arrays merge across scopes and deny wins when one variable appears with both modes.

nodes.label: Mask fields (extract, decode, maskClaims, maskDuplicates, injectHosts, onExtractNoMatch)
nodes.rationale: Optional fields that narrow what a mask entry replaces: extract masks only a capturing group so the rest stays parseable, decode: "jwt" substitutes a structurally valid fake token, maskClaims masks named JWT payload claims, maskDuplicates replaces verbatim copies elsewhere, and injectHosts limits where the proxy substitutes the real value. onExtractNoMatch decides whether a non-match warns, denies or stops sandbox setup, and deny is upgraded to error where the read block would not be enforced.

nodes.label: sandbox.credentials.allowPlaintextInject
nodes.rationale: Allows mask substitution on plain HTTP as well as TLS-terminated HTTPS. On plain HTTP the upstream identity is unverified and the credential travels in cleartext, so the docs restrict it to trusted test networks.

nodes.label: sandbox.credentials.awsPairs and sigv4
nodes.rationale: awsPairs links custom-named access-key, secret-key and session-token variables into one AWS credential for SigV4 re-signing, since only the conventional trio is paired automatically. sigv4 decides whether streaming uploads, presigned URLs and SigV4A signatures the proxy cannot re-sign are denied or passed through to receive AWS's own rejection.

nodes.label: Degrade an invalid managed credential entry to deny
nodes.rationale: When a managed sandbox.credentials entry fails validation but still has a valid path or name and a mask or deny mode, Claude Code degrades it to deny with a warning so the credential stays blocked rather than silently unmasked; an entry with an unknown mode or invalid path is stripped. Remaining valid entries are still enforced, and a wholly invalid credentials value is dropped while the rest of sandbox applies.

nodes.label: sandbox.network
nodes.rationale: Controls which hosts, ports and sockets sandboxed commands reach, with the sandbox routing outbound traffic through a proxy that enforces the lists. Array sub-keys merge and deduplicate across scopes, so a project can add domains to a user list.

nodes.label: sandbox.network.allowedDomains
nodes.rationale: Pre-allows domains so the sandbox does not prompt for them, accepting wildcards such as *.example.com, an optional :port suffix, and bracketed IPv6 literals. Without it the sandbox prompts the first time a command reaches a new host.

nodes.label: sandbox.network.deniedDomains
nodes.rationale: Blocks domains with the same wildcard, port and IPv6 syntax as allowedDomains, and a denied domain stays blocked even inside an allowed wildcard. This list merges from every settings source even under allowManagedDomainsOnly, so a developer can always tighten it.

nodes.label: sandbox.network.strictAllowlist
nodes.rationale: Denies hosts outside the allowlist outright instead of deciding by permission mode, which otherwise runs the classifier in auto mode, denies in dontAsk, allows under bypassPermissions and otherwise asks. It applies to sandboxed commands only, so in-process tools such as WebFetch still follow their permission rules, and a true from any honored source keeps it on.

nodes.label: sandbox.network.allowManagedDomainsOnly
nodes.rationale: Locks the network allowlist to managed settings: only managed allowedDomains and WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules are honored, and a non-allowed domain is blocked rather than prompted. Denied domains still merge from every source.

nodes.label: Unix socket access in the sandbox
nodes.rationale: allowUnixSockets lists socket paths permitted on macOS and is ignored on Linux and WSL2, where the seccomp filter cannot inspect socket paths; allowAllUnixSockets is the only way to permit them there. The docs warn a socket path can grant broad access, naming /var/run/docker.sock as control of the Docker daemon.

nodes.label: sandbox.network.httpProxyPort and socksProxyPort
nodes.rationale: Point the sandbox at an organization's own HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy to inspect HTTPS traffic, apply filtering rules or log every request. With only one of the two set, Claude Code still runs its own proxy for the other protocol.

nodes.label: sandbox.network.tlsTerminate
nodes.rationale: Has the sandbox proxy terminate TLS so it can read HTTPS request contents; the docs call it experimental and mask credential substitution requires it. An empty object generates an ephemeral CA for the session, or caCertPath and caKeyPath supply one, and it is read only from managed settings, --settings and user settings.

nodes.label: Permission rules feed the sandbox lists
nodes.rationale: Claude Code adds a session's permission rules to the sandbox lists: Edit allow and deny rules to allowWrite and denyWrite, Read deny rules to denyRead, and WebFetch(domain:...) allow and deny rules to the network domain lists. The Linux write-list wildcard limitation therefore applies to Edit rules too, which the /sandbox Config tab warns about.

nodes.label: The sandbox is an OS boundary, permission rules are not
nodes.rationale: Filesystem lists are enforced at the OS sandbox boundary, so they apply to every subprocess a sandboxed command starts, such as kubectl, terraform or npm, and not only to Claude's file tools. This is why permissions.deny points at the sandbox for OS-level enforcement of secret files.

nodes.label: autoCompactEnabled
nodes.rationale: Compacts the conversation automatically as context approaches the limit; it appears in /config as Auto-compact and defaults to true. DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT turns it off for one session, and whichever of the two turns it off, the other cannot turn it back on; the manual /compact keeps working either way.

nodes.label: autoCompactWindow
nodes.rationale: Sets how full the context window gets before automatic compaction, from 100000 to 1000000 tokens, capped at the model's own window. The /autocompact command writes it, and --autocompact then CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW outrank it for one session.

nodes.label: autoMemoryEnabled and autoMemoryDirectory
nodes.rationale: autoMemoryEnabled turns auto memory on or off, with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY overriding it for one session in either direction; autoMemoryDirectory relocates the store from ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/. From project or local settings the directory key is honored only under the same workspace trust rule as hooks, since a cloned repository can supply those files.

nodes.label: claudeMd
nodes.rationale: Injects CLAUDE.md-style instructions as organization-managed memory without deploying a separate file, written as the text of a CLAUDE.md with line breaks as \n. Claude Code loads it as a managed memory entry ahead of user and project CLAUDE.md files.

nodes.label: claudeMdExcludes
nodes.rationale: Glob patterns or absolute paths matched against absolute file paths to skip specific CLAUDE.md files when memory loads, aimed at monorepos where other teams' files are irrelevant. Exclusions apply only to user, project and local memory files; a managed policy CLAUDE.md cannot be excluded.

nodes.label: env
nodes.rationale: Sets environment variables for every session and the subprocesses Claude Code starts, which is how a variable from the environment-variable reference is applied to every session or rolled out to a team. A value here overwrites a shell export, an empty string cancels one, and values are plain text in the file, so rotating credentials belong in apiKeyHelper or otelHeadersHelper instead.

nodes.label: Variables env cannot set from a repository
nodes.rationale: Project and local settings cannot set variables a checked-out repository should not control: those choosing where Claude Code writes its files (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, CLAUDE_CODE_TMPDIR, HOME, TMPDIR, the XDG_* family), those exporting session content (OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES and the beta tracing pair), and those changing how Claude Code starts or syncs. Identity and messaging variables Claude Code exports itself are ignored from every file.

nodes.label: fileCheckpointingEnabled
nodes.rationale: Snapshots files before each edit so /rewind can restore them; it appears in /config as Rewind code (checkpoints) and defaults to true. In a -p run or an Agent SDK session the key is ignored, and checkpointing comes from the SDK option or CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_SDK_FILE_CHECKPOINTING instead.

nodes.label: plansDirectory
nodes.rationale: Chooses where plan mode writes plan files, resolved relative to the project root, with the default ~/.claude/plans kept when the path resolves outside the project.

nodes.label: skillListingBudgetFraction and skillListingMaxDescChars
nodes.rationale: Each turn Claude sees a listing of skills with their descriptions, capped at a fraction of the context window (default 0.01) and at a per-skill character cap (default 1536). Over the cap Claude Code keeps every skill's name but drops the descriptions of the least-used skills, so those skills stay invocable but are less likely to be chosen; /doctor reports the listing's context cost.

nodes.label: askUserQuestionTimeout
nodes.rationale: Lets an unanswered AskUserQuestion dialog auto-continue after 60s, 5m or 10m of idle time, submitting whatever options were already selected; the default "never" waits indefinitely. It is user-or-managed scoped and the /config row is hidden while managed settings or --settings set it.

nodes.label: autoContinueAtUsageLimit
nodes.rationale: After a claude.ai usage limit stops a session, Claude Code waits in the open session and continues the task automatically once the limit resets. It is read from user, --settings and managed settings only, and unusually, when none of those set it, a project or local file that sets it turns the feature off rather than being ignored.

nodes.label: dialogExpiry
nodes.rationale: Sets the deadline, default 5m, for dialogs forwarded to a remote client such as Remote Control or an SDK host, for a held cross-session message approval, and for the mid-session Fable usage-credits consent prompt. When no answer arrives the dialog is cancelled and Claude Code continues with its no-action default; permission prompts and AskUserQuestion use their own flows.

nodes.label: axScreenReader
nodes.rationale: Renders flat, screen-reader friendly text without decorative borders or animations. Screen-reader mode forces the classic renderer, so the tui setting has no effect while it is active, though attached background sessions still render fullscreen.

nodes.label: defaultShell
nodes.rationale: Chooses whether Bash or PowerShell runs the commands typed with the ! prefix. The powershell value works only while the PowerShell tool is on, and if the named shell is unavailable Claude Code silently uses the other one.

nodes.label: Prompt-input editing keys
nodes.rationale: A family governing the input box: editorMode picks normal or vim bindings, vimInsertModeRemaps maps a two-character INSERT sequence such as jj to Escape, keybindingFlavor makes Ctrl+W delete back to whitespace as Bash does, emojiCompletionEnabled controls :shortcode: suggestions, spellcheck underlines misspellings using an installed aspell, hunspell or ispell, and promptSuggestionEnabled hides the grayed-out predictions. The remap, spellcheck and keybinding keys are user-or-managed so a repository cannot remap your keystrokes.

nodes.label: fileSuggestion
nodes.rationale: Runs a command of your own to supply @ file-path autocomplete instead of the built-in traversal, useful in a large monorepo with a pre-built index. The command gets hook-style environment variables and JSON with a query field on stdin, must print newline-separated paths, is cut off after five seconds, and at most 15 results are shown.

nodes.label: footerLinksRegexes
nodes.rationale: Renders clickable footer badges when a regex matches turn output, including tool results and Claude's own responses, turning IDs printed by issue trackers and review tools into links. Named capture groups fill {name} placeholders in the url and label templates.

nodes.label: Footer badge constraints
nodes.rationale: Captured values are URL-encoded and the constructed URL must keep the template's literal origin, URLs over 2048 characters are dropped, the scheme must be http/https or a recognized editor or workspace deep-link scheme, labels truncate to 28 columns, and at most 5 badges render. Patterns are matched on the main thread when a turn completes, so a nested quantifier can freeze the session.

nodes.label: statusLine
nodes.rationale: Runs a command to render a status line below the prompt with context such as model, cost or git branch, with optional padding, refreshInterval and hideVimModeIndicator. Under allowManagedHooksOnly, or a disableAllHooks set outside managed settings, only the managed value runs.

nodes.label: subagentStatusLine
nodes.rationale: Rewrites rows in the subagent task display: Claude Code sends the visible rows as one JSON object with a tasks array carrying each subagent's id, name, status, model and tokenCount, and replaces the row for each id written back as an {id, content} line. Rows not written back keep the default rendering.

nodes.label: spinnerTipsOverride, spinnerTipsEnabled and spinnerVerbs
nodes.rationale: Customize the spinner: tips can be added or replaced through tips entries or a tipsFile with per-tip id, cooldownSessions and priority, label sets the prefix, and excludeDefault hides the built-in rotation while still falling back to it when no custom tip loads. Project and local settings contribute plain string tips only; spinnerVerbs appends or replaces the rotating verbs, and spinnerTipsEnabled: false hides all tips.

nodes.label: Terminal rendering keys
nodes.rationale: A family controlling appearance: theme picks a built-in, daltonized, ANSI-only or custom palette, tui chooses the fullscreen alt-screen renderer or the classic one, syntaxHighlightingDisabled turns off code coloring, terminalProgressBarEnabled reports progress to ConEmu, Ghostty and iTerm2, prefersReducedMotion cuts animations, and autoScrollEnabled and wheelScrollAccelerationEnabled govern fullscreen scrolling. Several read a value older versions left in ~/.claude.json when no settings file sets them.

nodes.label: verbose and viewMode
nodes.rationale: verbose shows every tool call's full input and output inline instead of a collapsed summary, and viewMode starts the session in default, verbose or focus view. viewMode overrides both verbose and a sticky /focus selection, and focus view needs the fullscreen renderer.

nodes.label: respondToBashCommands
nodes.rationale: By default Claude Code adds a ! shell command's output to the conversation and Claude replies to it; setting false adds the output to context without a reply, so several commands can be run and asked about together.

nodes.label: showClearContextOnPlanAccept
nodes.rationale: Adds a first option to the plan approval menu, Yes, clear context and …, that approves the plan, clears the conversation context and implements from the plan alone. The label names the permission mode the session continues in and how much context planning used.

nodes.label: respectGitignore
nodes.rationale: Controls whether the @ file picker leaves out files matching .gitignore patterns, defaulting to true. When no settings file sets it, Claude Code falls back to a respectGitignore value in ~/.claude.json that the /config toggle writes.

nodes.label: attribution
nodes.rationale: Customizes what Claude Code adds to commits and pull requests through commit and pr strings and a sessionUrl Boolean. Setting commit or pr makes Claude Code ignore the deprecated includeCoAuthoredBy and use its default text for whichever of the two is left unset.

nodes.label: attribution.commit
nodes.rationale: Sets the attribution text added to git commits, including trailers, with an empty string hiding it. The default is Co-Authored-By: <name> <noreply@anthropic.com> where the name is the active model, degrading to "Claude" when the version cannot be confirmed and "Claude Code" when the model ID matches no Claude model.

nodes.label: attribution.pr
nodes.rationale: Sets the attribution text added to pull request descriptions, with an empty string hiding it. The default is the line 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code).

nodes.label: attribution.sessionUrl
nodes.rationale: Decides whether Claude Code appends the claude.ai session link when it commits or opens a pull request from a cloud or Remote Control session, added as a Claude-Session commit trailer and as a link in PR descriptions.

nodes.label: includeCoAuthoredBy (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Deprecated since v2.0.62 in favour of attribution, which separates the commit trailer, the PR text and the session link. Claude Code still honors a false from files that predate attribution, but ignores it once attribution.commit or attribution.pr is set.

nodes.label: includeGitInstructions
nodes.rationale: Setting it false removes two things from Claude's prompt at session start: the built-in commit and pull-request instructions in the Bash tool description, and the git status snapshot of the repository in the system prompt. It is aimed at users who supply their own git workflow skills; cloud sessions never include the snapshot.

nodes.label: prUrlTemplate
nodes.rationale: Points the PR links Claude Code renders at an internal review tool instead of github.com, substituting {host}, {owner}, {repo}, {number} and {url} from the gh-reported URL. It applies only to links Claude Code renders itself, so a PR number Claude writes in prose is left alone.

nodes.label: hooks
nodes.rationale: Registers commands, prompts, agents, HTTP requests or MCP tools to run at lifecycle points, keyed by hook event and holding matcher groups whose entries have a type of command, prompt, agent, http or mcp_tool. Hooks merge across files rather than replacing each other, and hooks from managed settings cannot be removed by another file.

nodes.label: allowedHttpHookUrls
nodes.rationale: Limits which URLs HTTP hooks may target, with * as a wildcard; an empty array blocks every HTTP hook. Hostname matching is case-insensitive and treats a trailing FQDN dot as equivalent, and the allowlist applies to hooks from every source including managed settings.

nodes.label: httpHookAllowedEnvVars
nodes.rationale: Sets an outer limit on which environment variables any HTTP hook may interpolate into a request header: a variable is usable only if both the hook's own allowedEnvVars and this key name it. It exists to stop a hook reading a secret it should not, even when its definition asks for it.

nodes.label: allowManagedHooksOnly
nodes.rationale: Restricts execution to managed hooks, Agent SDK hooks, and hooks from plugins force-enabled in managed enabledPlugins, matched on the full plugin@marketplace ID so a same-named plugin from another marketplace stays blocked. It also disables command-sourced plugins and marketplace headersHelper commands, narrows statusLine, fileSuggestion and subagentStatusLine to managed values, and makes /goal unavailable.

nodes.label: disableAllHooks
nodes.rationale: Turns off hooks, a custom status line and a custom file suggestion command at once without deleting them. Its reach depends on the file: in managed settings it disables every configured hook including managed ones while Agent SDK hooks keep running, and in any other file it spares managed hooks, SDK hooks and force-enabled plugin hooks.

nodes.label: Status line and file suggestion gates
nodes.rationale: Two ordered decisions govern statusLine, fileSuggestion and subagentStatusLine: they are off entirely when managed settings set disableAllHooks or the folder is untrusted, and narrowed to managed settings under allowManagedHooksOnly, a non-managed disableAllHooks, or --safe-mode. Under narrowing a managed value runs and your own value is skipped without warning.

nodes.label: disableWorkflows and enableWorkflows
nodes.rationale: disableWorkflows turns dynamic workflows and the bundled workflow commands off for everyone the settings reach, while enableWorkflows is the personal toggle /config writes to user settings. disableWorkflows and an organization's workflows policy take precedence, so enableWorkflows: true cannot turn workflows back on while any source turns them off.

nodes.label: workflowKeywordTriggerEnabled
nodes.rationale: Decides whether typing the keyword ultracode in a prompt starts a dynamic workflow; setting false lets the word be typed without triggering one. The ultracode effort setting, /workflows and saved workflow commands are unaffected, and before v2.1.160 the keyword was workflow.

nodes.label: workflowSizeGuideline
nodes.rationale: Advises Claude how many agents to aim for in a dynamic workflow: small is fewer than 5, medium fewer than 15, large fewer than 50, and unrestricted removes the guideline. It is advice sent to the model, not an enforced cap, and a settings value takes precedence over the /config row stored in ~/.claude.json.

nodes.label: disableBundledSkills
nodes.rationale: Removes the skills and workflows bundled with Claude Code entirely, while built-in commands such as /init stay typable but hidden from the model. Skills from plugins, .claude/skills/ and .claude/commands/ are unaffected.

nodes.label: disableSkillShellExecution
nodes.rationale: Turns off inline shell execution in skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin and additional-directory sources, replacing each command with [shell command execution disabled by policy]. A true in managed settings cannot be overridden by a false elsewhere, and bundled and managed-deployed skills are unaffected.

nodes.label: skillOverrides
nodes.rationale: Hides or collapses a skill without editing its SKILL.md, mapping a skill name to on, name-only (listed without its description), user-invocable-only (hidden from the model but still typable as /name) or off. Overrides do not apply to plugin skills, and the /skills menu writes them to .claude/settings.local.json.

nodes.label: syncClaudeAiSkills
nodes.rationale: Setting false stops downloading the skills enabled on a claude.ai account into ~/.claude/skills/synced/ and hides the ones already synced, moving them to a trash directory when set in user or managed settings. Claude Code honors only false; true is the same as unset and never turns syncing on.

nodes.label: enabledPlugins
nodes.rationale: Turns individual plugins on or off keyed by plugin-name@marketplace-name, with an unlisted plugin following its defaultEnabled value. Project settings outrank user settings, so opting out of a project-enabled plugin means setting false in .claude/settings.local.json, and a managed false blocks installation at every scope.

nodes.label: extraKnownMarketplaces
nodes.rationale: Registers additional plugin marketplaces by name so a repository's users or an organization get them without adding them by hand, each with a source object and an optional autoUpdate flag. Entries from a repository's own files wait on workspace trust, and when two files define the same name the highest-precedence entry is taken whole, inheriting no fields, so a redefinition cannot combine one file's headers with another file's URL.

nodes.label: strictKnownMarketplaces
nodes.rationale: A managed allowlist of marketplace sources, enforced on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh and auto-update, before any network or filesystem operation. An empty array is a complete lockdown blocking even the official Anthropic marketplace, and any allowlist also stops @skills-dir plugins loading unless a skills-dir entry is added.

nodes.label: Marketplace source types
nodes.rationale: Marketplace sources come as github, git, url, npm, file, directory, hostPattern, pathPattern and skills-dir entries, the last three matching by regex or opting the skills scan back in. A url marketplace downloads only marketplace.json, so its plugins cannot use relative paths; hostPattern takes a host from git URLs only in the forms git itself treats as SSH addresses, and file and directory sources never match it.

nodes.label: GitHub owner wildcards
nodes.rationale: A github entry whose repo is "<owner>/*" matches every repository under that owner, and works only in strictKnownMarketplaces and blockedMarketplaces. Only the whole repository-name position may be a wildcard, so entries such as */plugins or acme-corp/tools-* are compared literally and match nothing.

nodes.label: Exact marketplace matching
nodes.rationale: Outside wildcard and regex entries, a user's addition is allowed only when the source matches an entry exactly, including the optional ref and path fields, which must match or both be undefined. The allowlist and blocklist deliberately differ: the blocklist matches any spelling including git URLs, is case-insensitive on the owner, and a missing ref or path blocks all of them.

nodes.label: blockedMarketplaces
nodes.rationale: A managed blocklist of marketplace sources checked on add and on every install, update, refresh and auto-update, so a marketplace added before the policy cannot be used to fetch plugins. Blocked sources are checked before download, so they never touch the filesystem.

nodes.label: disableCommandPluginSources
nodes.rationale: Blocks the command plugin source, which installs a plugin by running a marketplace-declared command on the user's machine, and stops loading ones already installed. Whenever command sources are blocked it also blocks marketplace headersHelper commands, except for a marketplace managed settings themselves declare; unset, it follows allowManagedHooksOnly.

nodes.label: pluginSuggestionMarketplaces
nodes.rationale: Names the marketplaces whose plugins may appear as contextual install suggestions in spinner tips and the /plugin Discover tab, drawn from each plugin's relevance declaration. A name takes effect only when the marketplace is registered and its source is declared in the same managed settings; the official Anthropic marketplace is exempt from that source requirement.

nodes.label: pluginTrustMessage
nodes.rationale: Appends an organization's own text to the plugin trust warning shown before installation, for example to state that plugins from an internal marketplace are vetted.

nodes.label: strictPluginOnlyCustomization
nodes.rationale: Blocks skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers from user and project sources so they can come only from plugins or managed settings, set as true for all four or an array naming the surfaces. The skills lock also stops custom commands and claude.ai-synced skills, the mcp lock stops ~/.claude.json and .mcp.json servers, and unrecognized surface names are ignored rather than failing the file.

nodes.label: pluginConfigs
nodes.rationale: Stores the non-sensitive answers given to a plugin's userConfig dialog, keyed by plugin ID, with sensitive options kept in the macOS Keychain or ~/.claude/.credentials.json instead. Project and local entries are ignored because the values are substituted into plugin hook, MCP and LSP configurations and a cloned repository must not supply them.

nodes.label: channelsEnabled and allowedChannelPlugins
nodes.rationale: channelsEnabled is the managed gate that must be true before channels work on Team and Enterprise plans and on Console accounts with managed settings; allowedChannelPlugins then replaces the default Anthropic allowlist with named marketplace-and-plugin pairs, and an empty array blocks every channel plugin.

nodes.label: Marketplace key aliases
nodes.rationale: From v2.1.232, extraKnownMarketplaces may be written additionalMarketplaces and strictKnownMarketplaces may be written allowedMarketplaces. Earlier versions ignore the alias, so a file read by a mixed-version fleet should keep the canonical spelling, and when both appear in one file the canonical value wins.

nodes.label: allowedMcpServers
nodes.rationale: Allowlists MCP servers by serverName, exact serverCommand array, or wildcard serverUrl, blocking any non-matching server wherever it is defined, including plugin servers, --mcp-config servers and managed-mcp.json servers. Once the list holds any serverCommand entry a stdio server must match one, and once it holds any serverUrl entry a remote server must match one; built-in and in-process sdk servers are exempt.

nodes.label: deniedMcpServers
nodes.rationale: Blocks specific MCP servers wherever defined, including claude.ai connectors, and takes precedence over allowedMcpServers so a server on both lists is blocked. Entries merge from every file even under allowManagedMcpServersOnly, and in-process sdk servers are exempt.

nodes.label: allowManagedMcpServersOnly
nodes.rationale: Makes the managed allowlist the only one that applies, ignoring allowedMcpServers in user, project and local settings so a user's own settings cannot broaden what the organization permits. The denylist still merges from every scope, so users can keep blocking servers for themselves.

nodes.label: allowAllClaudeAiMcps
nodes.rationale: Loads the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself alongside a deployed managed-mcp.json, which otherwise takes exclusive control of MCP servers and suppresses them. Users cannot re-enable connectors that exclusive control suppressed, and the allow and deny lists still apply to the connectors this key loads.

nodes.label: disableClaudeAiConnectors
nodes.rationale: Stops Claude Code fetching or connecting the claude.ai MCP connectors. A true in any settings file applies, so a checked-in project file can opt a repository out, but a project-level false cannot override a user or managed true.

nodes.label: Project .mcp.json server approvals
nodes.rationale: Three keys govern servers declared in a project's .mcp.json: enabledMcpjsonServers approves named servers, enableAllProjectMcpServers approves them all without a prompt, and disabledMcpjsonServers rejects named servers and takes precedence over both. Claude Code writes them to .claude/settings.local.json from the approval dialog, and in an untrusted folder it honors them only from user, managed and --settings sources.

nodes.label: agent
nodes.rationale: Runs the main thread as a named subagent, applying that subagent's system prompt, tool restrictions and model to the session, and sets the default agent for sessions dispatched from claude agents. A plugin's own settings.json can also supply this key.

nodes.label: crossSessionInbound
nodes.rationale: Chooses what a session does with messages from your other sessions: accept delivers them, hold shows a notice without delivering, and refuse drops them; unset decides per message from the two sessions' permission-mode classes. A project or local value applies only when stricter than a trusted source's, and an unrecognized value holds messages, or is treated as refuse when it comes from managed settings.

nodes.label: isolatePeerMachines
nodes.rationale: Requires explicit approval before Claude's SendMessage reaches one of your sessions beyond this machine, and the prompt appears even in bypassPermissions mode. A true from any scope applies, so a checked-in project file can turn the requirement on but not off.

nodes.label: disableAgentView
nodes.rationale: Turns off background agents and agent view: claude agents, --bg, /background and the on-demand supervisor. CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_VIEW turns it off for one session, and whichever of the two turns it off, the other cannot turn it back on.

nodes.label: processWrapper
nodes.rationale: Places a corporate launcher command in front of the background processes Claude Code starts on macOS and Linux, appending Claude Code's own command line, so the launcher must exec into Claude Code. It is ignored on Windows, where every process starts unwrapped.

nodes.label: teammateMode
nodes.rationale: Chooses where agent team teammates are shown: in-process inside the main terminal pane, or split panes via tmux or iTerm2, with auto detecting which is available. The default is in-process, changed from auto in v2.1.179.

nodes.label: worktree
nodes.rationale: Configures how Claude Code creates and manages git worktrees for --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool, and isolated subagents and background sessions, holding baseRef, symlinkDirectories, sparsePaths and bgIsolation. Copying gitignored files into a new worktree is done with a .worktreeinclude file rather than a setting.

nodes.label: worktree.baseRef
nodes.rationale: Chooses which ref new worktrees branch from: the default fresh branches from origin/<default-branch> for a clean tree matching the remote, while head branches from the local HEAD so unpushed commits and feature-branch state are present. Inside a linked worktree, head resolves to that worktree's HEAD.

nodes.label: worktree.symlinkDirectories
nodes.rationale: Symlinks named directories from the main repository into each worktree, such as node_modules and .cache, so large directories are not duplicated on disk.

nodes.label: worktree.sparsePaths
nodes.rationale: Checks out only the listed directories plus root-level files in each worktree through git sparse-checkout, which is faster in large monorepos. While a sparse worktree exists git enables extensions.worktreeConfig in the repository's shared .git/config.

nodes.label: worktree.bgIsolation
nodes.rationale: Decides how background sessions isolate file edits: the default worktree blocks Edit and Write in the main checkout until the session calls EnterWorktree, while none lets background jobs edit the working copy directly. Outside a git repository a failing WorktreeCreate hook releases the block so the session can edit in place.

nodes.label: agentPushNotifEnabled and inputNeededNotifEnabled
nodes.rationale: Two mobile push toggles, both default false and both delivering only while Remote Control is connected: agentPushNotifEnabled lets Claude push when it decides a notification is worth sending, and inputNeededNotifEnabled pushes when a permission prompt or question is waiting.

nodes.label: awaySummaryEnabled
nodes.rationale: Shows a one-line session recap when you return to the terminal after a few minutes away; setting false or turning off Session recap in /config stops it. The recap never appears in non-interactive mode.

nodes.label: enableArtifact
nodes.rationale: Turns off the Artifact tool, which publishes session output as a private web page on claude.ai. It is a one-way lock: a false in any file turns the tool off for the sessions that file covers and no file, environment variable or /config row can turn it back on, and true is the same as unset.

nodes.label: disableArtifact (deprecated)
nodes.rationale: Deprecated in favour of enableArtifact. Claude Code still honors disableArtifact: true as equivalent to enableArtifact: false and ignores disableArtifact: false, and before v2.1.242 a higher-precedence file could override a lower file's true rather than the key acting as a lock.

nodes.label: disableDeepLinkRegistration
nodes.rationale: Stops Claude Code registering the claude-cli:// protocol handler with the operating system, which it otherwise does after the first prompt of an interactive session. It is aimed at environments where protocol-handler registration is restricted or managed separately.

nodes.label: disableDesktopLocalSessions
nodes.rationale: Turns off Code sessions that run on the device in the desktop app, greying out the Local environment and refusing to start or resume an on-device session, including an SSH connection back to the same machine; SSH to other hosts and cloud sessions are unaffected. Only the JSON Boolean true takes effect and a string "true" logs a warning.

nodes.label: disableRemoteControl
nodes.rationale: Turns Remote Control off everywhere it can start: claude remote-control, the --remote-control flag, auto-start and the in-session toggle are all refused with a message naming the organization's policy.

nodes.label: preferredNotifChannel
nodes.rationale: Chooses how Claude Code notifies on task completion or a waiting prompt, from auto, terminal_bell, iterm2, iterm2_with_bell, kitty, ghostty or notifications_disabled. With auto it sends a desktop notification in iTerm2, Ghostty and Kitty, rings the bell in Terminal.app only when its audible bell is off, and does nothing elsewhere.

nodes.label: remote.defaultEnvironmentId
nodes.rationale: Picks the default cloud environment for sessions created with claude --cloud, written by /remote-env. An Anthropic-hosted env_ ID follows normal precedence so a repository can override the user pick, while a self-hosted ccpool_ ID is honored only from user settings, managed settings and --settings so a checked-in file cannot steer sessions onto it.

nodes.label: remoteControlAtStartup
nodes.rationale: Connects Remote Control automatically when each interactive session starts instead of waiting for /remote-control. A true from project or local settings is ignored, so a repository can turn auto-connect off for its checkout but never on.

nodes.label: sshConfigs and sshHostAllowlist
nodes.rationale: sshConfigs adds named SSH connections to the Desktop environment dropdown, shown as managed and uneditable when deployed that way; sshHostAllowlist limits which hosts a Desktop SSH session may reach, matching case-insensitively after ~/.ssh/config resolution, with an empty array turning SSH sessions off. Only the Desktop app reads either key.

nodes.label: apiKeyHelper
nodes.rationale: Runs a command through the system shell whose output Claude Code sends as both the X-Api-Key and Authorization: Bearer headers, for dynamic or rotating credentials such as short-lived vault tokens. The value is cached for five minutes by default and re-fetched on a 401 or 403 or when the cached JWT has expired, and from project or local settings it does not run until workspace trust is accepted.

nodes.label: awsAuthRefresh
nodes.rationale: Runs a command such as aws sso login to refresh the credentials in the .aws directory when Bedrock credentials stop working. Claude Code checks the current credentials against STS first and runs the command only when that check fails.

nodes.label: awsCredentialExport
nodes.rationale: Runs a command that prints AWS credentials as JSON so Claude Code can call Bedrock with credentials that do not live in .aws, accepting the aws sts and aws configure export-credentials shapes. Unlike awsAuthRefresh it always runs when set, and the credentials are scoped to Claude Code's own Bedrock client so shell commands still see ambient credentials.

nodes.label: forceLoginMethod
nodes.rationale: Restricts login to claudeai, console, or gateway. The gateway value is honored only from a managed source on the machine, and claudeai or console in any file also stops Claude Code offering the keyless Console sign-in. Every first-party login path enforces it except the terminal's interactive login screen, which only pre-selects the method.

nodes.label: forceLoginGatewayUrl
nodes.rationale: Sets the gateway URL the /login Cloud gateway screen connects to, since that screen has no URL field and otherwise tells the user to contact IT. It is read only from managed-settings.json, the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry or a policy helper, and an invalid URL is dropped while the rest of the file applies.

nodes.label: forceLoginOrgUUID
nodes.rationale: From a managed source, requires claude.ai logins to belong to one organization UUID or any of several; from any other file a single UUID only pre-selects that organization during login without restricting it. A managed empty array or unparseable value blocks every login with a misconfiguration message.

nodes.label: gcpAuthRefresh
nodes.rationale: Runs a command to refresh Google Cloud Application Default Credentials when Claude Code finds them expired or unloadable, so Agent Platform requests keep working. Without it the credential error simply tells the user to run gcloud auth application-default login.

nodes.label: otelHeadersHelper
nodes.rationale: Runs a command at startup and periodically after that to generate the headers sent with OpenTelemetry exports, for backends whose tokens rotate, expecting a JSON object of string header values on stdout. The refresh interval comes from CLAUDE_CODE_OTEL_HEADERS_HELPER_DEBOUNCE_MS.

nodes.label: autoUpdatesChannel
nodes.rationale: Chooses whether background auto-updates and claude update follow latest or stable, where stable is typically about a week old and skips releases with major regressions. Homebrew installs ignore the key because the cask names the channel, and switching to stable in /config offers to set minimumVersion rather than downgrade.

nodes.label: minimumVersion
nodes.rationale: Keeps auto-updates and claude update from installing any version below the given one, so moving to the stable channel does not downgrade a newer latest build. It constrains updates only; making Claude Code refuse to start below a version is requiredMinimumVersion's job.

nodes.label: requiredMinimumVersion and requiredMaximumVersion
nodes.rationale: Managed-only floor and ceiling on the version allowed to start: outside the range Claude Code exits at startup telling the user to install an approved version. The check runs at startup only so a running session continues, updates skip versions above the ceiling, and claude update, claude install and claude doctor keep working so a user can recover.

nodes.label: Desktop tool restriction keys
nodes.rationale: Three managed keys turn off tools in the desktop app while the terminal CLI ignores them: browserExternalPageTools keeps Claude's tools off external pages in the Browser pane, disableBrowserExternalNavigation blocks external browsing for people and Claude alike while localhost previews keep working, and disableMobileSimulatorTools blocks Claude's tools in the iOS Simulator pane while people keep manual use.

nodes.label: cleanupPeriodDays
nodes.rationale: Sets how many days Claude Code keeps session transcripts and other application data before a background sweep deletes them, defaulting to 30 with a minimum of 1. Zero fails validation, so long retention means a large value such as 3650.

nodes.label: desktopSessionCleanupPeriodDays
nodes.rationale: Adds an age limit for transcripts of sessions started or continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork, which are otherwise kept at any age. A transcript is deleted only once older than both this limit and cleanupPeriodDays, and a managed cleanupPeriodDays makes this key ignored.

nodes.label: feedbackDrafts
nodes.rationale: Controls Claude-drafted feedback: notify shows a card when Claude queues a draft, quiet drafts silently with a count in the prompt footer, and off removes the SendFeedback tool so Claude cannot queue drafts at all. A managed value takes precedence over the user setting and the key is ignored in project and local settings.

nodes.label: feedbackSurveyRate
nodes.rationale: Sets the probability between 0 and 1 that the session quality survey appears when a session is eligible, with 0 suppressing it. Unset, Claude Code uses the rate Anthropic sets remotely, or a built-in 0.005 on Bedrock, Agent Platform and Foundry, which receive no remote configuration.

nodes.label: skipWebFetchPreflight
nodes.rationale: Skips the WebFetch domain safety check, which sends each requested hostname to api.anthropic.com before fetching, for deployments with restrictive egress. With the check skipped WebFetch attempts any URL without consulting the blocklist, so WebFetch permission rules become the only restriction.

nodes.label: Telemetry switches are environment variables
nodes.rationale: The switches that turn off usage metrics and error reports are not settings keys: DISABLE_TELEMETRY, DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC are set in the env key or the shell. Only feedbackDrafts and feedbackSurveyRate turn their features off from a settings file directly.

nodes.label: disableSideloadFlags
