nodes.rationale: Rejects --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents and --mcp-config at startup, which users could otherwise pass to bypass strictKnownMarketplaces for one run, and applies the same check to surfaces that start the CLI with those flags internally. In cloud sessions Claude Code instead drops the server-delivered MCP servers and starts, and a --mcp-config of only in-process sdk entries is still accepted.

nodes.label: forceRemoteSettingsRefresh
nodes.rationale: Blocks CLI startup until server-managed settings have been freshly fetched and exits if the fetch fails, for environments that cannot accept even a brief window running without policy. Claude Code honors a true from any admin-controlled managed source, applies it only in sessions that fetch those settings, and exempts the claude auth subcommands so expired credentials can be fixed.

nodes.label: managedSourcesBehavior
nodes.rationale: Chooses between first-wins, where the highest-priority managed source carrying a policy key supplies the policy and lower sources contribute only the cross-source keys, and merge, where every admin source contributes its keys. Claude Code reads the key from the highest source carrying it or a policy key, so a lower source cannot opt itself into combining with the source above it.

nodes.label: How merge combines each kind of key
nodes.rationale: Under merge, lists combine entries from every source, locks apply the strictest value any source sets, restriction allowlists such as availableModels, allowedMcpServers and strictKnownMarketplaces are taken whole from the highest source that sets one, credential and login helpers are read from the highest-priority source only, env merges per variable, and every other key takes the highest source's value. modelOverrides is ignored entirely when a higher source sets availableModels without it.

nodes.label: parentSettingsBehavior
nodes.rationale: Decides what happens to managed settings supplied by an embedding host such as the Agent SDK or an IDE extension when an admin-deployed managed tier is also present: first-wins drops them, merge applies them under the admin tier through a restrictive-only filter. With no admin tier the host's settings apply as the only managed tier, still filtered to restrictive values.

nodes.label: policyHelper
nodes.rationale: Runs an executable that computes managed settings at startup, so policy can derive from device posture, identity or a remote service instead of a static file. It is read only from the macOS plist, the Windows HKLM registry or the managed settings file, and only when that is the highest-priority managed source delivering settings.

nodes.label: policyHelper.path
nodes.rationale: Names the helper executable, required when policyHelper is set. It must be an absolute path in normalized form with no . or .. segments, and on Windows a drive-letter or UNC path ending in .exe.

nodes.label: policyHelper.timeoutMs
nodes.rationale: How long Claude Code waits for the helper before treating the run as failed, minimum 1000 ms and default 10000. A timed-out run fails the same way as a non-zero exit, so at startup Claude Code refuses to start.

nodes.label: policyHelper.refreshIntervalMs
nodes.rationale: Re-runs the helper in the background on an interval, at least 60000 ms, so policy changes reach a running session without a restart. A successful refresh replaces the previous managed settings; a failed one leaves the existing policy in effect.

nodes.label: The policy helper output envelope
nodes.rationale: The helper runs with no arguments, gets CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION in its environment, and must print a JSON envelope of at most 1 MiB whose settings sit under a managedSettings key; a bare settings object applies nothing and reports no error. When managedSettings is emitted it becomes the only managed source for the run, so the MDM, file and HKCU sources are ignored and parent settings never merge.

nodes.label: Policy helper failures fail closed
nodes.rationale: A helper run fails on a bad path, a missing regular file, a non-zero exit, a timeout, a failure to start, more than 1 MiB on stdout or stderr, or output that is not a single JSON object with a repairable managedSettings. A failed startup run prints the reason, including the helper's stderr, and refuses to start; the docs call the refusal deliberate and tell a helper needing outage resilience to serve from its own cache and exit 0.

nodes.label: wslInheritsWindowsSettings
nodes.rationale: Makes Claude Code on WSL read managed settings from the Windows policy chain, with HKLM and the Windows managed settings file above /etc/claude-code and HKCU below it. It is honored only from an admin-writable Windows source, HKCU joins the chain only by also setting it true, and a Windows source holding only this key does not count as a policy source.

nodes.label: IDE keys in ~/.claude.json
nodes.rationale: autoConnectIde connects to a running VS Code or JetBrains IDE automatically from an external terminal, defaulting to false, and autoInstallIdeExtension installs the IDE extension automatically from a VS Code terminal, defaulting to true; diffTool chooses whether a proposed edit opens in the IDE diff viewer or stays in the terminal. All three are ignored in settings.json.

nodes.label: Prompt keys in ~/.claude.json
nodes.rationale: externalEditorContext starts the Ctrl+G editor buffer with Claude's last response as # comment lines, keeping the last 50 lines and stripping them on save, and permissionExplainerEnabled controls the Ctrl+E model-generated explanation of a Bash or PowerShell command, labelled Low, Med or High risk. Both are ignored in settings.json.

nodes.label: teammateDefaultModel (removed)
nodes.rationale: Removed in v2.1.234 along with its /config row Default teammate model, so setting it has no effect on current versions. Through v2.1.233 it named the model for agent-team teammates a prompt did not name a model for, with null meaning follow the lead's model.

nodes.label: Claude Code settings
nodes.rationale: Settings are the JSON keys that change how Claude Code behaves: which model it starts with, what it can run without asking, which files it cannot read, how it looks in the terminal, and what an organization enforces. Claude Code reads them from JSON settings files in several locations, and the file a setting is read from decides who the setting applies to.

nodes.label: Settings files and who they affect
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reads settings from four files — user, shared project, project local, and managed — and an organization can also deliver managed settings from the claude.ai console. In the File column '~/.claude' is the .claude folder in the home directory and a bare '.claude' is the .claude folder inside the project.

nodes.label: Setting scope
nodes.rationale: Each settings source has a scope: the set of people and projects a setting saved in it applies to — just you, everyone in a project, or everyone in an organization. Choosing the file is therefore how you choose the audience a setting reaches.

nodes.label: User settings (~/.claude/settings.json)
nodes.rationale: '~/.claude/settings.json' applies to you in every project on this machine, and reaches nothing on a teammate's machine or in a cloud session. It is where personal preferences belong: theme, editor mode, default model, and your own permission rules.

nodes.label: Shared project settings (.claude/settings.json)
nodes.rationale: '.claude/settings.json' applies to everyone working in the folder that contains it, and holds team permissions, hooks, plugins and project environment variables. It reaches a teammate's clone or a cloud session only once it is committed to version control; until then it is just a file on your disk.

nodes.label: Project local settings (.claude/settings.local.json)
nodes.rationale: '.claude/settings.local.json' applies to you in one project only, and is applied over the committed '.claude/settings.json' — so a team file setting "model": "claude-sonnet-5" can be overridden for your sessions alone. It is for personal overrides and for testing before you share.

nodes.label: Managed settings
nodes.rationale: Managed settings are deployed by an organization through 'managed-settings.json', an MDM or OS-level policy, server-managed settings from the claude.ai console, or an embedding host's SDK 'managedSettings' option. They apply wherever Claude Code runs on the machine and nothing a developer sets overrides them, apart from a few security-sensitive exceptions.

nodes.label: Server-managed settings
nodes.rationale: Server-managed settings are fetched by Claude Code from the claude.ai admin console or a self-hosted Claude apps gateway. They are the only managed delivery mechanism that reaches a cloud session, and in a Cowork session running on your machine Claude Code does not fetch them from the console at all.

nodes.label: ~/.claude.json
nodes.rationale: Beyond the four settings files, Claude Code keeps a fifth file '~/.claude.json' that it writes for itself and users need not edit. It holds the sign-in session, MCP server configurations, per-project state such as trust decisions, and the global config keys that '/config' writes.

nodes.label: Global config keys
nodes.rationale: Global config keys apply only from '~/.claude.json'; they cannot be set from a repository file and '--settings' cannot set them either. '/config' writes them there on the user's behalf.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
nodes.rationale: On Windows '~/.claude' means '%USERPROFILE%\.claude'. Setting CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR relocates the home-directory files: Claude Code then stores settings, session history and plugins there instead.

nodes.label: Installing creates no settings file
nodes.rationale: Installing Claude Code does not create any settings file. An existing file came from an organization's deployment, a committed project file, or from you or Claude Code creating the user and project-local files later.

nodes.label: Share settings with your team
nodes.rationale: Committing '.claude/settings.json' gives everyone who clones the repository the same permissions, hooks, telemetry and plugins, while each teammate can still override it in their own '.claude/settings.local.json' without a commit. Some committed keys wait for folder trust and a few never take effect from a repository file at all.

nodes.label: Workspace trust gating
nodes.rationale: 'permissions.allow' rules, 'permissions.additionalDirectories', 'extraKnownMarketplaces' and most 'env' values from a committed project file apply only after each teammate trusts the folder; until then they still see prompts and get no plugins from a marketplace the file declares. 'deny' and 'ask' rules apply right away.

nodes.label: Local file kept out of git automatically
nodes.rationale: The first time Claude Code writes '.claude/settings.local.json' in a git repository that does not already ignore it, it adds '**/.claude/settings.local.json' to the global git excludes file — 'core.excludesFile' when the global config sets it to an absolute or '~'-prefixed path, otherwise '$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/ignore' or '~/.config/git/ignore'. A file you created by hand must be gitignored yourself.

nodes.label: Local allow rules do not wait for trust
nodes.rationale: Because the project-local file is yours and not the repository's, Claude Code applies its 'allow' rules without the workspace-trust step it requires for the committed file — but only while the file stays untracked. If the file is tracked by git, the trust step applies to it too.

nodes.label: Local file lives at the repository root
nodes.rationale: Starting Claude Code in a subdirectory of a git repository makes it read and write '.claude/settings.local.json' at the repository root, applying an approval across the whole repository; in a worktree it uses the main checkout's root. It stays with '.claude/settings.json' instead outside a repository, when the root is your home directory, on Windows, or when the root or its '.git'/'.claude' entry is not owned by your user. Before v2.1.211 the file stayed in the starting directory, and such a file is still read alongside the root one, with the root's value winning on a shared key.

nodes.label: Primary working directory decides which project files load
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reads the shared '.claude/settings.json' from the session's primary working directory, so a file committed at the repository root requires starting Claude Code there. After moving the session with '/cd' it reads both project files from the new directory instead, which requires v2.1.246 or later.

nodes.label: /config menu
nodes.rationale: '/config' opens a Config tab listing a short set of personal options such as theme, editor mode and verbose output — not every settings key — and saves the choice for you. A single option can be set without the menu as '/config verbose=true'. It is part of the terminal interface: the VS Code chat panel and desktop app do not open it.

nodes.label: Editing a settings file
nodes.rationale: The direct route is to open the settings file for the scope you want and add or change a key — for example a 'permissions' block that allows 'Bash(npm run lint)' and denies 'Read(./.env)'. After saving, '/status' confirms the file loaded.

nodes.label: Settings files are strict JSON
nodes.rationale: Settings files are strict JSON: a '//' comment or a trailing comma is a syntax error, and Claude Code reports the file as a Settings Error at the next start.

nodes.label: Published JSON schema ($schema)
nodes.rationale: The '$schema' line points at https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json, giving autocomplete and inline validation in any editor that supports JSON schema. The schema can lag the newest CLI releases, so a validation warning on a recently documented key does not mean the configuration is invalid.

nodes.label: Change a setting for one session
nodes.rationale: A value can be tried for one session without saving it, by '--settings', a key's own flag, or the key's paired environment variable; settings files stay as they were. By contrast, commands run inside a session mostly save the choice — '/config' writes to settings files, '/model' saves a new default, and '/effort' saves the level as the default for the current model.

nodes.label: --settings flag
nodes.rationale: '--settings' takes a key as inline JSON or a path to a file and is applied above user, project and local files and below managed settings, merging with the files by the same rules as any other level. It can set any key the user settings file can, but not Managed or Global config keys, and it lasts one session without writing to any file.

nodes.label: Per-key command line flags
nodes.rationale: Some keys have their own flag — '--model' for 'model', '--effort' for 'effortLevel' and 'modelSettings'. Each key's entry on the settings reference lists its per-session overrides and which one takes precedence.

nodes.label: Paired environment variables
nodes.rationale: A key's paired shell variable exported before running 'claude' changes it for that session, such as ANTHROPIC_MODEL for 'model'. Which one wins is decided per pair: ANTHROPIC_MODEL applies over the 'model' key from any file, while ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL applies only when no file sets 'model'.

nodes.label: Settings reload without a restart
nodes.rationale: Claude Code watches the settings files and reloads them on change, applying most edits to the running session — including 'permissions', 'hooks' and credential helpers such as 'apiKeyHelper' — across user, project, local and managed settings. Managed settings arriving via MDM or the claude.ai console instead reach a running session on a schedule.

nodes.label: ConfigChange hook
nodes.rationale: Claude Code runs the 'ConfigChange' hook for each settings-file change it detects during a reload. It does not run it for managed settings that arrive from MDM or the claude.ai console.

nodes.label: Keys read only at session start
nodes.rationale: Some keys are read only once at session start, so an edit to them never reaches the running session; admin-side keys such as 'requiredMinimumVersion' also wait for a restart. The ones a user is most likely to edit mid-session are 'model', 'effortLevel'/'modelSettings' and 'outputStyle', each with a slash-command route instead.

nodes.label: model key
nodes.rationale: 'model' sets the model a session starts with and is read only at session start; '/model' switches mid-session, and pressing 's' in the picker switches without saving a new user default. Each model has its own prompt cache, so the first request after a switch re-reads the whole conversation uncached.

nodes.label: effortLevel and modelSettings effort
nodes.rationale: 'effortLevel' and 'modelSettings' are read at session start, so '/effort' is the way to change effort mid-session. Some levels, such as 'max' and 'ultracode', apply to the current session only rather than saving as a default.

nodes.label: outputStyle key
nodes.rationale: 'outputStyle' is part of the system prompt, so Claude Code applies an edit to it only after '/clear' or a restart.

nodes.label: The system prompt is not published
nodes.rationale: Claude Code's system prompt is not published. Standing instructions are given instead through 'CLAUDE.md' files or the '--append-system-prompt' flag.

nodes.label: /status Setting sources line
nodes.rationale: '/status' shows a 'Setting sources' line naming each settings file loaded for the current session, and shows in parentheses how managed settings reached the machine. It confirms which files were read but not which file supplied each key, and the Config tab is not a view of settings.json contents.

nodes.label: claude doctor
nodes.rationale: 'claude doctor' lists the entries Claude Code rejected and the details of each error. It is the way to see what was dropped after a '-p' run, which shows no dialog and silently continues with the rest.

nodes.label: A broken settings file
nodes.rationale: Mistyped JSON or a value Claude Code does not accept is reported at the start of an interactive session, and what it shows depends on how much of the file is affected — a whole-file Settings Error, a per-entry Settings Warning, a managed-settings partial enforcement, or a Configuration error for '~/.claude.json'.

nodes.label: Settings Error
nodes.rationale: A Settings Error means a user, project or local file has invalid JSON or a value the schema rejects. At the start of an interactive session Claude Code shows a dialog offering to fix the file with Claude's help, exit, or continue without the broken settings.

nodes.label: Settings Warning
nodes.rationale: A Settings Warning means only individual entries failed — a malformed permission rule or an unknown hook event name — so Claude Code skips those values and keeps the rest of the file in effect.

nodes.label: Configuration error (~/.claude.json unparsable)
nodes.rationale: When '~/.claude.json' cannot be parsed, Claude Code copies the broken file to '~/.claude/backups/.claude.json.corrupted.<timestamp>' and asks whether to exit and fix it by hand or reset to the default configuration; a '-p' run prints the error and exits. Previous state is recovered by copying back one of the five most recent '.claude.json.backup.<timestamp>' files.

nodes.label: Settings precedence stack
nodes.rationale: When the same key appears in more than one place Claude Code uses the value from the highest level that sets it. Highest first: managed settings, command line arguments, project local settings, shared project settings, user settings.

nodes.label: Environment variables are not a precedence level
nodes.rationale: Environment variables are not a level in the precedence stack: when a behavior has both a shell variable and a settings key, which applies is decided per pair rather than by level. An 'env' block inside a settings file is an ordinary key and does follow the levels.

nodes.label: Lists merge instead of overriding
nodes.rationale: When the same list key, such as 'permissions.allow', is set in more than one file, Claude Code combines the lists rather than picking one, so each file can add entries without removing another file's. Four model-related keys follow their own rules instead.

nodes.label: fallbackModel
nodes.rationale: 'fallbackModel' is an ordered chain in which position carries meaning, so Claude Code takes the whole value from the highest-precedence file that defines it rather than merging entries.

nodes.label: modelPicker
nodes.rationale: 'modelPicker' holds one ordered list of rows plus a replace flag, so rows from two sources are never merged. Claude Code takes the whole value from the highest of managed settings, '--settings' and user settings that defines it, and ignores the key in project and local settings; it requires v2.1.242 or later.

nodes.label: availableModels
nodes.rationale: 'availableModels' is the organizational lock on model choice: it constrains '/model', '--model' and the 'model' key in a developer's own files. When applied managed settings define it, that list applies as-is and user/project/local entries are ignored unless an embedding app supplies its own list; across non-managed scopes the arrays merge as usual.

nodes.label: modelSettings
nodes.rationale: 'modelSettings' is resolved one model at a time, together with 'effortLevel'; the key's own reference entry states which file's value applies to a given model.

nodes.label: Exceptions to managed settings precedence
nodes.rationale: For a few security-sensitive keys Claude Code honors a restrictive value from a scope that otherwise could not override managed settings. A table names each key, the value honored, and the scopes it may come from.

nodes.label: disableClaudeAiConnectors
nodes.rationale: 'disableClaudeAiConnectors' is honored as 'true' from any scope, even when a managed source sets 'false' — so a project 'true' stays on.

nodes.label: enableArtifact / disableArtifact
nodes.rationale: 'enableArtifact: false' from any scope, and 'disableArtifact: true' from any scope, are honored even when a managed source sets 'true'; once off, nothing turns the Artifact tool back on. Requires Claude Code v2.1.242 or later.

nodes.label: isolatePeerMachines
nodes.rationale: 'isolatePeerMachines' is honored as 'true' from any scope, even when a managed source sets 'false'.

nodes.label: remoteControlAtStartup
nodes.rationale: 'remoteControlAtStartup' is honored as 'false' from '.claude/settings.json' or '.claude/settings.local.json' even when a managed source sets 'true'; a project or local 'true' is ignored.

nodes.label: crossSessionInbound
nodes.rationale: 'crossSessionInbound' honors a stricter value from '.claude/settings.json' or '.claude/settings.local.json' on the ladder accept < hold < refuse, over managed, '--settings' and user values. A project or local value that is not stricter is ignored.

nodes.label: useAutoModeDuringPlan
nodes.rationale: 'useAutoModeDuringPlan' honors 'false' from any managed source, '--settings', '~/.claude/settings.json' or '.claude/settings.local.json' even when the winning managed source sets 'true'; a 'false' in the shared '.claude/settings.json' is ignored.

nodes.label: syncClaudeAiSkills
nodes.rationale: 'syncClaudeAiSkills' honors 'false' from any managed source, '--settings', '~/.claude/settings.json' or '.claude/settings.local.json' even when the winning managed source sets 'true'; a 'false' in the shared '.claude/settings.json' is ignored.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST
nodes.rationale: An app that runs Claude Code inside itself and sets CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST is also an exception: its model configuration is taken over 'model', 'fallbackModel' and 'modelOverrides' from every managed source and over model-selection variables in a managed 'env' block. A managed 'availableModels' allowlist stays in force unless the app supplies its own.

nodes.label: Settings in cloud sessions
nodes.rationale: A cloud session on Claude Code on the web, or from 'claude --cloud', runs in a cloud environment on a fresh clone rather than on your machine, so it reads the committed '.claude/settings.json' but not user or project-local files. On the web '/config' opens the Claude Code section of claude.ai settings instead of changing a value; changing a setting there means an environment variable on the environment or a committed key.

nodes.label: Troubleshoot a setting that doesn't apply
nodes.rationale: When a key does not take effect, start with '/status' to see which files loaded, then match the symptom: a higher level or a flag/variable sets the same key, a security key keeps its strict value, the file is broken, a managed change has not arrived yet, a committed key is ignored or waiting for trust, or permission rules combined differently than expected.

nodes.label: Keys ignored in a repository file
nodes.rationale: Keys whose Scope column on the settings reference reads 'User, local, or managed', 'User or managed', 'Managed' or 'Global config' never apply from the shared repository file, so committing them does not reach teammates. Global config keys apply only from '~/.claude.json'.

nodes.label: autoContinueAtUsageLimit
nodes.rationale: 'autoContinueAtUsageLimit' is the exception to keys ignored in a repository file: a repository file can still switch it off — while that file sets the key and no user, '--settings' or managed value does, Claude Code reads the setting as off.

nodes.label: permissions key
nodes.rationale: Each entry under 'permissions' is a rule naming a tool and what it may do, in 'allow', 'ask' and 'deny' lists — for example allowing 'Bash(npm run lint)' while denying 'Read(./.env)'. Edits to 'permissions' are picked up by a running session without a restart.

nodes.label: permissions.allow rules
nodes.rationale: Choosing 'Yes, and don't ask again' on a permission prompt saves an 'allow' rule to the project-local file, and such a rule does not outrank an 'ask' rule from a project or managed file — which is why the same tool can still prompt. In the VS Code extension the approval card lets you pick the destination file, including the shared project file; the CLI writes only to the local file.

nodes.label: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly
nodes.rationale: Claude Code merges 'permissions.allow' across scopes, so an organization's allow rules apply alongside a developer's — unless the organization sets 'allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly'.

nodes.label: Check what your organization enforces
nodes.rationale: When an organization manages Claude Code, some settings are decided for the developer and nothing in their own files changes them; '/status' names the managed source that applies. A managed change that has not arrived yet is fixed by restarting, since managed sources reach a running session on a delivery schedule.

nodes.label: Advanced setup page
nodes.rationale: The Claude Code 'Advanced setup' page covers system requirements, platform-specific installation, verification, authentication, updates, binary integrity, and uninstallation. It defers a guided first session to the quickstart and first-time terminal users to the terminal guide.

nodes.label: System requirements
nodes.rationale: Claude Code declares a supported matrix of operating system, hardware, network, shell, and geographic location, plus additional runtime dependencies. Running outside that matrix is unsupported.

nodes.label: Supported operating systems
nodes.rationale: Supported operating systems are macOS 13.0+, Windows 10 1809+ or Windows Server 2019+, Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 10+, and Alpine Linux 3.19+.

nodes.label: Hardware requirements
nodes.rationale: Claude Code requires 4 GB or more of RAM and an x64 or ARM64 processor.

nodes.label: Internet connection requirement
nodes.rationale: An internet connection is required; the network configuration page documents the network access requirements. Availability is also limited to Anthropic supported countries.

nodes.label: Supported shells
nodes.rationale: Claude Code supports Bash, Zsh, PowerShell, or CMD as the host shell.

nodes.label: ripgrep dependency
nodes.rationale: ripgrep is usually bundled with Claude Code and powers search; if search fails the docs route to the search-and-discovery troubleshooting section. On musl distributions a system ripgrep must be installed instead.

nodes.label: Installation methods
nodes.rationale: Claude Code ships through several installation channels — the native installer (recommended), Homebrew, WinGet, signed apt/dnf/apk repositories, and a global npm package — all delivering the same native binary. After install, running `claude` in a project directory opens an interactive session.

nodes.label: Native installer
nodes.rationale: The recommended install is `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash` on macOS/Linux/WSL, `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex` in PowerShell, or the install.cmd fetch in CMD. Native installations update automatically in the background.

nodes.label: Homebrew casks (claude-code vs claude-code@latest)
nodes.rationale: `brew install --cask claude-code` tracks the stable channel (about a week behind, skipping releases with major regressions) while `claude-code@latest` tracks latest. Homebrew installs do not auto-update and keep old versions on disk until `brew cleanup`.

nodes.label: WinGet install
nodes.rationale: `winget install Anthropic.ClaudeCode` installs on Windows and does not auto-update; `winget upgrade Anthropic.ClaudeCode` must be run periodically. A WinGet upgrade can fail while Claude Code is running because Windows locks the executable.

nodes.label: Signed apt/dnf/apk repositories
nodes.rationale: Claude Code publishes signed apt, dnf, and apk repositories, each offering a `stable` channel (about a week old) and a `latest` channel. Package-manager installs do not auto-update through Claude Code; updates arrive through the system upgrade workflow, and apt/dnf/apk upgrades need elevated privileges.

nodes.label: Global npm install
nodes.rationale: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` installs the same native binary as the standalone installer. Upgrade with `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest` rather than `npm update -g`, which respects the original semver range, and never use `sudo npm install -g`.

nodes.label: npm package Node.js 22 requirement
nodes.rationale: As of v2.1.198 the npm package requires Node.js 22 or later. On an older Node.js, npm prints an EBADENGINE warning rather than failing, and `claude` still runs because the installed binary is native and does not invoke Node at runtime.

nodes.label: Per-platform optional dependency binary
nodes.rationale: npm pulls the native binary through a per-platform optional dependency such as `@anthropic-ai/claude-code-darwin-arm64`, linked into place by a postinstall step. Supported platforms include darwin-arm64/x64, linux-x64/arm64 (glibc and musl), and win32-x64/arm64; the package manager must allow optional dependencies.

nodes.label: Desktop app alternative
nodes.rationale: Users who prefer a graphical interface can run Claude Code through the Desktop app on macOS, Windows, or Linux instead of the terminal.

nodes.label: Windows setup options
nodes.rationale: On Windows the choice is native Windows, WSL 2, or WSL 1, decided by where the projects live and which features are needed. Sandboxing is supported only under WSL 2.

nodes.label: Native Windows install
nodes.rationale: The native Windows path runs the installer from PowerShell or CMD with no Administrator rights and no prerequisites; Git for Windows is optional. It suits Windows-native projects and tools but does not support sandboxing.

nodes.label: WSL install
nodes.rationale: Under WSL you run the Linux installer inside the WSL distribution and launch `claude` from the WSL terminal, not from PowerShell or CMD. WSL setups do not need Git for Windows.

nodes.label: Sandboxing on Windows
nodes.rationale: Sandboxed command execution is supported only with WSL 2; native Windows and WSL 1 do not support sandboxing.

nodes.label: Git for Windows
nodes.rationale: Git for Windows is recommended (but optional) on native Windows because it provides Git Bash, which is what lets Claude Code offer the Bash tool.

nodes.label: Bash tool on Windows
nodes.rationale: With Git for Windows installed, Claude Code uses Git Bash to back the Bash tool on native Windows.

nodes.label: PowerShell tool
nodes.rationale: Without Git for Windows, Claude Code runs shell commands through the PowerShell tool. When Git for Windows is present the PowerShell tool is available alongside Bash: on by default for claude.ai and Console accounts, and enabled with CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1 on Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH
nodes.rationale: If Claude Code cannot find Git Bash, the `CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH` env entry in settings.json points it at the bash.exe path explicitly.

nodes.label: Alpine / musl setup
nodes.rationale: On Alpine and other musl/uClibc distributions the install command needs `bash` and `curl`, and the runtime needs `libgcc`, `libstdc++`, and `ripgrep`. Alpine ships none of bash/curl by default, so the documented install fails with a 'not found' error until they are added; ripgrep lives in the community repository.

nodes.label: USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP=0
nodes.rationale: On musl-based distributions `USE_BUILTIN_RIPGREP` must be set to `0` in the settings.json `env` block so Claude Code uses the system ripgrep instead of its bundled build.

nodes.label: Verify your installation
nodes.rationale: After installing, the install is confirmed with a version check and, for a deeper look, a diagnostics command. A `command not found` or other error routes to the install/login troubleshooting page.

nodes.label: claude --version
nodes.rationale: `claude --version` prints a version number such as `2.1.211 (Claude Code)` on a working installation, and prints the exact version requested when a specific version was installed.

nodes.label: claude doctor
nodes.rationale: `claude doctor` prints read-only installation and settings diagnostics without starting a session — install health, settings-file validation errors, warnings with suggested fixes, the result of the most recent update attempt, and whether the launcher was created by the native installer.

nodes.label: Authenticate
nodes.rationale: After installing, you log in by running `claude` and following the browser prompts; the Authentication page covers all account types and team setup.

nodes.label: Paid account requirement
nodes.rationale: Claude Code requires a Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise, or Console account; the free Claude.ai plan does not include Claude Code access.

nodes.label: Third-party API providers
nodes.rationale: Claude Code can also run against a third-party API provider — Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, or Microsoft Foundry — instead of a first-party account.

nodes.label: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY approval prompt
nodes.rationale: If the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable is set, Claude Code prompts once to approve that key instead of opening a browser login.

nodes.label: Update Claude Code
nodes.rationale: Update behaviour splits by install method: native installs update automatically in the background, while Homebrew, WinGet, and Linux package installs require manual updates by default. Settings control the channel, a version floor, and whether updating happens at all.

nodes.label: Background auto-updates
nodes.rationale: Claude Code checks for updates at startup and periodically while running; updates download and install in the background and take effect at the next start. If an npm global install cannot auto-update because the npm global directory is not writable, a one-time startup notice appears and `claude doctor` lists the fixes.

nodes.label: Custom launcher at ~/.local/bin/claude
nodes.rationale: On macOS and Linux the native installer manages `~/.local/bin/claude` as a symlink into `~/.local/share/claude/versions/`. Since v2.1.207 a user-supplied launcher at that path is left in place — new versions still install under `versions/` and the launcher chooses which runs — and every installed version is retained because Claude Code cannot tell which one the launcher needs. Removing the launcher and running `claude update` hands management back.

nodes.label: claude update
nodes.rationale: `claude update` applies an update immediately without waiting for the next background check, reporting 'Successfully updated from <old> to version <new>' or that Claude Code is already up to date. Homebrew, WinGet, and apk installs report 'Claude is up to date!' instead.

nodes.label: autoUpdatesChannel setting
nodes.rationale: `autoUpdatesChannel` in settings.json (or `/config` -> Auto-update channel) selects which release channel auto-updates and `claude update` follow. Managed settings can enforce one channel across an organization.

nodes.label: latest release channel
nodes.rationale: `"latest"` is the default channel and delivers new features as soon as they are released.

nodes.label: stable release channel
nodes.rationale: `"stable"` serves a version typically about one week old, skipping releases with major regressions. The same stable/latest split appears in Homebrew cask names and in the apt/dnf/apk repository URLs.

nodes.label: minimumVersion floor
nodes.rationale: `minimumVersion` establishes a floor that background auto-updates and `claude update` refuse to go below, so switching to the stable channel cannot downgrade a newer latest build. Switching latest -> stable via `/config` offers to set it to the current version; switching back clears it. In managed settings it is an org-wide minimum users cannot override.

nodes.label: requiredMinimumVersion / requiredMaximumVersion
nodes.rationale: `minimumVersion` only constrains updates; the managed settings `requiredMinimumVersion` and `requiredMaximumVersion` make Claude Code refuse to start outside a version range, and updates also respect the maximum ceiling.

nodes.label: DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER
nodes.rationale: Setting `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER` to `"1"` in the settings.json `env` key stops only the background update check; `claude update` and `claude install` still work.

nodes.label: DISABLE_UPDATES
nodes.rationale: `DISABLE_UPDATES` blocks all update paths including manual ones — the setting to use when distributing Claude Code through your own channels and requiring users to stay on the version you provide.

nodes.label: CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE
nodes.rationale: Setting `CLAUDE_CODE_PACKAGE_MANAGER_AUTO_UPDATE` to `1` makes Claude Code run the Homebrew or WinGet upgrade command in the background when a new version appears, showing a restart prompt on success and the manual command when the upgrade is blocked. It targets only the Claude Code package; apt/dnf/apk stay manual because they need elevated privileges.

nodes.label: Install a specific version or channel
nodes.rationale: The native installer accepts either a version number or a channel name as an argument (e.g. `bash -s stable`, `bash -s 2.1.89`), and the channel chosen at install time becomes the default for auto-updates.

nodes.label: Binary integrity and code signing
nodes.rationale: Release integrity rests on a GPG-signed per-release manifest of SHA256 checksums plus platform-native code signatures, so verifying the manifest signature transitively verifies every binary it lists.

nodes.label: Claude Code release signing key
nodes.rationale: The release signing key is published at https://downloads.claude.ai/keys/claude-code.asc and its fingerprint must read 31DD DE24 DDFA B679 F42D 7BD2 BAA9 29FF 1A7E CACE. The apk variant of the key is checked with sha256sum against 395759c1f7449ef4cdef305a42e820f3c766d6090d142634ebdb049f113168b6.

nodes.label: Signed release manifest.json
nodes.rationale: Every release publishes a `manifest.json` of SHA256 checksums for each platform binary, fetched from https://downloads.claude.ai/claude-code-releases/<version>/ alongside a detached `manifest.json.sig`. Manifest signatures exist for releases from 2.1.89 onward; earlier releases publish checksums without a signature.

nodes.label: gpg --verify of the manifest
nodes.rationale: `gpg --verify manifest.json.sig manifest.json` must report a Good signature from 'Anthropic Claude Code Release Signing <security@anthropic.com>'. The accompanying 'key is not certified with a trusted signature' warning is expected for a freshly imported key; the fingerprint comparison is what establishes authenticity.

nodes.label: Binary SHA256 check against the manifest
nodes.rationale: The binary's SHA256 (sha256sum on Linux, shasum -a 256 on macOS, Get-FileHash in PowerShell) is compared with `platforms.<platform>.checksum` in manifest.json; an installed native binary is checked at ~/.local/share/claude/versions/<VERSION>.

nodes.label: Platform code signatures
nodes.rationale: macOS binaries are signed by 'Anthropic PBC' and notarized by Apple (verify with codesign), Windows binaries are signed by 'Anthropic, PBC' (verify with Get-AuthenticodeSignature), and Linux binaries are not individually code-signed — Linux integrity comes from the manifest signature or the package manager's repository key.

nodes.label: Uninstall Claude Code
nodes.rationale: Removal follows the installation method: delete ~/.local/bin/claude and ~/.local/share/claude for a native install, uninstall the Homebrew cask or WinGet package, remove the apt/dnf/apk package plus its repository configuration and key, or `npm uninstall -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`.

nodes.label: Check for conflicting installations
nodes.rationale: If `claude` still runs after uninstalling, there is likely a second installation or a leftover shell alias from an older installer; the troubleshooting page's 'Check for conflicting installations' section finds and removes it.

nodes.label: Remove configuration files
nodes.rationale: Deleting ~/.claude, ~/.claude.json, and a project's .claude and .mcp.json removes all settings, allowed tools, MCP server configurations, and session history — an irreversible cleanup step separate from removing the binary.

nodes.label: Remove other Claude clients first
nodes.rationale: The VS Code extension, the JetBrains plugin, and the Desktop app also write to ~/.claude/, so the directory is recreated the next time any of them runs; complete removal requires uninstalling those clients before deleting the configuration files.

nodes.label: Skill (SKILL.md)
nodes.rationale: Skills extend what Claude can do: you create a SKILL.md file with instructions and Claude adds it to its toolkit. Claude uses a skill when relevant, or you invoke it directly with /skill-name.

nodes.label: When to create a skill
nodes.rationale: Create a skill when you keep pasting the same instructions, checklist or multi-step procedure into chat, or when a section of CLAUDE.md has grown into a procedure rather than a fact. Unlike CLAUDE.md content, a skill's body loads only when used, so long reference material costs almost nothing until needed.

nodes.label: SKILL.md structure
nodes.rationale: Every skill needs a SKILL.md with two parts: YAML frontmatter between --- markers telling Claude when to use the skill, and markdown content with the instructions Claude follows. The directory name becomes the command you type.

nodes.label: Custom commands merged into skills
nodes.rationale: Custom commands have been merged into skills: a file at .claude/commands/deploy.md and a skill at .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy and work the same way. Existing .claude/commands/ files keep working; skills add a directory for supporting files, invocation-control frontmatter, and automatic loading.

nodes.label: Agent Skills open standard
nodes.rationale: Claude Code skills follow the Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io), which works across multiple AI tools. Claude Code extends the standard with additional features such as invocation control, subagent execution, and dynamic context injection.

nodes.label: Bundled skills
nodes.rationale: Claude Code ships bundled skills such as /doctor, /code-review, /batch, /debug, /loop and /claude-api. They are prompt-based — Claude is given detailed instructions and orchestrates the work with its tools — whereas most built-in commands execute fixed logic directly. Some load automatically; others such as /verify run only when invoked.

nodes.label: disableBundledSkills setting
nodes.rationale: The disableBundledSkills setting turns off every bundled skill except /doctor. In v2.1.205 and later /doctor stays typable; to hide it too, set the DISABLE_DOCTOR_COMMAND environment variable or a skillOverrides entry of "doctor": "off".

nodes.label: Run-and-verify bundled skills
nodes.rationale: Three bundled skills work together to launch your app and confirm changes against the running app instead of just tests: /run launches and drives the app, /verify builds and runs it to confirm a change does what it should, and /run-skill-generator teaches both how to build and launch the project. /run and /verify work without setup by inferring the launch from project type, README, package.json or Makefile.

nodes.label: /run-skill-generator recorded recipe
nodes.rationale: Launch inference becomes unreliable for projects needing a database, env file, graphical session or multi-step build. /run-skill-generator gets the app running from a clean environment, captures the install commands, env vars and launch script, and commits them as a per-project skill at .claude/skills/run-<name>/ that /run, /verify and other agents then follow.

nodes.label: /verify self-recorded recipe
nodes.rationale: When /verify has to build and drive an app with no recorded recipe it writes what worked to .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md at the repo root (or the touched package directory in a monorepo), replacing the bundled /verify there; requires v2.1.200+. Since v2.1.205 Claude edits the file only when a run was steered wrong, so it can be committed without per-session diffs.

nodes.label: Where skills live
nodes.rationale: Where a skill is stored determines who can use it: enterprise (managed settings, all users in the organization), personal (~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, all your projects), project (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, this project only) and plugin (<plugin>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, wherever the plugin is enabled).

nodes.label: Skill name conflict resolution
nodes.rationale: When skills share a name Claude Code resolves by source: enterprise overrides personal, personal overrides project; any of those overrides a bundled skill of the same name but not that bundled skill's aliases; plugin skills use a plugin-name:skill-name namespace so they cannot conflict; a skill beats a same-named .claude/commands/ file; and any local source beats a skill synced from claude.ai.

nodes.label: Nested .claude/skills directories
nodes.rationale: Skills also load from nested .claude/skills/ directories below the working directory, becoming available the first time Claude reads or edits a file in that subdirectory, so a monorepo package can ship its own skills. A nested skill that clashes with another name appears under a directory-qualified name such as apps/web:deploy, and invoking the unqualified name appends the qualified variants with an instruction to also invoke the one whose directory holds the files being worked on.

nodes.label: Reserved 'synced' folder name
nodes.rationale: The folder name 'synced' is reserved in the enterprise, personal and project skill locations in any capitalization: Claude Code downloads claude.ai-enabled skills into ~/.claude/skills/synced/ when CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS is set in non-interactive mode, and skips a skill you author at that name.

nodes.label: Skill directory symlinks
nodes.rationale: A <skill-name> entry in the enterprise, personal or project locations can be a symlink to a directory elsewhere on disk; Claude Code follows it and reads SKILL.md from the target, and loads the skill once if the same target is reachable from more than one location. Plugin skills handle symlinks differently.

nodes.label: Skill folder as a skills-dir plugin
nodes.rationale: Adding a .claude-plugin/plugin.json to a skill folder makes it load as a plugin named <name>@skills-dir, so it can bundle agents, hooks and MCP servers. In a project's .claude/skills/ this requires accepting the workspace trust dialog first.

nodes.label: Live change detection
nodes.rationale: Claude Code watches ~/.claude/skills/, the project .claude/skills/ and .claude/skills/ inside an --add-dir directory, picking up added, edited or removed skills within the current session without a restart. It covers SKILL.md text only; for a skill folder that is also a plugin, changes to hooks/, .mcp.json, agents/ and output-styles/ need /reload-plugins. A newly created top-level skills directory needs a restart to be watched.

nodes.label: Discovery from parent directories
nodes.rationale: Project skills load from .claude/skills/ in the directory where Claude Code starts and in every parent directory up to the repository root, so starting in a subdirectory still picks up root skills. On v2.1.246+, moving the session with /cd adds the new directory's project skills. Skills in nested directories below the starting directory are not loaded at startup and do not appear in autocomplete until Claude touches a file there.

nodes.label: --add-dir skill-loading exception
nodes.rationale: --add-dir and /add-dir grant file access rather than configuration discovery, but skills and commands are an exception: Claude Code loads .claude/skills/ and .claude/commands/ from each added directory, including directories the Agent SDK adds via additionalDirectories/add_dirs. The permissions.additionalDirectories setting in settings.json grants file access only and loads no skills, commands or subagents, despite the identical TypeScript option name.

nodes.label: project setting source requirement
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads skills, commands and subagents from an added directory only when the 'project' setting source is enabled, which is the default; if you pass --setting-sources or set settingSources/setting_sources explicitly, include 'project'. In --safe-mode none of the three load.

nodes.label: strictPluginOnlyCustomization and bare mode
nodes.rationale: A strictPluginOnlyCustomization managed policy and bare mode treat the three customization types differently: a skills lock turns off both .claude/skills/ skills and .claude/commands/ commands, while .claude/agents/ subagents are governed by the policy's separate agents entry. Bare mode still loads skills but skips commands and every .claude/agents/ folder, and does not watch skill directories at all.

nodes.label: Skills in Cowork and cloud sessions
nodes.rationale: Cowork sessions and cloud sessions, including routines, do not read ~/.claude/skills/ on your machine; both load the skills enabled for your claude.ai account, synced at session start, and cloud sessions additionally load project skills committed to the cloned repository. A personal-only skill therefore reports as not found when a routine invokes it. Desktop scheduled tasks are different — they run locally and load skills like any local session.

nodes.label: Skills synced from claude.ai
nodes.rationale: Because Claude Code downloads a synced skill from your claude.ai account rather than reading a file you wrote on the machine where the session runs, it applies rules to synced skills that do not apply to locally stored skills. The /skills menu and /context group them under 'claude.ai sync' and the / menu marks their origin.

nodes.label: Downloading synced skills locally
nodes.rationale: Outside Cowork and cloud sessions, Claude Code downloads synced skills only during a non-interactive run with the -p flag and CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS=1; the prompt does not affect the download. They land in ~/.claude/skills/synced/ and persist after the run, so later interactive sessions load them, but the command must be re-run after enabling or changing a skill on claude.ai. CLAUDE_CODE_SYNC_SKILLS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS bounds the wait.

nodes.label: Synced skill name collisions
nodes.rationale: Claude Code skips a synced skill whose name matches any other command — a built-in, a bundled skill, a local or plugin skill, a .claude/commands/ file or an MCP prompt — and reserves its own built-in and bundled names even when unavailable in the session. Name comparison ignores case, spacing and invisible characters and folds compatibility forms such as fullwidth letters and dash variants, though a look-alike letter from another alphabet counts as a different name.

nodes.label: Synced skill frontmatter handling
nodes.rationale: Claude Code honors a synced skill's frontmatter in every kind of session, so an allowed-tools grant goes through the normal permission flow, and it sanitizes the display text the skill supplies — removing control characters and escaping angle brackets in text that reaches Claude so it cannot imitate Claude Code's internal formatting.

nodes.label: Synced skill body handling
nodes.rationale: What happens to a synced skill's body depends on the session: in a cloud session it behaves like a local skill because the container is isolated; in a Cowork desktop session it behaves locally except that every ! command line is replaced with the disableSkillShellExecution placeholder; in any other local session Claude Code runs no ! commands, does not attach @-referenced files, and does not substitute ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} or ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}, so all of these reach Claude as literal text.

nodes.label: Removing a skill
nodes.rationale: Removal depends on origin: delete the directory for a personal or project skill; an administrator deletes it from the managed settings directory for an enterprise skill; disable or uninstall the providing plugin (then /reload-plugins or restart) for a plugin skill; turn it off on claude.ai for a synced skill, since deleting the directory by hand only causes the next sync to re-download it; and use disableBundledSkills or a skillOverrides "off" entry for a bundled skill.

nodes.label: Reference skill content
nodes.rationale: Reference content adds knowledge Claude applies to current work — conventions, patterns, style guides, domain knowledge. It runs inline so Claude can use it alongside the conversation context, as in an api-conventions skill listing RESTful naming and error-format rules.

nodes.label: Task skill content
nodes.rationale: Task content gives Claude step-by-step instructions for a specific action such as a deployment, commit or code generation. These are often invoked directly with /skill-name, so they commonly set disable-model-invocation: true to stop Claude triggering them, and may set context: fork to run in their own subagent context.

nodes.label: Keep the skill body concise
nodes.rationale: Once a skill loads, its content stays in context across turns, so every line is a recurring token cost. State what to do rather than narrating how or why, and apply the same conciseness test used for CLAUDE.md content.

nodes.label: Frontmatter parsing rules
nodes.rationale: Skill behavior is configured with YAML frontmatter between --- markers at the top of SKILL.md. All fields are optional and only description is recommended. Claude Code reads the frontmatter only when the opening --- is the file's first line, otherwise the whole file including the markers is treated as content. Since v2.1.218 boolean fields also accept yes/no/on/off/1/0 in any case.

nodes.label: description and when_to_use fields
nodes.rationale: description says what the skill does and when to use it and is what Claude matches on; if omitted, the first paragraph of markdown is used. when_to_use adds trigger phrases or example requests and is appended to description in the skill listing. The combined text is truncated at 1,536 characters in the listing, so the key use case goes first.

nodes.label: disable-model-invocation
nodes.rationale: disable-model-invocation: true means only you can invoke the skill — its description is kept out of Claude's context, it cannot be preloaded into subagents, and as of v2.1.196 it will not run when a scheduled task fires with the skill as its prompt. Use it for workflows with side effects such as /commit, /deploy or /send-slack-message; if Claude tries anyway, Claude Code blocks the call and tells it not to reproduce the steps another way.

nodes.label: user-invocable: false
nodes.rationale: user-invocable: false means only Claude should invoke the skill: Claude Code hides it from the / menu and does not run it when you type /name. Use it for background knowledge that is not a meaningful user action, such as a legacy-system-context skill.

nodes.label: Invocation control and context loading
nodes.rationale: By default both you and Claude can invoke a skill, its description is always in context and the full content loads on invocation. With disable-model-invocation: true only you can invoke it and its description is not in context; with user-invocable: false only Claude can invoke it while the description stays in context. Subagents with preloaded skills differ: the full skill content is injected at startup.

nodes.label: allowed-tools pre-approval
nodes.rationale: allowed-tools grants permission for the listed tools during the turn that invokes the skill and clears when you send your next message; it does not restrict which tools are available, and ordinary permission settings still govern unlisted tools. Workspace trust does not gate it — a project skill's allowed-tools applies even in a -p run in an untrusted folder — so review checked-in skills' allowed-tools before running Claude Code in a repository.

nodes.label: disallowed-tools
nodes.rationale: disallowed-tools removes tools from Claude's available pool while the skill is active — useful for an autonomous skill that should never call AskUserQuestion — and the restriction clears on your next message. Like deny rules, it cannot remove EndConversation while any other tool remains; blocking tools across all skills and prompts needs deny rules in permission settings.

nodes.label: model and effort fields
nodes.rationale: model sets the model while the skill is active for the rest of the current turn without saving to settings, accepts the same values as /model or 'inherit', is ignored when the organization's availableModels allowlist excludes it, and with context: fork sets the forked subagent's model instead. effort overrides the session effort level with low, medium, high, xhigh or max, depending on the model.

nodes.label: context: fork
nodes.rationale: Adding context: fork runs a skill in isolation: the skill content becomes the prompt driving a subagent that has no access to your conversation history. It only makes sense for skills with explicit instructions — a skill of guidelines with no task gives the subagent no actionable prompt and it returns without meaningful output.

nodes.label: agent field and Explore/Plan agents
nodes.rationale: The agent field picks which subagent configuration executes a forked skill — a built-in Explore, Plan or general-purpose agent, or a custom subagent from .claude/agents/ — defaulting to general-purpose, and it determines model, tools and permissions. A forked skill loads CLAUDE.md except when the agent is Explore or Plan, which skip CLAUDE.md and git status to keep context small.

nodes.label: Background execution of forked skills
nodes.rationale: A forked subagent runs in the background by default, returning its result into the conversation when it completes; background: false waits within the invoking turn instead (before v2.1.218 forked skills always blocked). Claude Code also waits in non-interactive/-p or SDK runs, with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1, when a prior invocation of the same skill is still running, and when a scheduled task fires the skill. A backgrounded fork gets the narrower background-subagent tool set and its edits fall outside session checkpoints, so /rewind cannot undo them.

nodes.label: hooks field
nodes.rationale: The hooks frontmatter field declares hooks that Claude Code registers when the skill is invoked and keeps running for the rest of the session; the hooks documentation covers the configuration format and the 'once' option.

nodes.label: paths field
nodes.rationale: paths takes glob patterns (comma-separated string or YAML list) that limit activation: when set, Claude loads the skill automatically only when working with files matching the patterns, using the same format as path-specific memory rules.

nodes.label: shell field (bash or powershell)
nodes.rationale: shell selects the shell for a skill's inline !`command` and ```! blocks, accepting bash (default) or powershell; powershell runs them via the PowerShell tool, which is on by default on Windows without Git Bash and needs CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL=1 on macOS, Linux, WSL and Bedrock/Google Agent Platform/Microsoft Foundry sessions.

nodes.label: metadata, license and compatibility fields
nodes.rationale: metadata is a free-form YAML map for your own key-value data read by your own tooling, which Claude Code does not act on and drops if it is not a map; license and compatibility come from the Agent Skills spec (compatibility accepting up to 500 characters) and Claude Code accepts but does not act on either.

nodes.label: Spec frontmatter limit outside Claude Code
nodes.rationale: Claude Code accepts every frontmatter field, but claude.ai uploads, the Skills API and packaging with package_skill.py accept only the spec's six fields — name, description, license, compatibility, metadata and allowed-tools — and any other field makes packaging or upload fail with a hard 'Unexpected key(s) in SKILL.md frontmatter' error. Claude Code-only body features such as dynamic context injection also do not function in claude.ai chat or through the API.

nodes.label: How a skill gets its command name
nodes.rationale: For a personal or project skill the command comes from the directory name and the frontmatter name only sets the display label; for a plugin skill name replaces the last command segment behind the plugin prefix (my-plugin/skills/review with name: fancy becomes /my-plugin:fancy, and bare /fancy also works unless taken). On v2.1.246+ a name already carrying the plugin prefix is not doubled, and a plugin-root SKILL.md takes its whole final segment from name, falling back to the plugin directory name.

nodes.label: String substitutions in skill content
nodes.rationale: Skill content supports $ARGUMENTS for the full argument string, $ARGUMENTS[N] and its $N shorthand for 0-based positional access, $name for arguments declared in the arguments frontmatter list, and the ${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}, ${CLAUDE_EFFORT}, ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} variables.

nodes.label: ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} in body and allowed-tools
nodes.rationale: Claude Code substitutes ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} and ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} (and, in plugin skills, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}) in two places: the skill's markdown content and Bash rules in allowed-tools. Using the same variable in both lets an allowed-tools rule match the exact bundled-script command the body tells Claude to run, so it executes without a permission prompt. ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} requires v2.1.196 or later.

nodes.label: Argument quoting, literals and escaping
nodes.rationale: Indexed arguments use shell-style quoting, so multi-word values must be quoted. An indexed placeholder with no argument stays unchanged while a named placeholder with none expands to an empty string. Argument values containing $1 or $ARGUMENTS are inserted literally and not re-expanded, and a single backslash before a placeholder escapes it, though a backslash never prevents substitution of a ${CLAUDE_*} variable.

nodes.label: Supporting files in a skill directory
nodes.rationale: A skill directory can hold extra files — reference.md, examples.md, scripts/helper.py — so SKILL.md stays focused and large reference material loads only when needed rather than every time the skill runs. Reference them from SKILL.md so Claude knows what each contains, and keep SKILL.md under 500 lines.

nodes.label: Skill content lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Invoking a skill puts the rendered SKILL.md into the conversation as a single message that persists across later turns, and Claude Code never re-reads the file, so guidance should be written as standing instructions. Re-invoking with identical rendered content adds only a short 'already loaded' note; differing content is appended in full. Auto-compaction re-attaches the most recent invocation of each skill, keeping the first 5,000 tokens each within a combined 25,000-token budget filled most-recent-first, so older skills can be dropped.

nodes.label: Passing arguments and stacking skills
nodes.rationale: Both you and Claude can pass arguments to a skill; if no placeholder receives them, Claude Code appends 'ARGUMENTS: <your input>' to the content. Several skills can be stacked at the start of one message — Claude Code expands the first plus up to five more and passes the trailing text to each — and expansion stops at the first token that is not an inline user-invocable skill, such as a forked /code-review (from v2.1.218) or /loop.

nodes.label: Dynamic context injection
nodes.rationale: The !`<command>` syntax runs shell commands before the skill content is sent to Claude, replacing the placeholder with the command's output so Claude receives actual data. Substitution runs once over the original file and output is not re-scanned, the inline form is recognized only at line start or after whitespace, and multi-line commands use a fenced ```! block.

nodes.label: disableSkillShellExecution setting
nodes.rationale: Setting "disableSkillShellExecution": true replaces each injected command in user, project, plugin and additional-directory skills and custom commands with '[shell command execution disabled by policy]' instead of running it. Bundled and managed skills are unaffected, and the setting is most useful in managed settings where users cannot override it.

nodes.label: How injected commands run
nodes.rationale: Injected commands run through the Bash tool or the PowerShell tool, except that shell: bash with no bash available fails the invocation before any command runs. They run in the session shell's current working directory, merge stderr into stdout under bash, run under the Bash tool's default 2-minute timeout (a timed-out command that can be backgrounded still renders and names the background task and output file, otherwise it is killed and aborts the invocation), and oversized output arrives as a file path plus a short preview.

nodes.label: When an injected command fails
nodes.rationale: A failed injected command aborts the entire skill invocation, not just its placeholder, and Claude never sees the content; the abort shows 'Shell command failed for pattern ...' with the output under [stderr]. Under bash any non-zero exit fails except exit code 1 from listed search and comparison commands, so append || true elsewhere. Injected commands never prompt: any permission check that does not return allow — including a rule that would normally ask — aborts the invocation, and allowed-tools can pre-approve an otherwise unmatched command.

nodes.label: Restricting Claude's skill access
nodes.rationale: Three ways control which skills Claude can invoke: deny the Skill tool in /permissions to disable all skills; use permission rules with Skill(name) for an exact match or Skill(name *) for a prefix match to allow or deny specific ones; or set disable-model-invocation: true to remove a skill from Claude's context entirely. A few built-in commands such as /init and /security-review are reachable through the Skill tool, while others such as /compact are not.

nodes.label: skillOverrides setting
nodes.rationale: skillOverrides controls skill visibility from settings rather than the skill's own frontmatter, for skills whose SKILL.md you do not want to edit. Each key is a skill name with one of four values: "on" (name and description listed, in the / menu), "name-only", "user-invocable-only" (hidden from Claude, still in the menu) and "off" (hidden everywhere, and since v2.1.199 also from Remote Control and Agent SDK command lists). Absent skills are treated as "on"; the /skills menu writes the file, and plugin skills are unaffected.

nodes.label: Evaluating a skill by baseline comparison
nodes.rationale: Seeing a skill trigger tells you Claude found it, not that it did what you intended, so measure two things separately: whether Claude invokes it on the prompts it should, and whether the output matches expectations. The check for both is a baseline comparison — run a few realistic prompts in a fresh session with the skill available and again with it disabled — and the session must be fresh because leftover authoring context masks gaps in the written instructions.

nodes.label: skill-creator eval plugin
nodes.rationale: The skill-creator plugin (installed with /plugin install skill-creator@claude-plugins-official) automates the comparison loop inside Claude Code: it stores test cases in evals/evals.json, spawns a subagent per case for a clean context while recording tokens and duration, writes pass/fail with evidence to grading.json, aggregates with-skill versus without-skill results into benchmark.json, runs blind A/B version comparisons, tunes descriptions from should-trigger and should-not-trigger prompts, and opens an HTML review viewer.

nodes.label: Sharing skills by scope
nodes.rationale: Skills are distributed at different scopes depending on the audience: commit .claude/skills/ to version control for project skills, create a skills/ directory in a plugin to package them, or deploy organization-wide through managed settings.

nodes.label: Bundled scripts for visual output
nodes.rationale: Skills can bundle and run scripts in any language, giving Claude capabilities beyond a single prompt. The worked example is a codebase-visualizer skill whose bundled Python script generates a self-contained interactive HTML tree of the repo, invoked through ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} so the path resolves at any install level; the pattern extends to dependency graphs, coverage reports and schema visualizations, with the script doing the work and Claude orchestrating.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting skill triggering
nodes.rationale: If a skill does not trigger, check that the description includes words users would naturally say, verify it appears in the available-skills list, rephrase the request, or invoke it directly. Malformed frontmatter YAML makes Claude Code load the body with empty metadata, so /skill-name still works but there is no description to match — run with --debug to see the parse error, or find unparseable files with claude plugin validate on the skills directory (v2.1.233+). A skill triggering too often needs a more specific description or disable-model-invocation.

nodes.label: Skill listing character budget
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads a listing of skill names and descriptions into context; the listing always keeps every name but shortens descriptions to fit a budget of 1% of the model's context window, dropping them starting with the least-invoked skills, which can strip matching keywords. /doctor estimates the cost, /context reports the post-budget size, and the budget is raised with skillListingBudgetFraction or SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET; per-entry text is capped at 1,536 characters, configurable with skillListingMaxDescChars.

nodes.label: Skills extend Claude
nodes.rationale: A skill is a SKILL.md file of instructions that Claude adds to its toolkit; Claude uses it when relevant or the user invokes it directly with /skill-name. Create one when the same instructions, checklist, or multi-step procedure keeps being pasted into chat, or when a CLAUDE.md section has grown into a procedure rather than a fact. Unlike CLAUDE.md, a skill's body loads only when used, so long reference material costs almost nothing until needed.

nodes.label: SKILL.md file structure
nodes.rationale: Every skill needs a SKILL.md with two parts: YAML frontmatter between --- markers telling Claude when to use the skill, and markdown content with the instructions Claude follows. Claude Code reads the frontmatter only when the opening --- is the file's first line; otherwise it treats the whole file, --- markers included, as skill content.

nodes.label: Custom commands merged into skills
nodes.rationale: Custom commands have been merged into skills: .claude/commands/deploy.md and .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md both create /deploy and work the same way, and existing .claude/commands/ files keep working. A command file is invoked by its file name and supports the same frontmatter except name and paths, which Claude Code ignores there. Skills add a directory for supporting files, invocation-control frontmatter, and automatic loading.

nodes.label: Agent Skills open standard
nodes.rationale: Claude Code skills follow the Agent Skills open standard (agentskills.io), which works across multiple AI tools. Claude Code extends the standard with additional features such as invocation control, subagent execution, and dynamic context injection.

nodes.label: Bundled skills
nodes.rationale: Claude Code ships bundled skills such as /doctor, /code-review, /batch, /debug, /loop, and /claude-api. They are prompt-based — detailed instructions that let Claude orchestrate with its tools — whereas most built-in commands execute fixed logic directly. Some are invoked automatically when relevant; others such as /verify run only on explicit invocation so longer checks spend time and tokens on demand.

nodes.label: disableBundledSkills setting
nodes.rationale: Setting disableBundledSkills to true turns off every bundled skill except /doctor. To hide a single bundled skill instead, set it to "off" in skillOverrides.

nodes.label: /doctor survives disableBundledSkills
nodes.rationale: The /doctor setup checkup stays typable when disableBundledSkills is on, in Claude Code v2.1.205 and later. To hide it, set the DISABLE_DOCTOR_COMMAND environment variable or a skillOverrides entry of "doctor": "off". Before v2.1.205, /doctor was a built-in command rather than a bundled skill.

nodes.label: /run bundled skill
nodes.rationale: /run launches and drives your app so a change can be seen working. It needs no setup, inferring the launch from the project type (CLI, server, TUI, browser-driven) and from README, package.json, or Makefile — inference that becomes unreliable for projects needing a database, an env file, a graphical session, or a multi-step build.

nodes.label: /verify bundled skill
nodes.rationale: /verify builds and runs your app to confirm a code change does what it should, without falling back to tests or type checks. It is one of the bundled skills that runs only when explicitly invoked.

nodes.label: /run-skill-generator
nodes.rationale: /run-skill-generator records the launch recipe instead of re-inferring it: it gets the app running from a clean environment, captures the install commands, env vars and launch script, and commits them as a per-project skill at .claude/skills/run-<name>/. Run it once per project, and again if the build or launch process changes.

nodes.label: /verify records its own recipe
nodes.rationale: When /verify has to build and drive an app with no recorded recipe, it writes what worked to .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md at the repo root (or the touched package directory in a monorepo); at the repo root that recorded skill replaces the bundled /verify. Requires v2.1.200+. From v2.1.205 Claude edits the file only when a run was steered wrong, so it can be committed without per-session diffs.

nodes.label: Where skills live
nodes.rationale: Storage location determines audience: enterprise (managed settings) for all users in an organization, personal ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md for all your projects, project .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md for one project, and <plugin>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md wherever the plugin is enabled. A <skill-name> entry may be a symlink whose target is read once even if reachable from several locations; the folder name 'synced' is reserved in any capitalization.

nodes.label: Skill name conflict resolution
nodes.rationale: When skills share a name Claude Code resolves by source: enterprise overrides personal, personal overrides project, and any of those overrides a bundled skill of the same name — but not the bundled skill's aliases, so typing /review never runs a local code-review skill. A skill beats a same-named .claude/commands/ file, and any local skill or command beats a skill synced from claude.ai.

nodes.label: Plugin skill namespace
nodes.rationale: Plugin skills use a plugin-name:skill-name namespace, so they cannot conflict with skills at other levels: my-plugin/skills/deploy/SKILL.md becomes /my-plugin:deploy and loads alongside a project deploy skill. The bare name also invokes it unless another command already uses that name.

nodes.label: Nested .claude/skills directories
nodes.rationale: Skills also load from nested .claude/skills/ directories below the working directory, becoming available the first time Claude reads or edits a file in that subdirectory. A nested skill sharing a name keeps both available: the nested one appears under a directory-qualified name such as apps/web:deploy, and invoking the unqualified name loads the project-root skill with a list of qualified variants appended so the matching variant is also invoked.

nodes.label: Live change detection
nodes.rationale: Claude Code watches ~/.claude/skills/, the project .claude/skills/, and .claude/skills/ inside an --add-dir directory, picking up added, edited or removed skills within the current session without a restart. It covers SKILL.md text only — a skill folder that is also a plugin needs /reload-plugins for changes to hooks/, .mcp.json, agents/, and output-styles/ — and a top-level skills directory created after startup requires a restart to be watched.

nodes.label: Discovery from parent directories
nodes.rationale: Project skills load at startup from .claude/skills/ in the launch directory and every parent up to the repository root, so starting in a subdirectory still picks up root skills. Moving the session with /cd on v2.1.246+ adds the new directory's project skills.

nodes.label: Skills from additional directories
nodes.rationale: --add-dir and /add-dir grant file access rather than configuration discovery, but skills and commands are an exception: Claude Code loads .claude/skills/ and .claude/commands/ from each added directory, including directories the Agent SDK adds via additionalDirectories/add_dirs. The permissions.additionalDirectories setting in settings.json grants file access only and loads no skills, commands, or subagents despite the identical TypeScript option name.

nodes.label: project setting source requirement
nodes.rationale: Claude Code loads skills, commands, and subagents from an added directory only when the 'project' setting source is enabled, which is the default. If --setting-sources is passed on the CLI, or settingSources/setting_sources is set explicitly in the SDK, 'project' must be in the list; in --safe-mode none of the three load.

nodes.label: strictPluginOnlyCustomization and bare mode
